title: 'AG Cautions on Use of AI, Effective Human Oversight Is Still Essential
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage. Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors. For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information. “But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said. He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected. “These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance. “For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded. Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here. Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges. The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly. Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use. Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders. “We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment. “Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added. The one-day forum gathers medical experts, insurers, lawyers, and judges in exchanging views on medical negligence, governance, and AI. Meanwhile, in her welcoming address, Zainun, the chairperson for the Financial Lines forum, said a decision made in a boardroom may engage directors' duties, regulatory standards, disclosure obligations, and insurance coverage. “The adoption of AI in a hospital may raise questions of clinical judgement, patient safety, informed consent, data governance, institutional responsibility, and professional indemnity. “A claim may begin as a private dispute, but reveal a broader weakness in governance, documentation, communication, and risk management. No single profession has all the answers. Judges see how disputes crystallise and how legal principles operate in real cases. Regulators see patterns across institutions and markets. Lawyers advise on duties, responsibility, and remedy,” she said. Zainun added that directors and general counsel confront the practical demands of governance. “Doctors and hospital leaders carry responsibility for patient care. Insurers and reinsurers and brokers understand how emerging risks are assessed, transferred, and ultimately borne. “Sound risk management begins before a claim arises by identifying exposures, strengthening safeguards, and preparing for the consequences of loss. Risk professionals, insurers and reinsurers bring combined experience that can help institutions make informed decisions about the risks they accept, reduce, or transfer. The purpose of this forum is to place these perspectives in conversations with one another,” she said. The forum is organised by Messrs Chan Ban Eng & Co (CBE) where its managing partner, JJ Chan, is the founder of the Financial Lines forum. Chan said that he is pleased that Malaysia now has its own dedicated, pro bono Financial Lines forum, and he is proud to have founded it. “Financial Lines connects specialist questions of medical negligence, corporate and directors’ liability, insurance and reinsurance, and AI governance risk. Bringing these disciplines together can help improve patient care, strengthen governance, and deepen understanding of claims and coverage,” he added. title: 'Asteel lantik bekas Ketua Polis Negara Razarudin sebagai pengerusi selepas Clifford Hii ambil alih syarikat - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 7 Okt - Asteel Group Berhad melantik bekas Ketua Polis Negara Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid sebagai pengerusi bukan eksekutif bebas dan pemegang saham pengawal Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong sebagai timbalan pengerusi eksekutif, berkuat kuasa pada Selasa. Perubahan lembaga pengarah itu menyusuli penutupan tawaran pengambilalihan mandatori pada 5 Oktober yang menyaksikan syarikat pelaburan Clifford, Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd, memegang 53.08% kepentingan dalam pengeluar keluli berkenaan. Clifford memperoleh kawalan pada Ogos menerusi pembelian 270 juta saham Asteel oleh Hii Capital, mewakili kepentingan 52.94%, dengan bayaran tunai RM20.25 juta atau 7.5 sen sesaham. Pembelian itu mencetuskan tawaran mandatori bagi baki saham pada harga yang sama. Jawatan Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai ditukar daripada pengerusi eksekutif kepada pengarah eksekutif merangkap pengerusi emeritus, menurut makluman syarikat kepada Bursa Malaysia. Asteel turut melantik Esther Teh Oun Pheng dan Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng sebagai pengarah bukan eksekutif bebas. Pengarah bukan eksekutif bukan bebas Christopher Hii Lu Ming serta pengarah bukan eksekutif bebas Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee dan Wee Hiang Chyn meletakkan jawatan atas sebab peribadi. Pengalaman dalam keselamatan dan perkhidmatan kewangan Razarudin, 63, mempunyai pengalaman lebih empat dekad dalam keselamatan negara dan penguatkuasaan undang-undang. Ketua Polis Negara ke-14 itu bersara pada Jun 2025 dan turut berkhidmat sebagai pengerusi bukan eksekutif bebas Advancecon Holdings Berhad. Clifford, 43, mempunyai pengalaman lebih 20 tahun dalam sektor pendidikan, hartanah dan teknologi kewangan. Bekas pengarah bukan eksekutif bukan bebas HCK Capital Group Berhad itu mengasaskan Gambit Group Sdn Bhd dan pernah memegang jawatan pengurusan kanan serta menganggotai lembaga pengarah, dengan pengalaman meliputi strategi korporat, pembangunan perniagaan, urus niaga, pelaburan, tadbir urus dan pengurusan projek. Beliau ialah anak kepada bekas wartawan yang beralih menjadi ahli perniagaan, Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, pengasas dan pengerusi eksekutif pemaju hartanah HCK Capital serta pengarah urusan kumpulan dan pemegang saham utama kumpulan pendidikan swasta SEG International. Esther Teh, 47, mengetuai audit dalaman dan pengurusan risiko di Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd serta merupakan pengarah bebas OMS Energy Technologies Inc yang disenaraikan di Nasdaq. Beliau mempunyai pengalaman lebih 20 tahun dalam audit, pengurusan risiko, perundingan, pelaksanaan perkhidmatan bersama, operasi dan kawalan kewangan. Jawatan terdahulunya termasuk ketua audit dalaman dan pematuhan kumpulan di Silverlake Axis Ltd, ketua pengurusan risiko dan jaminan bagi bahagian digital kumpulan di Petroliam Nasional Bhd serta pengurus kanan perundingan pengurusan di Accenture. Dr Lor, 62, mempunyai pengalaman lebih 35 tahun dalam perkhidmatan kewangan dan berkhidmat sebagai penasihat kepada Global ESG Leadership Organization serta Kementerian Ekonomi dan Kewangan Kemboja. Beliau pernah menjadi ketua pegawai eksekutif (CEO) dan pengarah eksekutif Canadia Bank PLC di Kemboja, CEO kumpulan EON Bank Bhd, pengarah bebas Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, pengarah rumusan perbankan di Hewlett Packard Enterprise, ketua perbankan pengguna kumpulan di RHB Bank Bhd serta pengarah urusan perbankan pengguna di DBS Bank Ltd. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp
body: 'Asteel names ex-IGP Razarudin chairman, Clifford Hii executive deputy chairman in board revamp KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Asteel Group Bhd (KL:ASTEEL) has appointed former Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Razarudin Husain @ Abd Rasid as independent non-executive chairman and new controlling shareholder Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong as executive deputy chairman. The boardroom reshuffle follows Clifford securing a 53.08% stake in Asteel at the closing of a mandatory offer on Monday via investment vehicle Hii Capital Holdings Sdn Bhd. Clifford emerged as Asteel’s controlling shareholder in August with the acquisition of an initial 52.94% stake in the company via a RM20.75 million cash deal at 7.5 sen apiece. This triggered a mandatory offer for the remaining 47.06% stake in Asteel, also at 7.5 sen apiece. Clifford, 43, the son of the journalist-turned-businessman Tan Sri Clement Hii Chii Kok, who is the founder and executive chairman of property developer HCK Capital Group Bhd (KL:HCK) and group managing director and major shareholder of private education group SEG International. Clement is also the founder of Gambit Group Sdn Bhd, whose subsidiaries are involved in information technology services, investment, business management consultancy and is a registered digital asset custodian under the Securities Commission Malaysia. Clifford, a former non-independent, non-executive director at HCK Capital, has more than 20 years of experience in the education, property and financial technology sectors. He had held senior management and board positions covering corporate strategy, business development, corporate deals and investments, corporate governance and project management. Razarudin, 63, who is also independent non-executive chairman of Advancecon Holdings Bhd (KL:ADVCON), brings more than four decades of experience in national security and law enforcement. He was Malaysia’s 14th police chief until his retirement in June 2025. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. His previous positions include independent director of Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, chief executive officer and executive director of Canadia Bank PLC in Cambodia, group CEO of EON Bank Bhd, director of banking solutions at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, group head of consumer banking at RHB Bank Bhd and managing director of consumer banking at DBS Bank Ltd. At Tuesday's market close, Asteel shares rose a sen or 10.5% to 10.5 sen, valuing the group at RM50.9 million. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. In separate filings, the steel manufacturer announced the appointment of Esther Teh Oun Pheng and Datuk Dr Lor Chee Leng as independent non-executive directors, while former executive chairman Tan Sri (Dr) Soh Thian Lai has been redesignated as executive director cum chairman emeritus. At the same time, non-independent non-executive director Christopher Hii Lu Ming, and independent non-executive directors Yan Ying Chieh, Khor Hun Nee and Wee Hiang Chyn have resigned, all citing personal reasons. Teh, 47, is head of internal audit and risk management at Usaha Tegas Sdn Bhd and an independent director of Nasdaq-listed OMS Energy Technologies Inc. She has more than 20 years of experience in internal and external audit, risk management, management consulting, shared-services implementation and operations and controllership. Her previous roles include group head of internal audit and compliance at Singapore-listed fintech company Silverlake Axis Ltd, head of risk management and assurance for group digital at Petroliam Nasional Bhd, and senior manager of management consulting at Accenture. Lor, 62, meanwhile, currently serves as an adviser to the Global ESG Leadership Organization and to Cambodia’s Ministry of Economy and Finance. He brings more than 35 years of experience in financial services, including banking transformation and strategy, corporate governance, risk management, credit oversight and consumer banking. His previous positions include independent director of Mizuho Bank (Malaysia) Bhd, chief executive officer and executive director of Canadia Bank PLC in Cambodia, group CEO of EON Bank Bhd, director of banking solutions at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, group head of consumer banking at RHB Bank Bhd and managing director of consumer banking at DBS Bank Ltd. At Tuesday's market close, Asteel shares rose a sen or 10.5% to 10.5 sen, valuing the group at RM50.9 million.

Banks typically maintain an average securities portfolio duration of around five to six years, which is considered moderate rather than long term. As a result, their investment portfolios are generally less sensitive to interest rate movements and face lower interest rate risk compared with portfolios concentrated on longer-dated securities. title: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential
body: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage. Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors. For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information. “But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said. He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected. “These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance. “For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded. Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here. Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges. The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly. Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use. Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines Forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders. “We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment. “Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added. title: 'AG cautions on use of AI, effective human oversight is still essential
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): While the emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) has been used extensively and relied upon in the last few years, Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar cautioned for the need for human oversight in its usage.

Dusuki said there is no doubt that AI offers significant opportunities in various sectors.

For instance, he said, in healthcare, it can assist clinical judgement while in the corporate sphere, it can support decision-making, improve efficiency, and help professionals process increasingly complex information.

“But as our reliance on these systems grows, so, too, does the importance of understanding how they are used and how they are governed. We need to ask some very practical questions: How reliable is the information produced by an AI system? What are the limits of its capabilities? Who is responsible for checking its output?” he said.

He questioned what would happen when the AI system does not perform as expected.

“These are not merely questions about technology. They are questions of governance, professional responsibility, and human oversight. Increasingly, they may also have consequences for legal liability and insurance.

“For any institution adopting AI, it is therefore important to understand why the technology is being used, what risks may arise from its use, and what safeguards are necessary. Technology may assist professional judgement, but effective human oversight remains essential,” he reminded.

Dusuki was delivering his keynote address at the Inaugural Financial Lines Forum at a hotel here.

Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin

Also present were Lembaga Tabung Haji chairman and RHB Bank founder Tan Sri Abdul Rashid Hussin, who delivered a special address, and former Federal Court judge Tan Sri Zainun Ali, former Chief Judge of Malaya Tan Sri Hasnah Mohamed Hashim, as well as former and current judges.

The AG said that while there are continuing issues in the usage of AI, there is a need to use it responsibly.

Dusuki said the use of AI requires engagement among those who develop the technology, those who deploy it, those who rely on it, and those who assess and manage the risks associated with its use.

Hence, he welcomed the organisation of such a forum like the Financial Lines Forum as it brings together legal professionals, healthcare practitioners, corporate leaders, insurers, brokers, and other stakeholders.

“We have an opportunity to learn from one another, to better understand the risks and opportunities before us, and to consider how our respective professions can respond responsibly to a rapidly changing environment.

“Ultimately, the question is not simply what artificial intelligence can do. The more important question is, how we, as professionals, choose to use it responsibly,” he added.

The one-day forum gathers medical experts, insurers, lawyers, and judges in exchanging views on medical negligence, governance, and AI.

title: 'RHB to charge merchants up to 0.60% on DuitNow QR payments
body: 'RHB Bank is revising the fees it charges merchants for accepting DuitNow QR payments, with the new rates taking effect on 26 October 2026. The bank informed its business customers of the change in a notice dated 3 October. Under the revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), merchants will be charged 0.35% of the transaction value when a customer pays using a current or savings account, or an e-wallet. Payments funded by a credit card, on the other hand, will come with a higher MDR of 0.60%. To put that into perspective, a merchant receiving a RM100 payment through DuitNow QR from a customer’s bank account or e-wallet will see RM0.35 deducted. If the same amount is paid using a credit card, the deduction goes up to RM0.60. The new rates apply to DuitNow QR payments processed across RHB’s card terminal devices, DuitNow QR Sound Box and Sound Box+, as well as Reflex Mobile and Tent Cards. Consumers will not be affected by the change, as the fee is charged directly to merchants rather than end-users. RHB stated that the revision aligns with the evolving payment landscape and ongoing servicing requirements, ensuring it can continue providing consistent service quality. Merchants seeking further details on the new rates are advised to contact their RHB home branch. Read more of our articles below! Berdasarkan notis pengumuman terbaharu daripada RHB Bank, penyelarasan kadar itu dilaksanakan selaras dengan perkembangan lanskap pembayaran digital tempatan serta keperluan perkhidmatan berterusan. Namun, caj baharu ini hanya terpakai kepada perkhidmatan perniagaan dan tidak melibatkan transaksi pembayaran oleh pengguna awam. Menerusi pelaksaan terbaharu ini, caj pemprosesan bagi perniagaan yang menggunakan Akaun Simpanan, Akaun Semasa, mahupun dompet digital ditetapkan pada kadar 0.35% daripada keseluruhan nilai transaksi. Manakala bagi transaksi pembayaran DuitNow QR yang dibuat menggunakan kad kredit pula, kadar caj yang bakal dikenakan adalah sebanyak 0.60%. Sebagai contoh, bagi setiap bayaran RM100 yang diterima daripada pelanggan menerusi akaun bank atau dompet digital, peniaga akan dikenakan potongan caj sebanyak RM0.35 (menerima RM99.65 bersih), manakala bayaran RM100 menerusi kad kredit pula akan dipotong sebanyak RM0.60 (menerima RM99.40 bersih). title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM1.6 bilion saham di Bursa Malaysia pada September 2026 - CGS International - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 6 Okt - Pelabur asing kekal sebagai penjual bersih ekuiti Malaysia pada September 2026 dengan aliran keluar bersih RM1.6 bilion, susut 17.1% berbanding RM2 bilion pada Ogos, menurut CGS International. Aktiviti dagangan kasar meningkat bagi kedua-dua belian dan jualan sepanjang bulan itu, namun pembelian asing meningkat lebih pantas sebanyak 12.1% bulan ke bulan kepada RM22.1 bilion berbanding kenaikan 9.5% dalam jualan kepada RM23.7 bilion. Bagaimanapun, tekanan jualan semakin meningkat menjelang akhir September apabila aliran keluar bersih terkumpul pelabur asing melebihi RM1 bilion antara 23 hingga 30 September. Peningkatan jualan pada penghujung bulan itu berlaku ketika Dewan Undangan Negeri Melaka dibubarkan. Perkembangan itu menjadikan jualan bersih terkumpul pelabur asing sebanyak RM6.5 bilion bagi sembilan bulan pertama 2026. Jumlah aliran keluar sejak 2024 pula mencecah RM33.1 bilion, manakala pegangan asing dalam ekuiti Malaysia susut ke satu lagi paras terendah baharu sebanyak 17.8% pada September. Pegangan asing susut kepada 17.8% Pelabur institusi tempatan turut mengambil pendekatan lebih berhati-hati pada September apabila pembelian bersih mereka merosot mendadak kepada RM206 juta daripada RM1.6 bilion pada bulan sebelumnya. Pelabur runcit tempatan pula meningkatkan pembelian bersih kepada RM1.4 bilion daripada RM375 juta pada Ogos, paras bulanan tertinggi sejak Januari 2025. FBM KLCI merosot 4.3% pada September untuk ditutup pada 1,651 mata, sekali gus menyebabkan prestasinya sejak awal tahun bertukar negatif. Prestasi itu lebih lemah berbanding Indeks MSCI All Country Asia ex-Japan yang susut 0.7% bulan ke bulan dan Indeks MSCI Emerging Markets yang turun 1%. Pasaran global secara keseluruhannya berdepan bulan yang mencabar, dengan hanya KOSPI Korea Selatan yang meningkat 0.7% dan Nikkei Jepun naik 0.5%. Dalam kalangan pasaran MIST iaitu Malaysia, Indonesia, Singapura dan Thailand, Straits Times Index Singapura mencatat prestasi terbaik dengan penurunan 0.4%, sekali gus menamatkan kenaikan selama lima bulan berturut-turut. Tenaga dan pembinaan mengatasi kelemahan pasaran SET Index Thailand pula susut 1.8% walaupun Fitch Ratings pada 18 September menyemak semula prospek negara itu kepada “stabil” daripada negatif, dengan menyatakan peningkatan keyakinan terhadap penstabilan hutang. FBM KLCI yang merosot 4.3% dan Jakarta Composite Index Indonesia yang jatuh 6.9% merupakan dua pasaran berprestasi paling lemah dalam kalangan negara MIST. Sentimen terhadap pasaran Indonesia merosot pada pertengahan bulan susulan kebimbangan fiskal selepas kemas kini belanjawan menunjukkan defisit sebanyak Rp240.1 trilion sehingga Ogos. Kelemahan turut berlaku secara meluas di Bursa Malaysia apabila hanya empat daripada 13 indeks sektor mencatat kenaikan pada September. 3 sektor berprestasi terbaik Tiga sektor berprestasi terbaik ialah tenaga yang meningkat 8.6%, pembinaan 7.1% dan utiliti 2.9%. title: 'RHB to charge merchants up to 0.60% on DuitNow QR payments
body: 'RHB Bank is revising the fees it charges merchants for accepting DuitNow QR payments, with the new rates taking effect on 26 October 2026. The bank informed its business customers of the change in a notice dated 3 October.  Under the revised Merchant Discount Rate (MDR), merchants will be charged 0.35% of the transaction value when a customer pays using a current or savings account, or an e-wallet. Payments funded by a credit card, on the other hand, will come with a higher MDR of 0.60%.  To put that into perspective, a merchant receiving a RM100 payment through DuitNow QR from a customer’s bank account or e-wallet will see RM0.35 deducted. If the same amount is paid using a credit card, the deduction goes up to RM0.60.  The new rates apply to DuitNow QR payments processed across RHB’s card terminal devices, DuitNow QR Sound Box and Sound Box+, as well as Reflex Mobile and Tent Cards. Consumers will not be affected by the change, as the fee is charged directly to merchants rather than end-users.  RHB stated that the revision aligns with the evolving payment landscape and ongoing servicing requirements, ensuring it can continue providing consistent service quality. Merchants seeking further details on the new rates are advised to contact their RHB home branch.

title: 'RHB Bank sees more upside for 4Q26
body: 'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank Bhd’s management has shared that there is sufficient runway to reposition the bank’s portfolio and capitalise on market opportunities for the fourth quarter ending Dec 31, 2026 (4Q26) after surging Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields weigh on non- interest income (NOII) in 3Q26. Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research said the bank’s near-term outlook faces pressure from elevated MGS yields, which could weigh on its 3Q26 NOII, but that management appears less downbeat on the 4Q26 outlook should MGS yields stabilise or retrace. The research house, which recently met with the bank’s management, maintained a “hold” call and target price of RM8 based on implied one time 2027 price to book, as most near-term drivers have been baked in, with no stronger immediate catalyst. “We came away from a recent meeting with RHB’s management feeling neutral on its earnings trajectory and asset quality outlook,” it said, with weaker trading income largely inevitable given the limited runway for recovery during 3Q26. “While stronger wealth, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, brokerage and loan-related fees should provide some cushion, these are unlikely to fully offset the trading-income shortfall.” The research firm said the impact on 3Q26 should be viewed more as a foregone trading upside rather than outsized losses, given RHB’s relatively small trading book. The Treasury has been tactically unwinding securities positions, crystallising gains where possible while reducing exposure. The bank’s return on equity (ROE) target range of 10.8% to 11% appears within reach despite the NOII headwinds, but only towards the lower end as the burden increasingly shifts to core operations, with loan growth of 6% and management having reset cost growth to less than or equal to 1%, providing scope for better operating leverage. “Credit cost is tracking around the lower end of its 13 basis points (bps) to 14bps guidance, with management comfortable at 13bps and hopeful of achieving 12bps should recoveries materialise,” HLIB Research said. Wealth sales have also risen 35% year-on-year as of June 2026, while bancassurance/takaful, brokerage and loan-related fees continue to gain traction. Taken together, these levers should partially cushion the NOII drag, although the path towards the upper end of management’s ROE ambition has become more challenging amid elevated bond yields. Capital management remains an important medium-term catalyst, with management targeting more clarity on its capital/dividend policy by 1Q27. The priority would be to ensure operations and targeted growth trajectory can be adequately funded while sustaining Common Equity Tier 1 around current levels. Should these growth requirements be met without absorbing the existing surplus, the excess capital could potentially be fully returned to shareholders. The existing dividend remains respectable, with projected dividend yield of 6.5% for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2027.

title: 'RHB online banking to drop support for older browsers from Oct 31
body: 'PETALING JAYA: RHB Bank has announced that its online banking platform will stop supporting older, outdated browsers from Oct 31. These outdated browsers will not be able to access the platform after this date. In a notice on its website, the bank says the change is intended to provide a safer and more secure banking experience for customers. It adds that this is due to older browsers no longer receiving security updates from their respective providers. The bank has set the minimum versions for five browsers, consisting of Google Chrome (V149 and above), Microsoft Edge (V149 and above), Mozilla Firefox (V151 and above), Opera (V130 and above), and Apple Safari (V18 and above). No action is needed if the browser is already on a newer version. For customers unable to update their browser to a newer version, RHB Bank advises them to use the RHB Mobile Banking App, available on both the Google Play Store and Apple App Store.

title: 'Foreign investors flee as KLCI slides 2.44pct
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Foreign investors stepped up their selling of Malaysian equities last week, while local institutions and retail investors increased their buying, as the FBM KLCI fell 2.44 per cent week-on-week (WoW) to 1,630.87 points. According to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd, foreign investors remained net sellers for a second consecutive week, with net outflows rising 65 per cent WoW to RM791.5 million from RM479.6 million previously. This brought their year-to-date (YTD) net outflow to RM6.71 billion. The heavier foreign selling came amid a worsening global bond sell-off, with US Treasury yields climbing to multi-decade highs. The 30-year US Treasury yield rose above 5.6 per cent, while the 10-year yield reached 5.34 per cent, with both at their highest levels since 2002. Selling also spread across global bond markets, while the Indonesian rupiah weakened past Rp18,000 to the US dollar as higher yields, oil prices and geopolitical tensions pressured Asian currencies. However, the International Monetary Fund said global bond markets continued to function in an orderly manner. Local institutional investors turned net buyers last week, recording RM301.2 million in net inflows, although this was 18 per cent lower WoW. Their YTD net buying position rose to RM4.35 billion. Local retail investors remained net buyers, with their net buying rising 4.44 times WoW to RM440.1 million, bringing their YTD net buying position to RM1.52 billion. Proprietary investors also remained net buyers, with net buying rising to RM50.2 million from RM13.8 million previously, lifting their YTD net buying position to RM839 million. At the sector level, foreign selling was concentrated in financial services and healthcare, with net outflows of RM367.1 million and RM173 million, respectively. Foreign buying was concentrated in technology and energy, which recorded net inflows of RM92.9 million and RM55.1 million, respectively. Their top net sells were Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB), Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) and Sunway Healthcare Group Bhd, while their top net buys were Southern Cable Group Bhd, Gamuda Bhd and Vitrox Corp Bhd. Domestic institutional investors focused their buying on utilities, construction and plantations, which recorded net inflows of RM252.1 million, RM182.8 million and RM111.7 million respectively. Their net selling was concentrated in technology, property and financial services, with outflows of RM89.5 million, RM75.7 million and RM53.3 million, respectively. Their top net buys were TNB, Gamuda and Sunmed, while their top net sells were Maybank, IOI Properties Group Bhd and MI Technovation Bhd. Retail investors' net buying was concentrated in financial services and property, with inflows of RM369.4 million and RM88.4 million, respectively. They were net sellers of construction and energy, with outflows of RM229 million and RM57.8 million, respectively. Their top net buys were Maybank, IOI Properties Group Bhd and RHB Bank Bhd, while their top net sells were Gamuda, Solavest Holdings Bhd and IJM Corp Bhd. Despite the broader market weakness, construction, real estate investment trusts (REITs) and technology were the top-performing sectors, while energy, property and industrial products underperformed. Average daily trading value was relatively unchanged WoW at RM2.9 billion. Meanwhile, Malaysia's Producer Price Index rose 10.7 per cent year-on-year in August 2026 from 9.7 per cent in July, driven by higher mining and manufacturing prices. Attention this week is expected to turn to the tabling of the 2027 budget on October 9, alongside developments surrounding a potential minimum wage adjustment and the Melaka state election. The Election Commission is scheduled to hold a special meeting on October 7 to determine key election arrangements, including the election writ, nomination and polling dates. CIMB Securities also highlighted geopolitical tensions, higher energy prices and El Niño as continuing global inflation risks. Three oil tankers were reportedly struck while transiting the Strait of Hormuz, while the US signalled the possibility of intensified military strikes against Iran and Saudi Arabia and reportedly prepared a new offensive against Iran-backed Houthis in Yemen.

title: 'RHB Could Face Earnings Pressure From Elevated Bond Yields
body: 'Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) has maintained its HOLD call on RHB Bank Bhd with an unchanged target price of RM8.00, saying the lender’s earnings outlook remains broadly stable despite pressure on non-interest income from the recent spike in Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields.  Following a recent meeting with RHB Bank’s management, HLIB said weaker trading income is likely to weigh on 3Q26 non-interest income (NOII), with limited time left in the quarter for market conditions to recover.  However, the research house said the impact should be viewed mainly as foregone trading upside rather than significant trading losses, given RHB’s relatively small trading book.  Management has also been tactically reducing securities exposure and crystallising gains where possible. HLIB said the outlook for 4Q26 is less negative, as RHB would have more time to reposition its portfolio should bond yields stabilise or decline.  Despite the NOII headwinds, RHB has retained its 10.8% to 11.0% return on equity target, although HLIB believes the group is now more likely to achieve the lower end of that range.  With securities trading becoming a less dependable earnings driver, greater reliance will fall on core operations.  Loan growth remains on track at around 6%, while management has reset cost growth guidance to 1% or below, potentially supporting better operating leverage.  Credit costs are also tracking near the lower end of RHB’s 13 to 14 basis point guidance, with management comfortable at around 13bps and seeing potential for around 12bps if recoveries materialise.  Other fee-based businesses are showing stronger momentum. Wealth sales increased 35% year-on-year as at June 2026, while bancassurance and takaful, brokerage, investment banking and loan-related fees have continued to improve.  HLIB said these areas should partially cushion the weaker trading contribution, although elevated bond yields have made the upper end of the ROE target more difficult to achieve.  HLIB said RHB’s asset quality outlook remains manageable, with management seeing no significant corporate credit concerns at present.  Gross impaired loan formation continues to come mainly from the SME and community banking segments, but the deterioration has been gradual rather than broad-based.  Potential recoveries could emerge from the corporate, commercial and Singapore portfolios, although management is not assuming substantial write-backs.  RHB is also maintaining underwriting discipline, remaining selective in mortgages and SME lending and avoiding aggressive pricing where risk-adjusted returns are unattractive.  Deposit competition remains manageable, while initiatives such as RHB Pay are aimed at capturing operating balances and structurally improving current and savings account deposits and funding costs.  HLIB said capital management remains one of RHB’s more important medium-term catalysts, with the bank targeting greater clarity on its capital and dividend policy by 1Q27.  A roughly 100-basis-point uplift in the CET1 ratio, equivalent to around RM2 billion, could potentially emerge following Basel III reforms in January 2028.  Management’s priority, however, remains ensuring that normal operations and targeted growth can be adequately funded while maintaining CET1 around current levels.  Any excess capital could potentially be returned to shareholders if future growth requirements do not absorb the surplus.  The stock currently offers a projected FY27 dividend yield of more than 6.5%, while a possible normalisation in the Overnight Policy Rate from 2.75% to 3.00% in 2027 could provide another earnings lever.  HLIB maintained its RM8.00 target price, based on an implied 1.0 times CY2027 price-to-book multiple, saying current valuations already reflect most near-term positives and that stronger catalysts are needed before it adopts a more constructive stance.

title: 'MGS sell-off set to hit RHB's Q3 earnings: HLIB
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: RHB Bank Bhd's near-term earnings are likely to come under pressure from higher Malaysian Government Securities (MGS) yields, said Hong Leong Investment Bank (HLIB) Research. Analyst Raymond Ng said the recent spike in MGS yields would likely hurt trading income in the third quarter of financial year 2026 (Q3 FY26), with limited time left in the quarter for a recovery. He said stronger contributions from wealth management, bancassurance/takaful, investment banking, broking and loan-related fees should provide some cushion but are unlikely to fully offset the trading income weakness. "The impact should be viewed more as foregone trading upside rather than outsized losses, given RHB's relatively small trading book," he said in a note. Ng said RHB's treasury division had also been tactically unwinding securities positions, crystallising gains where possible while reducing exposure. However, the bank's management remained more positive on the fourth quarter, with scope to reposition the portfolio and capture opportunities if bond yields stabilise or retreat. Despite the near-term earnings pressure, management maintained its return on equity (ROE) target of 10.8 per cent to 11 per cent, supported by about six per cent loan growth, cost growth of no more than one per cent and benign credit costs. Ng said the target remained within reach, although RHB was more likely to end up at the lower end of the range. Credit costs are tracking at around 13 basis points, at the lower end of management's 13 to 14 basis points guidance, while wealth sales rose 35 per cent year-on-year as of June 2026. On asset quality, Ng said there were no major red flags, with deterioration in the small and medium enterprise (SME) segment remaining gradual and manageable. "Gross impaired loan formation continues to stem largely from SME and community banking, although management has not seen a meaningful acceleration in stress," he said. He added that RHB remained selective in mortgage and SME lending and was not chasing growth through aggressive pricing where risk-adjusted returns were unattractive. Meanwhile, capital management remains a medium-term catalyst, with management targeting greater clarity on its capital and dividend policy by the first quarter of 2027. Ng said a potential 100-basis-point uplift in RHB's common equity tier-one ratio following the Basel III reforms in January 2028 could translate into about RM2 billion of additional capital. However, any excess capital return would depend on the group's growth requirements and ability to maintain its CET1 ratio at around current levels. HLIB maintained its "Hold" call on RHB with an unchanged target price of RM8, based on an implied 1.0 times the calendar year 2027 price-to-book ratio. RHB currently offers a projected FY27 dividend yield of more than 6.5 per cent, while a potential increase in the overnight policy rate from 2.75 per cent to three per cent in 2027 could provide another earnings boost.

title: 'Weekly Strategy - 5 Oct 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI came under significant selling pressure last week, falling to a 42-week low of 1,630 and marking a fresh 2026 low amid persistent foreign fund outflows. Investor sentiment was further weighed down by rising U.S. Treasury yields and concerns over higher borrowing costs, while heightened geopolitical uncertainty surrounding the U.S.-Iran conflict raised concerns over its potential inflationary impact. Although bargain hunting provided intermittent support following the sharp sell-off, recovery attempts lacked momentum and proved short-lived amid continued caution. Consequently, the benchmark index ended the week firmly in negative territory. Week-on-week, the FBM KLCI plunged 40.75 points, or 2.44 percent to 1,630.87, as falls on Sunway Bhd (-33sen), KLK (-RM1.52), Petronas Chemicals (-28sen), RHB Bank (-36sen) and 99 Speed Mart (-14sen) offset gains on Gamuda (+22sen), Axiata (+1sen) and Tenaga (+7sen). Average daily traded volume last week declined to 3.48 billion shares versus the 3.52 billion shares the previous week, while average daily traded value rose marginally to RM2.89 billion, from the RM2.88 billion average the previous week. Foreign Selling Drags the FBMKLCI Further Below Its August Peak The FBMKLCI enters the week on a fragile footing after closing 7.0% below its August high of 1,753.22 on broad-based selling. Foreign investors remained the main source of pressure. They sold a net RM799.9mn in the week ended 2 October, extending YTD outflows beyond RM6.4bn. However, the coming week carries an unusually dense set of catalysts. Budget 2027 will be tabled on Friday, 9 October. U.S. Treasury yields sit at their highest in more than two decades, and crude oil hovers above USD 100 per barrel. President Trump has said the war will not end before the 3 November midterm elections. The U.S. is also reportedly deploying up to 10,000 troops, along with ships and aircraft carriers, to the region. As such, pressure on oil prices is unlikely to ease soon. Budget 2027 and Melaka Polls Dominate Domestic News Flow Budget 2027 on 9 October is the week's key domestic catalyst. We forecast another expansionary Budget of RM438.9bn (+3.7%), with development expenditure directed towards infrastructure, renewable energy and digitalisation. Revenue is projected at RM363.5bn (+4.9%), lowering the fiscal deficit to 3.3%, which continues the narrowing trend from 3.7% of GDP in 2025 and 3.5% in 2026. Investors will look for three things. First, a credible consolidation path despite higher oil-linked subsidy costs. Second, the scale of development spending, which drives contract flow. Third, any changes to targeted fuel subsidies under BUDI95, or new revenue measures. Politics also return to focus. The Election Commission meets on 7 October to set nomination and polling dates for the Melaka state election, following the assembly's dissolution on 18 September. The result will be read as an early test of voter sentiment ahead of GE16. Meanwhile, the 3Q26 results season is approaching. Pre-results positioning is likely to favour companies with pricing power, given the gap between elevated producer prices and tame consumer inflation. We expect the FBMKLCI to trade cautiously in the first half of the week, before Budget positioning lends support. Valuations remain undemanding. The index trades at 13.7x consensus CY27 PER, about 13% below its 15.8x long-term average. Our end-2026 target of 1,730 implies 6.1% upside from the 2 October close. Hence, we view the pullback as an opportunity rather than a warning. Investors should favour defensive and quality names, complemented by growth exposure to Budget themes. Our preferred picks include GAMUDA (BUY, TP:RM5.65), TM (BUY, TP:RM8.80), SIMEPROP (BUY, TP:RM2.10) and NESTLE (BUY, TP:RM128.80). Any weakness around Budget Day or the late-October FOMC meeting should be used to build positions selectively. (Please refer to our Preview of Budget 2027 report “Strengthening Resilience, Sustaining Growth”, which was released on 9 September for details). Industrial Output Data to Test the Export Boom Budget and politics aside, domestic data are light but relevant. The key release is August industrial production (IPI), due at 12.30pm on 9 October, hours before the Budget speech. IPI growth moderated to 4.7% YoY in July from 6.5% in June. Manufacturing (+6.4%) offset a 3.2% contraction in mining, where crude oil output fell 13.1%. We expect August output to firm from July's pace. Exports surged 45.5% YoY to RM191.05bn in August, led by E&E, petroleum products and LNG. Shipments to the U.S. and China also reached record monthly highs. An IPI print above 5% would therefore reinforce our 2026 GDP forecast of 5.1%. Conversely, a print below July's 4.7% would suggest that export strength reflects prices more than volumes. That risk deserves attention, as the S&P Global Malaysia Manufacturing PMI slipped to 49.9 in September from 50.2. Weak Payrolls Cool Hike Bets; FOMC Minutes Next U.S. data will shape how far the Federal Reserve tightens. The Fed raised rates by 25bps to 3.75–4.00% on 16 September in a unanimous 12-0 vote, and 16 of 19 policymakers project at least one further hike this year. However, the case for an October move has weakened sharply. August core PCE inflation came in at 3.0% YoY (consensus 3.3%), and several Fed officials struck a dovish tone. Last Friday's payrolls report reinforced that shift. The U.S. added only 29,000 jobs in September, well short of the Bloomberg survey of 90,000 and below the bottom of the 60,000 to 130,000 forecast range. Revisions also cut a combined 60,000 jobs from July and August, leaving July in contraction (-10,000). Unemployment edged up to 4.2% from 4.1%. Wage pressure eased as well, with average hourly earnings up just 0.1% MoM (3.0% YoY, from 3.1% in August). October hike odds now stand at about 22%, against roughly 70% in late September. With the labour market losing momentum, this week's data will test whether inflation allows the Fed to pause. ISM Services opens the week on 5 October, with Bloomberg forecasts pointing to an easing to about 55.2 from 55.4. Still, the prices component matters more. ISM Manufacturing prices surged to 77.9 in September from 71.1, even as the headline missed (54.5 vs 55.0 expected). The FOMC minutes on 7 October will show how many members favoured a faster pace. Finally, the University of Michigan survey on 9 October will be watched for inflation expectations, after the one-year gauge rose to 4.6% in September. A firm reading on prices would keep a further hike in play before year-end. Conversely, softer prices would support the view that September marked the last move of this cycle. China Returns From Golden Week With Firmer PMIs China's mainland markets are closed from 1 to 7 October for the National Day holiday and reopen on 8 October. No major Chinese data are scheduled this week, as September CPI and PPI follow on 14 October. Still, investors will digest the September PMIs released before the break. The official manufacturing PMI returned to expansion at 50.1 (consensus 50.1; August 49.8). The non-manufacturing PMI beat expectations at 50.2 (consensus 49.3; August 49.0), while the private RatingDog manufacturing PMI rose to a five-month high of 52.1 (consensus 51.6). This is encouraging after 2Q26 GDP growth eased to 4.3% YoY. However, the gap between the official and private readings leaves the strength of the recovery open to debate. Early Golden Week figures point to firm travel demand. Rail trips hit a record 25.2mn on 1 October, and Macau visitor arrivals rose 22.3% YoY on the first day. Spending data will matter more. Soft spending would revive concern over China's 4.5– 5.0% growth target. Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) said its wholly-owned Indonesian unit, PT Perindustrian Sawit Synergi (PT PSS), has received the arbitral award in a dispute involving the termination of a gas supply agreement. The award is not expected to have any material impact on the group’s earnings, net assets or gearing for FY26. KLK said that while the arbitration proceeding was ongoing, PT PSS and PT GN concurrently engaged in mediation process to explore an amicable resolution of the dispute. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Gas Malaysia Bhd (Not Rated) aims to make a final investment decision on plans for its first regasification terminal by the 2HCY27. The facility to be built in Yan, Kedah, is due to come online by the end of 2030. The proposed terminal, announced in March, is being jointly developed with Japan's Tokyo Gas and Dutch group VTTI at an estimated cost of between RM2.0bn and RM3.0bn (US$490.0mn to US$735.0mn). (The Edge) Mah Sing Group Bhd has signed a collaboration term sheet with Kinergy Advancement Bhd (Not Rated) to provide technical advisory and evaluate power infrastructure for its proposed data centre developments. Mah Sing entered into the non-binding and nonexclusive agreement with Kinergy to assess captive power plant options and Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme frameworks for its sites at Southville City in Bangi, Selangor, and Meridin East in Pasir Gudang, Johor. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Samaiden Group Bhd’s wholly owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd has secured contracts from Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd to undertake engineering, construction and commissioning works, including the supply of solar components, for a 99.99 megawatts alternating current (MWac) large-scale solar photovoltaic plant. The contracts’ value or location of the proposed facility was not disclosed. (Bursa Malaysia/The Star) Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd, part of Berjaya Corporation Bhd (Not Rated), said the enforcement on its properties by Pahang authorities was “unconscionable and totally unacceptable”. The action, taken amid dispute over a sharp jump in quit rent, was also “unreasonable” and impinges on Berjaya Hills’ legitimate expectation to carry on its business and operations in a peaceful manner. The group has secured an interim stay from the court and is seeking leave from the Federal Court to argue its case. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) The Road Transport Department (JPJ) will suspend MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd (Not Rated), both under MYEG Group, as its collection agents effective 12.01am next Monday. JPJ said the decision was made after taking into account the group’ compliance with the terms and conditions of their agreements, as well as outstanding obligations that have yet to be fulfilled or settled. (Bursa Malaysia/New Straits Times) Seal Incorporated Bhd’s (Not Rated) non-interested shareholders are advised to vote in favour of providing associate company MSR Green Energy Sdn Bhd (MSRGE) a corporate guarantee of RM58.7mn to help it complete several solar projects. UOB Kay Hian, its independent adviser, highlighted that the corporate guarantee allows MSRGE to obtain and utilise vital banking facilities without direct cash or equity injections from Seal, thereby preserving the group's working capital. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Inta Bina Bhd has launched its second property development project, a 499-unit serviced apartment project in Bukit Jelutong, Shah Alam, with a projected gross development value of RM291.0mn. The development will comprise two residential blocks, commercial space and supporting facilities. Construction will take 36 months to complete. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Adnex Group Bhd's (Not Rated) has secured a contract from Bursa Malaysia Bhd for refurbishment works at its Exchange Square main building. The RM14.2mn contract, accepted on 2 October 2026, covers refurbishment works at levels six, 14 and 15 of the building. The works are expected to take three months and are targeted for completion in 4QCY26. (Bursa Malaysia/New Straits Times) PMCK Bhd (Not Rated) has proposed to diversify into the import and supply of medical consumable products by acquiring Derberg Sdn Bhd and Marpoliq Sdn Bhd for RM52.8m in cash. PMCK will fund the purchase through a combination of bank borrowings and internal funds. This includes a RM5.3mn deposit, RM41.5mn payable upon completion, and a further RM6.0mn that will only be paid if the companies meet the agreed profit targets for FY27 and FY28. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) TXCD Bhd (Not Rated) has secured a RM110.0mn subcontract from Vestland Bhd (Not Rated) to build a 62-storey Sovo commercial development in Section 44, Kuala Lumpur. The contract's value is about 1.8x TXCD’s market capitalisation of RM62.3mn as at Friday’s close. Work has commenced and is slated to end by 31 December 2028. (Bursa Malaysia) DPI Holdings Bhd’s (Not Rated) subsidiary Eastern Forever (Sabah) Sdn Bhd is acquiring a 2.05-acre industrial land in Kota Kinabalu, Sabah, for RM7.6mn cash. The vacant industrial lot has a 99-year lease expiring on 31 December 2098. The acquisition is in line with the group’s strategic plans to expand its fast-moving consumer goods distribution network and warehousing capacity in Sabah and East Malaysia, thereby enhancing operational efficiency and market presence in the region. (Bursa Malaysia/The Star) Country Heights Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) said its 80.9%-owned subsidiary Golden Horse Palace Bhd has been served with a winding-up petition over two outstanding Industrial Court awards involving RM312,653. GHPB operates the luxury Palace of the Golden Horses hotel at The Mines. It is a major subsidiary of Country Heights, in which the group’s total investment stands at about RM219.0mn. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) Meridian Bhd's (Not Rated) auditors are doubting survival of the group, drawing attention to multiple material uncertainties and missing accounting records. UHY Malaysia PLT issued a ‘disclaimer of opinion’ in its report on Meridian, meaning that they refused to vouch for the accuracy of the financial statements prepared, and flagged the group’s ability to continue as a ‘going concern’ and to remain afloat. (Bursa Malaysia/The Edge) The Securities Commission Malaysia has approved construction firm Lim Seong Hai Capital Bhd’s (Not Rated) transfer of its listing to the Main Market from the ACE Market. The slated transfer comes a year and a half after LSH transitioned from the LEAP Market in March 2025. It was listed on the LEAP Market in July 2021. (The Edge) PETRONAS Chemicals Group Bhd announced on 2 October 2026 that its chief executive officer Mazuin Ismail will retire effective 1 January 2027. Izwan Ismail, 51, has been appointed to replace him. Mazuin, 58, who also serves as the company’s managing director, assumed the role in January 2024. He has spent his entire 35‑year career within the PETRONAS Group. (The Edge) Malaysia’s semiconductor industry has asked Putrajaya to up reinvestment and research incentives, ease access to skilled foreign talent as well as reduce friction of doing business in Budget 2027 to enable the next phase of growth, as competition for investment intensifies globally. While Malaysia continues to attract significant investments — with RM16.9bn approved investments in the semiconductor subsector in 2025 — the Malaysia Semiconductor Industry Association (MSIA) said rapid developments in artificial intelligence, geopolitical tensions, changing supply chains and competition for investment and talent were increasing pressure on Malaysia to strengthen its semiconductor policies. Malaysia “must respond by strengthening the policy enablers that support long-term industry competitiveness” given rapid advances in artificial intelligence, geopolitical developments, changing global supply chains and intensifying competition for investment and talent are reshaping the global semiconductor landscape, it said. (The Edge) Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain and is ready to expand cooperation in various fields, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar said the cooperation would cover healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and smart manufacturing. He said the areas were among those discussed during his meeting with Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa, who is visiting Malaysia in conjunction with the 2026 Formula 1 (F1) Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. “Malaysia welcomes investment from Bahrain, while Malaysian companies are ready to leverage Bahrain as a gateway to the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) market, for the prosperity and well-being of the people of both countries. We also used the meeting to discuss efforts to strengthen Malaysia-Bahrain ties, including expediting senior officials’ consultations to activate the High-Level Joint Committee and strategically advance the bilateral agenda. In line with the aspirations of the Madani Economy and Bahrain Economic Vision 2030, we are committed to expanding cooperation in healthcare, Islamic finance, technology, tourism, food security, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity and smart manufacturing,” he said. (The Edge, Bernama) The SME Association of Malaysia (SMEAM) has called on the government to place greater emphasis on the outcomes of its assistance to small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in Budget 2027, rather than on the amount allocated for various programmes. SMEAM national president Dr Chin Chee Seong said the effectiveness of SME support should be assessed based on whether it leads to measurable improvements in productivity, investment, business growth and competitiveness. At a joint press conference with the Malaysia Retail Chain Association (MRCA) on Friday, Chin said grants should be tied to results, such as demonstrable gains in automation or business performance. Instead of providing assistance based solely on eligibility, he suggested that businesses demonstrate improvements in areas such as automation, competitiveness or business performance before receiving support. (The Edge) Malaysian manufacturers must accelerate the adoption of automation to boost productivity and reduce their dependence on foreign labour, said Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin. He said the government has gradually reduced the foreign workforce quota from about 20% previously to 15%. Foreign workers currently account for 13% of the total workforce. The government targets to further reduce this to 10% by 2030. This gradual reduction will give businesses time to do so but it is happening too slowly, he said. “Every sector is being informed about it. Everyone knows it’s going to be difficult. Businesses understand this; we are not reducing it overnight but gradually,” he told reporters after launching the Malaysia Smart Manufacturing Awards (MSMA) 2027. (The Edge, Bernama) Malaysia is still far from achieving its target of transforming 3,000 manufacturers into smart factories by 2030, with only 93 having successfully completed the transformation so far. Deputy Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Sim Tze Tzin said 161 more manufacturers were currently in the process of transformation and were expected to do so by December 2026. “Under our New Industrial Master Plan 2030, we want to achieve 3,000 smart factories, but unfortunately, our take-up rate is still very low. Only 93 have successfully transformed, and 161 on the way by December 2026. So, we are still very far away from 3,000,” he told reporters after the launch of the Malaysia Smart Manufacturing Awards (MSMA) 2027. He said the government was focusing on helping manufacturers that lacked the financial capacity and capabilities to adopt smart manufacturing technologies. (The Star) US manufacturers in Malaysia shift to local suppliers, cut Chinese inputs amid tariffs, survey shows American manufacturers operating in Malaysia are reducing their reliance on Chinese inputs and turning to local suppliers as they adapt to pressure from US tariffs, according to a survey. The American Malaysian Chamber of Commerce’s (AMCHAM) latest Economic Impact Survey found that companies responded to tariff pressure by reorganising their procurement, repricing products and reshaping their workforce, rather than simply absorbing higher costs or pulling out of Malaysia. Of the 21 manufacturers that source inputs from China, none increased their reliance on Chinese suppliers after the tariffs took effect. Meanwhile, nine companies, or 43% of the 21, reduced their reliance on China. These companies are concentrated in electronics manufacturing services and hightechnology hardware, sectors with historically deep supplier linkages to China. Separately, AMCHAM said 15 of the 44 manufacturers surveyed, or 34%, increased the share of their inputs sourced from Malaysia in response to tariff pressure. (The Edge) Japan is no longer experiencing deflation so does not need excessively loose monetary policy for the pursuit of a higher inflation rate, Economy Minister Minoru Kiuchi said on Friday. Monetary policy decisions are the jurisdiction of the Bank of Japan (BOJ), Kiuchi added, declining to comment on whether the government opposed further central bank interest rate hikes. "Japan has emerged from an era where it needed the kind of reflationist policies taken under Abenomics," Kiuchi said at a regular news conference, adding that Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi's policies were different from the massive stimulus introduced by the late former prime minister Shinzo Abe in 2013. Kiuchi made the remarks in response to reporters asking about a summary of opinions of the BOJ's September policy meeting, which showed a government representative called for caution over further interest rate hikes. The remarks add to commentary from the government dismissing the viewpoint that it was pursuing reflationist policies to bolster demand through expansionary fiscal and monetary steps. (Reuters) US job growth slowed more than expected in September, but that likely does not signal a material shift in the labour market, with the weakness likely related to a calendar quirk. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 29,000 jobs last month after a downwardly revised 133,000 rise in August, the Labour Department's closely watched employment report showed on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast payrolls advancing 90,000 after a previously reported 162,000 surge in August. Estimates ranged from as low as 35,000 to as high as 180,000. Volatility linked to seasonal adjustment factors, the model the government uses to strip out seasonal fluctuations from the data, probably accounted for both the meagre payroll gains last month and the downward revision to August's count. (Reuters) Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the recent rise in US Treasury yields was in line with global trends and didn’t warrant consternation, even as worries about persisting price pressures pushed some benchmark rates to their highest in more than two decades. “I would be concerned if we were having some kind of idiosyncratic rise,” Bessent said during an interview with Axios published on Saturday. “We’re not seeing people selling treasuries to buy German bonds or Japanese bonds I can’t control the bond market. What I can do is get people to slow down and think,” he said. Bessent also touted the US financial intervention to rescue Argentina and left the door open to similar rescues in the future. The Trump administration last year bought the peso and provided the government of Javier Milei — a Trump ally — with a US$20bn (RM81.7bn) swap line, which helped Argentina defend its currency and ward off a full-blown economic crisis. (Bloomberg) President Donald Trump said he won’t ban US diesel exports, after Group of Seven nations and their partners agreed to release some of their emergency fuel stockpiles in a bid to bring down soaring prices. “Europe has a lot of diesel and they’re going to be making a major world contribution — and so are we,” Trump told reporters Friday at the White House. “And we’re not going to be doing the export ban.” The bloc, which includes major economies from Europe, North America and Asia, agreed to release as much as 100mn barrels of emergency oil and diesel stocks, after an intense pressure campaign from the Trump administration. “I did ask them, and we’re going to have a lot of oil,” Trump added. Trump’s declaration comes amid a record surge in prices for diesel, which fuels much of the modern economy, powering farm equipment, propelling US shipping and supplying heat and power to rural communities. (Bloomberg) New orders for US factory goods barely rose in August as strong demand for electrical equipment, appliances and components was offset by weakness in commercial aircraft orders. Factory orders edged up 0.1% after a downwardly revised 0.8% jump in July, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Friday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast orders gaining 0.1% after a previously reported 0.9% rise in July. Orders increased 6.8% on a year-over-year basis in August. Factory orders in August were restrained by a 4.3% drop in orders for civilian aircraft and parts. Orders for motor vehicle bodies, parts and trailers rose 0.8%. Machinery orders soared 1.1%. Orders for computers and electronic products were unchanged but were up 14.7% year over year. Orders for electrical equipment, appliances and components surged 1.1%. (Reuters) President Donald Trump said on Friday that a US trade deal with South Korea now includes US$8.4bn for an oil recovery project. "The Republic of Korea Deal keeps getting BETTER! 8.4bn Dollars for an enhanced Oil Recovery Project. Producing more Oil and Gas means American Energy Dominance and Energy Security in the World for the Future!" Trump wrote on Truth Social. The announcement is the latest in a series of economic and investment deals Trump is highlighting ahead of November's midterm elections, as he seeks to reinforce his economic record amid voter concerns over the Iran war and high gasoline prices. Trump unveiled plans on Wednesday for South Korea to invest some US$200bn in US projects, but Seoul quickly suggested one key element, a US$54bn pipeline for an LNG project in Alaska, was not yet set in stone. Trump said the investment would include the construction of eight large-scale nuclear power plants, a natural gas pipeline and a 6-gigawatt power Generation Facility in Texas. (Reuters) Eurozone inflation surged more than expected in September and is likely to increase further in the coming months on soaring energy costs, keeping pressure on the European Central Bank to raise interest rates and governments to help struggling consumers. Inflation in the 21 nations sharing the euro currency jumped to 3.8% in September from 3.2% a month earlier, exceeding expectations for 3.6% in a Reuters poll, driven primarily by fuel, natural gas, and to a lesser extent, food costs. A closely watched 'core' figure, which excludes volatile food and fuel prices and signals underlying trends, accelerated to 2.5% from 2.4%, on a pick-up in services prices, data from Eurostat, the EU's statistics agency, showed on Friday. (Reuters) Opec+ has agreed in principle to keep oil production targets steady for November, three sources close to the matter said ahead of the group's meeting on Sunday. Gulf Opec+ producers have been pumping well below output targets in the face of continuing export disruptions from the US-Israeli war on Iran, with exports fluctuating at 60-80% of normal levels in recent months. The war has also delayed the group's output capacity review — crucial to determine members’ 2027 output quotas — because it has thrown estimates of future production potential into uncertainty, industry sources have said. The seven core Opec+ members pumped 25mn barrels per day in August, up 630,000 bpd from July, yet still roughly five million bpd below prewar levels in February, Opec data shows. (Reuters) World food prices rose in September to their highest in nearly four years as logistics disruptions and weather concerns affected crop markets, the United Nations' Food and Agriculture Organization said. Fears about a severe El Niño weather pattern have pushed international sugar prices to an 18-month high, while a war-related collapse in Black Sea trade pushed wheat futures to a three-year peak early last month. The FAO Food Price Index, which tracks monthly changes in international prices for a basket of food commodities, averaged 136.0 points, up from a revised 134.0 for August and the highest reading since November 2022. FAO's benchmarks for cereal, sugar and vegetable oil prices all rose last month, though meat and dairy quotations fell. (Reuters) Governments around the world are running out of room to shield consumers from higher energy prices resulting from the Iran war and other crises, with fuel subsidies potentially costing more than US$1tn this year, a United Nations study found. Global policy interventions to cushion the impact of rising food and energy prices will become more difficult to sustain as a result of higher borrowing costs and what’s on track to be the strongest El Niño on record, according to a UN Development Programme report released Friday. The UNDP warned the next couple of months will be particularly important for governments that have deployed price caps, subsidies and tax rebates as oil near US$100-abarrel and elevated borrowing costs squeeze already strained budgets. “The horizon over the next few weeks and months is uncertain because we don’t see a very clear pathway out of the three-pronged crisis,” said UNDP’s chief economist George Gray Molina, pointing to the Iran war, borrowing costs and the weather phenomenon El Niño. title: 'Pelabur asing jual RM799.9 juta ekuiti Bursa Malaysia untuk minggu kedua - MBSB Research - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt – Pelabur asing terus mengurangkan pegangan dalam pasaran saham Malaysia apabila mencatatkan jualan bersih RM799.9 juta bagi minggu berakhir 2 Oktober 2026, menurut MBSB Research. Jualan bersih itu menjadikan aliran keluar dana asing di Bursa Malaysia berterusan untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan pelabur asing menjadi penjual bersih pada kesemua lima hari dagangan sepanjang minggu berkenaan. “Jualan paling tinggi direkodkan pada Rabu sebanyak RM228.4 juta, diikuti Khamis RM187.9 juta, Selasa RM172.4 juta, Isnin RM142.1 juta dan Jumaat RM69.1 juta,” kata MBSB Research dalam nota kajiannya. Pelabur tempatan ambil peluang Berbeza dengan pelabur asing, institusi tempatan meneruskan trend pembelian bersih untuk minggu kedua berturut-turut dengan aliran masuk RM352.4 juta. Pelabur runcit pula meneruskan pembelian bersih bagi minggu keenam berturut-turut dengan jumlah aliran masuk sebanyak RM447.5 juta. Ini menunjukkan tekanan jualan daripada pelabur asing sebahagiannya diimbangi oleh penyertaan pelabur tempatan. Dari segi aktiviti dagangan, purata dagangan harian pelabur runcit meningkat 3.7%, manakala institusi tempatan susut 7.9%. Penyertaan pelabur asing pula meningkat 8.6%. Sektor teknologi, tenaga jadi pilihan pelabur asing Walaupun pelabur asing secara keseluruhan mencatatkan jualan bersih, terdapat beberapa sektor yang masih menerima aliran masuk dana. Sektor teknologi menerima aliran masuk asing tertinggi sebanyak RM131 juta, diikuti sektor tenaga sebanyak RM93.2 juta dan pembinaan sebanyak RM78.4 juta. Sebaliknya, sektor perkhidmatan kewangan mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM460.6 juta, diikuti utiliti RM339.8 juta dan penjagaan kesihatan RM163.1 juta. Dari sudut saham pula, antara kaunter yang menerima aliran masuk bersih asing tertinggi ialah Gamuda sebanyak RM86.2 juta, Solarvest Holdings RM65.4 juta, Westports Holdings RM55.1 juta dan Southern Cable Group RM53.4 juta. Dalam tempoh sama, Tenaga Nasional Berhad mencatatkan aliran keluar asing terbesar sebanyak RM278.1 juta, diikuti Malayan Banking RM159.3 juta dan RHB Bank RM135.9 juta. September turut menyaksikan jualan pelabur asing Trend tersebut turut dapat dilihat sepanjang September apabila pelabur asing menjual bersih saham Malaysia sebanyak RM1.69 bilion. Dalam tempoh sama, institusi tempatan mencatatkan pembelian bersih RM205.7 juta, manakala pelabur runcit membeli bersih RM1.48 bilion.
