title: 'Banking Sector - FBM KLCI 50: Lower Bank Weight, Limited Passive Impact
body: 'The FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) will expand from 30 to 50 constituents in December, reflecting the significant growth in Bursa Malaysia's market capitalisation and the broader depth of its listed universe. While the FBM KLCI remains the country's flagship equity benchmark, its current 30 constituents represent only about 60% of the market's total capitalisation, below the approximately 70% coverage typically achieved by major global large-cap indices. The expansion aims to provide a broader representation of the Malaysian equity market while enhancing sector diversification through greater exposure to Technology, Energy and Industrials. To facilitate a smooth transition and minimise potential market disruption, the 20 additional constituents will be introduced in two stages. In the first phase, effective 21 December 2026, the new entrants will be included at 50% of their eventual index weights. The selection cut-off date will be 23 November 2026, with the final list of constituents announced on 3 December 2026. The second phase, effective 21 June 2027, will increase these constituents to their full index weights, completing the transition. Concurrently, the FBM Mid 70 Index will be streamlined to 50 constituents and rebranded as the FBM Mid Cap Index, while the overall FBM Top 100 Index universe remains unchanged at 100 stocks. The expansion is expected to create a more diversified and less concentrated benchmark. Based on market data as at 30 June 2026, the weight of the largest constituent is projected to decline from 13.2% to approximately 11.1% upon completion of Phase 2. Similarly, the combined weighting of the top five constituents is expected to fall from 50.0% to 42.1%, while the top 10 stocks will account for 57.2% of the index versus 67.9% under the current composition. The expanded FBM KLCI will also better represent non-financial sectors. Technology stocks will enter the benchmark for the first time, with an estimated 2.4% weighting upon full implementation. Industrials is expected to increase from 6.2% to 9.1%, Consumer Discretionary from 0.9% to 2.9%, Real Estate from 3.1% to 4.0%, and Energy from 1.0% to 2.0%. For the banking sector, the key implication is a structural dilution in index representation rather than a change in fundamentals. Financials' weighting is expected to decline from 42.7% currently to 39.4% in Phase 1 and 36.6% after Phase 2 is completed. In contrast, financial stocks will be more represented in the revamped FBM Mid Cap Index, with the sector's weighting projected to increase from 8.8% to 14.3%. In this report, we assess the implications of the FBM KLCI expansion for financial stocks and the broader banking sector. The reduction in Financials' index weight could result in passive selling of existing banking constituents. However, we believe the actual flow impact should remain modest given the relatively small pool of assets tracking the FBM KLCI. Based on our estimate of approximately RM3.0bn in KLCI-tracking passive assets under management (AUM), we estimate gross passive selling of around RM202mn across the six existing banking constituents, partly offset by around RM22mn of potential passive buying into Alliance Bank if it is included in the expanded benchmark. This would result in net estimated passive outflows of approximately RM180mn from the seven affected banking stocks. Importantly, the estimated RM180mn net outflow represents only around 0.06% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of approximately RM280bn across the seven affected banks. This suggests that the headline reduction in the Financials weighting is unlikely to translate into material selling pressure on banking stocks. Rather, we view the rebalancing primarily as a potential source of temporary stock-specific volatility and portfolio repositioning around the implementation dates. The relatively modest flow impact is also supported by the phased implementation. Assuming the RM3.0bn passive AUM and underlying index weights remain unchanged, approximately half of the estimated flow would occur during Phase 1 in December 2026, with the remaining adjustment taking place when the new constituents reach their full weights in June 2027. This should reduce the immediate impact of the rebalancing on banking stocks. While we estimate KLCI-tracking passive AUM at approximately RM3.0bn, the actual pool could differ depending on how much is benchmarked to the index. To assess the sensitivity of our conclusion, we estimate the potential net banking-sector outflows under different passive AUM assumptions Even under a higher RM5.0bn passive-AUM assumption, estimated net selling would amount to approximately RM300mn, equivalent to only around 0.1% of the combined free-float market capitalisation of the affected banks. As such, we believe the conclusion that the index expansion represents a relatively modest direct flow event remains intact across a reasonable range of passive-AUM assumptions. Alliance Bank has been identified as one of the 20 indicative candidates for inclusion in the expanded FBM KLCI. If selected, we estimate that the bank could receive approximately RM21.8mn of incremental passive demand based on its potential 0.73% increase in index weighting and our RM3.0bn passive-AUM assumption. We believe the potential index inclusion provides an additional technical catalyst to an already supportive fundamental investment case. Alliance Bank's gross loans expanded by 9.5% YoY, significantly above the industry average of around 5%, supporting continued market-share gains. Asset quality also strengthened, with net credit cost falling to 0.3bps from 14.4bps a year ago, driven largely by recoveries from its corporate portfolio. Its 37.7% CASA ratio provides a relatively stable and low-cost funding base, which should help the bank manage ongoing deposit repricing pressures and preserve NIM. Hence, Alliance Bank offers both a fundamental and technical catalyst - stronger-than-industry loan growth and asset quality on the one hand, and potential incremental demand from KLCItracking passive funds on the other. If confirmed as an index constituent, greater benchmark visibility could also increase its relevance among institutional investors. With the estimated index-related flows relatively small, we believe earnings delivery, NIM trends, credit costs and capital returns will remain the key determinants of banking-sector valuations. The sector continues to benefit from steady loan growth, resilient non-interest income, sound asset quality, and healthy capital and liquidity buffers. We forecast sector earnings growth of 4.8% in CY26 and 5.1% in CY27, while average return on equity is expected to remain stable at approximately 10.2%-10.3%. Malaysian banks also remain a key source of dividend yield, with sector dividend yields expected to increase from an average of 4.8% in CY25 to 5.2% in CY26 and 5.4% in CY27. Against this backdrop, we view the FBM KLCI expansion primarily as a technical and portfoliopositioning event rather than a fundamental negative for the banking sector. While several largecap banks could experience modest passive selling, we believe the magnitude of these flows is insufficient to materially alter the sector's valuation outlook. Instead, share-price performance should continue to be driven predominantly by earnings growth, NIM trends, credit costs, dividend expectations and valuation. We maintain our NEUTRAL stance on the banking sector. The expansion of the FBM KLCI will structurally reduce Financials' representation from 42.7% to 36.6% upon full implementation, creating some passive selling pressure across existing large-cap banking constituents. However, based on our estimated RM3.0bn KLCI-tracking passive AUM, the resulting net outflow of approximately RM180mn appears modest relative to the banks' free-float market capitalisation. The two-phase implementation should further limit the immediate impact, with the index changes spread across December 2026 and June 2027. We therefore expect any flow-driven volatility to be temporary and stock-specific rather than a material sector-wide liquidity event. We reiterate our HOLD calls on CIMB and Hong Leong Bank, while maintaining our BUY recommendations on Alliance Bank and Affin Bank. We upgrade Public Bank, RHB Bank, AMMB, and Maybank to BUY from hold, as recent share price weakness has created a more compelling risk-reward opportunity. Our preferred exposure remains Alliance Bank, supported by its industry-leading loan growth, improving asset quality and resilient funding profile. Its potential inclusion in the expanded FBM KLCI provides an additional technical catalyst. Key downside risks to our sector outlook include further NIM compression, potential deterioration in asset quality and slower-than-expected loan growth. These risks could be exacerbated by escalating geopolitical tensions, weaker economic activity and softer business sentiment, which may weigh on credit demand and earnings growth across the sector. title: 'Era of Cheap Debt Is Over as Corporates Face Tightening Credits — BIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 28): The era of cheap debt is over and rising global bond yields will squeeze earnings, pushing some corporates towards bank loans, BIMB Securities said. Credit conditions are tightening, hurting firms with unhedged floating rate debts, large refinancing needs and those facing upcoming maturities, the research house said. Capital-intensive and highly leveraged companies face greater earnings risk, amplified by weaker credit quality, the house noted. “In contrast, we see tech as one of the outlier sectors — where most stocks are actually net cash,” BIMB Securities said in a note. Unlike true artificial intelligence firms or data centre operators grappling with intensive capital expenditure plans, Malaysian tech stocks is a key rotation sector for the coming era of elevated rates, the house noted. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rate earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating. Bond issuances hit record highs in 2025 and corporates have continued to sell more debt this year tapping into the relatively inexpensive markets. “But this is likely to change as global rates outlook shifts to higher for longer,” BIMB Securities said. The house’s view is for the yield on 10-year government bonds to hold around 3.90% till end of the year but shift towards 4.00% by end-2027. Among the top 100 firms by market capitalisation, utilities, property, telecommunications, construction, healthcare and real estate investment trusts are the most exposed sectors, BIMB Securities flagged. The house also singled out IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) for its high floating rate debt exposure. Genting Bhd (KL:GENTING) and Genting Malaysia Bhd (KL:GENM) were also highlighted as both companies will have to come to the market to refinance substantial debt with sizeable maturities over the next 12 months. Banking stocks, meanwhile, could benefit from the shift, especially those with strong corporate lending franchises, the research house said. Malayan Banking Bhd (KL:MAYBANK), CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL:RHBBANK), in particular, could benefit from the temporary migration of borrowers from the bond market to bank loans, the house said. title: 'CIMB Share Buyback, Market Watching
body: 'CIMB Group Holdings Bhd’s ongoing share buyback programme could mark a significant shift in how Malaysian banks manage excess capital, although investor acceptance will depend on how the programme is balanced against expectations for special dividends, according to MBSB Research.  The research house maintained its Buy call on CIMB but trimmed its target price to RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times.  MBSB said CIMB has been buying back shares daily since Sept 21, acquiring 20.76 million shares for about RM163 million, implying a weighted average purchase price of RM7.85 per share.  The shares, equivalent to about 0.192% of CIMB’s issued share capital, are currently being held as treasury shares and have not been cancelled.  The buybacks form part of CIMB’s RM2 billion capital return programme, of which RM700 million has already been distributed through special dividends.  If the remaining RM1.3 billion were used entirely for share repurchases, MBSB estimated CIMB could buy back around 1.5% of its total share base.  The research house said the programme is aimed at improving earnings per share, return on equity and dividend per share, particularly as CIMB remains slightly behind its FY2026 ROE target.  Share Buybacks Face Malaysian Investor Test  MBSB cautioned, however, that share buybacks have historically received a mixed response in Malaysia, where many local investors tend to favour direct cash dividends.  This differs from markets such as Singapore, where share repurchases are more established as a capital-management tool.  MBSB said CIMB’s relatively high level of foreign investor participation could help support acceptance of the strategy, although market expectations for further special dividends remain high.  The research house noted that the impact of buybacks would also be less permanent if the treasury shares are eventually reissued rather than cancelled.  Its scenario analysis showed that a 1.5% share buyback could lift FY2027 forecast EPS to 75.7 sen from 74.5 sen, ROE to 11.1% from 10.9%, and DPS to 49.2 sen from 48.4 sen, assuming a 65% dividend payout.  Under that scenario, MBSB estimated the implied target price could rise to RM9.46.  Capital Return Could Be Revised Higher  MBSB said there is also a possibility CIMB could eventually revise its RM2 billion capital return programme higher if additional capital becomes available.  Potential sources could include capital repatriation from subsidiaries, restructuring of less profitable businesses and changes arising from Basel requirements.  The research house said the market will be watching whether CIMB’s approach succeeds, as it could encourage other larger banks to consider similar capital-management strategies.  MBSB identified Public Bank and RHB Bank as potential candidates, given their mature dividend payout levels, relatively strong capital positions and exposure to foreign investors.  Earnings Outlook Remains Supportive  MBSB expects CIMB’s FY2027 core net profit to reach RM8.05 billion, rising 4% from FY2026, with ROE at 10.9% and dividend yield at 6.2%.  The research house continues to view CIMB positively on the back of strong non-interest income growth, wealth management momentum, cost discipline and improving profitability.  However, it flagged potential net interest margin compression, dividend disappointment and weakness in the Indonesian business as key downside risks.  At RM7.79 as of Sept 30, CIMB was trading at about 1.13 times FY2027 forecast book value, with MBSB projecting a total return of about 24.3%, including dividends.

title: 'Stock Focus
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL: CIMB) could potentially raise its RM2 billion capital return commitment to increase the chances of its share buyback programme garnering investor acceptance, according to MBSB Research.  A higher capital-return commitment could help offset potential disappointment among investors who are expecting a larger portion of the RM2 billion to be returned via special dividends, the research house said.  “To increase its chances of success, we think there is a likelihood of CIMB positively revising to the RM2.0 billion figure, and that CIMB is confident enough on its ability to garner sufficient capital before signalling to the market via share buybacks,” MBSB Research said in a note on Thursday.  “We would not put it past CIMB’s management to pull off such a manoeuvre — they’ve surprised us positively multiple times in the past,” it added.  MBSB Research noted that share buybacks have historically not been successful in Malaysia. CIMB’s share buybacks make up a portion of its RM2 billion capital return scheme, of which RM700 million has already been returned via special dividends.  The primary purpose of the share buybacks is for CIMB to further drive its earnings per share, return on equity (ROE) and dividend per share figures, MBSB Research noted, particularly as the bank is slightly behind on its ROE target for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026).  The research house noted CIMB has been buying back shares every day, tallying up to 20.76 million shares for RM163 million since Sept 21 thus far.  Who could follow CIMB?  CIMB’s share buyback programme is also being watched for its potential implications on other banks, according to MBSB Research.  The research house described the programme as the first major share buyback scheme by a Malaysian bank for capital management purposes in many years, and said a successful outcome could encourage other large banks to consider similar measures.  It listed Public Bank Bhd (KL: PBBANK) and RHB Bank Bhd (KL: RHBBANK) as possible candidates.  Public Bank, it noted, has already received shareholder approval for a share buyback of up to 10% of its shares, although it has not done any yet. Its management has maintained that this is a capital optimisation option rather than a set path they want to go down, the research house added.  RHB Bank, meanwhile, has high capital ratios and historically releases excess capital via larger payouts in the fourth quarter, MBSB Research noted. It is currently preparing a new capital release plan, which is scheduled to be announced by the first quarter of FY2027, the research house added.  MBSB Research maintained its “buy” call on CIMB but with a lower target price of RM9.20 from RM9.29, based on an unchanged FY2027 forecast price-to-book value of 1.33 times. body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Malayan Banking Bhd (KL: MAYBANK) fell below RM10 for the first time in nearly nine months and banking stocks mostly declined on Thursday amid rising bond yields.  Higher yields generally hurt banks as they take larger paper losses from lower prices of the bonds they hold, which eats into capital and forces them to book losses if they sell. Banks will also have to increase their rates to attract depositors, leading to higher funding costs.  That would weigh on banks’ near term non-interest income as well as their capital ratios, Affin Hwang Investment Bank flagged in a note on Thursday.  Maybank, the country’s top bank in terms of assets, fell for the third straight day and closed down 0.4% at RM9.95. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL: CIMB) and Hong Leong Bank Bhd (KL: HLBANK) each declined over 1%.  The Bursa Malaysia Financial Services Index, which also tracks non-bank firms such as insurers and stockbrokers, fell to its lowest level in 10 months.  The US Federal Reserve raised interest rate earlier this month for the first time in three years, sending the yield on the 10-year benchmark Malaysian Government Securities to as high as 4.18% before moderating.  A growing number of economists expect Bank Negara Malaysia to raise the overnight policy rate in November during the final scheduled monetary policy review for the year.  Rising yields tend to lead to higher corporate bond yields, which also tie-in to capital raising decisions both for banks and other corporates and subsequently, fee income to the banks, Affin Hwang said.  Maybank and Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd (KL: ABMB) have on their books the longest bond duration — the length of time for a bond to repay its cost in cash flows while also being a measure of sensitivity to changes in interest rates — according to the research house’s analysis.  Public Bank Bhd (KL: PBBANK) and Hong Leong Bank, meanwhile, have the shortest duration. In terms of capital ratios, Maybank, RHB Bank Bhd (KL: RHBBANK) and CIMB could see the largest drops, while Public Bank and Hong Leong Bank would see the least due to their portfolios’ shorter duration, the house added.

title: 'You can prove the other side was wrong, win the case, and still end up with almost nothing - Newswav
body: 'That is basically what happened in a recent Court of Appeal case. A buyer successfully proved that RHB Bank had wrongly terminated an auction sale. So you might think the next part was easy. The bank was wrong. Pay the buyer. The Sessions Court awarded the buyer RM863,795.37. The High Court agreed. But the Court of Appeal later cancelled almost the entire award and ordered the money to be returned to RHB. Why? Because saying, “You caused me a loss” is not enough. You still have to prove exactly how much you lost. For example, the buyer claimed RM350,000 based on the difference between the property price and a valuation done many years later. The problem was that the breach happened in 2007, but the valuation was from 2020. The buyer also claimed more than 15 years of rental payments. But there were gaps in the documents, and problems showing that all of that rent was actually caused by the bank’s actions. There was also a RM5,000 legal fee claim, but again, there was not enough basis to simply make the bank pay it. The RM26,000 deposit was different. The Court agreed the buyer was entitled to it, but the money had already been sent to the Registrar of Unclaimed Moneys, so it had to be claimed from there. The lesson is simple. Winning the argument is only step one. You must also be able to show: What exactly did you lose? How did you calculate it? Did the other side actually cause that loss? Do you have documents to prove it? Did you do anything to reduce the loss? If you cannot prove those things properly, even a very large damages award can disappear on appeal. Case: RHB Bank Berhad v Tee Ban Tiong, Court of Appeal, decided on 27 August 2026. title: 'Three Banks Lose Buy Ratings as Bond Yields Rise; Hong Leong Names PBBANK Its 4Q Top Pick
body: 'Hong Leong Investment Bank analyst Raymond Ng Ing Yeow downgraded AMMB Holdings, CIMB Group Holdings and RHB Bank to “Hold” from “Buy” in a banking-sector review. He cut their target prices to RM6.70 from RM7.80, RM8.10 from RM8.70 and RM8.00 from RM9.50, respectively. In contrast, he upgraded Public Bank to “Buy” from “Hold” and raised its target price to RM5.30 from RM4.90, naming it his top banking pick for 4Q26. Raymond Ng Ing Yeow is ranked No.10 among 17 financial services analysts on StockTipRatings, based on data since 2023. He holds a 66% expert rating, with a 7% average return and a 56% success rate across stocks he covered over the one-year period following his calls. The changes come as the yield on 10-year Malaysian Government Securities rose to 3.94% on September 25 from 3.60% at end-June. Higher yields reduce the market value of bonds already held by banks, potentially weighing on treasury-related non-interest income before the benefit of reinvesting at higher yields emerges. Raymond said the immediate impact appears manageable, but repeated increases in yields could make earnings less predictable and limit further gains in bank valuations. Under his hypothetical 30-basis-point yield-rise scenario, the estimated gross mark-to-market impact for AMMB Holdings and Bank Islam Malaysia is equivalent to about 10% of their projected annual non-interest income, compared with 4.5% for CIMB Group Holdings and 3.2% for RHB Bank. Public Bank’s direct earnings sensitivity is lower at 1.3%. These are pre-tax estimates that exclude hedging and other offsets—not cuts to earnings forecasts. Raymond said the three downgrades reflect weaker visibility over non-interest income and a higher hurdle for bank-share valuations to rise further. He favours Public Bank for its exceptionally low impaired-loan ratio, resilient earnings and relatively limited direct earnings exposure to the bond-market sell-off, although its bond holdings could still affect book value. He maintained a “Neutral” sector view, noting that foreign investors sold a net RM1.3 billion of Malaysian banking shares between July 1 and September 25, while higher bond yields have made fixed-income investments more competitive. title: 'Isu tutup akaun bank RHB syarikat perkapalan Maritime Network: Keputusan injunksi  23 Oktober ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Mahkamah Tinggi, di sini, menetapkan 23 Oktober ini untuk memutuskan permohonan injunksi sebuah syarikat perkapalan bagi menghalang RHB Bank Berhad daripada menutup dua akaun lama milik syarikat itu sementara menunggu penyelesaian saman penuh. Pesuruhjaya Kehakiman, Elesabet Paya Wan menetapkan tarikh berkenaan selepas mendengar hujahan peguam P Taneswaran yang mewakili Maritime Network Sdn Bhd dan peguam bank berkenaan, Gan Khong Aik. Terdahulu, Taneswaran berhujah bahawa pihak bank gagal menunjukkan sama ada plaintif, Maritime Network sudah melanggar mana-mana terma atau keperluan yang boleh menyebabkan akaunnya ditutup. Beliau turut berhujah bank mempunyai kewajipan fidusiari dan kewajipan berjaga-jaga terhadap pelanggannya, Maritime Network. Bagaimanapun, Khong Aik berhujah tiada hubungan fidusiari atau kewajipan berjaga-jaga antara bank dan syarikat perkapalan itu, dengan menyatakan hubungan antara bank dan pelanggannya adalah hubungan antara penghutang dengan pemiutang. Pada Oktober tahun lalu, Mahkamah Tinggi memberikan injunksi sementara bagi menghalang RHB Bank daripada menutup kedua-dua akaun berkenaan sementara menunggu pendengaran permohonan injunksi penuh syarikat itu. Menurut dokumen mahkamah, Maritime Network membuka dua akaun dengan RHB sejak 23 September 2005, masing-masing membabitkan akaun pelbagai mata wang dan akaun semasa. Bagaimanapun, pada 6 Oktpber tahun lalu, syarikat itu menerima notis penamatan bertarikh 1 Oktober yang memaklumkan bank berhasrat menutup kedua-dua akaun serta menamatkan semua perkhidmatan dalam tempoh 14 hari. Bank didakwa berbuat demikian atas alasan berlaku pelanggaran dasar dan garis panduan dalaman, namun tidak menjelaskan dasar atau garis panduan yang didakwa dilanggar. Syarikat itu turut memaklumkan terdapat pertikaian berterusan antara kedua-dua pihak berkaitan akaun berkenaan, yang sebelum ini telah dibawa ke Mahkamah Tinggi melalui permohonan penzahiran dokumen, tetapi ditolak pada 2 Julai tahun lepas. Syarikat itu kemudian mengemukakan rayuan kepada Mahkamah Rayuan, yang pada Disember tahun lalu membenarkan rayuannya terhadap keputusan menolak permohonan penzahiran praperbicaraan berkenaan. Susulan itu, Mahkamah Rayuan mengarahkan RHB mengemukakan garis panduan Minimum Due Diligence (MDD) yang mengawal selia urus niaga pertukaran asing kepada syarikat berkenaan dalam tempoh 45 hari. Maritime Network seterusnya mendakwa tuduhan umum yang dikemukakan bank menyebabkan syarikat itu berada dalam keadaan tidak menentu serta dinafikan peluang untuk membela diri, yang didakwa sebagai penyalahgunaan kuasa sehingga menjejaskan haknya. Syarikat itu turut mendakwa tindakan bank berkenaan menunjukkan niat untuk menindas, bukannya melindungi kepentingan sahnya dalam urusan perbankan.

title: 'High Court to rule Oct 23 on Maritime Network’s bid to keep RHB accounts open
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court here today fixed Oct 23 to rule on a shipping company’s bid to restrain RHB Bank Berhad from closing two of its long-standing accounts, pending the disposal of its full suit.  Judicial Commissioner Elesabet Paya Wan set the date after hearing submissions from P. Taneswaran, acting for Maritime Network Sdn Bhd, and the bank’s counsel, Gan Khong Aik.  Taneswaran submitted that the bank had failed to establish any breach of terms or requirements by the plaintiff, Maritime Network, that would justify closing its accounts.  He further argued that the bank owed Maritime Network both a fiduciary duty and a duty of care.  Gan countered that no fiduciary relationship or duty of care arose between the bank and the shipping company, submitting that the relationship between a bank and its customer was that of debtor and creditor.  In October last year, the High Court granted a temporary injunction restraining RHB from closing the two long-standing accounts, pending the hearing of the company’s application for a full injunction.  According to court documents, the company has held a multi-currency account and a current account with RHB since 2005.  On Oct 6, 2025, it received a termination notice dated Oct 1, 2025, stating that the bank intended to close both accounts and terminate all related services within 14 days, citing breaches of its internal policies and guidelines.  The company, however, claimed that RHB had failed to specify which policies or guidelines had allegedly been breached.  The plaintiff said an ongoing dispute over the accounts had earlier led to its pre-trial discovery application being dismissed by the High Court on July 2, 2025.  The company subsequently appealed to the Court of Appeal, which in December last year allowed its appeal against the dismissal of the pre-trial discovery application. title: 'RHB Makeover Flexi Loan for Home Renovation
body: '21st September 2026 - 3 min read You can now include renovation costs in your home loan with the Makeover Flexi Loan, from RHB Bank and The Makeover Guys. It covers up to 90% of the property’s value, plus up to 30% more for renovation and related costs, for a total of up to 120%. With a standard home loan, you can usually borrow up to 90% of the property’s value, and the renovation is paid for separately with savings, a personal loan, or a renovation loan. The extra 30% can go towards your renovation, legal and documentation fees, and Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance (MRTA). MRTA is insurance that pays off the rest of your home loan if you pass away or become totally and permanently disabled. If you take an Islamic home loan, the same cover is called Mortgage Reducing Term Takaful (MRTT). It’s also a full flexi loan. You can put extra cash, like a bonus, into the loan, which lowers what you still owe and the interest you pay on it. If you need that money back later, you can take it out again, which is called a redraw. As an example, on a RM500,000 home, you could borrow up to RM450,000 to buy the property, and you’d pay the remaining RM50,000 yourself as your down payment. You could then borrow up to RM150,000 more for your renovation, MRTA, and legal fees. The final loan amount you get depends on RHB Bank’s check of your income and any loans you already have. Since the renovation is part of your home loan, you apply once and make one monthly repayment. Home loan interest rates are generally lower than personal loan rates. Your renovation cost is also spread over your home loan’s repayment period of up to 35 years or until you turn 70, whichever comes first, while most personal loans run for up to 10 years. The savings you’d have set aside for renovation can go towards furniture or your emergency fund instead. RHB Bank pays out the renovation money bit by bit, each time your contractor finishes a stage of the work. The renovation is done through The Makeover Guys, which handles the design, project management, and construction. Your renovation budget is set when you apply for the loan, so get a quote first to see how much of the extra 30% you’ll need. You can also compare home loan rates before sending an enquiry through The Makeover Guys’ website. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates. title: 'OPR berpotensi naik 25 mata asas tahun depan -MBSB Research
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR - Kadar Dasar Semalaman (OPR) Malaysia berpotensi meningkat sebanyak 25 mata asas pada 2027 didorong oleh jangkaan bahawa kadar faedah global terus meningkat, menurut MBSB Research.  Firma penyelidikan itu memaklumkan pasaran menjangka peningkatan 25 mata asas lagi untuk Kadar Dana Persekutuan (FFR) Amerika Syarikat (AS) menjelang akhir 2026, dengan negara lain berpotensi mengambil langkah yang sama.  “Terdapat kemungkinan kenaikan OPR sebanyak 25 mata asas — kenaikan sebanyak 50 mata asas dilihat sukar berikutan OPR tidak bergerak seiring dengan FFR dan inflasi tempatan adalah terkawal.  “Bagaimanapun, tiada keperluan mendesak untuk menaikkan OPR berikutan ekonomi domestik yang kukuh,” menurutnya dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini, sambil menambah sebarang kenaikan OPR dijangka pada 2027.  Kenaikan OPR secara amnya akan memberi manfaat kepada margin faedah bersih (NIM) bank berikutan hasil pinjaman yang lebih tinggi boleh menjadikan pendanaan borong lebih berdaya maju dan memberikan kelegaan daripada persaingan deposit.  Berdasarkan analisis senarionya, MBSB Research memaklumkan AmBank, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Public Bank Bhd dan RHB Bank Bhd berpotensi memperoleh manfaat NIM yang lebih besar daripada kenaikan kadar faedah manakala CIMB Group Holdings Bhd dan Malayan Banking Bhd dapat menghadapi impak daripada pendedahan terhadap pasaran Indonesia.  Secara keseluruhan, MBSB Research mengekalkan saranan positifnya terhadap sektor perbankan, disokong oleh prospek dividen, pertumbuhan pinjaman perniagaan, pendapatan fi dan kawalan perbelanjaan operasi walaupun terdapat beberapa faktor berkaitan pertumbuhan, terutamanya pinjaman perniagaan dan pendapatan pengurusan kekayaan, dijangka tidak berpanjangan.  — BERNAMA

title: 'RHB, The Makeover Guys Offer Flexi Loan for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: 'RHB Bank has partnered with renovation firm The Makeover Guys to offer financing that covers both a property purchase and renovation costs. The Makeover Flexi Loan provides eligible customers with financing of up to 120% of the property’s value. This comprises up to 90% for the home purchase and an additional 30% for renovation work, mortgage insurance or takaful, legal costs and documentation fees. Borrowers can repay the loan over a maximum of 35 years or until they reach the age of 70, whichever comes first. Its Full Flexi features allow them to make additional repayments and redraw funds when needed. Renovation funds will be released progressively as contractors reach project milestones. The facility is designed for homeowners and property investors. Customers can access consultation, interior design, project management and construction services through The Makeover Guys. “We have seen customers delay moving in, renovate room by room over several years or compromise on what they originally wanted because the renovation budget was not available upfront. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one,” said Gavin Liew, Founder & CEO of The Makeover Guys. “As homeownership needs evolve, financing solutions must evolve as well. Traditionally, property financing and renovation financing have been treated as separate decisions, even though both are fundamental to creating a home. We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing these financing needs together under a single solution,” said Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, Group Community Banking, RHB Bank Berhad. title: 'The Makeover Guys and RHB Bank Introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan with Up to 120% Financing for Home Purchase and Renovation
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, MALAYSIA – Media OutReach Newswire – 15 September 2026 – The Makeover Guys has partnered with RHB Bank Berhad as RHB Bank’s Home Makeover Partner to introduce the Makeover Flexi Loan– an integrated financing solution that enables eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility, with financing support of up to 120% of the property’s value. Demand for home renovations continues to rise in Malaysia. The home improvement and renovation market was valued at RM47.7 billion in 2024 and is projected to grow to RM59.2 billion by 2029, as more homeowners invest in upgrading their living spaces to suit changing lifestyles and personal preferences. While home financing is widely available, renovation financing is often treated as a separate borrowing decision. This means many homeowners need to secure additional financing or rely on personal savings after purchasing a property before they can begin renovations. The Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank offers a different approach by enabling eligible customers to finance both their home purchase and renovation under a single facility. Instead of managing separate financing arrangements, homeowners can plan both from the outset, providing greater financial certainty and a more seamless homeownership journey. The Makeover Flexi Loan, Powered by RHB Bank offers: - Up to 120% financing under a single facility for home purchase and renovation - Up to 90% financing for the property purchase, with an additional up to 30% for renovation works, Mortgage Reducing Term Assurance or Takaful (MRTA/MRTT), and legal and documentation fees - Financing tenure of up to 35 years, or until the borrower reaches the age of 70, whichever comes first - Full Flexi features, allowing customers to make additional repayments and redraw funds based on their financial needs - Progressive disbursement of renovation financing according to contractor milestones throughout the renovation process and is suitable for both homeowners and property investors “Every month, we meet homeowners who are excited to receive the keys to their new homes, only to realise that renovation requires another significant financial commitment. A typical renovation can cost anywhere between RM50,000 and RM150,000, depending on the property type, and many buyers simply are not prepared for that additional expense immediately after purchasing their home,” said Gavin Liew, Founder & CEO of The Makeover Guys We have seen customers delay moving in, renovate room by room over several years or compromise on what they originally wanted because the renovation budget was not available upfront. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one. It gives them greater financial certainty and makes it easier to create a home that reflects the way they want to live,” Gavin added. “As homeownership needs evolve, financing solutions must evolve as well. Traditionally, property financing and renovation financing have been treated as separate decisions, even though both are fundamental to creating a home. We saw an opportunity to bridge that gap by bringing these financing needs together under a single solution,” said Sien Vee Loc, Head of Consumer Finance, Group Community Banking, RHB Bank Berhad. Partnering with The Makeover Guys allows us to combine RHB’s financing expertise with trusted renovation capabilities to address a growing market need. Together, we are making it easier for eligible customers to move from purchasing a property to creating a home that meets their lifestyle and investment goals,” Vee Loc added. As Malaysia’s housing market continues to evolve and more buyers enter the market, expectations are shifting beyond financing the purchase of a property to supporting the homeownership journey as a whole. The residential segment remained the largest contributor to Malaysia’s property market in the first quarter of 2026, accounting for 58.8% of all property transactions, with nearly 53,000 residential transactions worth more than RM22 billion. The collaboration connects customers with The Makeover Guys’ end-to-end renovation expertise, providing a complete renovation experience spanning consultation, curated interior design, project management and construction, allowing customers to move from financing their property to completing their home through a single, connected journey.Rather than managing financing, renovation and project delivery separately, customers can now plan every stage together, providing greater certainty over costs, timelines and the overall renovation experience. The partnership further strengthens its commitment to making quality renovations more accessible by combining trusted renovation expertise with financing solutions that support customers from the moment they purchase a property through to the completion of their home. Through this collaboration, The Makeover Guys and RHB Bank are bringing financing and renovation closer together, giving homeowners and property investors a more connected way to plan, finance and complete one of life’s most important investments. The Makeover Flexi Loan changes that by allowing homeowners to plan both their property purchase and renovation together from day one. It gives them greater financial certainty and makes it easier to create a home that reflects the way they want to live," Gavin added. title: 'RHB Pay simplifies how businesses manage digital payments
body:
'
Launch partners of RHB Pay commemorate the launch of Malaysia's first bank-owned unified online payment gateway.

Malaysia’s first bank-owned unified payment platform helps businesses bring multiple payment channels together, with faster settlement and simpler reconciliation.

For businesses, getting paid is only one part of the equation. Knowing where the money is, when it will reach the bank account and how to reconcile transactions can be just as important, particularly for businesses handling high volumes of digital payments.

Launched by RHB Bank Berhad, RHB Pay is Malaysia’s first bank-owned unified online payment platform, bringing payment collection, settlement and reconciliation onto a single platform. Built on RHB’s banking infrastructure with bank-grade security, it is designed to give businesses greater control over their collections and cash flow.

Digital payments have established themselves as an integral part of modern commerce. Malaysia recorded more than 18 billion electronic payment transactions in 2025, highlighting the growing role of digital payments in how businesses collect and manage money.

For merchants, the proposition is straightforward: accept payments through cards, FPX, DuitNow and e-wallets through one integration, while having a consolidated view of transactions and settlement.

But the move to digital payments can also bring its own set of operational headaches, particularly for mid-sized corporates and small and medium enterprises (SMEs) that have to manage separate systems, logins, settlement files and reconciliation processes across different payment methods. That fragmentation adds friction as businesses shift more volume away from cash handling and its associated costs.

RHB Pay is designed to reduce that fragmentation by bringing the different payment channels into one integration layer. This means merchants do not have to build and maintain separate integrations for each payment method they offer.

The unified platform also simplifies onboarding and verification across payment channels, reducing the time and effort required for merchants to get started. It is also designed to accommodate new digital payment channels as they emerge, without requiring merchants to build another integration each time.

Getting cash into the business faster

A payment platform’s value does not end when a customer completes a transaction. Settlement is where many merchants feel the biggest strain. How quickly funds reach their accounts can have a direct bearing on working capital and day-to-day cash flow.

With some third-party payment arrangements, funds can take one to five days to reach the merchant’s bank account, depending on the payment method and settlement arrangement. By comparison, RHB Pay is designed to provide real-time or next-day settlement directly into the merchant’s RHB account, giving them faster access to their collections.

For those operating on tight cash cycles, that can mean having funds available sooner for supplier payments, inventory replenishment and other operating expenses.

Less time spent matching transactions

Reconciliation is another area where payment fragmentation can create additional work. Traditionally, businesses spend considerable time and manual effort matching end-of-day sales across disparate e-wallet portals, card terminals and bank transfers. RHB Pay consolidates these transactions into a standardised report within its portal, which can be reconciled directly against the merchant's bank statement. This gives businesses a single view of their collections, rather than having to pull information from multiple payment platforms and match them manually.

A consolidated view becomes more useful as payment volumes grow, giving businesses greater visibility over their cash position while reducing the administrative work involved in reconciliation.

Built on banking infrastructure

Security and reliability become increasingly important as more payment collections move online. RHB Pay is built on RHB’s banking infrastructure, operating within the bank’s governance and regulatory framework. This gives merchants added assurance over the handling of their funds and payment data.

RHB Pay also leverages Malaysia’s wider payments infrastructure, including PayNet’s national payment rails such as FPX and DuitNow, alongside technology partners across the payments ecosystem.

The platform’s roadmap will see further use of AI and data analytics, including in areas such as reconciliation, fraud management, cash flow forecasting and financial planning.

More than a payment gateway

For RHB, the strategic opportunity extends beyond payment processing fees.

By bringing merchants’ payment collections into the bank, RHB can deepen its relationship with businesses through the transaction flows that run through their day-to-day operations. These flows can also support the bank’s broader transaction banking proposition, including deposits, working capital financing and other financial solutions.

According to research by CIMB Securities, RHB’s enhanced transaction banking capability could lift the Group’s net interest margin (NIM) by about five basis points over time, equivalent to an estimated RM170 million in additional net interest income.

Rather than focusing solely on generating payment gateway fees, RHB’s core strategy centres on capturing merchant transaction flows to build low-cost, sticky Current Account and Savings Account (CASA) deposits. These transaction-linked deposits are embedded in merchants’ daily cash flow cycles, which can make them stickier than deposits acquired primarily through interest rate pricing.

The ability to better understand businesses’ transaction flows could also support more targeted working capital financing and other banking solutions as businesses grow, while creating opportunities for broader fee income and cross-selling.

CIMB Securities maintains a “Buy” rating on RHB Bank with a target price of RM9.20, citing the potential for the bank to strengthen its CASA franchise and deliver capital-efficient earnings growth, alongside its dividend yield and Common Equity Tier 1 (CET1) capital position.

Building for the next phase of digital payments

The immediate benefits are simpler payment collection, faster access to funds and less time spent on reconciliation.

RHB also sees scope to build on this with AI and data analytics, with potential applications in cost management, cash flow planning, fraud management and other operational areas.

The longer-term opportunity is to give businesses greater visibility into the money flowing through their operations, rather than simply providing another channel to accept payments.

title: 'RHB Completes Five-Year Anti-Corruption Plan
body: 'RHB Banking Group has completed all 27 initiatives under its five-year Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan. The plan ran from 2022 to 2026 and focused on strengthening governance, managing corruption risks and improving accountability across the group. Achievements under the plan included the first phase of the Corporate Integrity System Malaysia Assessment. During Integrity Week 2026, RHB also held anti-corruption training and promoted the reporting of potential misconduct. Tan Sri Ahmad Badri Mohd Zahir, Chairman of RHB Banking Group, said, “The successful completion of our Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan is an important milestone, but it is only one step in our broader journey to strengthen trust and accountability across the organisation. As expectations continue to evolve, integrity must remain at the heart of how we serve our customers, engage our stakeholders, and create long-term value.” RHB is now developing an Organisational Anti-Corruption Strategy aligned with Malaysia’s National Anti-Corruption Strategy 2024–2028. Dato’ Mohd Rashid Mohamad, Group MD and Group CEO of RHB Banking Group, said, “The completion of our Organisational Anti-Corruption Plan is not the end of the journey, but the beginning of the next chapter. As we develop the Organisational Anti-Corruption Strategy, our focus is on embedding integrity, accountability, and ethical conduct more deeply into every decision, every interaction, and every outcome.” Featured image: (From lef): Azman Shah Md Yaman, Group Chief Legal & Governance Officer, RHB Bank Berhad; Tan Sri Ahmad Badri, Non-Independent Non-Executive Chairman, RHB Bank Berhad; and Dato’ Mohd Rashid Mohamed, Group Managing Director/Group Chief Executive Officer of RHB Banking Group

title: 'Creador acquires RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar
body: 'Creador acquires RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar This article first appeared in The Edge Malaysia Weekly on August 31, 2026 - September 6, 2026 SOUTHEAST Asian private equity firm Creador, through its philanthropic arm Creador Foundation, is understood to have recently added at least two more properties in downtown Kuala Lumpur to its growing city-centre portfolio — the historic RHB building in Jalan Tun H S Lee and Bangunan UOB in Medan Pasar, according to sources familiar with the matter. The Edge reported in July that the RHB building, a 13-storey office block located at 75 Jalan Tun H S Lee, had been on the market with a reserve price of RM30 million. Sources familiar with the deal say the building has changed hands close to the reserve price. The property carries considerable heritage weight. It was originally the landmark headquarters of Kwong Yik Bank, Malaya’s first local bank, founded in 1913. The building was formally opened in 1965 by then prime minister Tunku Abdul Rahman Putra Al-Haj and became part of RHB’s lineage after Rashid Hussain Bhd took a 75% stake in Kwong Yik Bank in 1996, ahead of its merger with DCB Bank the following year to form RHB Bank. RHB has already announced that its branch at the address will cease operations in January 2027. Details on the Bangunan UOB deal at 10-12 Medan Pasar are limited, although the road itself sits in the same historic banking and commercial belt as Jalan Tun H S Lee, just north of Dataran Merdeka — squarely within the footprint of the areas Creador, together with its founders’ Alaka Holdings Trust, has been actively involved in restoration initiatives. According to sources, Creador Foundation bought Bangunan UOB and the two shoplots next to it for slightly less than RM40 million. During a visit to the area on a Friday afternoon, the transformation to the area was apparent with ongoing construction and restoration works. A source tells The Edge that of the 27 buildings in the Medan Pasar area, 17 of them are believed to have been acquired by Creador while the other 10 have been leased. On Aug 13, Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh announced a collaboration between Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL) and Creador Foundation to revitalise Medan Pasar’s public space as well as improve rainwater management. The acquisitions of the buildings would extend a heritage-property push that Creador, through its philanthropic arm Creador Foundation, has been on since 2024, when it began restoration work around Medan Pasar and Central Market in Kuala Lumpur’s historic district. Its efforts have already delivered several visible wins, with the revival of a shuttered row of shophouses in Medan Pasar, including the Sin Seng Nam corner lot, now home to the popular KLCG Confectionery & Bakery. Creador Foundation’s most ambitious project to date is Muara Arts Gallery, a public art gallery dedicated to modern and contemporary Malaysian and Southeast Asian art. The gallery, with a total built-up of about 20,000 sq ft and is slated to open in November, sits across six Art Deco shophouses from the 1930s. The performing arts theatre, Muara Arts Theatre, is currently under construction and is expected to be completed in 2029. Established in 2018, Creador Foundation was founded by Creador founder and CEO Brahmal Vasudevan and lawyer wife Shanthi Kandiah, founder of SK Chambers. Creador, incorporated in 2011, is known for its investments in brands such as MR DIY, Hock Kee Kopitiam and BIG Pharmacy. The private equity fund has about US$3.1 billion (RM12.52 billion) in assets under management, according to its website. Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy. title: 'Bursa retreats after opening higher on selling pressure
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Wednesday but retreated shortly after, weighed down by selling activity in selected heavyweight counters, led by financial services and industrial products and services. At 9.11am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) eased 3.68 points to 1,629.67 from Tuesday’s close of 1,633.35. The index opened 0.19 points higher at 1,633.54. However, on the broader market, gainers outpaced decliners 221 to 180, with 306 counters unchanged, 2,083 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 327.37 million units worth RM150.56 million. Hong Leong Bank eased 10 sen to RM21.98, CIMB slid 15 sen to RM7.55, and Press Metal Aluminium fell six sen to RM7.13. These three counters collectively pulled down the composite index by a combined 7.23 points. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng noted that Wall Street maintained its positive momentum overnight, with the S&P 500 testing an intra-day record high underpinned by a tech-inspired rally. “This is despite the US 10-year yield remaining elevated at 5.286% while Brent stayed above the US$100 per barrel mark. Over in Hong Kong, the Hang Seng Index maintained its uptrend, underpinned by renewed interest in tech-related stocks as sentiment recovered amid the steadying crude oil prices,” he told Bernama. Back home, Thong said he is anticipating bargain-hunting activities to emerge, although any upside may be hampered by selling from foreign funds following the FBM KLCI’s mildly positive close yesterday. “In view of this, we expect the index to continue consolidating within the 1,630-1,640 range today,” he added. Among other heavyweights, AMMB slipped five sen to RM6.42, Petronas Gas erased eight sen to RM17.20, and Mr D.I.Y. edged down one sen to RM1.24. IHH Healthcare added three sen to RM7.94, and Maybank gained two sen to RM9.99. In active trade, Top Glove gained 5.5 sen to 93 sen, and Supermax added 2.5 sen to 48.5 sen, while Zetrix AI and Ni Hsin inched down half a sen each to 8.5 sen and 37 sen, respectively. Metronic Global was flat at half a sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries jumped 62 sen to RM45.58, Nestle gained 32 sen to RM91.58, and Mi Technovation rallied 19 sen to RM6.19. Critical Holdings bounced 12 sen to RM2.81, and Hengyuan Refining Company gained nine sen to RM3.55. Among the top losers, TMK Chemical cut eight sen to RM2.61, and Pekat fell five sen to RM2.91, while Stratus Global and Solarvest slipped four sen each to RM3.09 and RM4.33, respectively. Malaysia Smelting shrank three sen to RM1.65. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 61.25 points to 17,795.36, the FBM Emas Index cut 5.46 points to 12,227.41, and the FBM Top 100 Index lost 9.15 points to 12,006.63. The FBM Emas Shariah Index gained 26.12 points to 12,185.10, and the FBM ACE Index edged up 0.94 points to 5,659.86. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index inched down 0.09 points to 180.32, the Energy Index gained 6.79 points to 847.51, and the Financial Services Index lost 134.06 points to 18,933.94. The Plantation Index gained 9.57 points to 9,051.74. title: 'F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia
body: 'Intipati berita - 300,000 pengunjung disasarkan hadir ke SIC, termasuk 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa. - F1 dijangka menjana impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion kepada Malaysia. - MOTAC & Tourism Malaysia menyediakan pakej pelancongan untuk menggalakkan pelancong asing tinggal lebih lama di Malaysia. - F1 turut menjadi platform mempromosikan pelancongan, budaya dan seni Malaysia sempena Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027. Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 300,000 pengunjung sempena penganjuran Formula One (F1) Grand Prix (GP) Bahrain di Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) dari 2 hingga 4 Oktober. Menurut laporan Berita RTM, daripada jumlah itu, kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa dijangka hadir ke SIC bagi menyaksikan perlumbaan berprestij tersebut. Ketua Komunikasi Korporat MOTAC, Firna Azura Ekaputri Marzuki berkata, berdasarkan unjuran Hong Leong Bank Research, penganjuran F1 itu dijangka memberi impak ekonomi sekitar RM1.3 bilion. Berdasarkan data penyelidikan Hong Leong Bank, penganjuran F1 ini sahaja dijangka mampu menjana pendapatan sebanyak RM1.3 bilion melalui sektor pelancongan sukan dan perbelanjaan pelancong asing. Setakat ini, kita menyasarkan kehadiran kira-kira 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa daripada keseluruhan 300,000 pengunjung yang dijangka membanjiri SIC bagi menyaksikan Grand Prix F1 tersebut. MOTAC ada sediakan pakej pelancongan? Menurut Firna Azura, penganjuran F1 ini turut bertepatan dengan Kempen Melawat Malaysia 2026–2027 dan menjadi platform untuk memperkenalkan budaya, seni serta produk pelancongan negara kepada pelancong antarabangsa. MOTAC menerusi Tourism Malaysia bersama SIC turut menyediakan beberapa pakej pelancongan bagi menggalakkan pengunjung luar negara melanjutkan tempoh penginapan mereka di Malaysia. Selain menyaksikan F1, kita turut menggalakkan mereka untuk berbelanja, membeli-belah dan melakukan aktiviti pelancongan seperti melawat destinasi menarik di negara ini. Ini kerana selepas penganjuran F1 di Malaysia, saingan seterusnya akan berlangsung di Singapura. Siapa terlibat dalam persiapan penganjuran? Dalam pada itu, persiapan di bawah Jawatankuasa Publisiti, Promosi dan Pelancongan kini dilaporkan mencapai kira-kira 90 peratus. Pelbagai kementerian dan agensi terlibat bagi memastikan penganjuran berjalan lancar, antaranya KUSKOP, KBS, Kementerian Komunikasi, Tourism Malaysia, Kraftangan Malaysia, Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG), Majlis Perbandaran Sepang serta SIC. Apa maksudnya untuk anda? Bagi memeriahkan lagi penganjuran F1 hari kejadian, beberapa program berskala besar turut diatur dari 23 September hingga 4 Oktober. Antaranya ialah Litar Rasa MADANI, Sepang Food Festival di Mitsui Outlet Park, Citrawarna Speed Festival dan RIUH Pitstop di TRX. Selain itu, Malaysia International Craft Fair 2026 turut berlangsung di Kompleks Kraf Kuala Lumpur. The post F1 Bukan Anjuran MOTAC, Tapi Peluang Besar Promosikan Malaysia appeared first on Oh! title: 'Ryt Bank Now Malaysia’s First Digital Bank to Support Apple Pay
body: 'Ryt Bank has become the first licensed digital bank in Malaysia to support Apple Pay, allowing cardholders to pay in stores, online and in apps. The bank also added Google Pay support in January 2026. Customers can add their Ryt Card through the bank’s app by selecting the Cards tab, tapping “Add to Apple Wallet” and following the on-screen instructions. Once they add the card to Apple Wallet on an iPhone, they have the option to add it to their other compatible Apple devices. According to the bank, transactions require authentication through the device’s built-in security features, including Face ID, Touch ID or a passcode. Card numbers are not shared with merchants or stored on Apple servers. Customers who misplace their iPhone can mark it as lost through Find My to suspend their card on the device. Other banks supporting Apple Pay in Malaysia include AmBank, CIMB, Hong Leong Bank, HSBC, Maybank, RHB and Standard Chartered. Apple also lists Wise Payments Malaysia as a participating card issuer, with support varying by issuer and card type. title: 'Daily Newswatch - 6 Oct 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI rose 0.1% to 1,631.8 points on Monday due to improved risk appetite in line with firmer regional markets, after softer US labour data eased expectations of further Fed tightening and took some pressure off bond yields. Technology (+1.7%), Health Care (+1.4%) and Financial Services (+0.5%) led sectoral gains, driven by Nestle (+0.5%), Hong Leong Bank (+0.2%) and Misc (+0.2%). Market breadth, however, was negative, with 598 losers ahead of 564 gainers, while 524 counters closed unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Monday as a weaker-than-expected US jobs report reduced bets on another Fed rate hike, lowering bond yields and setting off a rebound in rate-sensitive technology stocks, following Wall Street's rally on Friday. Taiwan's TAIEX led regional gains (+2.6%), followed by Japan's Nikkei 225 (+2.4%) and Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+0.3%), while markets in mainland China and South Korea were closed for public holidays. In their last trading sessions, Chinese gains were led by Health Care (+2.9%), Consumer Staples (+1.7%) and Financials (+1.0%), with CanSino Biologics (+20%), Shanghai Model Organisms (+19.9%) and Suzhou Novoprotein Scientific (+13.5%) the top performers. In South Korea, Health Technology, Commercial Services and Health Services each rose 1.6%, driven by Enplus, Pusan Cast Iron and CK Solution. European equities mostly advanced on Monday, with STOXX 50 gaining 0.2% and STOXX 600 adding 0.3%. Spanish stocks led, surging over 1% after PM Pedro Sánchez called a snap November 29 election following a parliamentary setback. France's CAC 40 fell around 1% on fiscal and political concerns ahead of the 2027 presidential election, with the euro weakening to a 17- month low. Schneider Electric plunged over 9% after announcing its largestever deal, a $22.6 billion acquisition of US software firm PTC, worrying investors. Banco Santander supported the market, climbing over 4%. US stocks closed higher Monday as heavyweight tech gains outweighed elevated oil prices and bond yields. The S&P 500 rose 0.7%, Nasdaq 100 gained 0.9% to a record 31,076 and Dow added 91 points. Strong earnings, consumer spending and AI investment supported equities despite rising borrowing and energy costs and inflation concerns. Hyperscalers Alphabet (+0.9%), Meta (+1.9%) and Microsoft (+1.5%) gained. Among chipmakers, Nvidia and Broadcom (both +2.1%) mostly offset Micron (-1%), AMD (-0.3%) and Intel (-2.6%). Tesla rose 2.2%; SpaceX jumped 7.6% on reported potential TSMC cooperation with Musk's Terafab. US: 10-Year Yield Rises to 5.33% on Monday The US 10-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.33% on Monday, near its highest level since March 2022 as investors assessed fresh economic data and prepared for the release of the Federal Reserve’s September meeting minutes. The latest ISM report showed that services-sector activity continued to expand, with the PMI at 54.9 in September, slightly below August but broadly in line with expectations. At the same time, cost pressures intensified, highlighting renewed inflation risks despite the moderation in business activity. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Losses as Mideast Exports Recover 5.33% on Monday Crude oil traded near $89 per barrel on Tuesday after declining for two consecutive sessions, pressured by signs that Middle East crude exports are recovering toward pre-war levels. JPMorgan said crude shipments have rebounded to 17.5 million barrels a day, or 98% of prewar levels, while product flows such as diesel and gasoline reached 3 million barrels a day, or 58%. (Trading Economics) US: Services Growth Eases as Price Pressures Intensify The ISM Services PMI fell to 54.9 in September 2026 from 55.4 in August, compared with expectations of 55. The index nevertheless remained in expansion territory for a 27th consecutive month, indicating continued growth in the US services sector. Business activity eased more noticeably, with the Business Activity Index dropping to 56.5 from 61.7, while new orders also moderated to 59.8. Employment improved, moving back above the 50 threshold to 50.1 after two months of contraction. (Trading Economics) US: Gold ticks higher on softer Fed outlook as strong dollar limits gains Gold prices advanced on Monday, supported by continued worries about rising US government debt and fading expectations of an immediate US Federal Reserve (Fed) rate hike, although a firmer dollar limited gains. Spot gold rose 0.4% to US$4,159.89 (RM17,001.89) per ounce by 1138 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery added 0.64% to US$4,188.70. (Reuters) UK: Expected to follow EU with China EV tariffs, report says The UK is preparing to impose import levies on Chinese electric vehicles to meet a key demand from the European Union, the Times of London reported, in a blow to a group that now accounts for nearly one in four cars sold in the country. Brussels has made clear that the UK faces being cut from the Made in Europe local-content rules if it does not act on the tariffs, the newspaper said, adding that EU officials are concerned the UK could become a backdoor for Chinese exports into Europe. (Bloomberg) UK: Job slump longer than during financial crisis, PMI says Britain’s jobs market is stuck in its longest downturn since the early 2000s, according to a closely-watched survey, surpassing the decline during the financial crisis. S&P Global’s UK purchasing managers’ index (PMI) said employers cut back on staff for a 24th consecutive month. (Bloomberg) UK: Hits 17-month low, dollar near pre-Liberation Day highs The euro slid to a 17-month low against the dollar on Monday as concerns about France's ability to rein in its budget deficit and a sharp bond market sell-off last week stirred fears of a return of sovereign debt crisis dynamics in the eurozone. French government bonds have come under pressure as expectations of higher policy rates and rising political uncertainty ahead of the 2027 election cast doubt on the ability of the euro area's second-largest economy to put its public finances on a more sustainable footing. (Reuters) CN: To pump $54bn into state banks and insurers to boost economy China is pumping tens of billions of dollars into eight state-owned banks and insurance companies to help shore up the country's financial system and boost its slowing economy. The cash injection, which is being led by China's finance ministry, will total 360 billion yuan ($53.6bn; £39.7bn), state news agency Xinhua said on Sunday. (BBC) JP: Service sector activity slows from five-month high, PMI shows Japan's service sector expanded at a weaker pace in September as business activity and new orders grew more slowly and earthquake disruption dampened demand, a business survey showed on Monday. The S&P Global final Japan Services Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) eased to 51.3 in September from a five-month high of 52.5 in August, a survey by S&P Global showed, worse than a flash reading of 51.6. (Reuters) JP: Takaichi pledges fiscal discipline as Japan's debt bill rises Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields. She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies. (Reuters) MY: Govt to boost high-value commodity exports, reduce reliance on food imports - minister The government remains committed to strengthening the nation’s agrifood sector by driving higher production and exports of high-value commodities such as pineapples and durians, while narrowing the country’s food trade gap. Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu said the move would not only boost the agrifood sector’s contribution to export earnings but also reduce the country’s reliance on food imports. (The Edge) MY: Govt dividend receipts up 1.4% to RM39.55b in 2025 on higher BNM, Khazanah payouts - AG's report The federal government received RM39.55 billion in dividends from its investments in 2025, up by 1.4% from RM39.01 billion a year earlier, as higher payouts from Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) and Khazanah Nasional Bhd outweighed lower receipts from other entities. The dividends came from 20 companies and two statutory bodies, compared with 21 companies and two statutory bodies in 2024. (The Edge) MY: BNM: Household financial position remains resilient amid West Asia risks The financial position of households has remained generally resilient, supported by Malaysia's stable labour market conditions, according to Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM). It said domestic policy measures, including expanded government cash assistance and continued fuel subsidies, have also helped contain the pass-through of higher global costs to domestic consumer prices. (The Edge) MY: Palm oil stockpiles balloon to record on output surge Palm oil inventories in Malaysia likely swelled to a record last month, buffering supplies of the world’s most-used vegetable oil as an intensifying El Niño threatens to disrupt production in the coming year. The burgeoning supplies could deepen a recent slump in prices, as traders also await a ramp-up in exports to major markets like India that would help draw down the massive stockpiles. (Bloomberg) IJM: Appoints Johan Idris as new chairman Construction and property conglomerate IJM Corporation Bhd has appointed non-executive chairman of KPMG Malaysia Datuk Johan Idris as its independent non-executive director and chairman, effective Monday. Johan, who previously served as KPMG Malaysia's managing partner and country senior partner, succeeds long-serving chairman Tan Sri Krishnan Tan following his retirement. (The Edge) ZETRIX: Owes JPJ RM314m from May to September this year; firm stopped RM231m cheque meant to settle arrears - Loke Zetrix AI Bhd owes the Road Transport Department some RM314 million as it failed to remit collections from May to September this year. The outstanding amount is the reason behind the ministry’s decision to suspend Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG under their three-year contract, which took effect on Monday, according to Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook. (The Edge) ZETRIX: Extends decline to lowest in more than a decade Zetrix AI Bhd fell to its lowest in 13 years after the Ministry of Transport revealed that the digital services company owed the government some RM314 million. The stock fell five sen or more than 40% to close Monday at 6.5 sen, the lowest since May 2013. More than one billion shares exchanged hands, the highest daily volume since Zetrix’ managing director Wong Thean Soon suffered forced selling on his accounts in September. (The Edge) JTGROUP: Bags two TNB contracts worth RM15.7m Jati Tinggi Group Bhd has secured two contracts from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) worth a combined RM15.7 million for underground cable works in Selangor and a submarine power cable monitoring system in Perlis. The larger contract, worth RM13.44 million, was awarded to Jati Tinggi’s wholly-owned subsidiary Jati Tinggi Holding Sdn Bhd for the installation, testing and commissioning of 11kV underground cables and related accessories for TNB’s distribution network in Selangor. (The Edge) CITAGLB: Unit secures RM29m portion of Thai waste-to-energy contract Citaglobal Bhd said on Monday its indirect unit LAWI Engineering GmbH (LAWI Germany) has secured a RM29 million share of a RM52.1 million contract for a waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Thailand. LAWI Germany, together with an unnamed consortium partner, was awarded the contract by Siam Power Co Ltd for the engineering, procurement and construction of a steam boiler plant for the Siam Power Naklang WTE project in Nakhon Ratchasima Province.
