title: '100bps Bond Yield Rise Could Cut Banks’ CET-1 By 46bps
body: 'A further 100-basis-point rise in bond yields could reduce Malaysian banks’ aggregate Common Equity Tier-1 (CET-1) capital ratio by about 46 basis points, although the impact should remain manageable due to Basel III-related capital relief and other mitigating measures, according to RHB Research.  RHB said the estimated sector-wide mark-to-market impact would amount to around RM8 billion at group level, with Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd among the more sensitive banks.  At group level, RHB estimated a 100bps parallel shift in yields could reduce CET-1 ratios by 88bps for Bank Islam, 62bps for Alliance Bank, 57bps for Maybank and 52bps for CIMB.  At the bank-entity level, the estimated impact ranges from just 11bps for Affin Bank to 104bps for Maybank, with Bank Islam and Alliance Bank also relatively more exposed.  By comparison, AMMB Holdings Bhd and Public Bank Bhd are viewed as better insulated.  RHB maintained AMMB, Maybank and Hong Leong Bank as its top sector picks.  Smaller Capital Buffers Than 2021-2022  RHB noted that the banking system weathered the sharp bond sell-off in 2021 and 2022 relatively well.  During that period, the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities yield climbed to 4.07% at end-2022 from 2.69% at end-2020, while the sector recorded an estimated RM16 billion in fair-value losses on securities classified as fair value through other comprehensive income.  Despite this, sector CET-1 ratios largely remained within the 14%-15% range, supported by strong earnings growth, large FVOCI reserve buffers and dividend reinvestment plans.  Banks also shifted more new securities purchases into held-to-maturity portfolios to reduce mark-to-market volatility.  This time, however, RHB said the sector has thinner cushions. FVOCI revaluation reserves currently stand at only about RM3.9 billion, compared with approximately RM9.7 billion previously.  AMMB is the only bank where its FVOCI reserve is estimated to exceed the potential hit from higher bond yields.  Basel III Reforms To Help Standardised Banks  RHB said banks using the standardised approach, including Public Bank, Hong Leong Bank, Alliance Bank, Affin Bank and Bank Islam, should benefit from capital release arising from Basel III reforms, which could offset much of the near-term mark-to-market impact.  For banks using the Internal Ratings-Based approach, RHB said measures such as corporate restructuring and dividend reinvestment plans could provide additional capital support.  The impact from securities classified as fair value through profit or loss is expected to be considerably smaller. Based on previous Bank Negara Malaysia stress tests, RHB estimated a 100bps yield move could have an impact of up to only around 6bps, reflecting the smaller size of FVTPL portfolios relative to FVOCI and held-to-maturity books.  Middle East Conflict Risks Still Contained  RHB also highlighted Bank Negara’s assessment that risks from the Middle East conflict are being transmitted mainly through the real economy and financial markets rather than through banks’ direct exposure to the region.  Higher input and logistics costs, together with softer demand, are putting pressure on business margins, particularly among SMEs in wholesale and retail trade, construction and manufacturing.  However, RHB noted that overall asset quality remains stable, with business impairment at 2.8% and the system-wide impairment ratio at 1.4%, while stress remains concentrated in selected segments rather than becoming systemic.  On funding conditions, RHB said BNM had attributed the rise in KLIBOR partly to thinner liquidity in the benchmark itself, although average banking-sector funding costs have also increased.  Regulatory liquidity ratios remain healthy, while the central bank appears comfortable with banks operating at somewhat lower liquidity levels rather than aggressively competing for higher-cost funding.

title: 'Banks weather Middle East shock with asset quality intact
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's banking sector asset quality remains broadly resilient despite the economic impact of the conflict in the Middle East, according to RHB Research. The firm said any repayment strain remained confined to pockets of the economy rather than becoming systemic. Citing Bank Negara Malaysia's recent assessment and engagement session, the firm said the main transmission channels from the conflict were through the real economy and global financial markets rather than direct bank exposures. Higher input and logistics costs, coupled with softer demand, were putting pressure on business margins, particularly among small and medium enterprises (SMEs) in the wholesale and retail trade, construction and manufacturing sectors. However, domestic demand and electrical and electronics exports continued to support overall economic conditions, while business and system impairment ratios remained steady at 2.8 per cent and 1.4 per cent, respectively. RHB Research said Stage 2 loans had also eased, while household borrowers remained resilient. Meanwhile, the banking sector could withstand higher bond yields, although a 100-basis-point rise could reduce the sector's common equity Tier-1 (CET-1) ratio by about 46 basis points after mitigation measures. The firm said the impact would be manageable but banks would have thinner capital cushions compared with the 2021-2022 bond sell-off. It estimated that a 100-basis-point parallel shift in bond yields could reduce sector CET-1 capital by about RM8 billion at the group level. Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd, Alliance Bank Malaysia Bhd and Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) were among the most sensitive to higher yields at group level, with estimated CET-1 reductions of 88, 62 and 57 basis points respectively. At the bank-entity level, Maybank was the most sensitive, with an estimated 104-basis-point reduction, followed by Bank Islam at 88 basis points and Alliance Bank at 70 basis points. RHB Research said banks using the standardised approach, including Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, Alliance Bank, Affin Bank Bhd and Bank Islam, should benefit from capital releases under Basel III reforms, cushioning much of the mark-to-market impact. For banks using the internal ratings-based approach, corporate restructuring and dividend reinvestment plans (DRPs) could provide some capital relief. RHB Research said the sector's buffers were thinner than during the 2021-2022 bond sell-off, when the 10-year Malaysian Government Securities yield rose to 4.07 per cent at end-2022 from 2.69 per cent at end-2020. The firm estimated that banks incurred about RM16 billion in fair-value losses on securities classified as fair value through other comprehensive income (FVOCI) over the two years. Despite this, the sector's CET-1 ratio remained broadly within 14 to 15 per cent, supported by strong net profit growth, sizeable FVOCI reserve buffers and DRPs. Banks also shifted some new security purchases into held-to-maturity portfolios to reduce exposure to mark-to-market losses. This time, however, the sector's FVOCI revaluation reserve has fallen to about RM3.9 billion from around RM9.7 billion previously. RHB Research said AMMB Holdings Bhd (AmBank) was the only bank whose FVOCI reserves exceeded its estimated loss from higher bond yields, making it relatively more insulated from the risk. On funding conditions, Bank Negara was said to have played down concerns that rising KLIBOR reflected thinning liquidity in the instrument, although average funding costs had increased. RHB Research said regulatory liquidity ratios remained healthy, with the central bank comfortable with banks operating at lower levels rather than paying excessively to secure funding. The firm's top picks in the banking sector are AmBank, Maybank and Hong Leong.

title: '13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty honours real estate excellence |  Penang Property Talk
body: '13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty honours real estate excellence Top developers celebrated the 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia in partnership with iProperty, presented by Lim Soh & Goonting Advocates & Solicitors, at The St. Regis Kuala Lumpur. Guided by the theme “Defined by Excellence,” the 2026 PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty recognised the country’s best in real estate across 62 categories. From township developers to breakthrough companies, this year’s awards were comprehensive, honouring the best in different real estate segments and regions. Timber Land Group won the evening’s top honour, Best Developer, marking its first-ever win in the category, in addition to Best Developer (East Malaysia). CPI Land was named Best Developer (Central Malaysia) alongside award-winning project Tuan Straits. Tanah Sutera took both Best Developer (Southern Malaysia) and Best Landed Homes Developer, buoyed by winning project The Seed. JLand Group, named Best Township Developer, collected the most awards of any company, covering Developer, Development, and Design categories for projects including Arena Larkin; Bandar Tiram; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – Aspiration Park; Ibrahim Technopolis (IBTEC) – STeP West; and Medora One. JRK Holdings Berhad won both Best Breakthrough Developer and Best Boutique Developer. Keck Seng (Malaysia) Berhad was named Best Mixed Use Developer, also winning for the project Daya 1 Residences, Taman Daya. Penang developers also made their mark at this year’s awards, with PTL Properties, Aspen and Pinnacle Group among the winners. PTL Properties was named Best Lifestyle Developer, with The Rimbun also winning Best Mass Market Landed Development (Northern) and Best Townhouse Development. Aspen’s Aspen Vision City received the Best Township Development (Northern) award, while Pinnacle Group won Best Premium High-Rise Development (Northern) for Pinnacle Bukit Gambier. Other companies with winning projects include Amalan Setar (M) Sdn Bhd, which won for Ixora Garden – Sari Alamanda 4 Phase 2; Armani Group (Armani Hallson Bukit Bintang); Astaka Kimlun Sdn Bhd (Amora Serviced Residence); BCB Land Sdn. (Straya Heights); Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd (Coronation Square; Coronade Twins – Serviced Residences); CTC Development Malaysia Sdn Bhd (CTC Skyone @ Bukit Chagar); Faire Development (bée); Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd (Taman Impian Emas); Infra Park Sdn Bhd (MLIMA Kiara); KEB Berhad (Residensi Cove @ Kota Syahbandar); Matrix Concepts (Levia Residence Puchong); OCR Templer Sdn Bhd (D’Templer Hilltop Residences); Peter’s Group (Cherita Residences); Puncak Concept Sdn Bhd (Puncak LakePark City @ Cyberjaya); R&F Development Sdn Bhd (R&F Princess Cove); Steadfast Properties (Laguna Residences); Tiram Industrial Park Sdn Bhd (Akasia Business Park); Tropicana Corporation Berhad (Clarissa Serviced Suites, Tropicana Cenang); UEM Sunrise Berhad (Intrika, Serene Heightshase s); and Worldwide Holdings Berhad (Pavonia Worldwide, Bukit Bandaraya Shah Alam). Outstanding real estate figures The 13th PropertyGuru Asia Awards Malaysia with iProperty celebrated some of the impactful figures in Malaysian real estate. Tan Sri Dato’ Seri Dr. Jeffrey Cheah KBE AO, founder and chairman of Sunway Group, received the Life Achievement Award. Dato’ Seri Azmir Merican, group managing director and chief executive officer of Sime Darby Property, was named Real Estate Personality of the Year. Dato’ Sri Edwin Tan Pei Seng, executive chairman of Paragon Globe Berhad, was honoured as Rising Star, while Ms. Maggie Ng Mui Kit, chief executive officer of Kuok Group Property Division (Southern), received the Woman Changemaker Award. Consumers, catalysts, and consistency The Consumer Demand Award continued this year, recognising the property that captured the strongest genuine interest from Malaysian property seekers. Determined by consumer views and leads across PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com.my, Leisure Farm Resort by Mulpha International was named Most In-Demand Bungalow/Villa, in addition to winning Best Resort-Style Township Development. The People’s Choice Awards also continued the tradition of tapping consumer opinion to identify the nation’s 10 favourite developers. This year, 15,383 votes were cast for developers that consumers in Malaysia admire and trust. The winners of the People’s Choice Awards in 2026 are: Berinda Group; Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd; CPI Land; Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd; JLand Group; KEB Berhad; Matrix Concepts; Pinnacle Group; Tropicana Corporation Berhad; and UEM Sunrise Berhad. In addition, PropertyGuru.com.my and iProperty.com.my presented several titles for the first time this year. IIB Experience Centre (IIBEX) by Iskandar Investment Berhad received the inaugural Real Estate Ecosystem Catalyst Award. The Consistency Excellence Awards also made their debut, recognising companies with consecutive years of wins at the awards. Gunung Impian Development Sdn Bhd won the 4-Year Consistency Excellence Award. Meanwhile, the 3-Year Consistency Excellence Awards were presented to Armani Group; Astaka Padu Sdn Bhd; Berinda Group; Coronade Properties Sdn Bhd; Iskandar Investment Berhad; JLand Group; R&F Development Sdn Bhd; and Tropicana Corporation Berhad. Live selection process Winners of the competitive categories were selected during the Live Judging Days from 30 June to 2 July 2026 at the Amari Hotel Kuala Lumpur. The evaluation process, independently supervised by HLB Ler Lum Chew, saw a multi-disciplinary panel from Malaysia’s leading professional bodies assess an expanded lineup of categories. This year’s panel was chaired by Datuk Ar. Ezumi Harzani Ismail, president of the Malaysian Institute of Architects (PAM) from 2020 to 2022, and included Ir. Ashwin Thurairajah, executive director, GreenRE Sdn Bhd; YBrs. Sr. Haji Ishak Ismail, president, Malaysian Institute of Property & Facility Managers (MIPFM) 2023–2027; Ms. Janice Chin, senior director, Capital Markets, JLL Appraisal & Property Services Sdn Bhd; Prof. Dr. Ir. Jeffrey Chiang Choong Luin, president, The Institution of Engineers Malaysia (IEM) 2024–2026; Dato’ Sr. Lau Wai Seang, president, Royal Institution of Surveyors Malaysia (RISM) 2017–2018; TPr. Sarly Adre Sarkum, chief executive officer, Green Building Index (GBI); Ar. Dr. Serina Hijjas, president, Malaysia Green Building Council (MGBC) 2023–2027; and Ms. Tan Hui Yin, partner, Tan Chap & Associates. Datuk Ar. Ezumi Harzani Ismail said: “Good design is the product of discipline, clarity of intent, and an understanding of how people inhabit space. What struck me most among this year’s winners was a shared design intelligence: sensitivity to context and climate, thoughtful handling of landscape and light, and a commitment to sustainability that goes beyond token gestures. From the elegant restraint of landed homes to the confident lines of high-rise towers, these projects show that Malaysian design has matured into something both internationally credible and distinctly our own. And with quality consistent across every tier, good design is not a privilege of the few but a standard we can deliver for all. On behalf of the judging panel, I congratulate every winner for raising the bar for Malaysian real estate.” Jules Kay, managing director of PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards and Events, said: “This year’s awardees share a commitment to thoughtful placemaking, sustainable design, and creating developments that enhance the way people live, work, and connect. From transformative township masterplans to beautifully crafted landed homes, this year’s winners show that excellence equals lasting value for communities. We are proud to celebrate developers that deliver value and quality to homebuyers. We also celebrate the individual leaders whose passion and foresight continue to inspire the industry. Together, these achievements set a benchmark for Malaysian real estate.” Winners may advance to the PropertyGuru Asia Property Awards Grand Final, recognising the Best in Asia on 11 December 2026 at The Athenee Hotel, a Luxury Collection Hotel, Bangkok. body: '丰隆银行3分行明年关闭，客户业务转移至附近分行！ 丰隆银行（Hong Leong Bank）将关闭3家位于吉隆坡的分行，最后营业日定于2027年2月19日（星期五），受影响分行的客户及业务将转移至附近分行。 根据丰隆银行官网资料，3家即将关闭的分行分别位于Segambut、Brickfields及Pandan Indah。 3家分行将搬去哪？ 其中，Segambut分行关闭后，相关业务将转移至Menjalara分行；Brickfields分行的业务则转往Bangsar分行。 至于Pandan Indah分行，相关业务将转移至Ampang Taman Putra分行。 这意味着，受影响客户日后仍可继续通过丰隆银行其他分行办理相关业务，不过需要前往新的指定分行。 2月19日最后营业 上述3家分行的最后营业日为2027年2月19日（星期五）。 客户若平时习惯到这些分行办理银行业务，可留意相关安排，并在分行关闭后前往指定的替代分行。 银行也建议客户根据自身需要，提前熟悉新的服务地点，以免分行关闭后影响日常银行业务。 全国仍有逾200家分行 尽管这3家分行将关闭，丰隆银行在全国仍维持规模庞大的实体服务网络。 目前，丰隆银行在全国拥有超过200家分行及1025个自助服务机（ATM），客户仍可通过其他分行及自助服务渠道办理相关银行业务。 随着银行业持续推动数码化，越来越多客户通过网上银行及手机应用办理转账、缴费及其他日常银行业务，银行也持续根据客户使用情况调整实体分行网络。 因此，这次关闭3家分行主要涉及相关地点的服务网络调整，客户的银行账户及业务并不会因为分行关闭而终止。

title: 'FBM KLCI charts slight gain at midday
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's benchmark index lagged enthusiasm, weighed down by persistent fears over geopolitical risk, inflation risks and a weak sentiment for equities. At noon, the FBM KLCI was up 1.84 points to 1,632.71, with heavyweight banks helping to shore up the market. AMMB rose 11 sen to RM6.50, Hong Leong Bank jumped 26 sen to RM22.90 and Public Bank was up three sen to RM7.46. On the broader market, the sentiment remained weak with 560 decliners compared to 477 gainers. There were 2.93 billion shares traded for a value of RM1.39bil. The technology sector was the biggest gainer, jumping 1.69%, while financial services rose 0.4% Telcos dove 2.12%, utilities dropped 0.51%, property shed 0.43% and energy slid 0.37%. Meanwhile, Zetrix AI continued its fall after the trading halt was lifted at 10am. The share hit limit down after falling 3.5 sen to eight sen, after news broke last Friday it owed over RM200mil in collections. VS Industry rose four sen to 33 sen and Cuscapi slid 0.5 sne ot 4.5 sen. In regional markets, Japan's Nikkei was up 2.08% to 69,730 while South Korea's Kospi gained 0.46% to 7,003. China's Shanghai Composite index added 0.31% to 3,842. Hong Kong's Hang Seng was nearly flat at 23,952.

title: 'FBM KLCI Edges Higher After Weak US Jobs Data
body: 'The FBM KLCI rebounded in early trade on Monday, supported by easing concerns over US interest rate hikes following weaker-than-expected US jobs data.  The benchmark index rose 4.53 points, or 0.28 per cent, to 1,635.39 at 9.05 am, recovering modestly after last week’s steep losses.  Banking stocks led the gains, with Maybank adding four sen to RM10.06, Hong Leong Bank rising six sen to RM22.70, Public Bank gaining four sen to RM4.70 and AMMB advancing six sen to RM6.45.  Apex Securities said it remained cautious on near-term risk appetite, noting that reduced rate hike concerns and resilient technology stocks were providing support while elevated bond yields and oil price swings could keep gains uneven.  “We remain cautious on the local bourse, as elevated bond yields and crude oil prices are likely to keep investors defensive.  “With key US labour market data pending, external headwinds should keep volatility elevated, and any recovery is likely to stay gradual until greater clarity emerges on the global rate and energy outlook,” it said in a note.  Among actively traded stocks, VS Industry rose three sen to 32 sen, Notion VTech gained 4.5 sen to 75 sen and GB Bond added 1.5 sen to 24.5 sen.

title: 'Diplomasi Sukan Anwar Letakkan Malaysia Kembali Di Persada Global – Penganalisis
body: 'Pendekatan Perdana Menteri Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim yang memanfaatkan sukan sebagai platform diplomasi, aktiviti ekonomi dan penjenamaan negara membantu meletakkan semula Malaysia di pentas sukan global, menurut penganalisis. Felow Kanan Global Peace Institute Profesor Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam berkata sejak beberapa bulan lepas, Malaysia telah menunjukkan betapa acara sukan global dapat dimanfaatkan bukan sahaja untuk menghiburkan orang ramai, tetapi juga memperkukuh hubungan antarabangsa, menjana aktiviti ekonomi dan mewujudkan rasa keterujaan di seluruh negara. “Sukan sering dianggap sebagai hiburan, tetapi bagi kerajaan, bidang itu juga boleh menjadi diplomasi, dasar ekonomi dan penjenamaan negara yang digabungkan menjadi satu,” katanya dalam kenyataan, hari ini. Formula Satu (F1) kembali ke Litar Antarabangsa Sepang (SIC) selepas sembilan tahun dan usaha Malaysia untuk memastikan akses kepada siaran Piala Dunia FIFA 2026 baru-baru ini, menunjukkan bahawa sukan juga dapat dimanfaatkan untuk memperkukuh penglibatan antarabangsa negara. Mohd Mizan berkata penganjuran F1 Grand Prix (GP) Gulf Air Bahrain di negara ini selama tiga hari hingga hari ini, menunjukkan dimensi antarabangsa diplomasi sukan, selepas GP Bahrain tidak dapat diteruskan di lokasi asalnya berikutan keadaan geopolitik di Asia Barat. Beliau berkata pengaturan itu melangkaui transaksi komersial yang melibatkan litar lumba kerana perkara itu dimudahkan dalam rangka hubungan antara Malaysia dengan Bahrain, dengan sokongan Yang di-Pertuan Agong Sultan Ibrahim dan Raja Bahrain Raja Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Putera Mahkota merangkap Perdana Menteri Bahrain Putera Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa turut berangkat ke Malaysia dan bertemu dengan Anwar pada hujung minggu perlumbaan berkenaan. Mohd Mizan berkata kehadiran Anwar pada sesi kelayakan di Sepang, melawat ke pit Mercedes-AMG Petronas dan penglibatan dalam majlis resepsi yang dianjurkan Putera Salman menunjukkan bahawa acara sukan itu dapat mewujudkan platform untuk penglibatan diplomatik. “Sukan mewujudkan platform diplomatik. Pemimpin bertemu, hubungan dua hala diperkukuh dan Malaysia diletakkan di hadapan khalayak global bukan melalui sidang kemuncak rasmi, tetapi menerusi satu daripada pertunjukan sukan yang paling dikenali di dunia,” katanya. Maklum balas orang ramai terhadap kembalinya F1 juga, katanya, sama penting dengan kira-kira 95,000 tiket tiga hari terjual pada akhir September dan SIC menjangkakan penjualan mencecah kira-kira 100,000 yang bakal menjadi jualan tiket tertinggi yang direkodkan untuk perlumbaan yang diadakan di litar tersebut. Beliau berkata acara itu juga menjana limpahan ekonomi yang ketara, dengan Kementerian Pelancongan, Seni dan Budaya (MOTAC) menganggarkan acara sukan tersebut mampu menarik kira-kira 300,000 pelancong termasuk sekitar 50,000 pelancong antarabangsa, manakala Hong Leong Bank Research mengunjurkan impak ekonomi kira-kira RM1.3 bilion melalui pelancongan sukan dan perbelajaan pelawat asing. “F1 tidak hanya memberikan manfaat kepada litar. Pengunjung berbelanja di hotel, restoran, pengangkutan, peruncitan dan pelancongan. Liputan televisyen membawa imej Malaysia ke seluruh dunia. Pasukan, penaja, wartawan dan pemimpin korporat global tiba di negara ini,” katanya. Berhubung sukan bola sepak, Mohd Mizan berkata keputusan kerajaan untuk memastikan Malaysia mempunyai akses kepada Piala Dunia FIFA 2026 mewakili dimensi domestik diplomasi sukan, berikutan bola sepak terus menjadi satu daripada sukan yang paling diikuti ramai di negara ini. RTM dan Unifi TV dilantik selaku penyiar rasmi, dengan kesemua 104 perlawanan dapat ditonton menerusi platform yang mengambil bahagian, manakala kerajaan memperuntukkan RM26.2 juta untuk memperoleh hak penyiaran, di samping kerjasama strategik dengan sektor swasta yang membantu meluaskan akses dan pengedaran, katanya. Beliau berkata akses kepada Piala Dunia melalui saluran yang sah dan mudah diakses mewakili satu bentuk keterangkuman sosial kerana acara sukan utama dapat mewujudkan pengalaman bersama merentasi kaum, umur, geografi dan pendapatan. “Semasa perlawanan bola sepak utama, restoran mamak, ruang tamu di rumah, dewan komuniti dan kawasan tontonan awam menjadi ruang yang dikongsi bersama-sama rakyat Malaysia,” katanya. Mohd Mizan berkata pendekatan Anwar menunjukkan bahawa diplomasi hari ini berlangsung jauh melangkaui bilik persidangan rasmi, dengan Malaysia menggunakan F1 dan FIFA untuk mendekatkan dunia dengan rakyatnya sambil memperkukuh kedudukan di pentas sukan antarabangsa. “Kadangkala, diplomasi berlaku melalui rundingan dua hala. Ada kalanya diplomasi terjadi menerusi bola sepak dan kadang-kadang, pada kelajuan 300 kilometer sejam di sekitar Sepang,” katanya. — BERNAMA.

title: 'From F1 to the World Cup: How Anwar is using sport as diplomacy to put Malaysia on the world stage - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 4 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s approach of leveraging sports as a platform for diplomacy, economic activity and nation branding is helping position Malaysia back on the global sporting stage, according to an analyst. Global Peace Institute, London senior fellow Prof Dr Mohd Mizan Mohammad Aslam said Malaysia had, in recent months, demonstrated how global sporting events could be used not only to entertain the public but also to strengthen international relationships, generate economic activity and create a sense of shared national excitement. “Sport is often treated as entertainment, but for governments it can also be diplomacy, economic policy and nation branding rolled into one,” he said in a statement today. Formula 1’s return to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) after nine years and Malaysia’s efforts to ensure access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup broadcasts demonstrated how sports could be used to strengthen the country’s international engagement. Mohd Mizan said Malaysia’s hosting of the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix from Oct 2–4 demonstrated the international dimension of sports diplomacy, after the Bahrain Grand Prix could not proceed at its original venue due to geopolitical conditions in West Asia. He said the arrangement went beyond a commercial transaction involving a racetrack, as it was facilitated within the wider relationship between Malaysia and Bahrain, with the support of His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia, and Bahrain’s King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa. Bahrain’s Crown Prince and Prime Minister Prince Salman bin Hamad Al Khalifa also travelled to Malaysia and met Anwar during the race weekend. Mohd Mizan said Anwar’s attendance at the qualifying session at Sepang, visit to the Mercedes-AMG Petronas pit and participation in a reception hosted by Prince Salman further demonstrated how the sporting event created a platform for diplomatic engagement. “Sport had therefore created a diplomatic platform. Leaders met, bilateral relations were reinforced and Malaysia was placed before a global audience not through a formal summit but through one of the world’s most recognisable sporting spectacles,” he said. Mohd Mizan said the public response to F1’s return was equally significant, with around 95,000 three-day tickets sold by late September and SIC expecting sales to reach about 100,000, which would be the highest ticket sales recorded for races held at the circuit. He said the event also generated significant economic spillovers, with the Ministry of Tourism, Arts and Culture estimating that it could draw around 300,000 tourists, including about 50,000 international visitors, while Hong Leong Bank Research projected an economic impact of approximately RM1.3 billion through sports tourism and foreign visitor spending. “Formula 1 does not benefit only the circuit. Visitors spend on hotels, restaurants, transport, retail and tourism. Television coverage carries images of Malaysia around the world. International teams, sponsors, journalists and corporate leaders arrive in the country,” he said. Turning to football, Mohd Mizan said the government’s decision to ensure Malaysians had access to the 2026 Fifa World Cup represented the domestic dimension of sports diplomacy, with football remaining one of the country’s most widely followed sports. RTM and Unifi TV were appointed official broadcasters, with all 104 matches made available through the participating platforms, while the government allocated RM26.2 million to secure the broadcasting rights and strategic cooperation with the private sector helped widen access and distribution, he said. Mohd Mizan also said that access to the World Cup through legitimate and accessible channels represented a form of social inclusion, as major sporting events could create shared experiences cutting across race, age, geography and income. “Few things temporarily dissolve Malaysia’s normal social divisions as effectively as sport. During major football tournaments, mamak restaurants, living rooms, community halls and public viewing areas become shared national spaces,” he said. He said Anwar’s approach showed that diplomacy today operated far beyond formal conference rooms, with Malaysia using F1 and Fifa to bring the world closer to its people while strengthening its position on the global sporting stage. “Sometimes diplomacy happens through bilateral negotiations. Sometimes it happens through football and sometimes, at 300 kilometres per hour around Sepang,” he said. — Bernama

title: 'Hong Leong Bank Wins Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards In M'sia
body: 'Hong Leong Bank has been named Malaysia’s winner at the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026, taking the prize in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category. The bank was recognized for modernizing a critical online business application by moving away from a monolithic architecture to a containerized environment powered by Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. Hong Leong Bank’s Modernization Efforts Hong Leong Bank identified scalability limitations and manual processes within a legacy application architecture as key obstacles to its digital banking ambitions. To address this, the bank transitioned the application from a monolithic framework into a containerized environment using Red Hat OpenShift, while also deploying Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to modernize its existing database infrastructure. The deployment unified virtual machines and containers onto a single common platform, reducing the complexity of managing separate infrastructure stacks. Manual virtual machine patching for containerized workloads was also eliminated as part of the transition. The most measurable outcome from the shift is a dramatic reduction in software deployment cycles, which dropped from months to weeks – applications can now scale dynamically during traffic spikes, giving the bank the agility to deliver new digital banking features at a faster pace without compromising reliability. William Streitberg, Chief Information and Technology Officer at Hong Leong Bank, noted that updating infrastructure requires understanding the right fit for each operation, and that Red Hat has provided a common foundation for both existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing new capabilities to be introduced faster while maintaining the reliability customers expect. Daniel Aw, Vice President and General Manager for APAC at Red Hat, said that enterprise technology success is increasingly about how effectively solutions work together rather than how many new technologies an organisation adopts. He highlighted that this year’s award winners are building open, flexible foundations that allow them to innovate on their own terms. Red Hat positions open source as a response to growing complexity in AI, hybrid cloud, and automation strategies, where organisations need the flexibility to choose technologies best suited to their specific business requirements. Pokdepinion: Cutting deployment cycles from months to weeks is going to net them plenty of benefits down the line.

title: 'AKPK Celebrates 20 Years with Strategic Partnership Program
body: 'Accra:The Credit Counselling and Debt Management Agency (AKPK) marked its 20th anniversary by hosting the 'Rencah Kita Pelbagai Rasa, Satu Makna' programme, aimed at strengthening relationships with strategic partners. According to BERNAMA News Agency, AKPK's chief executive officer, Azman Hasim, highlighted that the cooking challenge, organized in collaboration with M Resort and Hotel, included 30 agencies such as financial service providers, media partners, and other strategic partners. The event symbolized the blending of diverse strengths and expertise to enhance financial resilience among Malaysians. Azman emphasized that the agency's anniversary reflects the collective success of various parties working towards a unified goal. He likened the impact of their work to a well-prepared dish, underscoring the importance of understanding each component's role in achieving meaningful outcomes. He also noted that each AKPK undertaking involves real people with lives that need support and rebuilding. The event underscored the importance of strategic partnerships in providing the necessary guidance and confidence to help individuals overcome financial challenges. The primary focus of the day was the relationships and communication fostered through the challenge, rather than the competition itself. Azman reiterated that while participants have different perspectives, they share a common goal of improving the wellbeing of Malaysians. The annual event, which introduces new activities each year, serves as a platform to honor the strategic partners that have contributed to AKPK's success over the past two decades. Notable participants included Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank), CIMB Bank Berhad (CIMB), Public Bank Bhd, Hong Leong Bank Bhd, and AmBank (M) Bhd.

title: 'Aktiviti buru saham pacu Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi, sentimen positif
body: 'Bursa Malaysia meningkat selepas mengalami pemulihan kecil pada akhir dagangan Jumaat, dipacu oleh aktiviti memburu saham-saham berharga rendah susulan jualan ketara baru-baru ini, kata penganalisis.  Lantunan itu bagaimanapun kekurangan momentum ketika pasaran Asia kekal diasak tekanan menjelang pengumuman data pasaran tenaga kerja Amerika Syarikat (AS).  Pada 5 petang, indeks penunjuk utama FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menokok 0.51 mata atau 0.03 peratus kepada 1,630.87 daripada paras penutup 1,630.36, semalam.  Indeks penanda aras itu yang dibuka menokok 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87, bergerak dalam jajaran 1,630.63 hingga 1,640.78 sepanjang sesi dagangan.  Sentimen pasaran positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi rugi iaitu 585 berbanding 541 manakala 558 lain tidak berubah, 1,089 tidak diniagakan dan 24 lain digantung dagangannya.  Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion daripada 3.1 bilion unit bernilai RM2.7 bilion, semalam.  Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata aktiviti penjualan pada baru-baru ini menyaksikan penilaian saham mewah yang lebih menarik, sekali gus berpotensi menggalakkan usaha pengumpulan saham secara berperingkat.  Namun pada masa sama, katanya, pelabur terus mengambil langkah untuk kekal bertahan berikutan perkembangan seperti hasil bon dan harga minyak mentah yang kekal tinggi.  “Bagi bursa tempatan pula, kami berpendirian berhati-hati di disebalik peningkatan berikutan risiko cabaran luar yang mungkin mengekalkan ketidaktentuan pasaran pada tahap tinggi,” katanya kepada Bernama.  Saham wajaran tinggi menyaksikan Maybank naik tujuh sen kepada RM10.02, Public Bank susut satu sen kepada RM4.66, CIMB berkurangan empat sen kepada RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional meningkat enam sen kepada RM12.96 dan IHH Healthcare meraih 10 sen kepada RM7.80.  Saham paling aktif menyaksikan Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources tidak berubah pada 18 sen, JCY International menokok 10.5 sen kepada 66 sen, V.S Industry naik dua sen kepada 29 sen dan PUC menambah satu sen kepada 4.5 sen.  Bagi saham paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries melonjak RM1.28 kepada RM42.40, UWC naik 47 sen kepada RM7.57, Vitrox menokok 46 sen kepada RM10.46, United Plantations meraih 42 sen kepada RM31.38 manakala UMS Integration meningkat 38 sen kepada RM9.03.  Saham yang mencatatkan penurunan ketara diterajui oleh Nestle yang susut 48 sen kepada RM89.52, Kuala Lumpur Kepong turun 42 sen kepada RM21, Enra berkurangan 25.5 sen kepada 72.5 sen manakala Allianz Malaysia dan Hong Leong Bank masing-masing menguncup 20 sen kepada RM20.80 dan RM22.64.  Di papan indeks pula, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 122.94 mata kepada 17,481.93, Indeks FBM Emas menokok 27.04 mata kepada 12,170.57 manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 24.52 mata kepada 11,957.68.  Indeks FBM Emas Syariah meningkat 47.31 mata kepada 12,060.32 manakala Indeks FBM ACE menokok 46.49 mata kepada 5,529.46.  Prestasi sektor menyaksikan Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik 0.79 mata kepada 178.52, Indeks Tenaga susut 1.98 mata kepada 833.03, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menguncup 20.40 mata kepada 19,040.51 manakala Indeks Perladangan meningkat 29.97 mata kepada 9,056.55.  Jumlah dagangan di Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion daripada 1.82 bilion unit bernilai RM2.42 bilion, semalam. title: 'Aktiviti buru saham pacu Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi, sentimen positif
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia meningkat selepas mengalami pemulihan kecil pada akhir dagangan Jumaat, dipacu oleh aktiviti memburu saham-saham berharga rendah susulan jualan ketara baru-baru ini, kata penganalisis. Lantunan itu bagaimanapun kekurangan momentum ketika pasaran Asia kekal diasak tekanan menjelang pengumuman data pasaran tenaga kerja Amerika Syarikat (AS). Pada 5 petang, indeks penunjuk utama FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) menokok 0.51 mata atau 0.03 peratus kepada 1,630.87 daripada paras penutup 1,630.36, semalam. Indeks penanda aras itu yang dibuka menokok 3.51 mata kepada 1,633.87, bergerak dalam jajaran 1,630.63 hingga 1,640.78 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Sentimen pasaran positif dengan kaunter untung mengatasi rugi iaitu 585 berbanding 541 manakala 558 lain tidak berubah, 1,089 tidak diniagakan dan 24 lain digantung dagangannya. Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion daripada 3.1 bilion unit bernilai RM2.7 bilion, semalam. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata aktiviti penjualan pada baru-baru ini menyaksikan penilaian saham mewah yang lebih menarik, sekali gus berpotensi menggalakkan usaha pengumpulan saham secara berperingkat. title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends slightly higher as technology counters dominate trading
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — Bursa Malaysia staged a slight recovery on Friday as bargain-hunting emerged following a recent sharp sell-off, said an analyst. However, the rebound lacked momentum as broader Asian markets remained under pressure ahead of key United States labour market data. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.51 points, or 0.03 per cent, to 1,630.87 from Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The benchmark index, which opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87, moved between 1,630.63 and 1,640.78 throughout the trading session. Market breadth turned positive with gainers leading losers 585 to 541, while 558 counters were unchanged, 1,089 untraded and 24 suspended. Turnover climbed to 4.23 billion units, worth RM2.70 billion, from 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion on Thursday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the recent sell-off had brought valuations of selected blue-chip stocks to more attractive levels, which could encourage gradual accumulation and provide some downside support. However, he said investors continued to adopt a defensive stance as bond yields and crude oil prices remained elevated. “As for the local bourse, we remain cautious despite today’s rebound, as external headwinds are likely to keep market volatility elevated,” Thong told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank rose seven sen to RM10.02, Public Bank fell one sen to RM4.66, CIMB eased four sen to RM7.65, Tenaga Nasional firmed up six sen to RM12.96, and IHH Healthcare added 10 sen to RM7.80. In active trade, Zetrix AI erased five sen to 11.5 sen, Jaks Resources remained unchanged at 18 sen, JCY International jumped 10.5 sen to 66 sen, V.S Industry ticked up two sen to 29 sen, and PUC went up one sen to 4.5 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries rose RM1.28 to RM42.40, UWC rallied 47 sen to RM7.57, Vitrox bounced 46 sen to RM10.46, United Plantations gained 42 sen to RM31.38, and UMS Integration improved 38 sen to RM9.03. Top losers were led by Nestle, which reduced 48 sen to RM89.52; Kuala Lumpur Kepong fell 42 sen to RM21; Enra trimmed 25.5 sen to 72.5 sen, while Allianz Malaysia and Hong Leong Bank both shaved off 20 sen to RM20.80 and RM22.64, respectively. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index rose 122.94 points to 17,481.93, the FBM Emas Index added 27.04 points to 12,170.57, and the FBM Top 100 Index advanced 24.52 points to 11,957.68. The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 47.31 points to 12,060.32, and the FBM ACE Index improved 46.49 points to 5,529.46. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.79 points to 178.52, while the Energy Index shaved off 1.98 points to 833.03. The Financial Services Index eased 20.40 points to 19,040.51, and the Plantation Index grew 29.97 points to 9,056.55. The Main Market volume increased to 2.67 billion units worth RM2.34 billion from 1.82 billion units valued at RM2.42 billion on Thursday. Warrant turnover soared to 973.40 million units worth RM160.21 million from 618.78 million units valued at RM72.71 million previously. The ACE Market volume eased to 593.05 million units valued at RM205.21 million from 650.13 million units worth RM226.92 million yesterday. title: 'HLB Meezani Account-i Offers Cash, Gold, And Cars In New Prize Draws
body: 'HLB Meezani Account-i holders stand a chance to win cash, gold bars, holiday packages, a Proton e.MAS 5, and a Porsche Cayenne in HLB Islamic’s second year of prize draws, which runs from 30 July 2026 to 29 July 2027. There are daily, weekly, monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws, with minimum balances ranging from RM100 to RM60,000 depending on the prize. HLB Islamic announced this year’s prizes at a rewards ceremony in Kuala Lumpur on 29 September 2026, held to mark the account’s first year. The bank said 43% of those who opened the account in its first year were new HLB Islamic customers. The Minimum Balance For Each Prize Each prize has its own minimum balance, and you get one entry for every full multiple of that amount. For example, keeping RM1,000 in the account when the day ends gives 10 entries in the daily draw, since the minimum balance is RM100. For the weekly draw, you get one entry for every RM200. Keeping RM2,500 at the end of the week gives 12 entries, and the extra RM100 doesn’t count. For quarterly and yearly prizes, entries are counted from each month-end balance and added up until the draw. Keeping RM2,000 in the account at the end of each month for a three-month quarter, for example, gives three entries for the 10g gold bar draw. Since the monthly, quarterly, and yearly draws all use your month-end balance, withdrawing money on the last day of the month can reduce your entries for that month, even if you put the money back a few days later. Some Payments And Deposits Can Earn Extra Entries The monthly and quarterly prizes also offer extra entries if you’ve already met the minimum balance for the relevant prize. You can earn additional entries by making at least 10 eligible QR or online payments from the account in a month, or by depositing at least RM2,000 in a single transaction. Doing both in the same month earns one more combo entry. Making 10 payments earns extra entries for the RM500 cash and Touch ‘n Go prizes. A deposit of RM2,000 or more earns extra entries for every prize in the table except the Proton e.MAS 5, which only gets the combo entry when you do both in the same month. The daily, weekly, and yearly draws don’t offer extra entries. Win Limits And Claiming Your Prize You can win the daily prize once a week at most, and the weekly prize once every two weeks. If your name is selected for more than one monthly prize in the same month, you’ll only receive the highest-value prize. The same applies to the quarterly and yearly draws. To qualify for the draws, you need to actively use HLB Connect from the start of each draw period until any prize is handed over. Winners are selected within 30 working days after each draw period ends and notified through the HLB Connect app within 14 working days after that. You have 30 working days from the announcement to claim your prize, after which the bank may award it to another winner. Cash prizes are credited directly into the winner’s HLB Meezani Account-i. Winners are responsible for any taxes or fees related to their prizes, and HLB Islamic may publish winners’ names with part of their IC numbers concealed. Non-cash prizes are handed over within 90 working days. Winners will need their winning letter and IC to collect them. Prizes can’t be exchanged for cash or transferred to someone else. Opening An HLB Meezani Account-i The account is Shariah-compliant and open to individuals who live in Malaysia. You need RM100 to open it and RM50 to keep it open. The account currently has an indicative profit rate of 0.05% p.a., calculated daily and paid monthly, as of 30 September 2026. You can deposit or withdraw money through HLB Islamic branches, ATMs, cash deposit machines, and online channels. Because it’s an investment account rather than a savings account or fixed deposit, HLB Islamic states that the money and returns aren’t guaranteed and the account isn’t protected by Perbadanan Insurans Deposit Malaysia (PIDM). The prize draws come on top of the account’s profit rate, so look at both when deciding where to keep your money. You can also compare the latest savings account and fixed deposit rates on RinggitPlus. You can open the account at an HLB Islamic branch or book an appointment through the HLB Islamic website. The full rules are set out in the campaign’s terms and conditions [PDF]. Follow us on our official WhatsApp channel for the latest money tips and updates.

Sentiment remained fragile amid persistent external uncertainties and a lack of domestic catalysts, with investors keeping a close watch on global bond yields, oil prices and overseas market developments for direction. Construction, Utilities and Plantation led sectoral losses, with all dropping 1.9%. This is dragged by Kuala Lumpur Kepong (-3.5%), Hong Leong Bank (-1.3%) and Press Metal Aluminium (-3.9%). Market breadth remained weak, with 749 losers against 342 gainers, while 496 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Thursday, led by strong gains in technology and semiconductor stocks following Micron Technology’s upbeat outlook, while softer-than-expected US inflation data eased expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike. Japan’s Nikkei 225 surged 3.3% to 68,957, Taiwan’s TAIEX gained 0.9% to a record 48,354, and South Korea’s KOSPI rose 2.0% to 6,971. Hong Kong and China markets were closed for the National Day holiday. European stocks opened the fourth quarter sharply lower on Thursday, weighed by rising global government bond yields and concerns that major central banks could keep interest rates higher for longer. The STOXX 50 fell 1.5% and the STOXX 600 dropped 1.3% to their lowest levels in around three and a half months, with financials leading the declines as banks fell more than 3.5%, while automobiles and parts and basic resources dropped between 1.5% and 2%. US stocks closed mostly higher on Thursday, recovering from earlier losses as the selloff in Treasuries eased. The S&P 500 gained 0.2% while the Nasdaq CI and the Dow ended broadly flat. The 10-year Treasury yield retreated from its highest level since 2002 as the unwinding of crowded positions helped ease pressure on equities. Treasuries also found support after Fed Vice Chair Philip Jefferson said more time may be needed to assess whether further rate hikes are warranted, lending some support to credit-sensitive stocks. Chipmakers also advanced, with Nvidia gaining 1.1%, AMD 0.6% and Micron 3.0% after the company issued an upbeat current-quarter outlook following strong fiscal fourth-quarter results. US: Manufacturing Activity Remains Robust, Prices Soar The ISM Manufacturing PMI edged down to 54.5 in September 2026 from 54.6 in August, compared to forecasts of 55. Still, the reading continued to point to robust growth in the manufacturing sector, with new orders (55.3 vs 53.7) and employment (52.7 vs 51.2) rising at a faster pace while production slowed slightly (56.7 vs 58.3. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Gains on Middle East Risks Crude oil traded around $93 per barrel on Friday after gaining for two consecutive sessions, as the US weighed sending another aircraft carrier to the Middle East, raising the prospect of an escalation in the war with Iran and further disruptions to regional energy supplies. The Pentagon is also considering the deployment of 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, giving President Donald Trump additional options if he decides to intensify attacks on Iran. (Trading Economics) US: Treasury Sell-Off Eases 5.3% on Thursday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note topped 5.3% on Thursday, its highest level since early 2002, before retreating slightly to 5.27%. The bond market has remained under pressure amid expectations of further monetary policy tightening by the Fed, as persistent inflationary pressures from higher oil prices and the lack of a resolution to the Middle East conflict continue to weigh on sentiment. Concerns over the US fiscal and debt outlook, along with resilient economic data, have added to the pressure. (Trading Economics) US: Benchmark yield hits highest since 2002 as bonds sell off The US benchmark yield climbed to the highest since 2002 as rising oil prices drove a renewed sell-off in global bonds. The yield on the 10- year Treasury note rose as much as six basis points to 5.34% on Thursday, rising past the 2007 peak. Earlier this week, the rate on 30-year US bonds also hit a 24-year high. (Bloomberg) US: House Price Growth Slows More Than Expected US private payrolls growth accelerated in September, the ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday. Private employment rose by 90,000 jobs this month after a downwardly revised 36,000 in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast private employment increased by 70,000 after a previously reported 38,000 advance in August. (Nationwide Building Society, United Kingdom) US: Gold Rises on Soft US PCE Inflation Data Gold climbed toward $4,200 an ounce on Thursday, recovering losses from the previous session as softer-than-expected US PCE inflation data reduced expectations for a Federal Reserve interest rate hike this month. The US PCE price index rose 0.3% in August, below the 0.4% forecast, while core PCE increased 0.2%, also coming in below expectations for a 0.3% gain. Markets now see roughly a 38% chance of a Federal Reserve rate hike in October, down from 51% before the PCE release. (Trading Economics) JP: 10-Year Yield Rises on Hawkish BOJ Outlook Japan’s 10-year government bond yield climbed above 3.1% on Thursday, returning to 30-year highs as strong economic data and hawkish signals from the Bank of Japan reinforced expectations for a faster pace of policy tightening. Central bank data showed manufacturing sentiment improved in the third quarter to its highest level in more than eight years, while overall business conditions reached their most favorable levels in decades. (Trading Economics) TW: Plans US$13 bil in extra energy spending given high global prices Taiwan's government said on Thursday that it plans to spend around T$415 billion (US$13.0 billion) this year to help its main power producer Taipower and oil refiner CPC absorb costs from sharply rising global energy prices due to the Middle East war. Taiwan has not passed on most of the rising costs to consumers, unlike in other parts of the world, and it heavily subsidises energy bills, helping to keep inflation down. (Bloomberg) MY: MEF welcomes minimum wage reprieve for MSMEs, backs sustainable wage growth The Malaysian Employers Federation (MEF) has welcomed the government's decision to grant micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) a reprieve from further increases in the current RM1,700 minimum wage, for the time being. title: 'Analysts Stay Neutral On Banks As Funding Costs, Asset Quality Risks Build
body: 'RHB Research has maintained its Neutral stance on Malaysia’s banking sector, citing pressure on net interest margins, rising bond yields, a gradual increase in gross impaired loans and thinner provisioning buffers despite resilient loan growth.  The research house said system loans expanded 5.7% year-on-year and 0.4% month-on-month in August 2026, bringing annualised year-to-date growth to 5.6%, slightly ahead of its full-year forecast of between 5% and 5.5%.  Non-household lending led the increase, rising 6.8% year-on-year, supported by transport and communications loans, which jumped 21%, utilities at 20%, and education and health at 14%.  Household loans grew 5.0% year-on-year, driven mainly by residential mortgages and auto financing, both of which expanded 5%.  RHB said lending indicators remained healthy, with loan applications up 13.8% year-on-year, approvals rising 19.3% and disbursements increasing 10.2% in August.  For the first eight months of the year, loan applications, approvals and disbursements rose 8.5%, 14.0% and 6.5% respectively, pointing to a healthy pipeline for near-term drawdowns.  System deposits increased 5.2% year-on-year in August, with current and savings account deposits rising 8%, ahead of 4% growth in fixed and other deposits.  The system CASA ratio improved to 32.5%, from 31.4% a year earlier.  However, the loan-to-deposit ratio rose to 89.8%, from 88.8% in July and 89.4% a year ago, while the liquidity coverage ratio eased to 145.9%.  RHB said margin pressure could intensify as lending growth continues to outpace deposit growth, while higher capital-market rates are expected to push up wholesale deposit costs and eventually spill over into retail funding rates.  The research house also flagged the potential impact of higher bond yields on trading income and mark-to-market valuations.  Total gross impaired loans rose 6.1% year-on-year and 1.2% month-on-month, lifting the system GIL ratio slightly to 1.44%, from 1.43% previously.  The increase was driven by wholesale and retail trade, households, transport and communications, and primary agriculture.  Within the household segment, the GIL ratio increased to 1.11%, with auto and personal financing showing notable deterioration.  At the same time, system loan-loss coverage remained broadly stable month-on-month at 81.4%, but was lower than 89.9% a year earlier.  RHB said capital positions remained comfortable, with the CET-1 ratio at 14.1% and the total capital ratio at 17.8%.  The research house maintained AMMB Holdings, Malayan Banking and Hong Leong Bank as its preferred banking names, while retaining a cautious sector view in the absence of strong near-term catalysts.

body: 'The FBM KLCI rallied 1.0% to 1,683.5 points on Tuesday, as strong buying in banking, semiconductor and technology stocks lifted the broader market in tandem with gains across regional markets. Technology (+2.3%), Utilities (+1.7%) and Financial Services (+1.3%) led sectoral gains, led by Hong Leong Bank (+0.5%), IHH Healthcare (+0.4%) and CIMB Group (+0.3%). Market breadth, however, was positive, with gainers outnumbering losers 678 to 458, and 572 counters unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Tuesday, supported by renewed optimism over the AI trade, easing oil prices and expectations of progress at the upcoming US-China summit. South Korea's KOSPI rose 0.2% to 7,017.9, followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+0.2%) at 25,087.8, Taiwan's TAIEX (+0.2%) at 47,800.2 and China's Shanghai Composite (+0.1%) at 3,952.1, while Japan's Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday. In South Korea, semiconductor stocks led the regional gains as investors returned to AIlinked trades following the rally in US chipmakers and technology stocks, with strong September semiconductor exports further supporting expectations for sustained chip demand. In China, sentiment was supported by technology and AI-related stocks, while investors remained focused on the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting and the potential extension of the US-China trade truce. European stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday, extending the previous session’s gains, supported by strength in technology and consumer staples. The Euro STOXX 50 rose 0.2% to 6,332, while the STOXX Europe 600 gained 0.3% to 643.6. AI-related stocks advanced alongside their US counterparts following positive sentiment around Meta’s Muse AI, boosting AI infrastructure and technology shares. Meanwhile, banks and insurers pared earlier gains as Eurozone sovereign yields and natural gas prices rose amid heightened tensions in the Middle East. US stocks closed mixed on Tuesday, with the Nasdaq reaching a record high on renewed optimism over AI and semiconductor stocks. The Nasdaq CI gained 0.5%, while the S&P 500 was essentially flat and the Dow Jones fell 0.4%. Technology stocks led gains, with Micron Technology rising 5.0% and Sandisk nearly 7.0%, supported by optimism over AI demand. Meanwhile, financial stocks weakened, with JPMorgan Chase and Wells Fargo falling more than 3%, as investors remained cautious over inflation and further rate hikes. Investors also monitored Middle East developments and the upcoming Trump-Xi meeting. US: Oil Falls for 6th Session Crude oil slipped below $90 per barrel on Wednesday, extending its decline to a sixth consecutive session as signs of progress emerged in renewed US-Iran talks and efforts continued to restore operations at a key pipeline in Saudi Arabia. President Donald Trump said officials held a “very productive” meeting with Iranian envoys, adding that he is weighing whether to pursue a negotiated agreement or “annihilate the Islamic Republic.” (Trading Economics) US: Fifth District Manufacturing Unexpectedly Declines Fifth District manufacturing activity edged down in September, according to the most recent survey from the Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond. The composite manufacturing index dropped to −2 from 4 in August. Two of its three component indexes decreased in September: shipments to −5 from 11 and new orders to −6 from 3. Meanwhile, the employment index increased to 7 from −2. (Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond) US: Treasury Yields Edge Up to 4.97% on Tuesday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury wavered before settling slightly higher at 4.97% on Tuesday, as traders continued to assess developments in the Middle East, oil prices and comments from Fed officials. In his speech to the UN General Assembly, US President Trump defended his decision to join Israel in launching military action against Iran but added that he believes the US would reach a deal with Iran right after the midterm elections in November. (Trading Economics) US: Borrowing overshoots in fresh budget setback for Healey Britain borrowed more than forecast in the first five months of the fiscal year, piling fresh pressure on Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey ahead of his debut budget next month. The fiscal deficit climbed to £77.3 billion — £8.1 billion more than the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) predicted in March. In August alone, borrowing came in higher than forecast at £18.3 billion. The OBR had predicted a deficit of £14.8 billion. (Bloomberg) EU: ECB's Lane sees inflation returning to target from mid-2027 - paper An energy shock pushing up oil and gas prices is likely to last longer than the European Central Bank (ECB) had anticipated in March, with geopolitical risks now looking elevated again, ECB chief economist Philip Lane was quoted as saying on Tuesday. "As a result, we believe this second wave of energy price increases should lead to higher and more persistent inflation, before it recedes towards our target starting in mid-2027," Lane told Swiss newspaper Le Temps. (Reuters) CN: And US discuss AI, investment on second day of trade talks Chinese and US officials wrapped up their second day of talks in New York on Monday to discuss artificial intelligence, investment and trade as they sought to advance negotiations ahead of President Xi Jinping’s visit to the US this week. Talks on Monday focused on delivering on what’s been agreed by the US and Chinese lead negotiators, China’s Vice Finance Minister Liao Min said in brief remarks outside the JPMorgan Chase & Co’s headquarters in New York, where the meetings took place. (Bloomberg) SK: Consumer Sentiment Recovers in September South Korea’s Composite Consumer Sentiment Index (CCSI) rose 2.1 points to 106.6 in September 2026 from August. Consumer sentiment regarding current living standards was unchanged at 92, while sentiment about the future outlook rose one point to 98. Sentiment regarding future household income increased two points to 102, while that concerning future household spending rose one point to 110. Consumer sentiment about current domestic economic conditions climbed four points to 83, while sentiment regarding future domestic economic conditions rose one point to 90. (The Bank of Korea) MY: To continue spending on development next year despite oil price pressures - Akmal Nasrullah Malaysia will keep spending on development in 2027 even as higher oil prices add pressure to the government’s subsidy bill. While the government is committed to development, the Ministry of Finance will manage the fiscal impact, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said.told reporters after the ministry’s monthly assembly on Tuesday. (The Edge) MY: To grow 4.7% in 2026 as Southeast Asian outlook brightens - World Economic Forum Malaysia’s economy is projected to grow 4.7% in 2026, supported by technology-related exports and investment as well as robust domestic demand, according to the World Economic Forum (WEF). In its latest Chief Economists’ Outlook — September 2026, the WEF said the growth outlook for Southeast Asia remains broadly resilient, with 97% of chief economists surveyed expecting growth in the region to moderate or strengthen over the next 12 months. (The Edge) MY: Regulations on cross-border e-commerce platforms being finalised, says Teo The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) is still in discussions with the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the Finance Ministry and the Customs Department on the regulatory framework for cross-border e-commerce platforms. Deputy Communications Minister Teo Nie Ching said the rules governing e-commerce platforms were being finalised, and MCMC, which is under her ministry, is the body that licensed such platforms. Speaking to reporters at the launch of the Asean-China Cross Border E-Commerce Expo 2026 (CBE 2026), she said MCMC was ready to proceed once it received directions from the two ministries. (The Edge) OIB: Applies to withdraw draft circular, listing application for RM280m related party deal to make 'essential updates' Property developer Oriental Interest Bhd has applied to withdraw its draft circular and listing application filed more than a month ago for its proposed RM280 million share‑based related party acquisition that would have marked its entry into the motorcycle financing and retail business. In a Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday, the company said it had submitted a letter to the regulator to withdraw the documents filed on Aug 18 to facilitate essential updates to the documents. (The Edge) MAYBULK: To expand into industrial property business with Klang land buy Transportation and logistics group Maybulk Bhd has proposed to buy a freehold industrial property in Bandar Bukit Raja, Klang for RM35.5 million cash. The property comprises 8,346 sq m of land together with a single-storey industrial building, an annexed office and a warehouse block, the group said in an exchange filing on Tuesday. (The Edge) MMAG: Proposes RM130 mil capital reduction to pare accumulated losses Loss-making MMAG Holdings Bhd, a company which counts NexG Bhd as a substantial shareholder, has proposed a RM130 million share capital reduction to wipe out part of the company’s accumulated losses. NexG is the company’s second largest shareholder with a 9.925% stake, while Future Star Sdn Bhd is its largest shareholder with a 19.904% interest. (The Edge) L&G: Targets RM1.5b GDV for first phase of Lembah Beringin industrial park Land & General Bhd plans to launch the first phase of its Lembah Beringin industrial park in Selangor in the first quarter of next year, with an estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM1.5 billion. The first phase of the project, which marks the property developer's expansion into the industrial segment, covers 240 acres of the group's 2,500-acre land bank in Lembah Beringin. (The Edge) GBBOND: Reports 8.22 times IPO oversubscription ahead of ACE Market debut GB Bond Holdings Bhd announced that its initial public offering (IPO) has been oversubscribed by 8.22 times, ahead of its planned listing on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market on Oct 1. In a bursa filing on Tuesday, the industrial adhesive maker said it received 5,333 applications from the Malaysian public for 190.02 million new shares, against 20.62 million shares offered. (The Edge) CUSCAPI: Seeks RM4.55m via private placement, second TS Wong-linked firm to tap equity market this week Cuscapi Bhd has proposed a private placement of up to 94.49 million new shares to raise up to RM4.55 million for working capital, making it the second company linked to businessman Wong Thean Soon, better known as TS Wong, to announce a share placement this week. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Tuesday, Cuscapi said about RM2.28 million of the proceeds will be used for operating expenses, including salaries, while another RM1.37 million will go towards payments to trade creditors such as hardware suppliers. (The Edge) SUNMED: Singapore's sovereign wealth fund cashes out over RM1 bil in Sunway Healthcare shares - report Singapore’s sovereign wealth fund sold shares in Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd worth over RM1 billion on Tuesday, according to a news report. The sale of 575 million shares was priced at RM2.08 a piece, Bloomberg reported, citing a term sheet. The price tag is a discount of 9% from the hospital operator’s closing price of RM2.29 on Monday, and near the lower end of the RM2.07-RM2.10 range marketed to investors. (The Edge) TNB: Court orders Tenaga to pay Projek Lebuhraya Usahasama RM10.5 mil for Penang bridge fire The High Court here has ordered Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) to pay RM10.52 million in special damages to Penang Bridge concessionaire Projek Lebuhraya Usahasama Bhd (PLUS) over a major fire incident in a cable tunnel beneath the bridge in February 2021. In a judgement delivered on Sept 16, 2026, High Court judge Ahmad Shahrir Mohd Salleh ruled that TNB was liable in both common law negligence and breach of statutory duty under Section 33A of the Electricity Supply Act 1990 (ESA 1990), for failing to detect and repair pre-existing mechanical damage on its 132kV high-voltage cables. (The Edge) SDG: Eco World-SD Guthrie JV sells 222 acres in Negeri Sembilan for over RM1b The developer of Eco Business Park 7 in Negeri Sembilan is selling two plots of industrial land for RM1 billion to a data centre operator. The parcels measuring 222 acres combined are being sold to Tera Data Centers, according to a statement from Eco Business Park 7 Sdn Bhd, a joint venture of Eco World Development Group Bhd, SD Guthrie Bhd and state agency NS Corporation. There are no details about the project planned on the land. (The Edge) VITROX: Hits record high as AI-driven growth boosts outlook Shares in ViTrox Corporation Bhd hit their highest level since the company’s listing on the ACE Market in 2005 on Tuesday, driven by its strong growth prospects amid the AI infrastructure boom. ViTrox designs & manufactures vision inspection system & handler for back-end semiconductor industry. In a The Edge Malaysia weekly’s Sept 21-Sept 27 issue, its co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng said the company’s numbers will double this year, with strong growth momentum expected to continue over the next few years. (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Reverses intraday gains to finish lower after touching new high; gains RM1.4b in market cap since August Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd surged to a fresh high on Tuesday, rising as much as 27 sen or 6.2% to RM4.61 during intraday trade. However, the counter then surrendered its gains as profit-taking set in, closing four sen or 0.9% lower at RM4.30. At the closing price, the refiner's market capitalisation stood at RM2.58 billion — up RM1.4 billion since August. (The Edge) YES: Inks underwriting agreement with Malacca Securities for ACE Market IPO Yes Group Management Bhd has inked an underwriting agreement with Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd for its initial public offering (IPO), in conjunction with the company’s upcoming listing on the ACE Market of Bursa Malaysia. The company operates the “Yes Travel” brand and is a meetings, incentives, conferences, and exhibitions (MICE) specialist, principally providing customised incentive travel solutions, as well as event planning and management solutions. The IPO comprises a public issue of 91.87 million new shares and an offer for sale of 45.93 million existing shares, representing a total IPO offering of 137.80 million shares. (The Edge) ZETRIX: TS Wong further trims Zetrix AI stake; investment vehicle exits substantial shareholder list Zetrix AI Bhd managing director Wong Thean Soon's stake in the company has now dropped to 11.06% from 11.97% last Friday, as Wong continued to pare his direct and indirect stakes in the company. His indirect stake is held via Asia Internet Holdings Sdn Bhd, which has now ceased to be a substantial shareholder of Zetrix AI following the disposal of 57 million shares on Friday — the same day it gained 6.24 million shares from Zetrix AI's dividend reinvestment plan (DRP). (The Edge) OGX: Ventures into renewable energy, targets data centre market OGX Group Bhd has ventured into the renewable energy (RE) industry, targeting opportunities in Malaysia’s growing data centre market through battery energy storage systems (BESS). In a statement Tuesday, the information technology infrastructure solutions provider said its wholly owned subsidiary OGX Green Tech Sdn Bhd will spearhead the new business. (The Edge) CHHB: Forced auction of Country Heights land cancelled due to lack of bidders A forced auction of Country Heights Holdings Bhd’s land in Kajang, Selangor was cancelled due to absence of bidders. Solicitors confirmed that the property, a piece of commercial land measuring about six acres, was not sold following the cancellation of the judicial auction via eLelong, the company said in an exchange filing on Tuesday.
