title: 'Daily Newswatch - 22 Sep 2026
body: 'The FBM KLCI edged up 0.1% to 1,666.9 points on Monday, snapping a threesession losing streak, as bargain hunting in selected blue-chip counters lifted the index amid easing concerns over the West Asia conflict and retreating oil prices. Energy (+3.0%), Utilities (+1.9%) and Transportation & Logistics (+0.5%) led sectoral gains, led by Hong Leong Bank (+0.4%), YTL Power (+0.3%) and Petronas Dagangan (+0.2%). Market breadth, however, was positive, with gainers outnumbering losers 654 to 552, and 517 counters unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Monday, supported by renewed strength in technology and semiconductor stocks, easing oil prices and improved sentiment ahead of the upcoming US-China summit. South Korea's KOSPI led regional gains, rising 1.7%, followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+1.2%), Taiwan's TAIEX (+1.1%) and China's Shanghai Composite (+1.0%), while Japan's Nikkei 225 was closed for a public holiday. In South Korea, chipmakers led the gains, with Samsung Electronics rising 5.0% after US semiconductor stocks rallied, while semiconductor exports surged 259% YoY to USD34.1 bn in the first 20 days of September, reinforcing expectations of strong chip demand and earnings. In China, sentiment was supported by gains in technology and healthcare stocks, while the PBOC maintained its key lending rates and investors awaited the Trump-Xi meeting. European stocks closed firmly higher on Monday, supported by lower sovereign yields and easing ongoing pressures from an adverse macroeconomic backdrop. The Euro STOXX 50 gained 1.3% to 6,318 and the STOXX Europe 600 rose 1.0% to 642. Natural gas and fuel prices pulled back following the weekend amid signs that GCC nations are chasing diplomatic ways with Iran to restart tanker flows through the Persian Gulf. The drop in yields aided the outlook of credit and supported banks, with UniCredit, Nordea, and BBVA adding between 3.2% and 2%. Lastly, a global rally for the AI infrastructure sector supported Infineon with a 4.3% jump, while ASML added 2.5%. US stocks rallied on Monday, supported by falling oil prices and lower Treasury yields, while optimism over the upcoming Trump-Xi summit further lifted sentiment. The Nasdaq CI surged 2.26%, while the S&P 500 and Dow gained 1.49% and 0.71%, respectively. Meta jumped 11.3% on optimism over its AI offering, Muse, while AMD and Intel surged 10% and 12.1%, respectively. Investors now await earnings from AutoZone and KB Home, along with speeches from Federal Reserve officials. US: Treasury Yields Edge Down 4.95% on Monday The yield on the US 10-year Treasury note fell 4bps to 4.95% on Monday, as traders started the new week with another decline in oil prices, amid hopes that diplomatic efforts could lead to a resolution to the conflict with Iran. Oil prices have now fallen for four consecutive sessions, easing some concerns over renewed inflationary pressures (Trading Economics) US: Gold Slips on Dollar Strength Gold prices edged lower toward $4,350 on Monday, pressured by a stronger US dollar and profit-taking after last week’s rally, while investors continued to monitor developments in the Middle East. Bullion reached its highest level in more than a week on Friday as falling oil prices eased concerns over prolonged inflationary pressures. Oil prices extended their decline at the start of the week as investors looked for signs of diplomatic progress on the Iran conflict around this week’s UN meetings, although tensions remained elevated as Iran and the US exchanged fresh threats on Sunday. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Holds Decline as Supply Concerns Ease Crude oil held below $96 per barrel on Tuesday after falling for four consecutive sessions, pressured by easing supply concerns in the Middle East and growing diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war. President Donald Trump is scheduled to address the UN General Assembly in New York later today and could meet with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on the sidelines. Trump is also expected to hold discussions with other Gulf nations and Chinese President Xi Jinping this week. (Trading Economics) US: AI adoption is driving hiring, but mostly for senior roles Companies using artificial intelligence are adding more jobs than those that are not but those gains sharply favour senior employees over junior workers, according to a new study spanning 41 countries. The number of employees in senior positions rose by 6.7% over five years at companies adopting AI while junior employment declined 3% in the same period, researchers Bharat Chandar of Stanford University and Bouke Klein Teeselink of King’s College London said in a paper released on Monday. (Bloomberg) US: Fed's Kashkari says inflation is still too high in 'all aspects' of US economy Minneapolis Federal Reserve president Neel Kashkari said on Sunday that inflation is too high across all sectors of the US economy, not just in rising oil prices. "So even if we strip out energy, which is really volatile, and strip out food — they matter a lot — but in terms of where the economy is going, inflation is still too high," Kashkari told Fox News' Sunday Morning Futures. (Reuters) US: Housing costs rise further out of reach ahead of mid-terms Barely six weeks out from the midterm elections, housing costs that many Americans have long said are too high are looking even more out of reach. The latest blow for consumers came Thursday, when Freddie Mac reported that rates for 30-year mortgages climbed to 6.95%, the highest since January 2025, when President Donald Trump returned to office. That report emerged after the Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, crushing any hopes that borrowing costs will come down soon. (Bloomberg) US: New data centres worth US$68 billion disrupted in US, data show Opposition to data centres continues to mount in the US. That is according to research group Data Center Watch, which said some 45 data centre projects worth US$68 billion (RM277.28 billion) were blocked or delayed by local pushback between April and June this year. Communities across the country are now pushing through moratoriums on new construction, often before developers can apply for permissions. (Bloomberg) US: EM investors are favouring local bonds as dollar debt lags Emerging-market investors are for now sticking with local-currency sovereign debt as surging Treasury yields dim the appeal of dollardenominated developing-nation bonds. Behind the strategy are attractive valuations and the potential to profit from carry trades, where investors borrow in low-yielding currencies to invest in higher-yielding assets. (Bloomberg) US: ECB launches key link between blockchain and euro payment system The European Central Bank on Monday began letting banks settle tokenised wholesale transactions in central-bank money while continuing efforts to develop a digital euro for consumers by the end of the decade. The so-called Pontes project links blockchain markets with the euro area’s existing payment systems. It will eventually be replaced by a longer-term solution known as Appia, for which a blueprint should be ready in 2028. (Bloomberg) CN: Yuan hits fresh multi-year peak as China's central bank eases curb ahead of Trump-Xi summit China's yuan strengthened to more than a 3-1/2-year high against the US dollar on Monday as the central bank softened its curb on currency appreciation ahead of the meeting this week between the leaders of China and the US.US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng concluded talks in New York on Sunday, laying the groundwork for US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping to consider at their summit from Sept 23-25. (Reuters) SK: Early exports maintain strong momentum on chip boom South Korea’s exports continued to grow at a solid pace in early September as global demand for artificial-intelligence supported semiconductor shipments and the broader trade-dependent economy. Exports adjusted for working-day differences rose 89.8% from a year earlier in the first 20 days of September, according to customs office data released Monday. That compared with an initially reported 61.5% increase during the same period in August. (Bloomberg) MY: Nearly two-thirds of Malaysians make RM2,200 or less a month in 2025 - official data Nearly two-thirds of Malaysia’s wage earners were in semi- and low-skilled jobs in 2025, with median monthly wages of RM2,223 or less, according to the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). Semi-skilled workers, who accounted for 55.6% of wage earners, had a median monthly wage of RM2,223, while low-skilled workers, who make up 7.8% of wage earners, earned RM1,758. Skilled workers, by comparison, earned a median RM5,057. Skilled workers make up 36.6% of total wage recipients. (The Edge) MY: Malaysians' average monthly salary up 4% to RM3,803 in 2025 - DOSM The average monthly salary and wage of Malaysians increased by 4.1% to RM3,803 in 2025, compared with RM3,652 the previous year, according to the Salaries and Wages Survey Report 2025 published by the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) on Monday. At the same time, the median monthly salary and wage increased by 5.3 % to RM2,940 from RM2,793 in 2024. (Berrnama) MY: REIT managers call for return of withholding tax relief in Budget 2027 The Malaysian REIT Managers Association (MRMA) hopes the withholding tax break on real estate investment trusts (REITs) dividends will be restored in Budget 2027. AmFIRST Real Estate Investment Trust (REIT) manager and chief executive officer Chong Hong Chuon told reporters after its annual general meeting and extraordinary general meeting that the association had submitted its requests to the government, including a review of the tax treatment for REIT distributions. (Berrnama) AAGB: Malaysia wins best low-cost airline award for 17th year as it renews operating certificate AirAsia Malaysia, the carrier operated by AirAsia Group Bhd, was recognised as the World’s Best Low-Cost Airline for the 17th consecutive year at the 2026 Skytrax World Airline Awards in London last Friday.The latest win comes as the airline marks 25 years of operations. (The Edge) INSPACE: Bags RM35 mil subcontract for renovation works Interior fit-out firm Inspace Creation Bhd has won a subcontract of RM34.75 million to undertake renovation works on commercial properties. In a Bursa Malaysia filing on Monday, the group stated that its indirectly wholly owned subsidiary, IDPM Builder Sdn Bhd, had accepted a letter of award for the project from an undisclosed customer on Monday. The company said it could not disclose the identity of the main contractor as well as the location of the project and specific details of the subcontract due to confidentiality and non-disclosure obligations. (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Hits four-year high after slew of good news Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd, hit a four-year high on Monday in a sudden spike in its share price, which came amid a slew of positive developments, including the renewal of a 10-year product supply deal with Shell Malaysia two weeks ago. The spike comes as brent crude futures fell to a week’s low of US$101.7 (RM415.06) a barrel. (The Edge) PWRWELL: Secures RM190m orders to supply low voltage switchgear for data centre in Johor Powerwell Holdings Bhd said on Monday it has secured two contracts worth RM190.42 million for the supply of low-voltage switchgear and related equipment for a data centre project in Johor. The electrical equipment manufacturer said its wholly owned unit, Powerwell International Sdn Bhd, will be supplying the equipment to a multinational technology corporation specialising in data centres. (The Edge) DIALOG: Gets PETRONAS approval for US$81m RAJA Cluster development plan Dialog Group Bhd said its RAJA Cluster small field asset production sharing contract (PSC) has received approval from Petroliam Nasional Bhd (PETRONAS) for an US$81 million (RM330.29 million) field development and abandonment plan. In a bourse filing on Monday, Dialog said the final investment decision for the plan was approved by PETRONAS through Malaysia Petroleum Management (MPM). (The Edge) EFORCE: Proposes RM11 mil private placement to fund working capital as TS Wong hit by selldowns Excel Force MSC Bhd, one of the companies linked to businessman Wong Thean Soon, has proposed a private placement to raise up to RM10.98 million for working capital and free up funds for a software project. The financial technology solutions provider plans to issue up to 60.99 million new shares, representing 10% of its existing issued share capital, to third-party investors to be identified later, according to its filing with Bursa Malaysia on Monday. (The Edge) WINSTAR: Plans RM300 million sukuk for investments, land acquisition, refinancing Winstar Capital Bhd proposes to issue a RM300 million sukuk to finance investments and land acquisition, as well as to refinance existing loans. The group, which lodged the sukuk murabahah programme with the Securities Commission Malaysia on Monday, said proceeds will also be used to defray issuance expenses and for working capital. (The Edge) SPSETIA: Launches 100-acre Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines S P Setia Bhd officially launched Setia Fontaines Heritage Park at Setia Fontaines in Kepala Batas, Penang — marking a significant milestone in the group's placemaking and township development efforts in Penang. According to a press statement on Sept 21, the launch was graced by Yang di-Pertua Negeri of Penang Tun Ramli Ngah Talib and his wife Toh Puan Raja Noora Ashikin Raja Abdullah, alongside state representatives, government agencies, strategic partners, invited guests, residents and members of the public. (The Edge) KGB: To collaborate with Tata Group's unit on Gujarat semiconductor fabrication facility Kelington Group Bhd has entered into a collaboration with electronics and semiconductor manufacturer Tata Electronics to advance the development of the latter’s semiconductor fabrication facility (Fab) in Dholera, Gujarat. Kelington said under the agreement dated Sept 18, the group will support the Tata Group’s unit in infrastructure and system deployment for the facility. (The Edge) PEKAT: Unit to lease 470 acres in Sungai Petani for 24 years for renewable energy activities Pekat Group Bhd said on Monday that it will lease about 470 acres of land in Sungai Petani, Kedah for renewable energy activities, including the development of solar photovoltaic systems and battery energy storage systems. In a bourse filing, the engineering services firm said its wholly owned unit Pekat Teknologi Sdn Bhd had entered into a conditional lease agreement with an unnamed company to lease the land. title: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank at APAC Innovation Awards 2026
body: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank at APAC Innovation Awards 2026 Red Hat has named Hong Leong Bank as the Malaysian winner of the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026, recognising the bank’s use of open source technologies to modernise its infrastructure and improve digital services. This year’s awards, themed “Unlock what’s next,” recognise 32 organisations across 13 Asia Pacific markets for using Red Hat solutions to address complex business challenges and drive innovation. The awards cover five areas: Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud-Native Development, Automation, Virtualization and AI. Hong Leong Bank Modernises Its Infrastructure Hong Leong Bank was recognised in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category for its efforts to improve the scalability and performance of a critical online business application. The bank moved the application from a traditional monolithic architecture to a containerised environment using Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. It also adopted Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to modernise its existing database infrastructure and bring virtual machines and containers together on a common platform. The move has helped reduce software deployment cycles from months to weeks while eliminating manual virtual machine patching for containerised workloads. The new architecture also allows applications to scale dynamically during periods of high traffic. According to Hong Leong Bank, the modernised infrastructure provides a more flexible foundation for introducing new digital banking capabilities while maintaining the reliability expected by customers. Red Hat said the 2026 winners demonstrate how open source technologies can help organisations simplify complex IT environments, modernise operations and create greater flexibility as technologies such as AI, hybrid cloud and automation continue to evolve. William Streitberg, Chief Information & Technology Officer at Hong Leong Bank, said the collaboration with Red Hat has provided the bank with a common foundation for both existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing new capabilities to be introduced more quickly. The recognition highlights Hong Leong Bank’s ongoing efforts to modernise its technology infrastructure while supporting the continued development of its digital banking services.

title: 'Red Hat Recognises Hong Leong Bank for Unlocking New Possibilities with Open Source at the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 for Malaysia
body: 'Red Hat, Inc., the world’s leading provider of open source solutions, today announced the winners of the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 for Malaysia. This year, Red Hat recognises Hong Leong Bank for their leadership through open source, demonstrating how open source technologies help organisations navigate complexity, modernise operations, and deliver sustainable growth. As organisations across Asia Pacific embrace AI, hybrid cloud, automation, and cloud-native technologies, managing complexity has become just as important as driving innovation. With AI strategies increasingly spanning different models, accelerators, and cloud environments, enterprises are looking to open source because openness brings choice, and choice brings greater flexibility. That flexibility enables them to adopt the technologies best suited to their business needs while building the agility needed to respond to change. Reflecting this year’s theme, “Unlock what’s next,” the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards 2026 celebrate organisations that are leading the way with open source. This year’s awards recognise 32 winners across the region whose innovative use of Red Hat solutions is helping solve complex business challenges and deliver meaningful outcomes for customers, employees, and communities. The winners were recognised for demonstrating how open source can help organisations turn complexity into opportunity. By modernising technology foundations, streamlining operations, and accelerating innovation, each organisation has delivered measurable outcomes that strengthen business resilience and create lasting value. Their achievements reflect Red Hat’s continued collaboration with enterprises across 13 APAC countries to solve real-world challenges through open source. The awards comprise five categories: Hybrid Cloud Infrastructure, Cloud-Native Development, Automation, Virtualization, and AI. Category: Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development Winner: Hong Leong Bank Hong Leong Bank, one of Malaysia’s leading digital-forward banks, has been recognised in the Virtualization and Cloud-Native Development category for its infrastructure enhancement efforts. As part of the bank’s continuous innovation efforts, the bank sought to improve scalability of a critical online business application by addressing legacy architecture and manual processes. To overcome these performance bottlenecks, Hong Leong Bank transitioned the application from a monolithic framework to a containerised environment using Red Hat OpenShift and Red Hat Application Foundations. The bank also deployed Red Hat OpenShift Virtualization to create a structured path for modernising its existing database infrastructure, effectively unifying virtual machines and containers onto a single, common platform. The architectural shift has transformed the bank’s operational efficiency, cutting software deployment cycles from months to weeks while eliminating manual virtual machine patching for containerised workloads. By enabling applications to scale dynamically during traffic spikes, Hong Leong Bank has built an agile foundation to accelerate the continuous delivery of innovative digital banking services. Supporting Quotes Daniel Aw, Vice President & General Manager, APAC, Red Hat APAC “Enterprise technology is becoming more complex than ever, but success is no longer about how many new technologies an organisation adopts. What matters more is how effectively these solutions work together to address real business challenges and deliver tangible value. This year’s winners demonstrate that the organisations best positioned for long-term success are those building open, flexible foundations that allow them to innovate on their own terms. Their achievements are a testament to what organisations can accomplish when technology decisions are guided by business needs rather than trends, and it is this approach that we are proud to celebrate through the Red Hat APAC Innovation Awards.” William Streitberg, Chief Information & Technology Officer, Hong Leong Bank “Enhancing a bank’s technology environment does not happen overnight, and updating infrastructure requires us to understand what is the right-fit for our operations. Red Hat has equipped us with a common foundation for both our existing and cloud-native workloads, allowing us to introduce new capabilities faster while maintaining the reliability our customers expect.”

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Stays Lower at Mid-Morning Trailed by Heavyweight Selling
body: 'Bursa Malaysia remained firmly in negative territory at mid-morning on Thursday, October 1, 2026, dragged down by selling pressure across key blue-chip counters, primarily in healthcare, industrial products, and utilities sectors. At 11:00 AM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slid 11.73 points to 1,639.44 compared to Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. The index had opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth was negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 484 to 273, while 460 counters traded unchanged, 1,556 untraded, and 12 suspended. Total turnover stood at 1.18 billion shares valued at RM769.76 million. Sectoral Pressure and Heavyweight Performance Heavyweight stocks across multiple sectors experienced selling pressure during the morning session: - Healthcare: IHH Healthcare dropped 13 sen to RM7.70. - Industrial Products: Petronas Chemicals shed 11 sen to RM4.07, Press Metal Aluminium slipped 9 sen to RM7.36, and Sunway fell 2 sen to RM4.40. - Utilities: YTL Power lost 6 sen to RM5.81, Tenaga Nasional dropped 2 sen to RM12.94, and YTL Corporation edged down 1 sen to RM2.27. - Financials: Banking stocks saw broad-based softness with Public Bank down 3 sen to RM4.67, while Maybank and CIMB eased 2 sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.77, respectively. Active Stocks and Top Gainers and Losers In active trade, ACE Market debutant GB Bond shed 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen, while Dagang Nexchange gained 2 sen to 50.5 sen. V.S Industry added 1 sen to 29 sen, Zetrix AI rose half a sen to 16.5 sen, and Jaks Resources dropped half a sen to 20 sen. Technology stocks featured among the session’s top gainers: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Up 62 sen to RM41.02. - Malayan Cement: Up 12 sen to RM5.57. - MI Technovation & Hengyuan Refining: Gained 10 sen each to RM5.30 and RM3.66, respectively. - Vitrox: Advanced 8 sen to RM9.99. On the decliners’ chart, Kuala Lumpur Kepong led losses, falling 74 sen to RM21.46. Other notable pullbacks included Allianz Malaysia (down 68 sen to RM20.94), Nestle (down 40 sen to RM89.60), United Plantations (down 30 sen to RM31.26), and Hong Leong Bank (down 28 sen to RM22.86). Broad Market and Sectoral Indices All major sectoral indices recorded declines at mid-morning, led by plantations and financials: - The Plantation Index tumbled 104.26 points to 9,092.41. - The Financial Services Index shed 87.09 points to 19,129.40. - The Energy Index eased 5.43 points to 840.27. - The Industrial Products and Services Index fell 1.24 points to 179.17. Across the broader index boards: - The FBM Top 100 Index fell 76.32 points to 12,008.12. - The FBM Emas Index dropped 72.18 points to 12,219.83. - The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 71.61 points to 12,104.73. - The FBM Mid 70 Index lost 71.17 points to 17,503.50. - The FBM ACE Index trimmed 22.64 points to 5,511.64. –NMT

body: 'Bursa Malaysia awarded its top CEO and CFO honours to Maybank’s Dato’ Sri Khairussaleh Ramli and Hong Leong Bank’s Malkit Singh Maan. We remain deeply grateful for the continued trust and strong support of our investment community, shareholders, and valued partners throughout this journey.” The awards recognised 32 winners across eight main categories for investor engagement, market communication and corporate transparency. title: 'Akaun Pelaburan Patuh Shariah HLB Islamic Menarik 43% Pelanggan Baharu
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: HLB Islamic meraikan ulang tahun pertama HLB Meezani Account-i menerusi Majlis Penyampaian Ganjaran Tahunan 2026.  Diperkenalkan untuk menggalakkan amalan kewangan yang sihat, akaun pelaburan harian patuh Shariah ini membolehkan rakyat Malaysia mengembangkan simpanan dan pelaburan mereka melalui saluran berisiko rendah.  Majlis tersebut turut mengiktiraf para pelanggan yang telah memulakan perjalanan kewangan mereka menerusi amalan menyimpan dan melabur secara berdisiplin.  Pada tahun pertama, HLB Islamic memberikan ganjaran kepada pemegang HLB Meezani Account-i menerusi cabutan harian, mingguan, bulanan, suku tahunan dan tahunan, dengan ganjaran termasuk sebuah Denza D9, hadiah wang tunai bernilai RM100,000 serta pakej percutian keluarga bernilai sehingga RM30,000.  Meneruskan momentum berkenaan, pihak Bank akan terus memberi ganjaran kepada pemegang akaun pada 2027 menerusi pelbagai hadiah menarik.  Antaranya termasuk sebuah Porsche Cayenne S E-Hybrid Coupé, empat buah Proton e.MAS 5, sebuah Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra setiap bulan, emas 999, pakej percutian, dan ganjaran tunai menerusi struktur cabutan yang sama.  Semakin banyak pelanggan menyimpan, semakin tinggi peluang mereka untuk menikmati lebih banyak ganjaran. Pelanggan juga boleh memperoleh penyertaan bonus melalui transaksi harian daripada HLB Meezani Account-i, termasuk pembayaran melalui QR Pay, pembayaran bil dan pelaburan secara berkala.  Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, berkata bahawa pengurusan harta dikenalpasti sebagai bidang perkembangan utama dalam Pelan Transformasi HLB. Fokus ini telah membawa kepada pengenalan Hayat @ HLB Islamic, pendekatan pengurusan harta holistik yang berteraskan falsafah “Pegangan Lestari Membimbing Kesenangan Masa Depan”.  Pendekatan ini merangkumi keseluruhan perjalanan pengurusan harta meliputi Penciptaan, Pengumpulan, Perlindungan, Penyucian, serta Pengagihan harta. HLB Meezani Account-i merupakan salah satu manifestasi pendekatan ini, membawa falsafah pengurusan harta Bank kepada penyelesaian pelaburan yang mematuhi prinsip Syariah.  “Perbankan Shariah sememangnya untuk semua. Pada asasnya, ia merupakan perbankan beretika yang berteraskan prinsip keadilan dan ketelusan, dengan memberi tumpuan kepada penggunaan dana dalam aktiviti yang dapat memberi manfaat secara mampan kepada masyarakat.  “Di HLB Islamic, kami bukan sekadar tempat untuk menyimpan wang. Pendekatan pengurusan harta Bank ini telah mendapat sambutan yang menggalakkan daripada para pelanggan, dengan 43% daripada mereka yang membuka HLB Meezani Account-i pada tahun pertamanya merupakan pelanggan baharu Bank.  Dengan jumlah pembukaan akaun serendah RM100 serta peluang menerima ganjaran secara berkala, akaun ini direka untuk menjadikan pembinaan kekayaan lebih mudah diakses, di samping menggalakkan pelanggan mengoptimumkan simpanan mereka melalui penyelesaian pelaburan yang patuh Syariah.  HLB Islamic komited untuk menjadikan usaha membina kekayaan lebih mudah dan dekat dengan masyarakat, dengan menyedari bahawa membentuk tabiat kewangan yang baik tidak semestinya perlu dilakukan secara terlalu rigid atau menakutkan. title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher Amid Bargain Hunting
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia's key index opened higher on Wednesday, driven by bargain hunting following recent losses, despite negative signals from Wall Street. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) increased by 4.34 points, or 0.26 percent, reaching 1,648.30 at 9.10 am, recovering from Tuesday's close of 1,643.96. The index began the day 2.53 points higher at 1,646.49. In the broader market, decliners outnumbered gainers 214 to 174, with 293 counters remaining unchanged, 2,174 untraded, and 95 suspended. The turnover was recorded at 265.65 million shares valued at RM151.82 million. Thong Pak Leng, vice-president of equity research at Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, noted that the market is becoming increasingly oversold, presenting opportunities for selective accumulation in fundamentally strong blue-chip stocks. He added that any recovery might be limited unless foreign selling decreases and banking heavyweights receive more support. Thong also pointed out that energy, renewable infrastructure, and certain defensive stocks could perform well, whereas technology stocks remain vulnerable due to high global yields. He predicted a cautious trading session, with bargain hunting around 1,640, keeping the index within the 1,635-1,655 range. Among heavyweights, Maybank rose three sen to RM10.02, Public Bank gained two sen to RM4.74, while CIMB fell two sen to RM7.76. title: 'Hong Leong Bank shines at Asian Banking and Finance Awards
body:
'

PETALING JAYA: Hong Leong Bank’s (HLB) business and corporate banking segment achieved a significant benchmark at the recent Asian Banking and Finance Awards, clinching four major accolades that solidify its standing as a regional industry leader.


Highlighted by its fifth consecutive win as Best SME Bank in Malaysia and securing Malaysia Domestic Technology & Operations Bank of the Year, the awards validate HLB’s distinct entrepreneurial DNA and reinforce its position as a regional leader for business and SME banking.


Adding to this regional momentum, HLB was also named the Singapore International Foreign Exchange Bank of the Year and won the Initiative Award for SME Cross Border Finance Innovation in Singapore.


Rooted in a 120-year entrepreneurial heritage, the bank’s approach to business banking stems from a lived understanding of tenacity, risk management, and commercial agility, positioning itself as an entrepreneurial bank, and not just a bank that builds entrepreneurs.


This heritage continues to make HLB a trusted growth partner for local businesses, driving a robust 9.5% year-on-year (y-o-y) expansion in its SME loan and financing portfolio as of March 31, 2026, spearheaded by a standout 10.8% y-o-y growth in the community SME banking segment, the group said in a statement.


HLB Group managing director and CEO Kevin Lam commented, “At the core of our operational vision is a refusal to treat modern business banking as a binary choice between digital automation and human partnerships. We believe that true innovation and growth happens when you get the right mix of people and technology.


“By anchoring our 120-year entrepreneurial heritage in trusted, personal advisory relationships and augmenting them with hyper-personalized digital infrastructure and strategic AI integration, our relationship managers can focus on deepening relationships, delivering sharp advisory, and co-create bespoke solutions built entirely around the entrepreneur.”


HLB managing director of business and corporate banking Yow Kuan Tuck said, “Our philosophy is to serve as a genuine, value-adding partner to our corporate and SME clients. By supporting and empowering business owners to grow their enterprises through our dedicated suite of banking solutions, we aim to build lasting success stories that ultimately reinvest in and enrich our communities.”


This philosophy is reflected across the bank’s end-to-end scalable business banking solutions, such as its specialized financing and collection frameworks for its SME clients. Supported by automated payment systems like direct debit and e-mandates, these initiatives stabilise business operations and streamline customer transactions with targeted loans and financing solutions.


HLB said it continues to accelerate digital adoption for its broader SME clientele through integrated digital payment solutions such as FPX, card acceptance, QR codes, and digital invoicing, simplifying cash collections for clients nationwide.


Extending across the Causeway, HLB pairs robust domestic operational technology with sophisticated foreign exchange and cross-border innovation across regional markets, effectively providing a frictionless, single-bank network which ensures that business clients looking to scale from domestic roots to regional markets enjoy unparalleled financial continuity, liquidity management, and international trade support.

title: 'HLB Islamic Berjaya Lonjak Pendapatan Usahawan Berpendapatan Rendah Langkawi Sebanyak 94%
body: 'Kuala Lumpur, 23 September 2026 – Selaras dengan komitmen untuk memperkasakan ekosistem perantaraan berasaskan nilai (“Value-based Intermediation” atau “VBI”), HLB Islamic (atau “Bank”) telah menyalurkan pembiayaan sebanyak RM138,600 kepada perusahaan sosial SURI Inspirasi (“SURI”) di bawah kerangka iTEKAD Bank Negara Malaysia (“BNM”). Inisiatif ini secara langsung menyumbang kepada peningkatan purata pendapatan bulanan sebanyak 94% serta menjana jumlah pendapatan baharu melebihi RM14,000 bagi usahawan yang menyertai program “Sustainable Reliable Income” (“SRI”) anjuran SURI.  Program SRI memperkasakan komuniti berpendapatan rendah untuk mengitar semula sisa fabrik menjadi barangan fesyen yang unik, yang secara langsung mewujudkan peluang pekerjaan dan memupuk semangat keusahawanan di samping mempromosikan fesyen sifar sisa serta pemerkasaan komuniti. Usahawan yang terlibat, yang majoritinya ibu tunggal berpendapatan rendah, telah menghasilkan 1,000 pasang pakaian seragam sekolah untuk pelajar di lima buah sekolah di Langkawi, sekali gus menjana penjimatan sebanyak RM30,000 bagi keluarga tempatan.  HLB Islamic meraikan pencapaian ini menerusi penyerahan mesin jahit berkualiti tinggi kepada para usahawan yang terlibat, menandakan peralihan daripada pembelajaran di dalam bilik darjah kepada pemilikan perniagaan secara aktif.  Menurut Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif HLB Islamic, “Visi kami tentang pengurusan kewangan berteraskan Hayat @ HLB Islamic, di mana pengurusan harta dilihat sebagai satu perjalanan yang bermula dengan Penciptaan Harta. Melalui kerjasama dengan SURI, kami menyediakan alat dan latihan asas yang diperlukan oleh komuniti untuk mencungkil potensi keusahawanan mereka. Kami berharap usaha ini akan menjadi pemangkin kepada perjalanan pembinaan kekayaan yang berterusan ke arah kebebasan kewangan yang bakal memperkayakan komuniti untuk generasi akan datang.”  Kejayaan ini menandakan satu pencapaian penting dalam kerjasama berterusan antara HLB Islamic dan SURI, yang mula menyertai ekosistem Bank ini sebagai peserta inisiatif HLB Jumpstart. Diperkenalkan bagi memupuk perusahaan sosial Malaysia yang berimpak tinggi menerusi bimbingan komersial, penjenamaan, serta pembinaan kapasiti digital, HLB Jumpstart telah menyediakan kerangka awal kepada SURI untuk memperluas operasinya. Hal ini membuktikan strategi jangka panjang Bank dalam memupuk usaha sosial menjadi rakan pelaksana berdikari yang mampu memberikan impak yang lebih meluas.

title: 'Hong Leong Bank declares 80 sen final dividend
body: 'by ANN ZAINUDDIN   HONG Leong Bank Bhd has declared a final single-tier dividend of 80 sen per share for the financial year ended June 30, 2026.   In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the group said the dividend will be payable on Oct 21, 2026.    The ex-date for the dividend is set for Oct 7, while the entitlement date falls on Oct 8 at 5pm.   Shareholders whose securities are transferred into their central depository system (CDS) accounts before 4:30pm on the entitlement date will qualify for the payout.   At market close, Hong Leong Bank’s share price declined 0.77% or 18 sen to RM23.20, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM50.29 billion.

title: 'HLB Islamic fund lifts Langkawi entrepreneurs’ income
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Aligned with its commitment to deepening its value-based intermediation (VBI) ecosystem, HLB Islamic has channeled RM138,600 in social financing towards social enterprise SURI Inspirasi under Bank Negara Malaysia’s (BNM) iTEKAD framework, which has led to a 94% average surge in monthly income and over RM14,000 in total new earnings for participating entrepreneurs of SURI’s Sustainable Reliable Income (SRI) programme.  The SRI programme empowers underserved communities to upcycle discarded fabrics into unique fashion items, creating sustainable jobs and encouraging entrepreneurship while promoting zero-waste fashion and community empowerment. As part of the programme, the participating entrepreneurs, predominantly underserved single mothers, produced 1,000 school uniforms for students across five schools in Langkawi, generating RM30,000 in savings for local families.  HLB Islamic commemorated the milestone through the handover of high-grade sewing machines to the participating entrepreneurs, marking the transition from classroom learning to active enterprise ownership.  According to HLBIslamic CEO Dafinah Ahmed Hilmi, “Our vision of financial stewardship is grounded in our Hayat @ HLB Islamic framework, which views wealth building as a purposeful journey across life stages, starting with wealth creation. Through our partnership with SURI, we are providing the community with the essential tools and training to unlock their entrepreneurial potential, and we hope this will catalyse a lifelong trajectory of building wealth towards financial independence that will enrich the community for generations to come.”  This success marks a significant milestone in HLB Islamic’s ongoing collaboration with SURI, who first entered the bank’s ecosystem as a participant of the HLB Jumpstart initiative. Launched to incubate high-impact Malaysian social enterprises through commercial mentorship, branding, and digital capacity building, HLB Jumpstart provided SURI with the early framework to scale its operations, illustrating the bank’s long-term strategy of nurturing social ventures into self-sustaining implementation partners capable of delivering widespread impact.

title: 'HLB Targets Wealthy Clients With New opus Privilege Ecosystem
body:
'

Hong Leong Bank is strengthening its affluent banking strategy with HLB opus, an invitation-only payment and lifestyle programme built for selected high-value clients.

The launch combines premium banking, travel benefits and wealth relationships into a single proposition.


At the centre is Southeast Asia’s first ceramic credit card.

HLB opus is also the first payment experience in Malaysia to use the Visa Infinite Privilege tier.

However, the bigger story is not the card material.

HLB is using opus to connect business banking, private wealth management and premium lifestyle benefits under one customer relationship.

HLB Connects Business Success With Personal Wealth

HLB calls the strategy its “One Bank” client success model.

The approach reflects how many high-net-worth customers interact with banks.

Their financial relationships can span business financing, corporate accounts, investments, private banking and personal spending.

HLB wants opus to sit at the personal end of that journey.

Business & Corporate Banking supports entrepreneurship and company growth.

Private Banking helps clients structure and preserve wealth.

Personal Financial Services then translates that relationship into travel, lifestyle and rewards benefits.

The model allows HLB to position opus as a product earned through a broader financial relationship rather than a conventional premium credit card application.

Ceramic Card Reinforces Exclusivity

The physical HLB opus card uses Convego Ceramic technology from Giesecke+Devrient.

Ceramic remains uncommon in the payment card industry, where most premium offerings rely on metal.

The HLB card is manufactured using extreme heat and pressure before undergoing diamond finishing.

The result is designed to be scratch resistant while offering a smooth texture and reflective appearance.

HLB sees the material as part of the product’s wider symbolism.

The name “opus” comes from the Latin word associated with work or achievement.

That concept is intended to connect the physical card with the professional and financial achievements of the clients invited to hold it.

Andrew Jong, HLB Managing Director of Personal Financial Services, said the product recognises the personal stories, sacrifices and ambitions behind client success.

Visa Infinite Privilege Expands Global Access

The privileges attached to the card extend well beyond payments.

HLB opus uses Visa Infinite Privilege, one of Visa’s highest-tier premium offerings.

Clients receive unlimited access to Plaza Premium Lounges around the world.

The package also includes immigration fast-track passes and access to selected Visa private clubs.

Additional status-matching benefits include Harrods Gold, ALL Accor+ Explorer Gold and Banyan Voyager.

These benefits target customers who travel frequently for business and leisure.

Visa Malaysia said affluent consumers are increasingly looking for experiences that feel personal and differentiated.

That shift is pushing premium banking products away from simple cashback and points propositions.

Enrich Partnership Strengthens Travel Rewards

Malaysia Airlines’ Enrich programme plays another important role in the HLB opus ecosystem.

Clients receive 60,000 Enrich Points after payment of the annual fee.

HLB has also created a higher conversion tier designed to reward overseas spending.

The bank says the arrangement gives opus clients the strongest Enrich Points earning potential in the region.

Cardholders can additionally earn one Elite Point for every RM10,000 spent overseas.

Elite Points can help travellers progress through Enrich status tiers.

The partnership also connects customers to reward opportunities across Malaysia Airlines and other carriers in the oneworld alliance.

Malaysia Aviation Group said the collaboration is intended to extend premium service beyond individual flights and into the wider travel experience.

HLB Looks Beyond Traditional Luxury Banking

The introduction of opus reflects changing expectations among affluent banking customers.

Luxury financial products once competed mainly through card materials, airport lounges and concierge services.

Those benefits still matter.

However, wealthy customers increasingly expect banks to understand their wider business, investment and personal needs.

HLB appears to be responding by combining multiple banking divisions around the same client.

That can create deeper relationships and make it harder for competitors to win individual parts of a customer’s financial business.

For HLB, the value of opus may therefore extend far beyond spending on the card itself.

Wealth Management Remains a Key Growth Area

HLB has been expanding its wealth capabilities alongside its business and corporate banking operations.

The bank’s Private Bank works with international wealth partners including Lombard Odier.

That gives HLB access to broader investment and wealth-management expertise for high-net-worth clients.

HLB opus adds a lifestyle layer on top of those capabilities.

The strategy allows the bank to follow a client from business growth through wealth accumulation and eventually into legacy planning.

Premium travel and lifestyle services then become part of that broader relationship.

HLB opus Is Really About Client Retention

The ceramic card may attract attention, but HLB’s larger objective is relationship depth.

An invite-only product gives the bank another way to recognise and retain its highest-value customers.

Premium rewards can strengthen loyalty among clients who already use HLB for corporate, private or personal banking.

At the same time, the exclusivity of the product can reinforce the perceived value of the wider banking relationship.

That makes HLB opus as much a customer strategy as a credit card launch.

Its combination of ceramic design, Visa Infinite Privilege services and Malaysia Airlines rewards gives HLB a distinctive premium proposition.

More importantly, it gives the bank another tool for keeping business, wealth and lifestyle banking under one roof.

You can earn points from things you probably already do, including: You can also earn points from FPX payments, cross-border QR payments, foreign currency conversions and linking an HLB account to an HLB Singapore account via LINKS. You can also earn 200 points for each friend or family member who successfully opens an eligible account through the HLB Connect app. The Connect Points aren’t prizes themselves. They’re used to earn entries into the promotion’s prize draws. You’ll need: And your points aren’t deducted when you earn an entry. For example, someone with 11,370 Connect Points would get one entry into the Grand Prize draw, two entries into the Second Prize draw and three entries into the Third Prize draw. You can check your points through the Points Tracker on HLB Connect. Don’t have the app yet? You can download it from the Apple App Store or Google Play Store, then log in and check your points. Any unused balance will be forfeited. The promotion ends on 20 November 2026, with winners due to be notified by 1 February 2027. title: 'Hong Leong Bank Launches HLB opus Ceramic Card
body: 'Hong Leong Bank has launched HLB opus, an invitation-only payment card aimed at its most affluent clients. The new card is Southeast Asia’s first credit card made from exclusive ceramic material. It is also Malaysia’s first payment experience built around the Visa Infinite Privilege tier. HLB is positioning opus as more than another premium card. Instead, the bank wants it to act as a gateway to exclusive travel, dining, wellness and concierge services for selected clients. HLB opus Uses Ceramic Instead of Metal Premium credit cards have increasingly relied on metal construction to create a sense of exclusivity. HLB has taken a different approach. HLB opus uses Giesecke+Devrient’s Convego Ceramic technology. The card is produced using high heat and pressure before being finished through diamond refinement. HLB says the result is a scratch-resistant card with a smooth surface and reflective finish. The ceramic construction is also intended to give the card a distinctive physical and acoustic character. For HLB, that physical design reflects the broader positioning of opus as a statement product rather than simply another payment tool. Andrew Jong, Managing Director of Personal Financial Services at HLB, said the bank created opus to recognise the achievements and personal journeys of its clients. He described the card as a tribute to success built through ambition, resilience and long-term effort. Visa Infinite Privilege Brings Global Benefits The new card is anchored around Visa Infinite Privilege. That gives clients access to a collection of premium international services. Benefits include unlimited access to Plaza Premium Lounges worldwide. Clients can also receive selected immigration fast-track services and access to Visa private clubs. Status-matching benefits are available with several luxury and travel programmes. These include Harrods Gold, ALL Accor+ Explorer Gold and Banyan Voyager. The range of benefits reflects HLB’s focus on internationally mobile clients. Jason Phua, Head of Clients at Visa Malaysia, said affluent customers increasingly value personalised experiences over traditional expressions of luxury. He said the partnership combines Visa’s premium privileges with HLB’s understanding of its high-value clients. HLB opus Targets Frequent Travellers Travel rewards form another major part of the HLB opus proposition. The bank has expanded its existing relationship with Malaysia Airlines’ Enrich loyalty programme. HLB says opus provides the highest Enrich Points earning potential in the region. Clients receive 60,000 Enrich Points after paying the annual fee. They can then increase their points earnings through overseas spending. HLB opus clients can also earn one Elite Point for every RM10,000 spent overseas. Those rewards can support status progression and redemptions across Malaysia Airlines and the wider oneworld airline network. Phillip See, Chief Executive Officer of Loyalty & Travel Services at Malaysia Aviation Group, said premium travellers increasingly expect benefits throughout their entire journey. He added that the partnership is designed to provide more flexibility, rewards and travel privileges. HLB Builds a Broader Privilege Ecosystem The card is also tied to HLB’s wider banking relationships. The bank describes this approach as its “One Bank” client success model. Under that structure, Business & Corporate Banking supports business creation and enterprise growth. Private Banking then focuses on protecting and structuring wealth. Personal Financial Services adds lifestyle and rewards benefits through products such as HLB opus. The strategy is designed to keep clients within the HLB ecosystem across different stages of their business and personal financial journeys. That makes opus more than a standalone credit card launch. It also serves as a visible extension of the bank’s affluent and high-net-worth customer strategy. Physical Cards Still Matter in a Digital Banking Era The introduction of a ceramic payment card comes at a time when digital wallets and virtual payment methods continue to grow. However, premium banks still see value in physical cards as status objects. Farouk Musthafa, Managing Director at Giesecke+Devrient Singapore, said physical cards remain an important tangible expression of distinction. He said HLB approached opus as a privilege-first product rather than a conventional card programme. That positioning helps explain the decision to use ceramic instead of more common plastic or metal materials. The card itself becomes part of the luxury experience. HLB Deepens Focus on Wealth and Affluent Banking The launch also supports Hong Leong Bank’s wider transformation strategy. Business banking and wealth management remain important growth areas for the bank. HLB has been strengthening its offerings across corporate banking, private banking and affluent financial services. Its Private Bank already works with global wealth partners including Lombard Odier. HLB opus adds another layer to that strategy by connecting financial relationships with premium lifestyle benefits. For selected clients, the bank wants business banking, wealth management and personal privileges to operate as one connected experience. HLB opus is therefore positioned as both a payment card and a symbol of that broader relationship. With ceramic construction, Visa Infinite Privilege benefits and enhanced Enrich rewards, HLB is clearly aiming at the highest end of Malaysia’s premium banking market.

title: 'Hong Leong Bank, PetChem Lead Bursa Losers As ViTrox Tops Gainers

title: 'Scientex to Acquire 503 Acres in Johor for RM580 Mil
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Scientex Bhd (KL:SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said in an exchange filing. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. The close proximity between Scientex’s existing projects and the proposed development will generate “better operational efficiencies through greater economies of scale”, the company said. An agreement has been signed between its wholly owned subsidiary Scientex Quatari Sdn Bhd and Pangkal Budiman Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Leong Hup Holdings Sdn Bhd. Scientex mainly manufactures flexible plastic packaging and develops affordable homes in Malaysia. The company has more than 11,000 acres of land spanning seven states across Peninsular Malaysia in its holdings, according to its website. The company has a goal of building 50,000 affordable homes throughout the nation by 2028 and has delivered 47,000 homes to date. The latest acquisition will be funded through a combination of internal funds and bank borrowings. As of July 31, 2026, Scientex held RM357.8 million in cash against total borrowings of RM2.05 billion. The deal is expected to be closed in the second half of 2027. “The lands are expected to provide a steady and sustainable property development model as Scientex continues to focus on affordably priced landed properties where demand continues to remain firm and resilient,” the company added. Shares of Scientex rose one sen or 0.3% to RM3.61 at Tuesday’s noon break, giving the company a market capitalisation of RM5.6 billion. title: 'Construction Firm SLGC Ends First Trading Day Below IPO Price
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm’s shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intraday low of 24 sen as more than 83 million shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140 million. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. “Now that SLGC is a listed company, the priority for us is to continue strengthening the business while staying disciplined in how we grow and we intend to keep improving on how we deliver,” managing director Yong Zheng Lin said in his speech at the listing ceremony. SLGC is a building construction contractor with G7 grade and got its start in 2009 under the name SLG Construction Sdn Bhd before being incorporated in 2024. The company also has an operations office in Taman Gembira, Kuala Lumpur. The company is mainly involved in design and building construction services for residential and non-residential works. SLGC's customers include property developers and building owners in Malaysia. The IPO raised about RM29.4 million for the company and another RM17.64 million for four selling shareholders that include Yong and his wife Chew Ka Yan. Liong Yang Herng, the company’s project director, and contract director Loo Chun Kok are also cashing out part of their stake in SLGC. The company has allocated RM9.2 million of the IPO proceeds towards acquisition of construction machinery and equipment, RM7.6 million to repay bank borrowings, and RM7.5 million for general working capital. The rest will cover software upgrades and listing expenses. M&A Securities Sdn Bhd acted as the principal adviser, sponsor, underwriter, and placement agent for the IPO. title: 'Samaiden Reveals RM238 Mil Contract Value for LSS5+ Solar Project
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Renewable energy solutions provider Samaiden Group Bhd (KL:SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. The group disclosed the contract value in a Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday, four days after announcing the contracts without revealing their value due to confidentiality restrictions. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (KL:YTL). YTL Construction, which is the project's main contractor, appointed Samaiden to undertake engineering, construction and commissioning works, as well as the procurement and supply of solar components for the 99.99MW alternating-current solar photovoltaic plant. The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. Samaiden said the scope of works includes the supply and delivery of materials, design, engineering, construction, testing and completion of the solar photovoltaic facility, with work to commence upon the issuance of a notice to proceed. The group had earlier posted record annual earnings and revenue for the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), its strongest performance since listing in 2020. Net profit for FY2026 surged 93.3% to RM39.07 million from RM20.21 million a year earlier, while revenue rose 3.1% to RM364.5 million from RM353.47 million. The group's order book stood at RM435.8 million as at end-June. Samaiden shares fell seven sen or 2.19% to close at RM3.12 on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM1.75 billion. Year to date, however, the counter is up 124.5%. title: 'Dialog JV Bags Onshore O&G Concession in Thailand
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Monday (Oct 5) that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round, according to Dialog's Bursa Malaysia filing on Tuesday. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. The development of L8/66 carries a minimum work commitment of US$14.3 million (RM58.4 million). The award remains subject to the finalisation and execution of the concession agreement and the fulfilment of its conditions precedent, with physical work expected to begin immediately after the agreement is signed. POES is a joint venture between Dialog’s wholly-owned Pan Orient Petroleum Pte Ltd and Thailand-based Sea Oil Energy Ltd, which holds the remaining 49.99%. Dialog, through POES, already operates the producing L53/48 onshore concession in Thailand, which is adjacent to the L8/66 block. L8/66 was previously part of the L53/48 concession before being relinquished to the Thai government under concession terms requiring portions of undeveloped acreage to be surrendered over time. Dialog said the new block has similar geological characteristics to L53/48 and gives POES access to additional acreage surrounding its existing producing fields. “The award of Concession L8/66 to POES further strengthens Dialog’s upstream portfolio and creates operational synergies by leveraging on the group’s integrated technical services across its diversified business model,” the company said. "Dialog will remain focused and steadfast in the pursuit of diversification across the upstream, midstream and downstream energy sector as well as the sustainable and renewable sector, to strategically position the group to weather different economic and oil price cycles, which is in line with the group's strategy of generating long term recurring income," it added. For the financial year ended June 30, 2026 (FY2026), Dialog’s net profit surged 95.4% to RM593.55 million from RM303.83 million a year earlier, as revenue grew 15.3% to RM2.88 billion from RM2.5 billion. The stronger FY2026 performance was driven by positive contributions across the group’s businesses, particularly its Malaysian operations, while its international businesses also recorded higher profit contributions on increased sales of specialist products and services. Dialog proposed a final dividend of three sen per share, bringing its total dividend for FY2026 to 4.7 sen per share or about RM265.93 million. Dialog shares closed two sen or 1.08% higher at RM1.87 on Tuesday, valuing the group at RM10.56 billion. Year to date, the counter has gained over 6%. title: 'Felda Claims Over RM1 Bil Fraud in Semarak Land Suit as Hearing Begins After Nearly Seven Years
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): The Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and its investment arm, Felda Investment Corporation Sdn Bhd (FIC), claim that 21 individual had conspired to defraud them of over RM1 billion in land and exposed them to RM1.7 billion in potential liabilities through the Kuala Lumpur Vertical City (KLVC) project. Felda and FIC made these allegations in a civil suit against the 21 over a 2014 master development agreement involving 20.066 acres of prime land along Jalan Semarak. Hearing of the suit commenced at the High Court here on Tuesday, seven years after it was initiated in 2019. The defendants include former Felda chairmen Tan Sri Mohd Isa Samad and Tan Sri Shahrir Samad, several former Felda directors general, master developer Synergy Promenade Sdn Bhd (SPSB), Synergy Promenade KLVC Sdn Bhd (SPKLVC) and lawyers. Felda and FIC’s counsel Kumar Kanagasingam said in his opening statement that the defendants had conspired to cause the agencies to enter into a series of questionable agreements and instruments to develop the land. Kumar said evidence would show that SPSB’s appointment as master developer had been predetermined before the boards of Felda and FIC deliberated on the decision. He said SPSB was the only party to submit a proposal for the KLVC project, while the FIC board was led to believe at a January 2014 meeting that several papers were under consideration. Kumar said the other proposals on record were sham submissions from companies owned by Abdul Rahman Soltan, a director and shareholder of SPSB and SPKLVC. FIC was, therefore, induced to appoint SPSB as master developer on Jan 24, 2014, he said. The plaintiffs allege that the land’s commercial value of RM1.062 billion was undercut by a development agreement that capped returns at RM500 million. The fraudlent scheme allegedly involved SPSB directors transferring land titles to themselves and related entities without payment to Felda. Separately, FIC was allegedly locked into a high-risk office leasing agreement that could expose it to an estimated RM1.7 billion in rental liabilities. Kumar said the KLVC project was engineered to enrich the Synergy Group at Felda and FIC’s expense. The plaintiffs are seeking the recovery of title and possession of all 24 parcels of land, damages for fraud, breach of fiduciary duty and dishonest assistance, and the dismissal of SPSB’s counterclaim. The first witness called was Mohamed Ghouse Shajahan, 52, who served on Felda’s board from July 26, 2018, to July 25, 2023. Kumar appeared for Felda and FIC alongside Mong Chung Seng, Wong Han Wey and Medha Ong. SPSB and SPKLVC are represented by RK Sharma, Amrit Pal Singh, Ng Jun Wei, Harmander Singh and JS Chew. In an email interview with The Edge in 2018, Synergy Promenade said that it transferred part of the land to its name “within the four corners of the agreements” entered by the group, Felda and FIC in order to obtain financing to be secured by first-party charges over the land. The company added it was granted power of attorney as the developer and Felda would receive “a minimum of RM500 million or 10% of the gross development value, whichever is higher”. The value of the land was “estimated to be around RM150 million to RM200 million”, the company said at the time. In March last year, Sharir read a statement in the High Court where he affirmed that the Felda land transactions and the subsequent re-transfer are "free from any vitiating factors". The statement was jointly issued with Synergy Promenade's Abdul Rahman, as part of a consent judgment in a defamation suit filed by Synergy Promenade. Both Abdul Rahman and Shahrir are named in Felda and FIC's civil action. title: 'Mosti’s Cradle Fund Sees Overcrowding in Applicants as 70% Are AI-related Startups
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Artificial intelligence (AI)-related startups now account for about 60% to 70% of the estimated 1,000 applications received by Cradle Fund each year, but investors are becoming more selective as the space grows increasingly crowded. Cradle Fund group chief executive officer Norman Matthieu Vanhaecke said the government agency has seen a sharp increase in startups positioning themselves as AI-driven, AI-enabled or AI-native. “The market is getting really, really crowded. So it's kind of tough for venture capitalists later on, and even for us as well, to really decide where to park, for us, especially taxpayers money into,” he said during a panel session at the Alliance Bank BizSmart Business Conference. "At the end of the day, for us, the return has to come back to the country and the people. So it's tough for us. So you have to really differentiate," he added. This has made it more difficult for investors and Cradle Fund, which manages taxpayer funds, to determine which AI businesses have sufficient potential to warrant funding, he said. Cradle Fund was created by the Ministry of Science, Technology and Innovation (Mosti) in 2023. It provides grants, equity investment, commercialisation support, and mentorship to tech entrepreneurs. Startups need to differentiate themselves by developing niche solutions that can serve not only the Malaysian market but also regional and international markets, Vanhaecke said. At the same conference, Sunway iLabs — the innovation arm of Sunway Bhd (KL:SUNWAY) — chief operations officer Karen Lau said investors also need to distinguish between companies that genuinely have AI capabilities and those that are simply using AI as part of their positioning. Investors are looking at the defensibility of the technology, including whether a startup is merely building a layer on top of existing frontier models or has technology that can be integrated deeply into customers’ business processes, she said. Meanwhile, fellow panellist 1337 Ventures CEO and founding partner Bikesh Lakhmichand said the firm looks for founders with expertise in a specific industry, such as healthcare, fashion or marketing, rather than startups built around generic AI applications. “What we are funding is your expertise in the sector, not so much AI,” he said, adding that startups need to demonstrate how their technology addresses specific workflows. Lakhmichand said generic AI applications could face greater competition as foundation models continue to develop. The panel also highlighted a broader shift in how investors assess startups, with traction, market potential and the ability to scale becoming more important than simply positioning a company as an AI business. The session was focused on What It Really Takes for Scaling, Funding, and Strategic Exits?, and was moderated by Redwood Global Capital managing partner Lennise Ng. title: 'Top Glove Expects An Even Better FY2027 After Strong FY2026
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Top Glove Corporation Bhd (KL:TOPGLOV) expects an even better FY2027 after its net profit tripled in the financial year ended Aug 31, 2026 (FY2026). Top Glove executive chairman Tan Sri Dr Lim Wee Chai said the group’s performance in FY2027 is expected to track global market demand growth of around 10%. "For FY2027 and ahead, we should be able to sustain and should be able to do better...the profit growth or sales growth should be about 10%, following the market growth," Lim said during the group's financial briefing following the release of its fourth-quarter results. "If we work harder and smarter, we should grow even better than 10% of the market growth rate…very likely that we will do better than FY2026," he added. Despite the optimistic outlook, the group faces operational headwinds from rising raw material costs, driven by persistent volatility in crude oil prices from the prolonged Iran war, and the hike in natural gas tariffs starting Oct 1. Top Glove joint managing director Ng Yong Lin said the 30% gas tariff hike is set to increase the group's cost per 1,000 pieces by 50 to 70 US cents (about RM2 to RM2.86), or 2% or 3%. However, the group was confident it could navigate these material cost pressures in FY2027 through disciplined cost and energy saving efforts. Ng said the group had reduced its energy consumption per 1,000 gloves by 30% to 35% compared to 2019 levels and expects automation and AI technology to cushion margins. To offset the rising raw material and gas expenses, the group is increasing average selling prices (ASPs) by US$2 to US$4 per 1,000 pieces for October and November. Currently, generic nitrile glove prices hover around US$21 to US$22 per 1,000 pieces. "So for the month of October, November, we have adjusted the glove selling price by about two to three dollars or even four dollars and that will be enough to cover other costs that increase," Lim said, adding that order books for October and November remain strong despite the price revisions. On competition from China glove manufacturers, Lim said the cost and pricing gap between Malaysian and Chinese makers has narrowed compared to three to four years ago. "The price difference for gloves sold from Malaysia compared to China used to have a big gap of about three to four dollars. Now, Malaysian manufacturers like us have improved our costing well. So our glove costing and selling prices are very close to theirs…there is not much difference anymore," Lim said. He added that attempts by some Chinese manufacturers to expand production into Southeast Asian nations such as Vietnam and Indonesia face operational challenges, including higher raw material import costs and reliance on Chinese expatriate staff, resulting in production costs increases of 10%. "Competition is there, but not as tough as two, three years ago," Lim said. For FY2026, the group's revenue grew 21% to RM4.23 billion from FY2025, supported by a 28% increase in sales volume. Net profit for the full year stood at RM308 million. Top Glove shares closed nine sen higher or 11.46% at 87.5 sen on Tuesday, giving the group a market capitalisation of RM7.2 billion. It was the second most active stock on Bursa Malaysia with 165.13 million shares changing hands. title: 'SLGC Mitigates Rising Construction Costs Through Value-engineering
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Construction firm service SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) said on Tuesday that it has undertaken value-engineering measures to cushion the impact of rising construction material costs amid geopolitical tensions. Value engineering is the process of adjusting a project with a client to achieve the same performance, while identifying alternatives to materials or specifications. “We have experienced construction material costs [having] increased recently, but we have managed this by proposing various value-engineering exercises to our clients,” its managing director Yong Zheng Lin told reporters after the company’s debut on Bursa Malaysia’s ACE Market on Tuesday. “For instance, we have suggested changes in specifications or brands to our clients as part of these exercises as a way for us to offset the rising cost,” he added. Construction costs have continued to rise in line with higher oil prices, exerting cost pressure on the group’s margins, though Yong did not indicate any specific figure for the percentage of costs increase. To mitigate the impact, the group said it is also negotiating with subcontractors and locking in material prices early with its suppliers. According to Yong, the group currently has a tender book of over RM1 billion, with an estimated success rate of 10% to 15%. As at Aug 12, the total unbilled contract value of its ongoing construction projects stood at RM1 billion, to be recognised progressively over the next five financial years until FY2030. On potential data centre contracts, Yong said: "We’re still exploring and discussing the opportunities but the group hasn't had any successful deal yet". For the financial year ended Dec 31, 2025 (FY2025), SLGC’s net profit dropped to RM13.99 million, compared with RM16.03 million a year earlier, but revenue rose to RM324 million from RM229.64 million. The group has two revenue segments, which residential segment contributed 74.95% out of total revenue for FY2025 and non-residential segment made up the remaining 25.05%. The company is mainly involved in design and building construction services for residential and non-residential works. SLGC’s customers include property developers and building owners in Malaysia. SLGC shares settled three sen or 10.7% lower at 25 sen on its maiden trading day on Tuesday, valuing the company at RM140 million. title: 'Rapidus Taps Four Malaysian Firms as Design Solution Associates for CORE Ecosystem
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Rapidus Corporation has roped in Malaysian firms — GreatAsic Technology Sdn Bhd, Infinecs Systems Sdn Bhd, Oppstar Bhd's (KL:OPPSTAR) Oppstar Technology Sdn Bhd and SkyeChip Bhd (KL:SKYECHIP) — as design solution associates to support the development of its global chip ecosystem framework. The Japan-backed Rapidus said it will establish the Rapidus Collaborative Open Rapid Ecosystem (CORE), a global ecosystem framework to support the development and mass production of cutting-edge semiconductors. As the first Rapidus CORE initiative, Rapidus said it is forming a group of design solution associates, which include 17 firms. "Today, semiconductor development requires more than just manufacturing technology; it is essential to integrate the entire semiconductor value chain — including research institutions, EDA (Electronic Design Automation), IP (intellectual property), design and manufacturing — to provide customers with a development and production infrastructure they can rely on. "Further, amid a global shortage of cutting-edge semiconductor talent, it is crucial to build a design ecosystem that enables customers to begin development at an early stage by collaborating with design-related companies," Rapidus said in a statement on Monday. The 17 firms include Malaysian companies, namely GreatAsic Technology, Infinecs Systems, Oppstar Technology, and SkyeChip. Other firms include Japan's Dai Nippon Printing, TOPPAN Inc, Toshiba Information Systems, MavissDesign, and NSW Inc and London-based AION Silicon. Also listed were Indian firms namely HCL Technologies Ltd, Infosys Ltd, Moschip Technologies ltd, and Wipro Ltd; US-based companies Cadence Design Systems and Synopsys, as well as Singapore's Quest Global Services. Design solution associates will serve as a bridge between customers and Rapidus, providing each company's design resources and specialised expertise to support the rapid evolution of semiconductor development. This will enable Rapidus to strengthen its support system — from design through manufacturing — to meet customer needs both in Japan and overseas. Moving forward, Rapidus will expand its CORE offerings beyond design to include EDA, IP and other categories. Rapidus is a Japanese state-backed semiconductor company founded in 2022 to mass-produce cutting-edge two-nanometer logic chips domestically by 2027. It was established through a partnership between the Japanese government and major private corporations, including Toyota, Sony, NTT, and SoftBank, to reduce Japan's reliance on foreign chipmakers like TSMC.
