title: 'Zetrix Says Still Finalising Amount Owed to JPJ After Loke Reveals RM314m Arrears
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314 million in unpaid remittances. It said this in a bourse filing on Tuesday following queries from Bursa Malaysia about several news reports by The Edge about the arrears, and the subsequent suspension of Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG Sdn Bhd as JPJ collection agents, which Zetrix confirmed. To Bursa's queries regarding the reasons for the suspension and the circumstances that led to it, Zetrix gave a similar answer: that it was due to delays in remittances to JPJ, and that the company is in the process of finalising the outstanding amount with JPJ. On steps taken to address the issue, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. As to how long the suspension would last, Zetrix said the suspension would remain in place until its discussions with JPJ, the Ministry of Transport and other relevant government authorities are completed. "The company anticipates that the temporary suspension will be lifted upon mutual agreement and acceptance of the proposed solution framework submitted by the company to the relevant authorities," it said. "The company is actively engaging with JPJ, the Ministry of Transport Malaysia and the relevant government authorities to finalise the outstanding matters and the proposed solution framework as expeditiously as possible, with a view to minimising operational downtime. The company will make further announcements once a formal timeline or resolution is confirmed," Zetrix added. On operational impact, the group flagged that the suspension will result in a temporary loss of revenue and profit contributions from JPJ services in the fourth quarter of its financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (4QFY2026), but did not give any estimates. The affected services include road tax and driving licence renewals, learner's driving licence applications, summons enquiries and payments, vehicle ownership transfers and the Malaysian Computerised Driving Theory Test. On Monday, Loke revealed that Zetrix owes JPJ RM314 million after failing to remit collections — which it was required to do daily, within one working day of each transaction — between May and September this year. This led to the ministry and JPJ holding four engagement sessions with the company and issuing 35 reminders for the arrears to be settled, to no avail, he said. The government subsequently suspended Zetrix and its subsidiary MyEG Sdn Bhd as JPJ collection agents. Loke also said Zetrix had issued the government a RM231 million cheque in September to settle the arrears, but the bank did not process it after the company instructed the bank to stop payment when the cheque was credited on Sept 30. The government will continue pursuing the arrears and could consider civil action, while Zetrix's JPJ services will not be restored until the outstanding amount is settled, Loke said. Even after payment, additional conditions would be imposed, including requiring collections to be credited directly into the government's account, he said. Zetrix, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, has provided online processing of JPJ services such as road tax and driving licence renewals since 2000, while its latest three-year contract began in May 2023. As of end-June, the company held RM541.6 million in cash and RM532.9 million in digital assets (cryptocurrencies), against RM2.19 billion in borrowings and RM90 million in trade payables, other payables and accruals. On Tuesday, Zetrix shares rebounded 2.5 sen or 38.5% to close at nine sen, valuing the company at RM727.1 million. The counter skidded to a 13-year low of 6.5 sen on Monday after its share price plunged 90% in just over a month following a sell-off at the counter that began at the end of August. The rout came amid reports that its largest shareholder Wong Thean Soon — better known as TS Wong — was facing forced selling. TS Wong's stake has since shrunk from 29% to 10%. title: 'Berjaya Says Core Berjaya Hills Businesses Unaffected by Pahang Enforcement Action
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Berjaya Corp Bhd (KL:BJCORP) said its main businesses at Berjaya Hills remain fully operational despite enforcement action by the Pahang authorities, and expects no material financial or operational impact from the issue. It said state authorities had sealed and restricted access to the staff quarters, central laundry, rabbit park and Japanese garden on Sept 28, while The Chateau Spa & Wellness Resort, Colmar Tropicale Hotel, Berjaya Hills Golf & Country Club and the greenhouses were unaffected. "The group's core operating facilities, including the hotels, golf club and greenhouses remain unaffected and continue to operate as usual," Berjaya Corp said in a bourse filing Tuesday. The disclosure was made in response to Bursa Malaysia's queries seeking details of the enforcement action — linked to a long-running dispute between Berjaya Hills Resort Bhd and the Pahang government over a sharp increase in quit rent imposed on the company's properties in the state — and how it would financially and operationally affect the group. Berjaya Hills claimed its annual quit rent jumped 13-fold to RM33.7 million in 2020 from about RM2.4 million in 2019, before being reduced to RM25.75 million following 11 appeals to the state government between April 2020 and December 2022. The company said it paid about RM42.65 million in quit rent and penalties "under protest" between 2020 and 2026, while continuing to seek a further review of the rates. In Tuesday's filing, Berjaya Corp said the higher quit rent expenses had been recognised through accruals for the respective financial years since the revised rates took effect in 2020. "Accordingly, the impact arising from the revised annual quit rent rates has been taken into account in the group's financial statements for the respective financial years and the revised rates have no material operational impact to the group," it added. Separately on Tuesday, Pahang Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Wan Rosdy Wan Ismail said the state government is open to discussions with Berjaya Hills to resolve the impasse, but stressed that any talks must be guided by existing legal provisions and regulations. "That is up to them (Berjaya Hills). We are taking actions based on the law. The state government is open to discussions, but they must be based on and guided by the law. There are regulations, so follow the rules," Wan Rosdy was quoted as saying by Bernama. Berjaya Hills had on Oct 2 called the enforcement action "unconscionable and totally unacceptable", arguing that it was unreasonable given that its application for leave to appeal the quit rent dispute remains pending before the Federal Court. Nevertheless, it also said it hoped the Pahang government would continue to engage with the company towards a "mutually acceptable and amicable resolution". The company, which has been challenging the revised quit rent through legal means with no success so far, first sought a judicial review at the Temerloh High Court. The application was dismissed in May 2024 on grounds that the court could not intervene in the state government's policy decision. That decision was upheld by the Court of Appeal on July 16 this year. This led to Berjaya Hills applying for leave to appeal to the Federal Court on Aug 14, with the hearing scheduled for Dec 8. Berjaya Corp closed unchanged at 25 sen on Tuesday for a market capitalisation of RM1.52 billion. title: 'Hannah: 88 More Open-space Lots Gazetted in KL, Bringing Total to 582
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): A total of 88 open-space lots in the federal capital have been gazetted in the first nine months of this year, bringing the number of legally protected lots to 582, covering 476.17 hectares. Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Federal Territories) Hannah Yeoh said the latest gazettement involved 26 lots covering 7.33 hectares, equivalent to about 10 football fields. “The gazettement provides clearer legal protection for open spaces and helps ensure they are preserved for public benefit. “Open spaces also play an important role in the urban environment by helping to absorb rainwater runoff, reduce the effects of urban heat and provide recreational areas for the community,” she said in a Facebook post on Tuesday. Hannah said the latest 26 lots were located across eight parliamentary constituencies: Bandar Tun Razak (six lots), Segambut (five), Seputeh and Cheras (four each), Wangsa Maju, Lembah Pantai and Batu (two each), and Setiawangsa (one). In Bandar Tun Razak, the areas are Alam Damai, Taman Damai Jaya and Taman Connaught, while in Segambut, they include Taman Segambut Indah, Taman Tun Dr Ismail, Taman Sri Hartamas, Taman Sri Kuching and Taman Sri Bintang. In Seputeh, the lots are in Taman LTAT, Taman Shanghai, Bandar Bukit Jalil and Taman Esplanad, while Cheras involves Taman Midah, Taman Connaught and Taman Bukit Ria. The other areas are: Taman Desa Melawati and Taman Setapak (Wangsa Maju); Bukit Persekutuan/Jalan Travers (Lembah Pantai); Taman Kok Lian (Batu); and Taman Keramat AU3 (Setiawangsa). The public can check the list, gazettement status and locations of all 582 open spaces via the MyHijau link on the official Federal Territories Land and Mines Office (PPTGWP) website at www.ptgwp.gov.my. The facility allows Kuala Lumpur residents and residents’ associations to check the status of open spaces in their neighbourhoods and help monitor and preserve them. title: 'BNM: Banks Working Towards Fraud Alert Before Transaction Is Completed
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Malaysian banks are working towards introducing fraud alert capabilities that can flag potential risks before a transaction is completed. A pilot test involving selected banks is targeted for the first half of 2027 ahead of wider implementation, Bank Negara Malaysia governor Datuk Seri Abdul Rasheed Ghaffour said in his speech text for a conference on financial crime and counter terrorism financing on Tuesday. “These alerts will prompt customers to pause, think and verify before proceeding,” he said. Fraudulent transactions and scams are a major problem globally. In Malaysia, the financial sector has prevented some RM1.9 billion in attempted fraudulent transactions, surpassing the RM1.2 billion prevented during the whole of 2025, according to the central bank’s data. More than 1,600 suspicious accounts, many of which were subsequently assessed as presenting mule-related risks, were flagged to-date by Malaysia’s digital payment backbone PayNet. The planned fraud alerts may introduce “additional friction for customers,” Abdul Rasheed acknowledged. “However, these measures are necessary to strike an appropriate balance between offering convenience and protecting customers from fraud, particularly authorised scams,” he stressed. title: 'World Bank Supports Malaysia’s Possible Integration of GST Elements Into SST
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): The World Bank has agreed that certain elements of the goods and services tax (GST) should be implemented into Malaysia’s sales and service tax (SST) to address its distortionary features. World Bank lead economist for Malaysia Apurva Sanghi said the government should address the SST’s nature as a cascading tax and, in turn, an embedded tax. The SST is a single-stage tax with no input credit mechanism. In other words, tax can become embedded in prices as goods and services move through the supply chain. “We believe what is required is neutral tax reform that relieves cascading and embedded effects on businesses, for example through input tax credits, while also broadening the tax base to bolster revenues," he said during a briefing on the October 2026 Malaysia Economic Monitor report. There has been much industry and policy discussion on what an integration of GST elements into the SST, or a formulation of a better SST, could look like. Discourse began after Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim announced the government is studying improvements to the existing SST, including whether it can incorporate elements of the GST, following a Budget 2027 engagement session in August. Malaysia implemented the GST in 2015 at a 6% rate under the administration of Datuk Seri Najib Razak. The implementation led to soaring inflation and widespread complaints of slow tax refunds that created a cash crunch for small- to medium-sized businesses. The tax was suspended on June 1, 2018, after Pakatan Harapan took over the federal government, and was subsequently abolished and replaced with the current SST on Sept 1, 2018. While Apurva agreed the SST can be improved if the cascading tax aspect is addressed, he did note the World Bank has held the view that the GST is a better solution, should its regressivity be offset with cash transfers to those vulnerable. “Trying to integrate GST elements with SST, I think of it as trying to integrate efficiency with empathy. “And, when you fuse both together, the risk is you may get neither,” he warned. GST, all being equal, is favourable to SST, Apurva noted. He said GST avoids cascading and embedded tax. “One of the stumbling blocks of GST 1.0, the previous GST regime, was the delay in issuing refunds. If that is addressed, then that definitely is yet another argument to think about GST,” he said. World Bank economist Deisigan Shammugam also highlighted that it has been a decade since then and that technology has improved since then. title: 'CIMB Considers Selling Philippine Business — Bloomberg
body: '(Oct 6): CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people, asking not to be identified because the process is private. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200 million (RM817 million), the people said. Deliberations are ongoing and CIMB may still decide not to sell, they said. A representative for CIMB didn’t respond to requests for comment. CIMB entered the Philippines in December 2018, and by September 2025 had 10 million customers, according to its website. CIMB also has a presence in Indonesia, Singapore, Thailand, Cambodia and Vietnam, as well as some operations in China, Hong Kong and the UK. The group said in August that its overall net income was RM1.94 billion in the second quarter, and that it’s continuing to “reallocate capital away from underperforming businesses”. CIMB announced in May that it was selling its automotive financing portfolio in Thailand. CIMB’s shares hit a 15-year high in January but have fallen 14% since, giving it a market value of about US$20.4 billion. title: 'Zetrix AI's Business Continuity Uncertain After JPJ Suspension — MBSB Research
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) faces uncertainty over its revenue collection business after the Ministry of Transport (MOT) suspended its services as a collection agent for the Road Transport Department (JPJ) over unremitted government funds totalling RM314 million. MBSB Research said that even if Zetrix AI has a proposal to resolve the outstanding remittances, financial liquidity poses an additional hurdle for the group. It noted that Zetrix AI reported cash and cash equivalents of RM541.6 million in the second quarter ended June 30, 2026 (2QFY2026), its short-term loans and borrowings stand higher at RM853.1 million, raising concerns over its ability to make immediate settlement payments. "Thus, we do not discount the possibility that Zetrix AI may have difficulties in making the payment in the near term," said MBSB Research in a note on Tuesday. Even if Zetrix AI manages to clear its arrears, the resumption of its collection agent role is not guaranteed, the research house said. "Potentially, should the group manage to resume the JPJ services, there may be changes in standard operating procedure (SOP) whereby the government revenue would need to be credited immediately. "This would prevent similar incidents from occurring. The group announced that it has submitted a proposal to resolve outstanding remittances and is working towards restoring the affected services, subject to the relevant approvals," it added. Furthermore, MOT’s active promotion of its proprietary MyJPJ application, alongside existing channels such as JPJ counters, kiosks, and the JPJ Public Portal, could diminish the long-term necessity for third-party collection agents. Such operational risks have prompted MBSB Research to place its recommendation and target price on the stock under review. The research house noted that despite four engagement sessions held since May with key stakeholders — including the Ministry of Finance — and 35 reminder notices issued by JPJ, the outstanding arrears remain unsettled. Consequently, MOT and JPJ are preparing to initiate legal proceedings to recover the unremitted funds. Meanwhile, MARC Ratings recently revised its MARCWatch status on Zetrix AI to “negative” from “developing”. MARC cited heightened concerns over corporate governance, transparency, and a lack of material information regarding a sharp rise in borrowings, alongside the recent resignation of the company’s external auditor, TGS TW PLT, due to portfolio rationalisation and resource management. MBSB Research is keeping its earnings forecasts unchanged for now, pending further developments. Non-AI and non-blockchain segments currently account for approximately 40% of the group’s total revenue. title: 'World Bank Urges Malaysia to Adjust SME Tax Structure in Budget 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Malaysia could simplify the income tax structure for smaller businesses by consolidating its current multiple rate structure into a consolidated single corporate tax rate, the World Bank said. The government could also consider phasing out the preferential treatment once firms grow beyond the threshold of small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs), Apurva Sanghi, lead economist for Malaysia at the World Bank, said during a briefing on Tuesday. “Changing the incentive structure that otherwise incentivises firms from graduating from SME status can help,” he said, suggesting that the government make the tax system more supportive for investment. In Malaysia, an SME in manufacturing is defined as having sales turnover not exceeding RM50 million or no more than 200 full-time employees. For services and other sectors, it's sales turnover must be not exceeding RM20 million or no more than 75 employees. The World Bank has provided its input to the Ministry of Finance on the drafting of the budget, like many other organisations. The multilateral institution would like to see tax measures in the upcoming Budget 2027 to address Malaysia’s low tax revenue as a share of the size of its economy, Apurva said. While 2027 is an election year, there are still ways to increase tax revenue without increasing tax rates, he noted. Apurva suggested lowering the current high thresholds at which higher marginal personal income tax applies, or placing clearer limits on personal income tax relief and deductions, particularly at the upper end of the income distribution. “Without going into details, I think it's a pretty reasonably well-known fact” that the T20, or the top 20% of the income earners, “capture the bulk of benefits of reliefs that are given by the government,” he added. title: 'Mesiniaga Wins Two-year RM32.3m Contract Extension From Customs Dept
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MYGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. According to the company’s bourse filing on Tuesday, the agreement does not include an automatic renewal clause. The MyGST system is the Customs Department's legacy online system for administering goods and services tax (GST), which was Malaysia's broad-based consumption tax from April 2015 until its abolition in September 2018. Malaysia's current sales and service tax (SST) system is administered through MySST, but MyGST system remains in operation as the agency maintains it to support other tax administrative matters, fulfil statutory/legal requirements and work procedures. Mesiniaga said the contract is expected to contribute positively to the group’s earnings and net assets for the financial year ending Dec 31, 2026 (FY2026) and subsequent periods until completion. For the first half of FY2026, Mesiniaga’s net loss narrowed to RM0.95 million from RM2.13 million in the previous period, while revenue was up by 22.4% to RM113.2 million. The group said it saw higher revenue from projects and services deliveries. Shares of Mesiniaga were down by one sen or 0.9% to RM1.16 at market close on Tuesday, giving the group a market value of RM70.1 million. body: 'The FBM KLCI rose 0.1% to 1,633 points on Tuesday due to positive regional sentiment, tracking gains across major Asian markets after Wall Street's tech-led rally overnight, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to cap risk appetite. Health Technology (+6.3%), Producer Manufacturing (+1.8%) and Health Services (+1.7%) led sectoral gains, driven by Nestle (+1.3%), Kuala Lumpur Kepong (+0.5%) and Petronas Chemicals (+0.2%). Market breadth was positive, with 664 gainers ahead of 450 losers, while 560 counters closed unchanged. Asian markets closed mixed on Tuesday as most bourses tracked Wall Street's tech-led rally, with Japan further supported by a strong government bond auction that eased yield concerns, while South Korea fell as chip heavyweights came under selling pressure amid worries over elevated bond yields. Japan's Nikkei 225 led regional gains (+1.1%), followed by Hong Kong's Hang Seng (+1.0%) and Taiwan's TAIEX (+0.2%), while South Korea's KOSPI fell 0.9%. Mainland China markets remained closed for the National Day holiday and will resume trading on Thursday. In South Korea, NonEnergy Minerals (-2.7%), Process Industries (-2.0%) and Producer Manufacturing (-1.8%) were the sectoral laggards, dragged by DH Autonex, Exicure Hitron and SG Global. In China, in their last trading sessions, the sectoral gains were led by Health Care (+2.9%), Consumer Staples (+1.7%) and Financials (+1.0%), with CanSino Biologics, Shanghai Model Organisms and Suzhou Novoprotein Scientific as the top performers. European stocks closed firmly higher Tuesday, led by banks, consumer discretionary and autos as sovereign yields' surge paused. Euro STOXX 50 and STOXX Europe 600 each added 0.5%, to 6,272 and 636. Long-dated euroarea yields mostly fell, especially in higher-debt economies, easing ECB antifragmentation intervention fears. Banks tracked rebounding credit: BNP Paribas jumped 2.5%; UniCredit, Santander and Deutsche Bank rose 1.5% each. Intesa Sanpaolo rebounded 1.3% as markets reassessed a potential Banca MPS acquisition's return impact. Schneider Electric sank 4.5% after agreeing to buy US software firm PTC for $22.6 billion. US stocks closed higher Tuesday, supported by heavyweight tech as surging bond yields paused, easing pressure on its credit outlook. The S&P 500 (+0.6%) and Nasdaq 100 (+0.5%) hit record highs, while the Dow gained 253 points. AI infrastructure and hyperscaler stocks mostly rose as fresh sector deals spurred speculative demand. OpenAI discussed $30 billion financing with UAE funds; Alphabet gained 0.3% before acquiring nuclear capacity from Constellation Energy (+12.2%). AMD jumped 2.8% as CEO Lisa Su signalled strong chip demand ahead. Microsoft rose 0.8%, Amazon 1.9% and Nvidia 0.1%. IMF: Cost-of-living crises have lasting impact on inflation expectations, poverty, IMF says 5.33% on Monday Sharp spikes in food and energy prices will likely become more common, the International Monetary Fund said, warning such crises drive inflation expectations higher for longer, worsen poverty and threaten economic stability. IMF research released on Tuesday examined three decades of strategies used by governments to mitigate price surges, as well as a new economic model that accounts for the higher inflation experienced by poorer households, which spend a higher share of their budgets on daily necessities. (Reuters) US: Oil Rises as Mideast Risks Remain 5.33% on Monday Crude oil climbed toward $90 per barrel on Wednesday, recovering from five-week lows as persistent risks to Middle East energy flows overshadowed signs of rising supply from the region. Iran has intensified attacks on tankers in the Strait of Hormuz in recent days, with the UK Maritime Trade Operations reporting nine incidents so far this month. (Trading Economics) US: Trade deficit widens in August amid strong imports 5.33% on Monday The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August, driven by a surge in imports of goods amid robust domestic demand, keeping trade on track to again subtract from economic growth in the third quarter. The trade shortfall increased 13.7% to US$105.6 billion (RM431.5 billion), the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis and Census Bureau said on Tuesday. (Trading Economics) US: 10-Year Treasury Yield Softens from 24-Year High The yield on the 10-year US Treasury note was at 5.26% on Tuesday, pausing a surge that peaked at a 24-year high of 5.33% touched yesterday, tracking the momentary dip in wholesale fuel prices. Oil bids were tamed by signs that some laden tankers passed through the Strait of Hormuz. The 10-year yield has surged over 110bps this year as risks of higher rates from the Federal Reserve, soaring federal deficit spending, and increasing corporate debt supply triggered a plunge in demand for duration. (Trading Economics) US: Logistics Growth 2nd-Highest in 4 Years The US Logistics Managers’ Index increased to 70.2 in September 2026 from 66.6 in August. It is the second-highest reading in four years, behind only June’s reading of 71.1. A faster increase was seen for Inventory Levels (58.9 vs 52.8) and Inventory Costs (79.9 vs 78.6) which is also having a significant effect on the warehousing market. Warehousing Capacity shrank the most since March 2022 (39.3 vs 53.5), potentially due to the fact that firms, particularly retailers, had run inventory down a bit and are not rushing goods in now ahead of potential holiday sales. Spot gold rose 0.4% to US$4,155.34 (RM16,977.89) per ounce by 10.09am EDT (1409 GMT). US gold futures for December delivery added 0.6% to US$4,182.30. title: 'Mplus Market Pulse - 07 Oct 2026
body: 'MY: Tracking positive regional performance, the local bourse continued to trade higher ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement. Market breadth turned positive, with 667 gainers against 456 losers. Sector-wise, both Technology and Healthcare outperformed with gains exceeding 3%, while Financial Services lagged the most. US: Wall Street logged solid gains with the Dow rising 0.5%, the S&P 500 gaining 0.6% to reach new record highs, and the Nasdaq jumping 0.5% higher as US 10-year Treasury yields slipped to 5.3%, while Brent crude hovered at USD100/bbl amid potential Strait of Hormuz supply disruptions. US: Wall Street may retain its constructive tone after the S&P 500 and Nasdaq reached fresh record highs, helped by easing Treasury yields and stabilising oil prices. AI remains a key earnings driver, with Marvell (MRVL) in focus after raising its FY2028 revenue target to USD20.0bn and guiding FY2031 revenue to USD70.0- 90.0bn, underpinned by strong demand for custom AI silicon and optical connectivity. Meanwhile, Salesforce (CRM) could benefit from renewed strength in enterprise software as concerns over AI disruption ease, while Meta (META) continues expanding its AI offerings to businesses through its Meta Enterprise Platform. MY: On the local front, the FBMKLCI is poised to track global tech strength, with sentiment supported by robust earnings and positioning ahead of Budget 2027 on 9 October. The semiconductor and automation space could remain in focus, with semiconductors, AI and high-value investments among the Government's key priorities. UWC stands out after 4QFY26 revenue jumped 71.1% to RM186.2m, while net profit surged 129.7%, reflecting stronger semiconductor demand and project execution. VITROX could also attract interest following a sharp improvement in 2QFY26 earnings. Meanwhile, TOPGLOV offers an earnings-driven play after 4QFY26 revenue rose 39.7% to RM1.25bn, with net profit surging 352.6%. Selective buying provided a minor lift to the local bourse on Tuesday, though the benchmark remains capped under key moving averages. Downside risk persists as the MACD histogram stays below zero while the RSI is oversold below 30. Key resistance is pegged at 1,648-1,663, while support is expected around 1,603-1,618. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200m (RM817m). (The Edge) Zetrix AI Bhd (ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314m in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. (The Edge) Top Glove Corporation Bhd (TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78bn pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72bn in FY2026. The group's net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63m in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83m in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25bn. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15. For the full FY2026, Top Glove's net profit nearly tripled to RM307.96m. Revenue increased 21% to RM4.23bn as volume grew close to 30%. (The Edge) Samaiden Group Bhd (SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99- megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238m. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. (The Edge) Mesiniaga Bhd (MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3m contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider's earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. (The Edge) Scientex Bhd (SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580m to boost the property developer's land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. (The Edge) Dialog Group Bhd (DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand's 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. (The Edge) Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (ELRIDGE) is investing RM45m to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45m in cash. (The Edge) Insights Analytics Bhd (IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44m subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. (The Edge) Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm's shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intra-day low of 24 sen as more than 83m shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140m. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. (The Edge) ZenaTech, Inc. (ZENA) advanced its ZenaDrone 2000 heavy-lift autonomous interceptor through prototype assembly in Sharjah, UAE, targeting Q1 2027 flight testing. Built with a 40 kg payload capacity and four-plus hours of hover endurance, the gasoline-powered platform will validate autonomous navigation and multi-target threat pursuit alongside its Interceptor P-1 system. (Investing.com) ONEOK, Inc. (OKE) completed its acquisition of Brazos Midstream's Permian Midland Basin natural gas gathering and processing assets for approximately USD 4.425 billion in cash. The transaction more than doubles ONEOK's Midland Basin processing capacity to roughly 2.3 billion cubic feet per day and adds 600,000 dedicated acres backed by long-term fixed-fee contracts averaging over 12 years. title: 'FBM KLCI Slips At Open As Budget 2027 Looms
body: 'The FBM KLCI opened slightly lower on Wednesday as investors remained cautious ahead of the tabling of Budget 2027, with the market continuing to search for fresh catalysts.  At 9.05am, the benchmark index fell 3.22 points to 1,630.13, remaining rangebound amid continued uncertainty.  Apex Securities said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 could provide some support to the local market, although a stronger recovery would likely require fresh foreign fund inflows and clearer direction on bond yields and geopolitical developments.  “We stay cautious on the local bourse this week, as easing crude oil prices and Budget 2027 expectations may offer some support, but a stronger recovery will likely require fresh catalysts such as foreign fund inflows and clearer direction on bond yields and geopolitical developments,” it said in a note.  The research firm also remained cautious on near-term global risk appetite, noting that the current rally was narrowly led by technology stocks while bond yields remained near multi-decade highs.  It said equities could remain vulnerable if the US Federal Reserve adopts a more hawkish tone.  Banking counters were among the early decliners, with CIMB falling seven sen to RM7.63 and Hong Leong Bank losing eight sen to RM22.  Press Metal shed six sen to RM7.13.  Among actively traded stocks, Metronic was unchanged at 0.5 sen and Zetrix AI remained at nine sen, while Top Glove jumped five sen to 92.5 sen.  Glove makers also gained amid renewed optimism in the sector, with Supermax rising two sen to 48 sen, Hartalega adding five sen to RM1.17 and Kossan gaining two sen to RM1.27.

title: 'PublicInvest Research Headlines - 7 Oct 2026
body: 'US: Trade deficit widens as imports hit record high. The US trade deficit widened more than expected in August as strong domestic demand drove imports to an all-time high, suggesting trade could again weigh on third-quarter economic growth despite higher tariffs. The deficit increased 13.7% to USD105.6bn, the largest since March 2025, compared with economists' expectations of USD102.0bn. (Reuters) EU: High yields may dampen energy inflation pass-through, ECB's Rehn says. Rapid energy inflation in the euro zone has yet to spread significantly into other goods and services, while higher bond yields could restrain growth and reduce the transmission of energy costs into broader prices and wages, ECB policymaker Olli Rehn said. Euro-zone inflation remains well above the ECB's 2% target, but policymakers are weighing persistent energy-driven price pressures against tighter financial conditions. Long-term yields have risen to more than decade highs amid higher US yields and European debt concerns. Financial markets currently price another two to three ECB rate increases during the tightening cycle, including around an 80% probability of a move by December. (Reuters) UK: High inflation has become embedded, BoE's Mann says. Inflation above the BoE's 2% target appears to have become embedded in the UK economy and could become further entrenched through wage negotiations early next year, BoE policymaker Catherine Mann said. Unlike the Fed and ECB, the BoE has kept rates unchanged since the outbreak of the Iran war, although markets now expect a rate increase in November. Mann highlighted the risk of inflation reaching around 4% near year-end, coinciding with the period when many employers negotiate annual pay increases. She said demand remained positive but not particularly strong, while businesses were adapting to elevated energy costs. (Reuters) China: Zinc exports surge as weak domestic demand leaves excess supply. China is on course to become a net exporter of refined zinc this year as soft domestic construction demand coincides with tight supply conditions in Western markets. Zinc exports jumped to 40,668 tonnes in August, the second-highest monthly level in almost two decades, while China recorded net exports of 4,388 tonnes during the first eight months of the year. Muted construction activity has weakened demand for galvanised steel, leaving Shanghai zinc inventories elevated, while an arbitrage opportunity created by tight London Metal Exchange supply has encouraged Chinese exports. (Reuters) Japan: BOJ signals readiness for further rate hikes to anchor inflation. BOJ Governor Kazuo Ueda said it was becoming increasingly important to anchor underlying inflation around the central bank's 2% target, signalling readiness to continue raising interest rates to prevent inflation from overshooting. Economic and price developments remain broadly consistent with BOJ forecasts, while the Tankan survey points to solid business sentiment. Rising raw-material costs are feeding into wholesale and consumer inflation, while long-term inflation expectations continue to rise. Ueda also cited risks from the Iran war, strong AI-related demand and a weak yen, adding that financial conditions remain accommodative even after September's rate increase. (Reuters) India: Markets price RBI hike, with risk of larger move. The RBI could tighten monetary policy more aggressively than expected as policymakers face broadening price pressures and sharply higher global bond yields. The one-month overnight indexed swap was around 5.55%, about 30bps above the current 5.25% repo rate, implying a 25bps hike is fully priced in while leaving some probability of a 50bps increase. Most economists polled by Reuters expect a 25bps hike, which would be the RBI's first rate increase since early 2023. Bankers estimate markets may be assigning roughly a 25% probability to a larger move.(Reuters) CIMB (Outperform, TP: RM8.70): Considers selling Philippine business. CIMB Group Holdings is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. (Bloomberg) Comments: According to Bloomberg, the deal could value the business at USD200m. While historically CIMB Philippine's contribution to the group is minimal and has swung into losses in 2025, we think that the potential sale is in-line with the group's strategy to redeploy capital into higher-return segments, which could potentially support ROE expansion. We maintain our Outperform call with an unchanged TP of RM8.70. Dialog (Neutral, TP: RM2.10): JV bags onshore O&G concession in Thailand. Dialog Group said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. (The Edge) Comments: We view the L8/66 concession award positively, given its proximity to Dialog's producing L53/48 fields and the ability to leverage existing facilities and operating expertise to optimise development costs. The USD14.3m minimum work commitment over six years provides measured exposure to potential reserve and production growth, with management indicating a low-to-mid-teens projected IRR. However, we leave our earnings forecasts unchanged as the project remains at a preliminary stage. We maintain our Neutral call with an unchanged TP of RM2.10. Zetrix: Says still finalising amount owed to JPJ after Loke reveals RM314m arrears. Zetrix AI said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314m in unpaid remittances. (The Edge) Samaiden: Reveals RM238m contract value for LSS5+ solar project. Samaiden Group said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238m. Samaiden's had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay SB (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation. (The Edge) Mesiniaga: Wins two-year RM32.3m contract extension from Customs Dept. Mesiniaga has won a RM32.3m contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider's earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in Nov 2023. (The Edge) OCK: Taps Phu Quoc infrastructure opportunities. OCK Group has signed a tripartite in-principle agreement with Southern Star Telecommunication Equipment Joint Stock Company (SPN), a subsidiary of JTOWER, and Sun Phu Quoc, a subsidiary of Sun Group, to deploy telecommunications infrastructure across designated Sun Group projects in Phu Quoc. (StarBiz) The KLCI might open stronger today as the S&P 500 climbed 0.6% Tuesday to a record after topping its prior all-time high set in August. Despite worries about everything from war to high inflation to pressure from the bond market, the index at the heart of many 401(k) accounts has soared 23% since hitting a bottom in late March. The Dow Jones Industrial Average added 253 points, or 0.5%, while the Nasdaq composite tacked 0.4% onto its own all-time high set the day before. The record-high stock prices are helping investors feel better about their finances, or at least less bad, when Americans are generally feeling discouraged about keeping up with the fast-rising cost of living. Many of the fears that sent the US stock market to its bottom in March have indeed come true. Oil prices are high because of the war with Iran, which has made inflation worse. Yields have cranked higher in the bond market, which threatens to slow the economy by making it more expensive for everyone to borrow money. And Americans broadly say they're feeling more pessimistic about the economy and where it's heading. But one vital source of support has remained resolute for the US stock market throughout: the relentless ability for companies to make more money. AI stocks have been a huge force driving the US market to records, including Nvidia's 28.3% surge so far this year. That's roughly double the broad market's gain. Constellation Energy jumped 12.2% for one of Tuesday's biggest gains in the S&P 500 because it's also riding that rising tide. Bond yields offered some slack on Tuesday after falling back from their highest levels in years or even decades. The yield on the 10-year Treasury, which is the focal point of the US bond market, eased to 5.28% from 5.31% late Monday. It fell after oil prices steadied themselves somewhat. The price for a barrel of Brent crude oil, the international standard, dropped to roughly $97 in the morning before pulling back to settle at $100.58. While that was up 0.3% from Monday's settlement price, it's still below the nearly $110 it was at a few weeks ago. In stock markets abroad, indices ticked higher in Europe as yields continue to swing in their bond markets amid concerns about high government debts and tight budgets. In France, tens of thousands of demonstrators marched in support of protests by students demanding more funding for schools. In Asia, Japan's Nikkei 225 jumped 1.1%, and Hong Kong's Hang Seng climbed 1%, but South Korea's Kospi dropped 0.9%. Back home, the KLCI added 1.6 points or 0.1% to 1,633.35. body: 'CIMB, Zetrix AI, Top Glove, Samaiden, Mesiniaga, Scientex, Dialog, Elridge Energy, Insights Analytics, SLGC KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 7): Here is a brief recap of some business news and corporate announcements that made the headlines on Tuesday: CIMB Group Holdings Bhd (KL:CIMB) is exploring a sale of its business in the Philippines as part of efforts to streamline and focus on bigger markets for growth, according to people with knowledge of the matter. The Malaysian lender is working with a financial adviser on the potential divestment and has reached out to prospective buyers to gauge interest, said the people. A deal could value the business at as much as US$200 million (RM817 million). — CIMB considers selling Philippine business — Bloomberg Zetrix AI Bhd (KL:ZETRIX) said the exact amount it owes the Road Transport Department (JPJ) is still being finalised between the two parties, a day after Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook said the company had accumulated RM314 million in unpaid remittances. In response to queries from Bursa Malaysia, the group reiterated that it had submitted a payment proposal to settle the arrears, and that the final sum and settlement terms remain subject to further discussions and formal agreement with authorities. — Zetrix says still finalising amount owed to JPJ after Loke reveals RM314m arrears Top Glove Corporation Bhd (KL:TOPGLOV) said labour shortage remains a primary constraint in scaling up production as it seeks to capture rising global demand following its best year since 2021. The group is targeting to raise annual running capacity by 8% to 78 billion pieces in the financial year ending Aug 31, 2027 (FY2027), from 72 billion in FY2026. The group’s net profit jumped nearly five times to RM157.63 million in the three months ended Aug 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) from RM34.83 million in the same quarter a year earlier. Revenue for the quarter surged 40% year-on-year to RM1.25 billion. A final dividend of 1.50 sen per share was also declared for FY2026 and payable on Dec 15. For the full FY2026, Top Glove’s net profit nearly tripled to RM307.96 million. Revenue increased 21% to RM4.23 billion as volume grew close to 30%. — Top Glove eyes higher output but says manpower remains key hurdle;Top Glove says ready for storms ahead as 4Q net profit jumps nearly five times Samaiden Group Bhd (KL:SAMAIDEN) said its contracts to undertake works for a 99.99-megawatt (MW) Large Scale Solar 5+ (LSS5+) project are worth RM238 million. Samaiden's wholly-owned subsidiary Samaiden Sdn Bhd had on Oct 2 entered into a works contract and a contract for the supply of solar components with Syarikat Pembenaan Yeoh Tiong Lay Sdn Bhd (YTL Construction), the construction unit of YTL Corporation Bhd (KL:YTL). The project is among the LSS5+ projects approved by the Energy Commission in September 2025. — Samaiden reveals RM238 mil contract value for LSS5+ solar project Mesiniaga Bhd (KL:MSNIAGA) has won a RM32.3 million contract from the Royal Malaysian Customs Department (RMDC) for the maintenance and licence renewal of its MyGST System. The contract marks a continuation of the information technology product and service provider’s earlier MyGST system agreement with RMCD that first started in November 2023. The new extension, which takes effect from Oct 16, 2026, will run until Oct 15, 2028. — Mesiniaga wins two-year RM32.3m contract extension from Customs Dept Scientex Bhd (KL:SCIENTX) is acquiring 503 acres in Pulai, Johor, for RM580 million to boost the property developer’s land bank. The plan is to turn the 14 plots of land currently owned by the Lau family of Leong Hup International Bhd (KL:LHI) into mixed development, the company said. However, it is too early to determine development value and other details, it noted. — Scientex to acquire 503 acres in Johor for RM580 mil Dialog Group Bhd (KL:DIALOG) said its 50.01%-owned joint venture company has been awarded concession rights and operatorship for the L8/66 exploration block onshore Thailand. The joint venture company, Pan Orient Energy (Siam) Ltd (POES), was notified by the Thai government on Oct 5 that it had been awarded the concession following a joint bid with CanAsia Energy Corp in Thailand’s 25th Onshore Bid Round. POES will operate the concession with a 70% participating interest, while Canada-listed CanAsia will hold the remaining 30% non-operating interest. — Dialog JV bags onshore O&G concession in Thailand Elridge Energy Holdings Bhd (KL:ELRIDGE) is investing RM45 million to venture into the manufacturing and sale of activated carbon business for use across water treatment, industrial purification and related filtration. This marks Elridge's move further downstream from its existing palm kernel shell biomass operations. Elridge said its wholly-owned subsidiary Lumeria Power Sdn Bhd (LP) had accepted a quotation from United Equipment Services (M) Sdn Bhd for the acquisition, installation and commissioning of six integrated activated carbon production chains for RM45 million in cash. — Elridge Energy invests RM45m to venture into activated carbon business Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB), which mainly provides asset management systems to water utilities, has secured a RM14.44 million subcontract to construct a water treatment plant in Sarawak's Miri division. The contract involves the construction, operation and maintenance of the Suai water treatment plant, which will have a capacity of seven million litres per day, as part of a project aimed at addressing acute water supply shortages in the Suai area. The construction is scheduled to begin on Oct 13 and to be completed by April 10, 2027, followed by a 60-month operation and maintenance period. — Insights Analytics secures contract for Suai water treatment plant in Miri Building construction contractor SLGC Bhd (KL:SLG) ended its first trading day on the ACE Market below its initial public offering (IPO) price. The construction firm’s shares closed at 25 sen on Tuesday, three sen or 10.71% lower than the IPO price of 28 sen per share, after hitting an intra-day low of 24 sen as more than 83 million shares exchanged hands. At the closing price, the company based in Johor had a market capitalisation of RM140 million. Ahead of the listing, SLGC shares were oversubscribed by just over three times by retail investors, while a portion of the IPO was undersubscribed and had to be reallocated to other investors. — Construction firm SLGC ends first trading day below IPO price The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'A trader’s guide to navigating Budget 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia’s consumer and construction stocks may emerge as beneficiaries of next year’s spending plan as Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim seeks to ease living costs while maintaining fiscal prudence. Anwar, who also serves as finance minister, is expected to announce measures to support households and sustain infrastructure spending when he unveils the annual budget on Friday. Investors will also be on watch for any update on a potential minimum-wage revision, which may boost consumption but add to earnings risk for companies. While Malaysia’s economy remains resilient, a renewed climb in oil prices is driving up fuel-subsidy costs, potentially weighing on the fiscal outlook and investor confidence. The spending plan ahead of a national election due early 2028 comes as Anwar seeks to rebuild public support following recent state poll setbacks. “Given the proximity to the 16th general election or GE16, this will be a people’s budget,” said Alexander Chia, analyst at RHB Research. “Social protection initiatives targeted at the lower and mid-income groups will be positive for the consumer, property, transport and healthcare sectors.” The country’s stock benchmark has fallen nearly 3% this year, lagging some South-East Asian peers including Thailand and Vietnam, as fiscal and political risks weigh. Moreover, foreign funds have sold US$1.59bil of local shares on a net basis so far in 2026. Several key areas warrant close attention in the Budget 2027 announcement. Budget 2027 is poised to include targeted assistance and measures to boost wages as the government seeks to temper the prospect of rising inflation on the cost of living. A likely increase in cash handouts to around RM17bil from RM15bil in 2026 should support mass-market consumption, according to Apex Securities analyst Wong Kai Heng. That should benefit retailers such as 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd and Padini Holdings Bhd, as well as food and beverage companies including Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd, CCK Consolidated Holdings Bhd and Oriental Kopi Holdings Bhd. Analysts expect a modest increase in the development expenditure, which would provide continued support for infrastructure investment. Key projects that could feature under Budget 2027 include the light rail transit in Penang, the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme and basic infrastructure projects in Sabah and Sarawak. “Potential beneficiaries of development expenditure expansion would be concentrated among contractors and suppliers exposed to water infrastructure and pipe replacement, flood mitigation, rural infrastructure, grid investment, and projects in Sabah and Sarawak,” Ivy Ng Lee Fang, an analyst at CIMB Securities, wrote in a report. That may boost firms in the construction industry, including Gamuda Bhd, IJM Corp Bhd and Malayan Cement Bhd. The government may allocate funds to upgrade the national grid and water infrastructure to support rising demand from data centres, according to Max Koh, an analyst at RHB Research. Greater funding, along with efforts under the National Energy Transition Roadmap, may benefit energy firms like YTL Power International Bhd and Tenaga Nasional Bhd. Meanwhile, Samaiden Group Bhd and Solarvest Holdings Bhd may also gain from new solar tenders. Investors in the bond market will be focused on the fiscal deficit target, as well as the debt supply for 2027 amid higher energy costs. Any further subsidies that could impact the government’s fiscal consolidation efforts may weigh on investor sentiment. “Prudent fiscal policy is increasingly appreciated by markets,” said Winson Phoon, head of fixed‑income research at Maybank Securities. “We expect further progress toward the government’s medium-term fiscal target of 3% of gross domestic product (GDP), potentially setting a target of 3.3% of GDP.” — Bloomberg

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi susulan sentimen positif serantau
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi hari ini, sejajar dengan peningkatan dalam kebanyakan pasaran utama Asia susulan kenaikan saham teknologi di Wall Street dalam tempoh semalaman, walaupun hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang tinggi terus mengehadkan minat terhadap risiko. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.60 mata kepada 1,633.35 berbanding 1,631.75 semasa ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks petunjuk pasaran itu yang dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38, bergerak antara 1,632.77 dan 1,641.20 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Dalam pasaran secara menyeluruh, kaunter untung mengatasi kaunter rugi sebanyak 667 berbanding 456 manakala 551 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,108 tidak diniagakan dan 13 yang lain digantung dagangan. Jumlah dagangan susut kepada 4.18 bilion unit bernilai RM2.95 bilion berbanding 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion semalam. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS dalam tempoh 10 tahun mencecah 5.349 peratus, paras tertinggi sejak 2002 manakala hasil bon 30 tahun meningkat seketika kepada 5.703 peratus. Semasa ditutup pada Isnin, S&P 500 meningkat 0.66 peratus kepada 7,773.95 mata manakala Indeks Komposit Nasdaq naik 1.05 peratus kepada 27,477.31 mata. “Dari sudut positif, harga minyak mentah Brent menyusut di bawah US$100 setong apabila eksport Asia Barat yang kekal kukuh serta pelepasan stok simpanan kecemasan oleh negara-negara Kumpulan Tujuh (G7) membantu mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap bekalan,” katanya kepada Bernama. Menurutnya di dalam negara, minat belian dapat dilihat dalam saham telekomunikasi dan berkaitan komoditi manakala aktiviti dagangan turut meluas kepada beberapa kaunter teknologi bermodal kecil, tenaga dan perladangan. “Kami yakin bahawa saham mewah terpilih boleh terus menarik aktiviti pembelian saham ketika harga rendah susulan pembetulan yang ketara minggu lepas. Bagaimanapun, ketiadaan pembelian susulan sepanjang tiga sesi dagangan lepas menunjukkan pelabur terus berwaspada, dengan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan hasil bon yang tinggi dijangka mengehadkan kadar pemulihan,” katanya. Sementara itu, Thong berkata penurunan harga minyak mentah dan harapan mengenai Belanjawan 2027 dijangka memberikan sedikit sokongan kepada sentimen. “Belanjawan akan dibentangkan pada Jumaat, dengan sektor strategik termasuk semikonduktor, kecerdasan buatan, pendigitalan, peralihan tenaga, farmaseutikal, logistik dan aeroangkasa antara bidang yang diberi tumpuan oleh kerajaan,” katanya. Bagi tempoh yang masih berbaki minggu ini, beliau menjangkakan indeks petunjuk pasaran itu kekal dalam fasa konsolidasi dengan kecenderungan untuk pulih secara sederhana apabila situasi terlebih jual memberikan sedikit sokongan kepada pasaran daripada penurunan selanjutnya. “Bagaimanapun, pemulihan yang lebih kukuh mungkin memerlukan pemangkin baharu, dengan Belanjawan 2027, aliran dana asing, hasil bon dan perkembangan geopolitik kekal sebagai faktor utama untuk diberikan perhatian. “Kami mengekalkan julat dagangan FBM KLCI pada 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata bagi minggu ini,” katanya. Antara saham wajaran tinggi, IHH Healthcare meningkat 15 sen kepada RM7.91 manakala Maybank dan CIMB masing-masing susut tiga sen kepada RM9.97 dan RM7.70. Public Bank turun empat sen kepada RM4.67 manakala Tenaga Nasional susut 10 sen kepada RM12.90. Bagi saham aktif, Zetrix AI dan Supermax masing-masing meningkat 2.5 sen kepada sembilan sen dan 46 sen, Top Glove menokok sembilan sen kepada 87.5 sen, V.S Industry naik satu sen kepada 33 sen manakala SLGC yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE susut tiga sen kepada 25 sen. Antara kaunter paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.56 kepada RM44.96, Nestle naik RM1.26 kepada RM91.26, Pentamaster melonjak 64 sen kepada RM6.08, Mi Technovation menokok 59 sen kepada RM6.00 manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong naik 46 sen kepada RM21.32. Kaunter paling rugi diterajui Dutch Lady Milk Industries yang susut 30 sen kepada RM29.70, Allianz turun 18 sen kepada RM20.62, TIME dotCom susut 16 sen kepada RM5.45 manakala Mega First Corporation dan Ayer Holdings masing-masing rendah 15 sen kepada RM2.85 dan RM7.55. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 melonjak 190.62 mata kepada 17,734.11, Indeks FBM Emas meningkat 42.52 mata kepada 12,232.87, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 42.40 mata kepada 12,015.78, Indeks FBM Emas Syariah meningkat 89.97 mata kepada 12,158.98 manakala Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 52.31 mata kepada 5,658.92. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian meningkat 1.44 mata kepada 180.41 namun Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan susut 72.14 mata kepada 19,068.0. Indeks Tenaga pula meningkat 10.78 mata kepada 840.72 manakala Indeks Perladangan melonjak 111.14 mata kepada 9,042.17. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran Utama susut kepada 2.59 bilion unit bernilai RM2.50 bilion daripada 3.13 bilion unit bernilai RM2.41 bilion pada Isnin. Jumlah dagangan waran turun kepada 932.44 juta unit bernilai RM171.80 juta daripada 1.04 bilion unit bernilai RM208.20 juta semalam. Jumlah dagangan Pasaran ACE meningkat kepada 653.91 juta unit bernilai RM276.54 juta daripada 611.02 juta unit bernilai RM267.66 juta sebelum ini. Sementara itu, kaunter produk dan perkhidmatan pengguna menyumbang sebanyak 204.53 juta saham yang didagangkan di Pasaran Utama, produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (298.70 juta), pembinaan (102.12 juta), teknologi (1.32 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (58.39 juta), hartanah (113.14 juta), perladangan (17.37 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (12.12 juta), dana tertutup (45,000), tenaga (69.91 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (294.68 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (25.52 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (38.51 juta), utiliti (36.68 juta), dan amanah perniagaan (59,700). -- BERNAMA

body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi hari ini, sejajar dengan peningkatan dalam kebanyakan pasaran utama Asia susulan kenaikan saham teknologi di Wall Street dalam tempoh semalaman, walaupun hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang tinggi terus mengehadkan minat terhadap risiko. Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 1.60 mata kepada 1,633.35 berbanding 1,631.75 semasa ditutup pada Isnin. Indeks petunjuk pasaran itu yang dibuka 4.63 mata lebih tinggi kepada 1,636.38, bergerak antara 1,632.77 dan 1,641.20 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Jumlah dagangan susut kepada 4.18 bilion unit bernilai RM2.95 bilion berbanding 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion semalam. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS dalam tempoh 10 tahun mencecah 5.349 peratus, paras tertinggi sejak 2002 manakala hasil bon 30 tahun meningkat seketika kepada 5.703 peratus. Semasa ditutup pada Isnin, S&P 500 meningkat 0.66 peratus kepada 7,773.95 mata manakala Indeks Komposit Nasdaq naik 1.05 peratus kepada 27,477.31 mata. "Dari sudut positif, harga minyak mentah Brent menyusut di bawah AS$100 setong apabila eksport Asia Barat yang kekal kukuh serta pelepasan stok simpanan kecemasan oleh negara-negara Kumpulan Tujuh (G7) membantu mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap bekalan," katanya kepada Bernama. Menurutnya di dalam negara, minat belian dapat dilihat dalam saham telekomunikasi dan berkaitan komoditi manakala aktiviti dagangan turut meluas kepada beberapa kaunter teknologi bermodal kecil, tenaga dan perladangan. "Kami yakin bahawa saham mewah terpilih boleh terus menarik aktiviti pembelian saham ketika harga rendah susulan pembetulan yang ketara minggu lalu. Bagaimanapun, ketiadaan pembelian susulan sepanjang tiga sesi dagangan lepas menunjukkan pelabur terus berwaspada, dengan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan hasil bon yang tinggi dijangka mengehadkan kadar pemulihan," katanya. title: 'Bursa Malaysia ends higher on positive regional sentiment
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ended higher today, in line with gains across major Asian markets following Wall Street's overnight technology-led rally, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to temper risk appetite. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 1.60 points to 1,633.35 from Monday's close of 1,631.75. The benchmark index, which opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38, moved between 1,632.77 and 1,641.20 throughout the trading session. On the broader market, gainers surpassed decliners 667 to 456, while 551 counters were unchanged, 1,108 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover decreased to 4.18 billion units worth RM2.95 billion, compared with 4.78 billion units worth RM2.89 billion yesterday. Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the US 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.349 per cent, its highest since 2002, while the 30-year yield briefly reached 5.703 per cent. At the close on Monday, the S&P 500 gained 0.66 per cent to 7,773.95 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 1.05 per cent to 27,477.31. "On a positive note, Brent crude oil eased below US$100 per barrel as resilient West Asia exports and the Group of Seven's (G7) emergency stockpile release helped alleviate supply concerns," he told Bernama. Domestically, he said buying interest was seen in telecommunications and commodity-related stocks, while trading activity also broadened to selected small-cap technology, energy and plantation counters. "We believe selected blue chips could continue to attract bargain hunting following last week's sharp correction. "However, the lack of follow-through buying over the past three sessions suggests investors remain cautious, with persistent foreign selling and elevated bond yields likely to limit the pace of recovery," he said. Meanwhile, Thong said easing crude oil prices and expectations surrounding Budget 2027 should provide some support to sentiment. "The 2027 Budget will be tabled on Friday, with strategic sectors including semiconductors, artificial intelligence (AI), digitalisation, energy transition, pharmaceuticals, logistics, and aerospace among the areas highlighted by the government," he said. For the rest of the week, he expects the benchmark index to remain in consolidation mode, with a mild recovery bias as oversold conditions provide some downside support. "Nevertheless, a stronger recovery may require fresh catalysts, with Budget 2027, foreign fund flows, bond yields and geopolitical developments remaining key factors to watch. "We maintain our FBM KLCI trading range of 1,620-1,650 for the week," he added. Among the heavyweights, IHH Healthcare Bhd gained 15 sen to RM7.91, while Malayan Banking Bhd and CIMB Group Holdings Bhdeased three sen each to RM9.97 and RM7.70, Public Bank Bhd shed four sen to RM4.67, and Tenaga Nasional Bhd slipped 10 sen to RM12.90. In active trade, Zetrix AI Bhd and Supermax Corp Bhd improved 2.5 sen to nine sen and 46 sen, respectively, Top Glove Corp Bhd put on nine sen to 87.5 sen, V.S Industry Bhd inched up one sen to 33 sen, while ACE Market debutant SLGC Bhd slid three sen to 25 sen. Among the top gainers, Malaysian Pacific Industries Bhd increased RM1.56 to RM44.96, Nestle (M) Bhd rose RM1.26 to RM91.26, Pentamaster Corp Bhd leapt 64 sen to RM6.08, Mi Technovation Bhd jumped 59 sen to RM6.00, and Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd improved 46 sen to RM21.32. title: 'Draft Penang Structure Plan 2040: Who are they building for?
body: 'This plan, the draft Penang Structure Plan 2040, is already well in progress. It has been put up for public display and feedback – but chances are, most people in Penang are not even aware of it. Look at it closely, and you will see that it looks like a developers’ and contractors’ dream. Plenty of ‘jobs for the boys’. Lot of land reclamation sites all over – about 12 from the looks of it. That includes the ‘Penang Gateway’ (no. 9 on the map) reclamation project somewhere in Batu Ferringhi. The SRS-proposed Islands B and C in the south are still on the map – despite previous reports that the project would be scaled down to just one island (Island A or the ‘Silicon Island’). There’s another large reclamation site on the southeast of Penang Island. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member And look at the half a dozen reclamation sites on the mainland. In the Penang channel, there appears to be a conflict in putting an earmarked reclamation project inside a zone that is supposed to be gazetted as a marine sanctuary – the unique Middle Bank seagrass strip in the Penang channel. Who are they building for, when the birth rate in Penang has shrunk well below population replacement level? Seems to me that Greed has taken over. Check out a new coastal ring highway on the east coast (no. 1). The third crossing (the tunnel?) is still on the map (no 6). They never give up, do they? And look at all the reclamation and ‘development’ slated for the area around Jerejak Island (no 9). Why are they indicating a 150-metre contour line above sea level, when at present there is a limitation on development above 76 metres about sea level? It seems they want to allow development on hill slopes even exceeding 300 metres above sea level, almost all the way up, subject to risk assessments and conditions. More multi-billion ringgit LRT links here and there but I don’t see much in the way of a “better, cheaper, faster” bus rapid transit and tram network. And where are the water taxi routes? Remember, after 18 years since the change in government in 2008, we still don’t have a more detailed local plan, which governs the permissible development and zoning densities allowed in your neighbourhoods. Why is that? And all this while, most of the Penang public remain blissfully in the dark about what is in store for them. title: 'Banned from Sarawak – but why?
body: 'Kua Kia Soong In August 2007, I arrived at Kuching airport to officiate at a graduation ceremony for teachers trained by New Era College, where I was then principal. I was not carrying drugs. I was not wanted by the police. I was not entering Sarawak to organise an insurrection. I was there to attend an educational ceremony. Yet I was stopped at immigration and told that I was not allowed to enter Sarawak. After I persistently asked why, I was apparently told that I was on a blacklist because of my “anti-logging activities”. I was then put on a flight back to Kuala Lumpur. The contemporary report of the incident records that I had been an active campaigner against the Bakun Dam and had participated in a fact-finding mission concerning Indigenous people displaced from the Bakun area. Think about that for a moment. A Malaysian citizen, travelling from one part of Malaysia to another, was effectively told: you are not welcome in this part of your own country because you opposed the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous communities. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Nearly 20 years later, the question remains: Sarawak may have the constitutional power to do this. But does it have the moral right? The legal argument is not the whole argument Let me be clear. I am not disputing that Sarawak possesses special immigration powers. These powers are rooted in the constitutional arrangements surrounding the formation of Malaysia. Article 161E protects certain constitutional safeguards for Sabah and Sarawak, while Part VII of the Immigration Act 1959/63 provides the statutory framework for immigration control. The Sarawak government itself describes immigration autonomy as an entrenched constitutional right. But there is a much more important question: what is that power for? The justification traditionally associated with Sarawak’s immigration safeguards was the protection of the state’s special interests – including its economy, employment, security, cultural identity and the interests of its people. The constitutional autonomy was not created as a blank cheque for excluding inconvenient Malaysians. There is a world of difference between immigration autonomy and political exclusion. If the purpose of the special powers is to protect Sarawak and Sarawakians, what exactly was Sarawak being protected from when I was turned away? A former Malaysian MP and college principal coming to officiate at a teachers’ graduation? Or an environmental campaigner who had criticised the Bakun Dam and logging? If the latter was the real reason, then the issue is no longer simply immigration administration. It becomes an issue of freedom of expression, political dissent and the abuse of administrative power. What exactly was my crime? My supposed offence was to oppose the destruction of forests and the displacement of Indigenous people. During the 1990s, I was active in opposing the Bakun Dam project. I participated in a fact-finding mission to investigate the conditions of Indigenous people displaced to Sungai Asap. So apparently, in the strange political dictionary of the time, defending forests and Indigenous communities could make a Malaysian an undesirable person in Malaysia. What next? The irony is almost unbearable. Sarawak has every reason to be proud of its unique constitutional position. But autonomy should mean more democracy, not less. It should mean that Sarawakians have greater control over their land, resources, culture and political affairs. It should not mean that the state acquires a constitutional moat around itself so that environmentalists, human rights defenders, academics or political critics can be kept outside. Otherwise, autonomy becomes a very peculiar proposition: the more autonomous the government becomes, the less accountable it becomes to citizens exercising their democratic rights. That cannot be the meaning of Malaysia’s federal bargain. Apparently, the issue has not disappeared. Just last week, Sahabat Alam Malaysia president Meenakshi Raman was denied entry into Sarawak. A Sarawak deputy minister said the state is not required to give advance notice to people barred from entering and that the relevant immigration laws give the state authority to stop people from entering. Civil society groups have called for the reasons and basis for the restriction to be disclosed. Thus, nearly two decades after my own experience, environmental defenders are still encountering the same question: Who gets to decide who is sufficiently ‘Sarawakian’ in spirit to be allowed into Sarawak? But what about international human rights? Here, the distinction between legal authority and international legitimacy becomes crucial. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights states in Article 13(2) that everyone has the right to leave any country, including his own, and to return to his country. The International Covenant on Civil and Political Rights goes further in Article 12(4): “No one shall be arbitrarily deprived of the right to enter his own country.” There is, however, an important qualification: Malaysia has not ratified the covenant. Therefore, I would not argue that my exclusion in 2007 was automatically a violation of a treaty obligation binding Malaysia under the covenant. But that does not make the international human rights question disappear. The Universal Declaration remains one of the foundational statements of the international human rights system. And Malaysia has repeatedly presented itself internationally as a country committed to human rights, democracy and the rule of law. The question is therefore not merely was Sarawak legally entitled to do it? It is: was it consistent with the human rights values Malaysia claims to uphold? And that is a much harder question for the authorities to answer. Sarawak’s forests are not a Sarawak-only issue. There is another irony here. Logging, Indigenous rights, biodiversity and environmental destruction are not purely ‘state matters’ in any meaningful moral sense. The rainforest does not stop at the Kuching immigration counter. Neither does climate change. Nor does the destruction of biodiversity. Nor does the displacement of Indigenous peoples. A Malaysian citizen concerned about what happens to Sarawak’s forests is not a foreign agitator. He is a Malaysian citizen concerned about Malaysia. And if Sarawak’s forests are part of Malaysia’s natural heritage, why should Malaysians be treated as outsiders for expressing concern about them? Indeed, the more internationally connected environmental politics becomes, the more absurd such restrictions appear. Malaysia wants to attract international investment. It wants to promote Sarawak as an ecological and cultural destination. It wants to speak proudly about sustainable development and Indigenous communities. Yet an environmental campaigner can apparently arrive at an airport and be told: Turn around. Your concern for our forests is unwelcome here. What kind of message does that send to the world? A constitutional right should come with a constitutional conscience. That is a question of political morality. And it is a question that Sarawak – and Malaysia – still has to answer. Nearly 20 years after I was turned away at Kuching airport, I am still waiting for a convincing answer. – Suaram Dr Kua Kia Soong, a former MP and former director of the human rights group Suaram.
