title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Higher On Positive Wall Street Momentum
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 6 – Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday morning, tracking positive overnight momentum on Wall Street as subdued crude oil prices—driven by a recovery in West Asia crude exports—helped offset a ongoing sell-off in US Treasuries. At 9:21 AM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) advanced 7.14 points, or 0.44 per cent, to reach 1,638.89 compared to Monday’s close of 1,631.75. The index had initially opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. Across the broader market, advancing counters outpaced decliners 272 to 202, with 364 counters remaining unchanged, 1,944 untraded, and 13 suspended. Market turnover stood at 440.19 million units valued at RM164.76 million. Heavyweight Movements and Sector Performance Heavyweight banking and energy-linked stocks led the early morning gains, helping push all main index boards higher. Key market movements across categories during early trade included: - Heavyweight Performance: Maybank and Tenaga Nasional each gained four sen to RM10.04 and RM13.04, respectively, while CIMB rose three sen to RM7.76. IHH Healthcare added two sen to RM7.78, while Public Bank traded flat at RM4.71. - Active Counters: Zetrix AI inched up half a sen to seven sen, Divfex added one sen to 16.5 sen, and Ramssol rose 2.5 sen to 86 sen. Meanwhile, ACE Market debutant SLGC fell 3.5 sen to 24.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange edged down half a sen to 50 sen. - Top Gainers: Plantation counters saw strong demand, led by Batu Kawan, which surged RM1.24 to RM20.22. Nestle and Kuala Lumpur Kepong gained 20 sen each to RM90.20 and RM21.06, respectively, followed by Petronas Dagangan (up 18 sen to RM19.38) and Genting Plantations (up 16 sen to RM5.82). - Top Decliners: HeiTech Padu dropped seven sen to 88 sen, while Thong Guan Industries, Sunway Construction Group, and Allianz Malaysia declined six sen each to RM1.44, RM7.55, and RM20.74, respectively. UMS Integration lost four sen to trade at RM9.36. - Index Breakdown: The Plantation Index posted significant gains, jumping 73.78 points to 9,004.81. The Financial Services Index surged 56.47 points to 19,196.61, the Energy Index gained 1.78 points to 831.72, and the Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.16 of a point to 179.13. The FBM Mid 70 Index advanced 41.29 points to 17,584.78, the FBM Emas Index added 44.30 points to 12,234.65, and the FBM ACE Index rose 7.73 points to 5,614.34. –NMT

title: 'Bursa Malaysia opens higher on positive Wall Street momentum
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday, in sync with Wall Street's positive overnight momentum, as muted oil prices following a recovery in West Asia crude exports offset a continued sell-off in US Treasuries. At 9.21am, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 7.14 points, or 0.44 per cent, to 1,638.89 from Monday's close of 1,631.75. The index opened 4.63 points higher at 1,636.38. On the broader market, gainers outpaced losers 272 to 202, with 364 counters unchanged, 1,944 untraded and 13 suspended. Turnover stood at 440.19 million shares worth RM164.76 million. Malacca Securities Sdn Bhd said Wall Street's positive overnight performance saw the Dow Jones Industrial Average, S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite advance by 0.2 per cent, 0.7 per cent and 1.1 per cent, respectively, while the Brent crude oil and 10-year Treasury yield reached US$100.3 per barrel and 5.3 per cent, respectively. "Locally, we expect investors to remain selective ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement, with attention centred on potential beneficiary sectors. "Mechanical and electrical players could continue to see buying interest, supported by the government's emphasis on artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure and Tenaga Nasional Bhd's 500-kilovolt National Grid Backbone project, favouring companies such as MN Holdings Bhd, Southern Cable Group Bhd, and Powerwell Holdings Bhd," it said in a research note today. In addition, Malacca Securities said efforts to reduce non-revenue water could also remain in focus, potentially benefiting companies such as ISF Group Bhd and Ranhill Utilities Bhd. "Lastly, 99 Speed Mart Retail could see renewed buying interest on expectations of higher consumer assistance allocations under Sumbangan Asas Rahmah and Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah," it said. Meanwhile, Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said Wall Street closed firmer, with the Nasdaq notching a fresh record high as traders decided to look past prevailing headwinds and instead focus on AI-related stocks to negate the impacts from escalating bond yields. "For today, we expect the index to hover within the range of 1,630-1,640 as the local bourse may be ripe for some bargain hunting activity," he told Bernama. Among the heavyweights, Maybank and Tenaga Nasional perked up four sen each to RM10.04 and RM13.04, CIMB put on three sen to RM7.76, IHH Healthcare increased two sen to RM7.78, while Public Bank was flat at RM4.71. In active trade, Zetrix AI inched up half a sen to seven sen, Divfex rose one sen to 16.5 sen, Ramssol gained 2.5 sen to 86 sen, while ACE market debutant SLGC eased 3.5 sen to 24.5 sen, and Dagang NeXchange inched down half a sen to 50 sen. Among the top gainers, Batu Kawan expanded RM1.24 sen to RM20.22, Nestle and Kuala Lumpur Kepong gained 20 sen each to RM90.20 and RM21.06, Petronas Dagangan perked up 18 sen to RM19.38, and Genting Plantations strengthened 16 sen to RM5.82. HeiTech Padu led the decliners, falling seven sen to 88 sen, Thong Guan Industries, Sunway Construction Group, and Allianz Malaysia slipped six sen each to RM1.44, RM7.55 and RM20.74, and UMS Integration shrank four sen to RM9.36. On the index board, the FBM Mid 70 Index gained 41.29 points to 17,584.78, the FBM Emas Index appreciated 44.30 points to 12,234.65, the FBM Top 100 Index widened 46.09 points to 12,019.47, the FBM Emas Shariah Index advanced 39.24 points to 12,108.25, and the FBM ACE Index improved 7.73 points to 5,614.34. Sector-wise, the Industrial Products and Services Index inched up 0.16 of a point to 179.13, the Energy Index gained 1.78 points to 831.72, the Financial Services Index jumped 56.47 points to 19,196.61, and the Plantation Index gained 73.78 points to 9,004.81.

title: 'GISBH Money Laundering Case to Proceed to Trial After Representation Rejected
body: 'SHAH ALAM (Oct 5): The Sessions Court here was informed on Monday that the representation submitted by the former chief executive officer (CEO) of GISB Holdings Sdn Bhd (GISBH) and three former company accountants to drop money laundering charges against them had been rejected. Following this, Deputy Public Prosecutor (DPP) Mohd Ashrof Adrin, who appeared alongside DPP Muhamad Ehsan Nasarudin, said the prosecution would proceed with the trial. “I regret to inform the court this morning that the prosecution wishes to state that the representation has been rejected and the prosecution will proceed with the trial. “We will be calling between 15 and 20 prosecution witnesses, and regarding the trial dates, I believe we will require six to eight days,” he said during case management proceedings before judge Datin Fatimah Zahari. The four accused are Nasiruddin Mohd Ali, 67, who faces 77 charges involving more than RM10 million; Hamimah Yakub, 74, facing 95 charges involving RM11.4 million; Asmat @ Asmanira Muhammad Ramly, 46, facing 68 charges involving RM4.7 million; and Mohd Khushairi Osman, 55, facing 91 charges involving nearly RM12 million. However, lawyer Datuk Rosli Kamaruddin, representing all four accused, informed the court that the defence intends to submit a new representation once the seized assets are officially returned to his clients. He said the new representation would, among other matters, address the possibility of resolving the case through a compound offer. “For the record, the previous representation did not address the issue of exploring a compound, so there may be a representation exploring this issue,” said Rosli, who was accompanied by lawyer Muhammad Zaim Rosli. He also requested the court to fix a case management date to determine the status of the new representation in January 2027. After hearing submissions from both parties, Fatimah fixed the trial for April 26 to 28, June 28 to 30 and July 6 to 8 next year, while the status of the second representation by all four accused will be heard on Jan 26. Meanwhile, Rosli also sought the court’s permission for the return of Nasiruddin’s passport to enable him to travel to Makkah. Nasiruddin, who appeared in court in a wheelchair, intends to meet his fourth wife, Ummu Mubaroqah Ashaari, 32, who is scheduled to undergo a Caesarean section this month. He said Muhammad Saleh Basharahil Hospital in Makkah had advised Nasiruddin to be present to provide consent for his wife’s surgery, as she is now full-term, although the exact date of the procedure has yet to be determined. Mohd Ashrof Adrin informed the court that the prosecution did not object to the application, subject to the conditions stipulated in the notice of application, including that the passport be returned to the court on or before Nov 10, 2026. The judge subsequently allowed the application subject to the stipulated conditions. On Sept 10, 2025, Nasiruddin and the three former company accountants pleaded not guilty at the Shah Alam Sessions Court to money laundering charges brought against them. The alleged offences were committed at bank branches in Selangor between 2020 and 2024 and involved transactions with various parties, including bank accounts belonging to GISBH Sdn Bhd, GISB Mart Sdn Bhd, GISB Travel and Tours Sdn Bhd and childcare centre companies. They were charged under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001 (Act 613), punishable under Section 4(1) of the same Act. If convicted, an offender is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding 15 years and a fine of not less than five times the amount or value of the proceeds of unlawful activity at the time the offence was committed, or RM5 million, whichever is higher. title: 'Mplus Market Pulse - 06 Oct 2026
body: 'MY: Tracking Wall Street's positive performance last Friday, the local bourse kickstarted the week higher, buoyed by gains in the banking heavyweights including PBBANK and CIMB. Sector-wise, Technology (+1.74%) continued to outperform, led by gains in VITROX and UWC, while Construction (-1.46%) declined the most. US: Wall Street closed higher on Monday as muted oil prices following recovering Middle East crude exports offset a continued sell-off in U.S. Treasuries. The Dow, S&P 500 and Nasdaq advanced by 0.2%, 0.7% and 1.1% respectively, while the Brent crude and 10-year Treasury yield reached USD100.3 and 5.3%, respectively. US: Given the broadly in-line Services PMI and ISM Non-Manufacturing PMI data, attention will now shift towards the FOMC meeting minutes overnight Thursday. Stock-wise, we favour Amazon (AMZN), supported by its USD496bn AWS-related backlog and USD220bn 2026 CapEx outlook as it aggressively expands AI data-centre capacity amid strong cloud and AI demand. This should also benefit Astera Labs (ALAB), given its exposure to AWS's next-generation Trainium infrastructure through its Aries Retimers and Scorpio Smart Fabric Switches. Hence, AMZN's aggressive data-centre expansion should provide a strong demand tailwind for ALAB. Lastly, investors could also look at Arista Networks (ANET), supported by the rollout of its next-generation 1.6Tb networking platform for AI infrastructure. MY: Locally, we expect investors to remain selective ahead of the Budget 2027 announcement, with attention centred on potential beneficiary sectors. M&E players could continue to see buying interest, supported by the government's emphasis on AI infrastructure and TNB's 500kV National Grid Backbone project, favouring companies such as MNHLDG, SGCBHD and POWERWELL. Efforts to reduce non- revenue water could also remain in focus, potentially benefiting companies such as ISF and RANHILL. Lastly, 99SMART could see renewed buying interest on expectations of higher consumer assistance allocations under SARA and STR. Despite the rebound yesterday, the FBMKLCI is still trading below the MA lines, with technical indicators showing weak signals as the MACD histogram continued to hover in the negative territory while the RSI is oversold. Key resistance is pegged at 1,646-1,651, while support is seen at 1,611-1,616. Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook told reporters that the suspension of Zetrix AI Bhd (ZETRIX) and subsidiary MyEG stemmed from RM314m in unremitted Road Transport Department collections from May to September. The collections should have been transferred daily within one working day of each transaction. The company issued a RM231m cheque to clear earlier arrears but the payment failed on Sept 30 after it instructed the bank not to process it. Following Loke's press conference, Zetrix AI issued a statement vowing to settle the dues to the government, and that it had submitted a proposal to resolve the issue. (The Edge) eJamin, an online bail payment system operated by a unit of Practice Note 17 company Pertama Digital Bhd (PERTAMA), ran for five years without a formal contract, the Public Accounts Committee found. Bail funds were also deposited into a commercial bank account held by Dapat Vista Sdn Bhd, instead of the federal government's consolidated trust account, in contravention of the Federal Constitution and the Financial Procedure Act 1957. Dapat Vista is 80% owned by Television Airtime Services Sdn Bhd, a 51%-owned subsidiary of Pertama Digital. The remaining 20% is held by the technology outfit HeiTech Padu Bhd (HTPADU). The bail deposit balance stood at RM193.71m as at end-2024. However, the committee discovered that only RM62.3m was held in bank accounts with the remaining RM130.8m invested by Dapat Vista in instruments including sukuk, without government approval or legal authority. The investment allowed Dapat Vista to earn RM4m to RM5m in interest, which the company regarded as "service income". (The Edge) Yinson Holdings Bhd (YINSON) has secured about US$600m (RM2.5bn) in additional firm contract backlog following an amendment to its contract for the FPSO John Agyekum Kufuor offshore of Ghana. The amendment covers a major upgrade to the FPSO vessel's gas handling and processing capacity and extends its firm contract by four years to 2036. The incremental day rates for the modification works and contract extension are valued at about US$810m and about US$600m of that is attributable to the group. (The Edge) Kelington Group Bhd (KGB) said its wholly owned unit has been awarded a second contract by a manufacturer operating in the Sama Jaya Free Industrial Zone in Kuching, Sarawak, worth about RM133m. The award covers the main structural steel works for the customer's data storage manufacturing facility, which is being expanded. Works will start immediately and are scheduled for completion by April 2028. (The Edge) Information technology solutions provider Go Hub Capital Bhd (GOHUB) has secured a five-year service contract worth RM65m from Keretapi Tanah Melayu (KTMB) unit Tenang Capital Bhd. Go Hub said the job is to provide maintenance and support services for KTMB's Integrated Ticketing System. (The Edge) Citaglobal Bhd (CITAGLB), via indirect unit LAWI Engineering GmbH (LAWI Germany), has secured a RM29m share of a RM52.1m contract for a waste-to-energy (WTE) project in Thailand. LAWI Germany, together with a consortium partner, was awarded the contract by Siam Power Co Ltd for the engineering, procurement and construction of a steam boiler plant for the Siam Power Naklang WTE project in the Nakhon Ratchasima Province. LAWI Germany will undertake the imported engineering and equipment supply portion valued at €6.33m (RM29m). (The Edge) West River Bhd (WESTRVR) has secured a RM17.5m subcontract for electrical, security and solar panel system works at the E-Metro Logistic Park in Bandar Bukit Raja 2, Selangor. The contract covers the supply, delivery, installation, testing and commissioning of electrical and extra-low-voltage systems, telephone services, security works and solar panel systems. (The Edge) Jati Tinggi Group Bhd (JTGROUP) has secured two contracts from Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TENAGA) (TNB) worth a combined RM15.7m. The larger contract, worth RM13.44m, is for the installation, testing and commissioning of underground cables and related accessories for TNB's distribution network in Selangor. The other contract, worth RM2.27m, is secured through a joint venture to install a distributed acoustic sensing system for TNB's submarine power cable system between Kuala Perlis and Teluk Apau on Langkawi. (The Edge) IJM Corporation Bhd (IJM) has appointed non-executive chairman of KPMG Malaysia Datuk Johan Idris as its independent non-executive director and chairman, effective Monday. Johan, who previously served as KPMG Malaysia's managing partner and country senior partner, succeeds long-serving chairman Tan Sri Krishnan Tan following his retirement. Datuk Lee Teck Yuen, who stepped in as the interim chairman at IJM's annual general meeting on Aug 27 to provide continuity while the board finalised its succession plan following Tan's retirement, has now been redesignated as a non-executive director. (The Edge) Datuk Clifford Hii Toh Leong has increased his stake in Asteel Group Bhd (ASTEEL) to 53.08% following the close of his unconditional mandatory takeover offer on Monday. The mandatory offer at 7.5 sen per share was triggered after Hii Capital acquired the initial 52.94% stake for RM20.25m in August. Separately, Asteel announced it has secured a RM15.8m contract from H.N. Lau Agency Sdn Bhd for the construction of a three-storey logistics complex in Shah Alam, Selangor. (The Edge) Chipmaker Qualcomm (QCOM) and chip technology firm Arm Holdings (ARM) started a new trial on Monday, with Qualcomm claiming Arm withheld chip testing tools required under their contract. Qualcomm also claims Arm leaked information to the media about its 2024 threat to cancel a critical license agreement, which hurt negotiations for a chip deal between Qualcomm and Meta Platforms (META). (Investing.com) Starbucks' (SBUX) has been sued by consumers who said the coffee chain falsely advertised eight protein beverages as "sugar-free" because they contain lactose, a naturally occurring sugar in milk. Federal law prohibits Starbucks from using "sugar- free" to describe beverages containing more than 0.5 grams of sugar per 12-ounce serving, the complaint said. title: 'CIMB IB Says Malaysia Could Widen Corporate Tax Base for Budget 2027, Cut Old Deductions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Malaysia could widen its corporate tax base by reviewing special and double deductions that have been in place for two to three decades, and remove deductions that no longer serve their original purpose, said CIMB Investment Bank. CIMB IB said, citing KPMG senior adviser on tax policy Dr Verrinderjeet Singh during a discussion, that the removal of selected deductions could lead to the government collecting more revenue while creating room for a lower headline corporate tax rate. “His [Verrinderjeet] proposal is selective: investment incentives remain important for attracting businesses, but their benefits need closer scrutiny. He links Malaysia’s shift towards outcome-based incentives to its response to Global Minimum Tax,” said CIMB IB. It added, “Their effectiveness will depend on monitoring whether investors deliver the intended economic benefits”. Malaysia’s headline corporate income tax rate is currently 24%, but the amount of tax companies ultimately pay is also affected by deductions, exemptions and investment incentives. On major tax changes, CIMB IB said Malaysia is unlikely to introduce new tax changes in Budget 2027, with stronger collection from existing taxes and a wider tax base offering the main scope for raising government revenue. The government is expected to focus on improving tax collection, particularly by bringing more businesses into the tax net and identifying income that is not fully reported. Smaller businesses are likely to offer more room for additional collections, as larger companies are already more visible to the tax authorities, said CIMB IB. “His central message was that stronger collection and targeted refinements to existing taxes offer the main near-term revenue opportunities. Against a continued focus on cost-of-living support and the social agenda, he expects few substantial tax changes in the coming budget,” said CIMB IB. E-invoicing could help identify unreported taxable activity, although smaller businesses face additional compliance and technology costs. CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet expects participation to broaden as economic conditions improve. CIMB IB also sees scope for greater use of data analytics by the Inland Revenue Board (IRB) and Customs to identify businesses and income outside the existing tax net. On indirect taxes, CIMB IB said Veerinderjeet does not expect the goods and services tax (GST) to return in Budget 2027. Instead, the focus is likely to remain on improving the existing sales and service tax (SST). SST is estimated to cover about 78% to 80% of goods and services, approaching the breadth of the former GST regime. CIMB said broader exemptions for business inputs could reduce the cascading of tax costs through supply chains, although this would come at the cost of lower tax receipts. Veerinderjeet also does not expect an increase in the 2% dividend tax on annual dividend income above RM100,000, an extension of capital gains tax to listed shares or a further increase in the 30% top personal income tax rate in Budget 2027, according to the note. “Dr Veerinderjeet argues that the government should ‘sweat our assets’ through better collection, supported by greater investment in tax agency analytics. These efforts can deliver incremental gains, while broader personal, corporate and indirect tax bases offer scope to lift tax-to-GDP towards 15% over time,” said CIMB IB economists. Veerinderjeet estimates only 15% to 16% of the workforce currently pays personal income tax, with low wages limiting the number of taxpayers. Higher wages would therefore be important in expanding the personal income tax base. Budget 2027 is expected to be tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. title: 'Carbon Tax Deferment Gives Ministry More Time to Finalise Regulatory, Policy Framework, Says Arthur
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The deferment of the carbon tax implementation is aligned with the Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Ministry’s efforts to establish a complete regulatory and policy framework before enforcing emission caps. Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup said the government decided to delay the tax, originally planned for this year, following global geopolitical developments that led to volatile energy prices, providing affected industries with a necessary buffer. Speaking during a Concorde Club dialogue session at Wisma Bernama on Monday, he said the postponement is also timely as the ministry works towards solidifying the required legal structure, including the National Carbon Market Policy and the upcoming Climate Change Act. “[The postponement] is also right because we need to have the proper framework and all that in place first. That’s why we’ve been successful in launching the National Carbon Market Policy and I hope that we can table the Climate Change Act soon. “Once that is up, then we have the framework and the policies all clearly in place, including the regulation, enforcement, the regulatory powers to give us to set the emission ceiling, and then we can know anything above the ceiling, then the carbon tax will come into place as a penalty to the polluters. “So, we’re not looking at this year for the carbon tax,” he said. Meanwhile, on Clean Air Regulations exemption, Arthur said exemptions for industrial plants under the regulation would only be extended to factory operators who demonstrate proactive measures toward technology adoption. He said while no new blanket extensions are being issued, factory operators whose exemptions expire by January next year must show clear steps toward compliance, with 2030 set as the final deadline for total compliance across all industries. “We had the Clean Air Regulations, which came into force in 2014, where plants, factories are not allowed to pollute above the 600 milligram per cubic metre...that was the regulation set...however, they have been enjoying exemptions up to this year. “So when I came in as the minister, I decided that I will not be issuing any more exemptions because the technology is available, the technology is accessible and if we are to meet our target of net zero emissions by 2050, we need to have all this in place and we definitely need the cooperation from the industries as well,” he said. He added that while operators need adequate time for feasibility studies and modifications, strict progress is required to qualify for temporary extensions. The session, titled “Building A Resilient Malaysia: Environment, Climate And Our Future”, was moderated by Bernama chairman Datuk Seri Wong Chun Wai. Also present was Bernama chief executive officer Datin Paduka Nur-ul Afida Kamaludin, as well as members of the local and foreign media based in Malaysia. title: 'Ex-secretary to PM's Graft Case: Temporary Passport Release for Shamsul Iskandar
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, a former senior political secretary to the prime minister, has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month. The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption. According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties. He said he intends to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11. “Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities. “Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the Madani principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit. Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14. He said the summit aims to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices. Shamsul Iskandar also said he plans to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December. During Monday's proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport. He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month. Deputy public prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online. However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release. Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective from Monday, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16. The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249 respectively, from Tei for the same purpose. The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024. In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei's company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah. All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction. title: 'PN Challenging Suspension in Court, Seeks Expedited Hearing as Melaka Polls Loom
body: 'PUTRAJAYA (Oct 5): Perikatan Nasional on Monday filed a legal challenge against its suspension and potential deregistration by the Registrar of Societies (RoS), and is seeking an expedited hearing to resolve the matter before the Melaka election. PN secretary-general Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan said the coalition wants to quash notices issued by RoS under Sections 13(2) and 13(2A) of the Societies Act 1966. Section 13(2) requires PN to explain its actions within 30 days or be deregistered. The Section 13(2A) notice informs PN that it must suspend its activities until it has responded to the matter. The suspension means PN cannot use its logo during the state polls. “The only reason given [for the notice and suspension] was that we did not invite Bersatu leaders for a meeting on July 16. But the official complaint by Bersatu was never given to us,” Takiyuddin, who is also secretary-general of PAS, said at a press conference on Monday. PN's application names RoS director-general Datuk Muhammad Zulfikar Ahmad and Home Minister Datuk Seri Datuk Sri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail as respondents. The Election Commission (EC) is expected to announce the date of the Melaka election after a meeting on Wednesday. The state polls must be held within 60 days of the Sept 23 dissolution of the Melaka assembly. Given the urgency, Takiyuddin said the coalition has also made a filing requesting that the case be expedited. “We want to ask the court to hear this case urgently because we need the court’s determination before the Melaka election is held,” he said. Takiyuddin said the coalition had engaged with the EC on this matter but the final word lay with the RoS. Asked whether PN component parties would use their own logos in the Melaka polls, Takiyuddin said: “These five parties, PAS, Wawasan, Gerakan, MIPP and Pejuang, have been negotiating that matter in view of all possibilities.” The suspension of PN comes after PAS said on June 8 it had ended political cooperation with Bersatu, the previously the dominant party in PN. However, the now beleaguered Bersatu was never expelled from the coalition. On Aug 11, Bersatu filed a complaint with RoS concerning its status in PN, as well as its exclusion from a PN Supreme Council meeting on July 16. RoS sent the show-cause notice to PN on Sept 22, and the suspension order the next day as the Melaka assembly was dissolved. Takiyuddin said PN sent a letter to RoS on Sept 24 to obtain an explanation on the notice and suspension, but has yet to receive a response. He said Bersatu was excluded from the July 16 meeting due to the party's breaches of its own constitution earlier that week. Takiyuddin claimed that a Bersatu Supreme Council meeting had decided to use the party logo instead of the PN logo for the Negeri Sembilan polls, but that meeting had insufficient quorum as per the party’s constitution. He said PN feared that its deliberations would be invalid if Bersatu took part in the coalition’s supreme council meeting while in breach of its own party constitution. In the coalition's court filing, it argues that suspension order violated procedural fairness and the rules of natural justice, as PN was neither provided with details of Bersatu’s complaint nor granted an opportunity to be heard. PN said the suspension order impedes its ability to endorse candidates and its use of its registered name and symbol during the state election, thereby infringing upon rights under Articles 4(1), 8(1), 10(1)(a), 10(1)(c), and 119 of the Federal Constitution. Apart from quashing the RoS notices, PN wants the regulator to furnish all complaint documents and communications related to Bersatu within three days, as well as a stay on the suspension pending the disposal of the judicial review. Case management was fixed for Oct 13 before High Court Judge Datuk Azizan Arshad. title: 'Autopsy Confirms Yong Peng Schoolgirl Died From Head Injury — Police
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): An autopsy on 16-year-old Irene Sofiya Mohd Khairool Faisal, who was believed to have been murdered at a school in Yong Peng, Johor, on Saturday, found that she died from blunt trauma to the head. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M Kumar said the post-mortem was conducted on Sunday by a pathologist from the Forensic Department of Sultanah Nora Ismail Hospital in Batu Pahat. “A 16-year-old boy was arrested on Oct 3 and has been remanded for six days until Oct 9 to assist investigations,” he said in a statement Monday. Kumar said the case was being investigated for murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code, with the school and Education Ministry giving police their full cooperation. He assured that the investigation would be conducted thoroughly, transparently and professionally, with no attempt to cover up the case or protect any party. “The case is still under investigation. The public is advised not to speculate or make comments that could interfere with the investigation or manipulate facts with the intention of causing public anxiety,” he said. Irene Sofiya was found unconscious and covered in blood in the school hall at about 5.50pm on Saturday. The suspect was arrested in the Yong Peng at about 7pm the same day. title: 'Bar Fails in Bid to Challenge Ex-AG Terrirudin's Appointment to Judicial Appointments Commission
body: '"The JAC merely recommends. The power of appointment lies with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the prime minister’s advice under [the law]. The alleged fear of bias from one of nine members of a body that decides nothing is remote, indirect, and speculative.” — High Court judge Norliza Othman. KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The Malaysian Bar has failed to get the green light to challenge former attorney general (AG) and sitting Federal Court judge Tan Sri Ahmad Terrirudin Mohd Salleh's appointment to the Judicial Appointments Commission (JAC). In dismissing the Bar's leave (permission) application to commence a judicial review, High Court judge Norliza Othman on Monday said that Terrirudin's appointment satisfies the criterium in law, namely that an apex court judge must be appointed by the prime minister. She said that the law does not extend to other implied requirements, such as seniority or length of service, as contended by the Bar. "[The law] is plain. It specifies the category of person: a Federal Court judge; and the appointing authority: the prime minister — and stops there. The applicant asserts both are satisfied, yet asks the court to read in implied requirements: seniority, length of service, prior High Court/Court of Appeal experience, freedom from unresolved allegations, consultation, and conformity with an asserted convention — none of which appear in the text. "Our function is to interpret the words used, not to supply the words omitted," she said adding that case law is against the Bar in this case. Terrirudin, who was appointed a Federal Court judge in November 2025, is serving a two-year term on the JAC, from Nov 15, 2025 to Nov 14, 2027. The JAC is a nine-member body responsible for recommending candidates for appointment to Malaysia's superior courts. The ex-AG's appointment drew brickbats from many quarters, with many highlighting that his selection departed from established practice by bypassing a more senior judge and could undermine perceptions of judicial independence. In the midst of this, the Bar filed the leave application on Feb 12, naming Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, the JAC, and the Malaysian government as respondents. Among the reliefs sought, the Bar is asking the court to quash Terrirudin's appointment, prohibit his appointment to any judicial office pending disposal of the proceedings, and compel the disclosure of minutes from a JAC meeting held on May 16, 2025. In her grounds of judgement, Norliza said that the Bar's argument that Terriruddin's appointment was irrational fails, as "nothing here is so deprived of logic or accepted moral standards that no sensible decision-maker could have reached it". She added that the Bar's argument that the decision contained illegality also failed. She added that the Bar also lacked locus standi to bring the action as they were not adversely affected by the appointment. "The JAC merely recommends," she said in her judgement, adding, "The power of appointment lies with the Yang di-Pertuan Agong on the prime minister's advice under [the law]. The alleged fear of bias from one of nine members of a body that decides nothing is remote, indirect, and speculative.” She ordered cost of RM3,000 to be paid to the Attorney General's Chambers (AGC). Former Bar presidents Zainur Zakaria, Steven Thiru and Datuk Ambiga Sreevenasan appeared for the Bar while senior federal counsel Datuk Shamsul Bolhassan led the team appearing for the AGC. title: 'MUFG Sees Ringgit Dipping Below RM4 Against US Dollar by 3Q 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): The ringgit is expected to outperform most Asian currencies in the final quarter of 2026, supported by Malaysia’s strong electronics exports despite pressure from higher oil prices, according to MUFG Bank. It also expects Bank Negara Malaysia to maintain the overnight policy rate at 2.75% until the third quarter of next year as inflation remains contained. The ringgit was trading around 4.09 against the US dollar on Monday morning. MUFG expects it to strengthen to 4.03 by end-2026, before advancing further to 3.98 by the third quarter of 2027. MUFG expects the ringgit to be the strongest performing Asian currency covered in its latest foreign-exchange outlook. “Malaysia’s electronics surplus continues to cushion the oil shock,” MUFG said, adding that Malaysia's trade position remains relatively resilient amid elevated energy prices. “This means higher oil prices are likely to remain a headwind for the ringgit rather than derail its medium-term outlook,” MUFG said. Malaysia is also benefiting from continued investment in information and communications technology, including data centres and cloud computing. Services investment approvals rose more than 20% year-on-year in the first half of 2026, supported largely by ICT-related investments. MUFG said stronger US spending on computers and related equipment has also helped support demand for Malaysian electrical and electronics exports. “MYR fundamentals remain intact despite higher oil prices and the recent bond sell-off,” the bank said. While near-term volatility could persist as investors watch higher fuel-subsidy costs and global bond yields, MUFG said Malaysia’s resilient external position, improving capital flows and attractive valuations should continue to support the ringgit over the medium term. The bank also pointed to Malaysia’s stronger economic growth, with gross domestic product expanding 6% year-on-year in the second quarter, compared with an average pre-pandemic growth pace of 4.9%. title: 'Mustapha Proposes Committee to Work Out Mechanism for Sabah, Sarawak Parliamentary Seat Increase
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud has proposed the establishment of a special committee under the Technical Committee of the Malaysia Agreement 1963 Implementation Action Council (MTPMA63) to work out the mechanism for increasing parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak. He also proposed that the special committee be co-chaired by him and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said. “The increase in the number of members of Parliament from Sabah and Sarawak has been included in the agenda of MTPMA63 and its Technical Committee meetings, and has also been discussed extensively at Cabinet meetings. “Following the decision, I held preliminary discussions with the Election Commission (EC) to seek its views and determine the next course of action,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat on Monday. He said this in response to a supplementary question from Datuk Willie Mongin (GPS-Puncak Borneo), who sought clarification on the mechanisms and legislative steps required to increase parliamentary seats for the two states. Mustapha said discussions on the matter would continue at upcoming meetings of the MTPMA63 Technical Committee. Meanwhile, he said 13 of the 26 matters under the MTPMA63 negotiation platform had been categorised as resolved, following decisions made at the first MTPMA63 meeting held on Sept 11. “Of the 26 matters, three have been categorised as partially resolved, five remain unresolved, while another five have been brought before the prime minister, the Sarawak premier and the Sabah chief minister for discussion,” he said. Mustapha said the MA63-related matters brought before the highest level for discussion and decision-making included oil royalties and petroleum cash payments, stamp duties, the Territorial Sea Act 2012, and state rights over the continental shelf. He said the Madani government was committed to expediting the resolution of all claims under the Malaysia Agreement 1963 (MA63), although the timeframe for resolving each claim was subject to the relevant legal processes. “The Madani government remains firmly committed to ensuring the prudent and inclusive implementation of MA63, grounded in the spirit of strong federalism,” he said. title: 'Food Waste Forms Nearly 40% of Nation’s Daily Solid Waste, Says Minister
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 5): Nearly 40% of the total 40,000 metric tonnes of solid waste generated in the country daily consists of food waste, according to Housing and Local Government Minister Nga Kor Ming. He said efforts to address this waste issue require the cooperation of all parties through a "whole-of-nation approach" involving both businesses and consumers to collectively change their attitudes and practices. “This is a form of waste. Food waste is not a crime, but it is a sin. It is a grave sin when edible food is simply thrown away,” he said during the question-and-answer session in the Dewan Rakyat Monday. Nga said this when replying a question from Datuk Mumtaz Md Nawi (PN-Tumpat) regarding the latest developments in efforts to reduce waste sent to landfills and to increase recycling rates. Meanwhile, he expressed confidence that the ministry would achieve its target of exceeding a 40% recycling rate by the end of this year. Nga noted that under the "Trash to Cash" recycling programme, the total collection of recyclable materials between January and August exceeded 7.86 million kilogrammes (kg), with a sales value of over RM2.85 million. “Secondly, the zero-waste community initiative involving the establishment of 17 active zero-waste community centres during the same period has collected over 111,504kg of recyclable materials,” he said. Additionally, Nga said a school-based recycling competition, involving 1,680 schools, successfully collected 4.95 million kilogrammes of recyclable materials, which were sold for RM2.98 million. “Based on calculations of the total collected from 2018 to last year, we managed to gather nearly 20 million kilogrammes of recyclable items, generating proceeds exceeding RM10.22 million,” he said. Responding to a supplementary question from Mumtaz regarding the specific controls and enforcement actions implemented by the Ministry of Housing and Local Government concerning cable theft including penalties imposed on third parties or buyers, he said the Cabinet views this issue seriously. “We constantly collaborate and engage with the Ministry of Home Affairs (KDN), including examining the need to amend relevant laws to ensure harsher penalties are imposed on cable theft offenders in the country. “There have been several instances where LRT (Light Rail Transit) operations were disrupted due to cable theft by syndicates; therefore, this matter (amending laws for heavier penalties) is crucial to ensuring we continue to safeguard public safety and the well-being of the people,” he said. title: 'Takaichi Pledges Fiscal Discipline as Japan's Debt Bill Rises
body: 'TOKYO (Oct 5): Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi on Monday pledged to "control" bond issuance and act swiftly against market turbulence, seeking to reassure investors worried about Japan's worsening public finances that have pushed up bond yields. She said the government would pursue fiscal sustainability even as it ramps up spending to bolster growth potential, including by reviewing existing tax breaks and subsidies. "Fiscal sustainability is obviously a prerequisite in pursuing our 'responsible and proactive' fiscal policy," Takaichi said in a policy speech to parliament. The remarks reflect mounting concern in Tokyo over rising Japanese government bond (JGB) yields, which would boost the cost of funding the premier's ambitious spending plans. The 30-year JGB yield hit a record high of 4.235% on Monday on jitters over the risk of increased debt issuance and inflation worries fuelled by the Middle East war. Japan's public debt, at roughly twice the size of its economy, is the largest in the developed world. Funding costs are climbing as the Bank of Japan raises interest rates and tapers bond purchases in an effort to wean the economy off decades of massive stimulus. Takaichi said the government will seek to draw in private investment in growth areas through "massive, long-term fiscal expenditure deployed in a well-planned, predictable manner." At the same time, it would keep a lid on annual bond issuance, calibrating borrowing to tax revenues, interest rates, debt-financing costs and economic and market developments, the premier said in the speech to an extraordinary parliament session that convened on Monday. "If the economy and markets make unexpected moves, we will scrutinise their impact and respond nimbly as needed," she added without elaborating. Fiscal policy is set to take centre stage in parliamentary debate in Japan as rising concerns over the fiscal health of advanced economies fuel a broader rise in global bond yields. The administration's immediate priority is passing legislation backing Takaichi's plan for a two-year tax cut on food items from next April, which sparked a bond selloff due to a lack of detail on how the revenue shortfall will be filled. The government is also preparing next year's budget, with ministries seeking record levels of spending. Separately, Takaichi said Tokyo will set aside multi-year funds for strategically important economic security initiatives. "We will implement policies steadily, get things done one by one, and communicate them carefully to the public and markets," Takaichi said. Keen to soothe market jitters, the administration has moved to dispel perceptions that its fiscal policy is reflationary or that it has leaned on the BOJ to refrain from hiking rates. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama said on Saturday that the government has begun refining its messaging to reassure investors that Takaichi is not pursuing reflationary policies. But not all are on board. Former BOJ deputy governor Masazumi Wakatabe, a reflationist academic who is currently a private member of the government's key economic panel, said the recent rise in JGB yields was due to expectations of further BOJ rate hikes rather than concern over Japan's finances, minutes of the panel's recent meeting showed on Monday. Wakatabe also said the government had ultimate responsibility in guiding economic policy and stressed the need for close coordination between the BOJ and the administration on monetary policy, according to the minutes of the meeting which debated the central bank's rate-hike decision last month. title: 'Bolsonaro Beats Expectations in Brazil Presidential Vote, Will Face Lula in Run-off
body: 'BRASILIA/SAO PAULO/RIO DE JANEIRO (Oct 5): Right-wing Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro will face leftist President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in a run-off of the presidential election later this month, after he exceeded expectations in Sunday's first-round vote with a slight lead over the incumbent. The election, which centred around the cost of living, corruption and insecurity in Brazilians' daily lives, follows a string of wins across Latin America by right-wing parties aligned with US President Donald Trump. Bolsonaro's stronger-than-expected performance, at 47% of votes versus Lula's 45%, is expected to buoy his campaign and may bolster Brazil's currency and stock market, which have risen on the prospects of the business-friendly challenger. Private surveys in the run-up to the election had forecast Lula leading the first-round vote by around three percentage points. "Brazil wants change and I am very happy with the results," Bolsonaro told reporters in Brasilia after nearly all tallies were reported, heralding "the end of the era of (Lula's) Workers' Party." The senator, son of right-wing former president Jair Bolsonaro, who is serving a 27-year sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election, now heads to an October 25 showdown with the leftist Lula. Addressing a crowd at a hotel in Sao Paulo, Lula said he had been convinced he would win the election in the first round. "Starting tomorrow, we begin a new campaign," he said, promising to show voters what he had accomplished as president. Despite growing worries over Brazil's public finances and sluggish economic growth, the campaign offered meager policy debate, as both leading candidates skipped the major TV debates. "The pollsters missed badly," said Robert Muggah, cofounder of think-tank Igarape Institute. "Expect the run-off polls, which show a dead heat, to understate Bolsonaro as well." Early on Sunday, Bolsonaro told journalists in Rio de Janeiro he was counting on "a protest vote from people who would otherwise vote for another candidate but are opposed to Lula." Thaise Lima, a 41-year-old lawyer on her way to vote in Sao Paulo, said her main goal was to get Lula's Workers' Party out of office. "I don't think Flavio is the best candidate, but I might decide to vote for him in the next few minutes," she said, adding that she wished psychiatrist and author Augusto Cury were a more viable candidate. Fernando Tempel, 49, a management consultant, told Reuters he was voting for Bolsonaro despite initially planning to vote for Romeu Zema, the former governor of Minas Gerais state. "The protest vote foreshadows what is to come in the run-off," said political analyst Rafael Favetti. "While this should benefit Flavio Bolsonaro now, his growth potential in the second round drops precisely because that support has already been front-loaded." Despite Brazil's falling inequality and unemployment, Lula has struggled to win over voters grappling with the high cost of living, heavy household debt and the threat of crime and more pervasive gang activity. Bolsonaro has sought to capitalise on cost-of-living concerns, while Lula moved to ban online gambling and, as the race tightened, expanded welfare and proposed fresh debt relief for families. Rising spending and public debt above 82% of GDP have stoked fiscal concerns that Brazil's next president will need to address. The government lowered its economic growth forecasts for this year and next to 2.0% and 2.3%, respectively. "I voted for Brazil to start growing again," said Marciano de Souza e Silva, a 52-year-old public servant in Brasilia who voted for Flavio. Scandals and fears of foreign interference ahead of the vote largely overshadowed policy debates during the campaign. Controversy surrounding the now-defunct Banco Master engulfed much of Brazil's political class after Daniel Vorcaro, who ran the bank, was arrested earlier this year and accused of a multi-billion-dollar fraud scheme, which he denies. A federal police investigation has looked into the banker's ties to figures across Brazil's political elite, including Bolsonaro, who is being investigated for suspected money laundering that police have tied to the case. Bolsonaro has denied wrongdoing. Throughout the campaign, Lula's allies have warned that the Trump administration might refuse to recognise election results if he wins, pointing to an aborted effort to send US officials to Brazil. Trump has not formally endorsed a candidate, though he hosted Senator Bolsonaro at the White House and praised him publicly. Reuters reported on Wednesday that Brazilian intelligence officials briefed a French and German delegation on alleged US and Russian interference before the election. The US has rejected claims of interference in Brazil's affairs. On Sunday afternoon, Brazil's electoral court chief Kassio Nunes Marques said the election was running smoothly. title: 'Asia Among Most Vulnerable to AI Correction, Asean Unit Warns
body: '(Oct 5): Southeast Asia plus China, Japan and South Korea are more at risk than most economies to any potential collapse in the artificial-intelligence boom, which could trigger shocks across financial markets and the real economy. The region is “particularly exposed” because it’s at the centre of global AI supply chains and “increasingly integrated into AI-related financial markets,” the Asean+3 Macroeconomic Research Office said in its 2026 Financial Stability Report published on Monday. “A disorderly correction could therefore propagate through multiple channels — including lower technology exports, portfolio losses, capital outflows, refinancing pressure on leveraged technology and infrastructure firms, and weaker investor confidence,” it said. The report comes amid growing investor concern about the AI boom, including the high valuation of tech companies, the surge in spending on chips and data centres, and circular financing deals in which companies appear to be funding each other. Tech-related exports have been helping Asia withstand the impact of high energy prices and US tariffs. Much of the physical production in the technology cycle takes place in Asia, from memory chips in South Korea to semiconductor assembly in Malaysia. The region accounted for two-thirds of the growth in global AI-related trade, Amro said. Should AI demand suddenly fall short, a pullback in capital spending would undermine export revenues, investments and broader economic growth. Some regional equity markets are also heavily concentrated on AI, such as South Korea, exposing them to a sharp correction in prices. Other markets like Japan and Hong Kong have come to move closely in line with US AI and technology firms, meaning shocks could also be transmitted even absent a domestic trigger, according to Amro. As hyperscalers increasingly turn to borrowings to fund costly data centre buildouts, higher leverage could amplify shocks if AI returns disappoint, the report said. Opaque private credit markets and circular financing deals could worsen the instability. “A sharp correction in AI-related financial assets could spill over to the broader financial system through forced deleveraging and tighter credit conditions,” Amro said. Central bankers around the world, from the Bank of England to the Monetary Authority of Singapore, have increasingly raised concerns about whether massive AI investments can be sustainable. The technology has developed at breakneck speed, but stiff competition among developers, higher borrowing costs and growing pushback against data centres and AI’s security threats have raised concerns. title: 'UK Job Slump Longer Than During Financial Crisis, PMI Says
body: '(Oct 5): Britain’s jobs market is stuck in its longest downturn since the early 2000s, according to a closely-watched survey, surpassing the decline during the financial crisis. S&P Global’s UK purchasing managers’ index (PMI) said employers cut back on staff for a 24th consecutive month. The figures will be a concern for Andy Burnham’s government ahead of the budget later this month with the intensifying energy shock and artificial intelligence (AI) threatening to dampen demand for workers. Employers have been shedding staff since the Labour government raised payroll taxes and the minimum wage shortly after returning to power in 2024. There were some signs of the slump bottoming out, however, as job cuts in the services sector were the smallest in almost a year. Furthermore, Britain’s official unemployment rate remains much lower than during the period after the global financial crisis. Britain’s labour market has been soft despite the wider economy smashing expectations during a resilient first half of the year. S&P’s survey suggested that the private sector is largely holding up against the energy shock for now, with demand boosted by stronger consumer spending and technology services amid a rush to harness AI. The composite PMI eased to 52 in September from 52.5 the previous month, remaining above the 50 threshold separating growth from contraction. It was slightly better than the 51.7 reading in the flash estimate. Still, the outlook has darkened since a resurgence in energy prices last month that has prompted traders to ramp up bets on the Bank of England raising interest rates several times to stop inflationary pressures spreading across the economy. “Subdued demand conditions and rising inflationary pressures contributed to weaker business activity expectations for the year ahead,” said Tim Moore, economics director at S&P Global Market Intelligence. “Greater-than-expected business requirements seem to have helped to stem the jobs downturn in recent months.” The survey pointed to price pressures growing. Firms’ cost burdens and the prices they charge customers both rose at the quickest pace since June. title: 'Saudi, UAE to Cooperate in Building Crude Stockpile in Asia — Report
body: 'TOKYO (Oct 5): A framework for Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates (UAE) to cooperate with Asian countries on oil stockpiling is set to be launched, with Japan supporting the initiative through financial assistance and stockpiling expertise, the Nikkei business daily said on Monday. Saudi, UAE to cooperate in building crude stockpile in Asia, Nikkei reports The Japan-led Asia Zero-Emission Community (Azec), a grouping of 11 countries including Southeast Asian nations, will hold a ministerial meeting in the Philippines on Thursday, where senior Saudi and UAE officials are expected to announce their intention to cooperate on oil stockpiling, the Nikkei said. The framework is expected to be included in a joint statement from the meeting, providing a basis for member countries to discuss expanding oil reserves with Middle Eastern producers, it said Specific details and the scale of cooperation will be worked out through bilateral discussions with Saudi Arabia and the UAE possibly expanding exports to participating countries or providing priority supplies in an emergency, Nikkei said Japan already leases domestic private storage tanks to state-owned oil companies in countries such as Saudi Arabia under a joint stockpiling scheme, which Japanese companies can access in an emergency Japan is expected to share the framework at a ministerial dialogue of the International Energy Forum in Saudi Arabia on Oct 11, the report said. A Japanese industry ministry official who spoke on condition of anonymity confirmed there will be dialogue between Saudi Arabia and the UAE and oil-consuming countries in Asia on the sidelines of the Azec ministerial meeting, although no concrete projects will be discussed. title: 'BT Buys Over TalkTalk to Save UK's Broadband Provider From Collapse
body: '(Oct 5): BT Group plc bought TalkTalk and PlatformX Communications Ltd out of administration, preventing the collapse of a UK broadband provider that is also a major customer. The deal, which is expected to have a total cash impact of £400 million (RM2.16 billion) for the 2027 fiscal year, was made “in the public interest” after talks to sell TalkTalk’s consumer and wholesale businesses fell through, BT said in a statement on Monday. “This is a genuinely unprecedented situation, where millions of citizens and businesses were at risk if TalkTalk had collapsed,” BT chief executive officer Allison Kirkby said in the statement. “Our immediate priority is to stabilise the business and provide a safety net for the households and businesses who rely on TalkTalk.” TalkTalk has struggled under its debt load since it was bought out in 2021 by Toscafund Asset Management LLP and private equity firm Penta Capital. The company was founded as a low-cost broadband provider, reselling wholesale access on BT’s Openreach network to consumers. However, high levels of competition and persistent inflation undermined its business. The deal will pay off after TalkTalk’s business stabilises and the companies combine operations, according to BT, which maintained its financial targets. BT shares rose 1.5% to 199.2 pence at 8.56am in London. TalkTalk ended talks with Octopus Investments to sell its wholesale network division, Sky News reported last month. That came after discussions with the private equity firm Epiris didn’t result in a deal. The two companies will continue to work separately while regulators review the deal. TalkTalk, which has lost customers in recent years, was the UK’s fourth-biggest broadband provider with an 8% market share, according to a 2025 Ofcom report. BT, formerly the UK’s phone monopoly, was the largest with a 30% share. UK State Secretary for digital Lisa Nandy will weigh wider public interest when reviewing the Competition and Markets Authority’s report on antitrust concerns. Critical infrastructure, including emergency services and hospital communications rely on TalkTalk’s services, Nandy’s department said in a statement. Kirkby sought government assurances beforehand that a takeover of TalkTalk would not trigger an in-depth antitrust review, the Financial Times reported previously. Over the last year, TalkTalk reported revenues of about £1.2 billion and was loss-making. The company has about 1.5 million retail customers and one million wholesale customers in the UK. title: 'Smoky Singapore Gears Up to Talk Money Ahead of F1
body: 'SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460. This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. title: 'Bursa Malaysia dijangka pulih sederhana minggu ini
body: 'PETALING JAYA: Bursa Malaysia dijangka memasuki fasa pemulihan sederhana minggu ini selepas mengalami tekanan jualan ketara minggu lalu, dengan indeks FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dijangka bergerak dalam julat 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata. Pensyarah Kanan i-CATS University College, Kuching, Profesor Madya Dr. Abu Sofian Yaacob berkata, indeks penanda aras itu berpotensi ditutup sekitar 1,640 hingga 1,650 mata sekiranya sentimen pasaran global bertambah baik. Katanya, paras 1,620 mata merupakan tahap sokongan penting, manakala 1,650 mata pula menjadi paras rintangan utama. “Sekiranya paras 1,650 mata berjaya ditembusi secara kukuh, terdapat ruang untuk FBM KLCI menguji paras 1,660 mata. “Bagaimanapun, kenaikan dijangka tidak berlaku secara agresif kerana pelabur masih berdepan beberapa ketidaktentuan luaran. “Antaranya termasuk hasil bon Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang masih tinggi, turun naik harga minyak mentah serta ketegangan geopolitik yang boleh meningkatkan semula risiko inflasi,” katanya kepada Utusan Malaysia. Menurut Abu Sofian, data pekerjaan AS yang lebih lemah memberikan sedikit kelegaan kepada pasaran kerana mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap kemungkinan pengetatan dasar monetari yang lebih agresif oleh Rizab Persekutuan (Fed). “Pada masa sama, perkembangan Wall Street dan hala tuju kadar faedah AS akan terus menjadi antara pemacu utama sentimen Bursa Malaysia minggu ini. “Di peringkat domestik, tumpuan juga akan diberikan kepada prestasi sektor perbankan, teknologi, utiliti dan tenaga, selain aliran dana asing,” katanya. Beliau berkata, secara keseluruhannya, pergerakan pasaran minggu ini lebih mencerminkan pemulihan teknikal dan pengumpulan saham secara selektif, berbanding permulaan satu rali kukuh. “Pelabur masih dijangka mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati sehingga terdapat isyarat lebih jelas mengenai hala tuju kadar faedah global, harga minyak dan perkembangan geopolitik,” katanya. Sementara itu, CIMB Securities berkata, FBM KLCI susut 4.33 peratus bulan ke bulan atau 74.71 mata kepada 1,651 mata pada September 2026, sekali gus mencatatkan prestasi bulanan terburuk setakat tahun ini. “Penurunan itu menjadikan prestasi FBM KLCI bagi tempoh sembilan bulan pertama 2026 susut 1.72 peratus. “Tekanan jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing dan peningkatan mendadak hasil bon global mengatasi prestasi ekonomi domestik Malaysia yang kekal berdaya tahan. “Pelabur asing merekodkan jualan bersih dianggarkan RM1.69 bilion pada September 2026, manakala pegangan asing dalam ekuiti Malaysia susut ke paras terendah sepanjang masa iaitu 17.8 peratus pada akhir September 2026 berbanding 18.1 peratus pada akhir Ogos 2026,” katanya. –UTUSAN The post Bursa Malaysia dijangka pulih sederhana minggu ini appeared first on Utusan Malaysia.

title: 'Rights-based approach needed to support longer, dignified lives for older people – Suhakam
body: 'The Malaysian human rights commission, Suhakam, commemorates the International Day of Older Persons 2026 under the theme ‘The age of longevity: Rethinking systems for longer lives’. The theme highlights the need to rethink policies, institutions and systems in response to longer life expectancy and ensure that older people can continue to enjoy their rights with dignity, equality and independence. Malaysia is experiencing a significant demographic shift. According to the Department of Statistics Malaysia, people aged 60 years and above accounted for an estimated 4.1 million people or 12% of Malaysia’s population in 2025, compared with 3.9 million or 11.6% in 2024. The DoS projects that Malaysia will become an ageing nation by 2036, when the proportion of people aged 60 years and above is expected to exceed 15% of the total population. This demographic change underscores the need for Malaysia to strengthen its preparedness for an ageing society and ensure that policies, services and systems remain responsive to the changing needs of its population. Suhakam stresses that preparing for an ageing society requires more than providing care and welfare assistance. Older people must have meaningful access to economic security, employment, affordable and accessible healthcare, adequate housing and social protection. They must also be protected from abuse, neglect, exploitation and discrimination and have access to public spaces and services. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member As digitalisation increasingly shapes access to information and essential public services, efforts towards digital inclusion should also be strengthened to ensure that older people are not left behind by technological changes. Meaningful participation must remain central to policies and decisions affecting older people. Their experiences, knowledge and contributions should be recognised and valued, with opportunities for them to participate in family, community, economic and social life according to their abilities and choices. The protection and wellbeing of older people also form part of Malaysia’s broader human rights commitments, including recommendations made during Malaysia’s fourth universal periodic review in 2024 to enhance the rights, protection and wellbeing of older people. Suhakam has continued to advance discussions on the rights of older people through forums and engagements focusing on economic, social and cultural rights, including social protection, healthcare, housing, employment and other aspects of wellbeing. These engagements have also examined the implications of an ageing population and Malaysia’s preparedness to respond to the needs and rights of older people at the national and state levels. At the regional level, Suhakam in its capacity as chair of the South East Asia National Human Rights Institutions Forum for 2026, has also brought the rights of older people into regional discussions as an emerging and cross-cutting human rights issue. Suhakam also reiterates its long-standing support for the development of specific legislation to protect the rights of older people in Malaysia. As early as 2018, Suhakam fully supported the development of an older people’s bill following efforts by the Ministry of Women, Family and Community Development to address gaps in existing laws, including in relation to elder abuse and neglect. Suhakam maintains that a dedicated legal framework would strengthen the protection of older people and help ensure that their rights, dignity and wellbeing are upheld as Malaysia transitions towards an ageing society. In conjunction with the International Day of Older Persons 2026, Suhakam will also commemorate Older Persons’ Day on 7 October at Rumah Seri Kenangan Cheras under the theme ‘Celebrating our older persons!’. This will honour the wisdom, experience and contributions of older people to our communities and nation. The programme reflects Suhakam’s commitment not only to advocate for the rights of older people but also to engage with them meaningfully, recognise their contributions and affirm their place as valued members of society. On this International Day of Older Persons, Suhakam calls on the government, relevant institutions, civil society, communities and families to strengthen collective efforts towards an inclusive society where people can age with dignity, remain active and independent according to their abilities and choices, participate meaningfully in decisions and communities, and continue to enjoy their human rights throughout all stages of life. – Suhakam The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand.
