title: 'Pintu itu terbuka pada tahun 2018. Ia boleh terbuka semula
body: 'Pada malam 9 Mei 2018, saya berada di rumah, terpaku di hadapan televisyen. Saya menonton dengan penuh keterujaan yang memuncak tatkala keputusan pilihan raya umum diumumkan sedikit demi sedikit. Menjelang akhir malam itu, pemerintahan selama lebih enam dekad oleh Barisan Nasional dan gabungan pendahulunya, Alliance atau Parti Perikatan, telah berakhir. Buat pertama kalinya, Malaysia menukar kerajaan persekutuannya menerusi peti undi. Rakyat telah memilih kerajaan Pakatan Harapan yang menjanjikan reformasi yang sekian lama dinanti-nantikan. Bagi ramai antara kita yang telah bertahun-tahun memperjuangkan reformasi, ia terasa seolah-olah sebuah keajaiban politik. Kita telah menyaksikan tatanan politik yang sama bertahan mengharungi pilihan raya demi pilihan raya serta protes demi protes. Kini, apa yang dahulunya dianggap mustahil, benar-benar telah berlaku. Sebuah pintu terbuka Perubahan itu membawa harapan. Timbul satu perasaan bahawa akhirnya sebuah pintu telah pun terbuka. Isu-isu yang sekian lama dibangkitkan oleh masyarakat sivil – kebebasan bersuara, akauntabiliti, kedaulatan undang-undang dan kebebasan institusi – tiba-tiba terasa seolah-olah boleh digapai. Namun, jangkaan sering kali dipengaruhi oleh keterujaan pada saat segalanya berlaku. Apabila euforia kian pudar, jelaslah bahawa pertukaran kerajaan dengan sendirinya tidak akan membawa reformasi. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Undang-undang, institusi dan amalan politik yang telah terbina selama berdekad-dekad tidak akan berubah dalam sekelip mata. Reformasi memerlukan masa, kehendak politik dan tekanan berterusan daripada orang ramai. Bulan-bulan awal kerajaan baharu itu kelihatan menjanjikan. Namun, kemajuan terbantut, dan peristiwa ‘Langkah Sheraton’ pada tahun 2020 menyebabkan kerajaan PH tumbang. Apa yang menyusul kemudian ialah satu tempoh ketidakstabilan politik yang melelahkan. Sebahagian besar harapan pada tahun 2018 akhirnya bertukar menjadi kekecewaan. Pilihan raya umum berikutnya pada bulan November 2022 membuka satu lagi peluang. Namun, tiada gabungan parti yang berjaya memperoleh majoriti. Anwar Ibrahim, yang sekian lama dianggap sebagai wajah gerakan reformasi, dilantik sebagai perdana menteri. ‘Kerajaan perpaduan’ pimpinannya turut merangkumi BN – gabungan yang telah ditentang oleh golongan reformis selama berdekad-dekad. Kembalinya PH ke tampuk kuasa disambut dengan rasa lega selepas bertahun-tahun dilanda ketidaktentuan. Walau bagaimanapun, orang ramai kekal berhati-hati, dan perasaan itu berasas. Boleh difahami jika reformasi mengambil masa. Namun, banyak reformasi yang sekian lama dituntut oleh masyarakat sivil telah ditangguhkan, dilemahkan atau diketepikan. Undang-undang yang bersifat menindas, seperti Akta Hasutan dan Seksyen 233 Akta Komunikasi dan Multimedia, masih terus digunakan. Kadangkala ia digunakan oleh pihak-pihak yang suatu ketika dahulu pernah berkempen menentang undang-undang tersebut. Penahanan pemimpin Mandiri Layanan yang diterima baru-baru ini oleh kumpulan yang diterajui golongan muda, Mandiri, menunjukkan betapa jauh lagi perjalanan yang perlu ditempuhi. Menurut Mandiri, awal bulan ini [September], akaun bank mereka dibekukan dan larangan perjalanan dikenakan tanpa sebarang penjelasan kepada umum. Kemudian, pada 18 September, pihak polis menyerbu pejabat yang dikongsi oleh Mandiri dengan Hayat, sebuah kumpulan yang menentang hukuman mati. Seterusnya, pada 22 September, polis menahan pengarah eksekutif Mandiri, Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi, dan pengarah kewangannya, Dobby Chew, di bawah undang-undang pencegahan pengubahan wang haram. Mereka telah hadir secara sukarela di hadapan pegawai penyiasat untuk memberikan keterangan. Kedua-duanya kemudian dibebaskan, namun siasatan masih diteruskan. Walau apa pun kesudahannya, cara tindakan keras ini dilakukan menghantar mesej yang menggerunkan kepada sesiapa sahaja yang bersuara. Undang-undang yang bertujuan memerangi pengubahan wang haram tidak seharusnya digunakan untuk menakut-nakutkan masyarakat sivil. Perkara ini tidak boleh diterima di bawah kerajaan yang pernah berjanji untuk membuka ruang demokrasi. Pihak berkuasa mesti mendedahkan asas siasatan tersebut serta menarik balik pembekuan akaun dan larangan perjalanan yang dikenakan tanpa penjelasan. Mereka juga mesti menghentikan penggunaan kuasa pencegahan pengubahan wang haram terhadap kumpulan masyarakat sivil. Nampaknya, pertukaran pihak yang memerintah tidak menjamin perubahan dalam cara kuasa digunakan. Itulah sebabnya detik sekarang ini penting. Tekanan terhadap masyarakat sivil bukanlah satu isu terpencil. Ia merupakan sebahagian daripada kerja reformasi demokrasi yang belum selesai. Malah, kemajuan yang perlahan menjadikan peranan masyarakat sivil semakin penting, bukan sebaliknya. Apabila kerajaan bertukar tetapi struktur asas kekal, perlu ada pihak yang bersedia untuk mempersoalkan, meneliti dan menuntut akauntabiliti. Hal ini telah difahami oleh Aliran sejak ditubuhkan pada tahun 1977. Ia terus membangkitkan persoalan mengenai demokrasi, hak asasi manusia dan keadilan sosial di bawah setiap kerajaan yang pernah memerintah Malaysia. Setelah terlibat dengan Aliran selama hampir dua dekad, saya sendiri telah menyaksikan beberapa perubahan tersebut. Saya juga melihat betapa mudahnya untuk berasa tawar hati apabila, selepas bertahun-tahun berjuang, kemajuan tidak sentiasa dicapai sepantas yang kita harapkan. Harapan dalam perjuangan yang panjang Namun, kita juga harus mengingati tahun 2018. Selama bertahun-tahun, perubahan kelihatan mustahil. Kemudian, secara tidak disangka-sangka, ia berlaku. Perkara ini seharusnya membuatkan kita berhati-hati untuk tidak menganggap keadaan hari ini sebagai sesuatu yang kekal. Kita tidak tahu bila perubahan akan berlaku lagi, atau dalam bentuk apa ia akan muncul. Namun, masa depan tidak terikat kepada masa kini. Itulah erti harapan dalam sebuah perjuangan yang panjang. Ia bukanlah satu kepastian bahawa segala-galanya akan menjadi seperti yang kita inginkan. Ia adalah kesedaran bahawa keadaan boleh berubah, dan bahawa apa yang kita lakukan sementara itu penting. Václav Havel menghabiskan masa bertahun-tahun sebagai seorang disiden sebelum menjadi presiden Cekoslovakia yang bebas. Beliau mengungkapkannya begini: harapan “bukanlah keyakinan bahawa sesuatu perkara akan berakhir dengan baik, tetapi kepastian bahawa sesuatu perkara itu bermakna, tidak kira bagaimana kesudahannya nanti.” Perjuangan demi Malaysia yang lebih demokratik sejak awal lagi tidak mungkin dimenangi hanya melalui satu pilihan raya atau satu kerajaan. Pengajaran tahun 2018 bukanlah bahawa perubahan itu mudah. Pengajarannya ialah bahawa perubahan itu boleh berlaku. Dan apabila kemajuan kelihatan perlahan, itu sudah cukup menjadi alasan untuk kita terus melangkah. title: 'MAPIM sasar RM5 juta bantu 66,000 penduduk Gaza - SAHIH
body:

MAPIM sasar RM5 juta bantu 66,000 penduduk Gaza

KUALA LUMPUR: Sekurang-kurangnya RM5 juta disasarkan untuk dikumpul Majlis Perundingan Pertubuhan Islam Malaysia (MAPIM) bagi membantu kira-kira 66,000 penduduk Gaza menghadapi musim sejuk yang semakin hampir.

Presiden MAPIM, Mohd Azmi Abdul Hamid berkata, kutipan menerusi Tabung Kemanusiaan Musim Sejuk Gaza 2026-2027 yang bermula hari ini akan berlangsung sehingga April tahun depan.

Menurutnya, bantuan akan disalurkan secara berperingkat bermula hujung Oktober ini, sebelum diteruskan pada pertengahan November serta Januari hingga April tahun depan.

“Bantuan meliputi makanan, pakaian musim sejuk, ubat-ubatan, keperluan kanak-kanak, khemah dan paling utama bekalan air bersih.

“Kita akan cuba menghantar kumpulan pertama bantuan hujung Oktober ini dan diteruskan secara berperingkat sehingga April,” katanya.

Beliau berkata demikian ketika ditemui pada Majlis Makan Malam Amal dan Pelancaran Kempen Bantuan Kemanusiaan Musim Sejuk Gaza 2026-2027, di sini, Ahad.

Mohd Azmi berkata, bantuan itu semakin mendesak berikutan musim sejuk bakal tiba dan dijangka berlangsung serentak dengan Ramadan pada awal tahun depan.

Katanya, MAPIM kini mengenal pasti rakan kerjasama di Malaysia dan Gaza bagi memastikan setiap bantuan dapat disampaikan secara telus dan berkesan.

Antara yang dipertimbangkan ialah Jawatankuasa Palang Merah Antarabangsa (ICRC), Doctors Without Borders serta beberapa organisasi kemanusiaan antarabangsa lain.

Menurutnya, MAPIM turut meneliti kaedah paling berkesan sama ada membeli barangan di Jordan atau Mesir sebelum dibawa masuk ke Gaza atau mendapatkan terus bekalan yang masih tersedia di wilayah berkenaan.

“Kalau kita gunakan kontena, ada masalah termasuk kemungkinan terpaksa menunggu lama untuk masuk sehingga menyebabkan barangan terutama makanan rosak.

“Kalau RM5 juta itu dikira berdasarkan kontena, jumlahnya tidak kurang daripada 20 kontena,” katanya.

Beliau berkata, MAPIM juga bersedia menggunakan laluan kemasukan yang dijangka tersedia pada November sekiranya ia berjaya dibuka.

Katanya, usaha itu memerlukan kerjasama kerajaan Malaysia dan Mesir terutama bagi mendapatkan kebenaran supaya bantuan dapat dibawa masuk ke Gaza.

Kempen berkenaan menyasarkan kira-kira 66,000 penerima di Khan Younis, Rafah, Deir Al-Balah, Jabalia dan Gaza City.

Orang ramai serta syarikat yang mahu menyumbang boleh menyalurkan sumbangan melalui akaun rasmi MAPIM di CIMB 8604556678.-SAHIH

title: 'EdgeProp Daily Digest — 6 October 2026 | EdgeProp
body: 'Daily Digest · Tuesday, 6 October 2026· Updated: about 4 hours ago Scientex proposes RM580.16m Pulai land purchase; Sunway Ipoh Mall reaches 80% leasing Scientex proposed a RM580.16 million Pulai land purchase, while Sunway reported 80% leasing at its upcoming Ipoh mall. Privasia received conditional approval for a Perak data centre. Residential launch reports, warehouse contracts, Merdeka 118 leasing figures and new fire-safety requirements broadened the property news flow ahead of Budget 2027. Quick takes - Privasia’s Silver Streams Technofarm received MITI approval for its Bagan Datuk data centre, on Tuesday (Oct 6). The approval letter was dated Sept 7 and required an off-grid energy supply with maximum demand of 50MW, compliant with applicable energy and renewable-energy rules. Approval did not establish that the power supply had been secured - Housing and data centre efficiency conditions feature in pre-Budget priorities, OCBC said. Its report specified neither housing allocations nor efficiency requirements. It identified development spending, estimated at RM86 billion annually under the 13th Malaysia Plan, as the main adjustment lever. Budget 2027 is scheduled for tabling on Oct 9. - Developer SevenCo broke ground on its first Klang Valley residential project, Maison Sungai Besi in Taman Castlefield, Kuala Lumpur. EdgeProp reported a 48-storey tower with 537 homes measuring 721 to 1,206 sq ft. The developer planned solar panels and EV charging bays. The ceremony marked construction commencement rather than completed homes. - Axis REIT had RM250 million in acquisitions under negotiation, with one or two announcements possible before year-end, Maybank Investment Bank said. The Edge reported that earlier seven-year and ten-year financing provided some protection against rising rates. Gearing was forecast at about 39% after signed acquisitions; the negotiating pipeline remained prospective Scientex signs conditional agreement for 14 Pulai parcels Packaging manufacturer and property developer Scientex Bhd proposed buying 14 freehold parcels in Mukim Pulai, Johor Bahru, for RM580.16 million. Its wholly owned subsidiary Scientex Quatari Sdn Bhd signed the conditional agreement with Pangkal Budiman Sdn Bhd, a subsidiary of Leong Hup Holdings Sdn Bhd, on Oct 6. The filing put the aggregate area at 502.5906 acres, or 21,892,847 sq ft, and the price at RM26.50 per sq ft. The land adjoins Taman Pulai Mutiara, Taman Pulai Mutiara 2, Taman Pulai Duta and Taman Pulai Duta 2. Scientex proposed a mixed-property development, but had not determined its gross development value, costs, profits or timetable. It said more than 90% of units launched in its existing Pulai developments had been sold. Completion was targeted for 2H2027, subject to block-title renewal and applicable land-transfer approvals. Funding would combine internal funds and borrowings. No independent valuation was undertaken, and shareholder approval was not required. The acquisition supported Scientex’s stated target of completing 50,000 affordable homes nationwide by 2028. Why it matters The purchase would expand Scientex’s landbank beside existing projects. Development value and delivery dates remained undetermined, and completion depended on the agreement’s conditions. Sunway Ipoh Mall reports leasing commitments ahead of 2027 opening Shopping mall owner and operator Sunway Malls said Sunway Ipoh Mall was 80% leased ahead of its scheduled 4Q2027 opening. Its Oct 6 statement described a RM1 billion development with 1.2 million sq ft of net lettable area across four retail floors and 400 shops. It unveiled 25 brands and concepts, including seven anchors and nine brands making their Perak debut. The mall forms part of the 1,350-acre Sunway City Ipoh township. Planned facilities include an ice rink, a 36-lane bowling centre, an exhibition centre and a ten-hall cinema. Sunway said portfolio occupancy was 98%, against a national average of 79%, and first-half sales grew 5%, compared with industry growth of 3.1%. Both comparisons were supplied by the group. At the same tenant-unveiling event, group managing director HC Chan sought Budget 2027 relief on mall electricity costs and SST. He proposed extending protection from fuel-adjustment charges to malls and considering an SST reduction to 3%. These remained industry requests, with no government approval announced. Why it matters Leasing commitments established part of the tenant base before opening. The mall's operating-cost proposals remained separate from any measures the government might adopt in Budget 2027. Bomba says designated premises must appoint fire-safety personnel from April 2027 Owners of 9,451 designated buildings will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers and Fire Safety Officers from April 1, 2027, Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said, according to Bernama on Oct 6. He said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, concerning the establishment of a Fire Safety Organisation at designated premises. He said owners would receive preparation periods of six to 18 months before full enforcement, depending on existing Fire Certificate expiry dates and inspection schedules. Nor Hisham said annual inspection reports prepared by managers would be assessed for certificate renewal, reducing the need for the department to inspect every building physically each year. The department expected appointments of 6,000 managers and 18,000 officers nationwide for industry needs from 2026 to 2030. It had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase providers and instructors. The requirement concerned designated premises subject to Fire Certificate obligations, rather than every property. Why it matters Affected building owners would need qualified personnel and an internal fire-safety organisation. Preparation and enforcement would depend on certificate renewal and inspection schedules. Also on the radar today Kimori report puts Phase 1 bookings at 73% Developer Premierex reported 73% bookings for Phase 1 of Kimori Residences in EdgeProp’s Oct 6 article, following the Oct 3 launch in Bukit Serdang. The freehold development comprises 418 units, with prices from RM481,600 and expected completion in 4Q2029. Layouts measure approximately 857 sq ft and 1,095 sq ft. The current report describes bookings, rather than completed sales. Setia and Gentari explore EV charging at selected developments S P Setia and Gentari Green Mobility signed an MoU to explore EV charging at selected Setia developments on Tuesday (Oct 6). The Oct 5 media release covered site identification, feasibility, installation, operation and maintenance. No sites, charging-point count or value were stated. Deployment remained subject to further work. Merdeka 118 rating report details leasing and housing plans MARC affirmed AAAIS/Stable on PNB Merdeka Ventures’ sukuk programme of up to RM6 billion, backed by PNB’s guarantee. About 70% of office space was sub-leased, while mall agreements covering 81% were signed or under negotiation. Two residential buildings with RM2 billion GDV were targeted for 1H2027 launch. EPF raises Pavilion REIT holding to 13.209% EPF acquired 12.24 million Pavilion REIT units on Sept 30, lifting its holding to 519.31 million units, or 13.209%, on Tuesday (Oct 6). Its previous holding was approximately 507.07 million units. The notice was dated Oct 1 and received on Oct 5. The transaction changed ownership of existing units. IJM appoints Johan Idris as chairman Construction and property conglomerate IJM appointed former KPMG Malaysia managing partner Datuk Johan Idris as independent non-executive chairman, effective Oct 5. EdgeProp’s Oct 6 report said Datuk Lee Teck Yuen was redesignated non-independent non-executive director. The change followed Tan Sri Krishnan Tan’s Aug 27 retirement and Lee’s interim chairmanship. MKH credit unit discloses RM127.92m loan balance Property developer MKH’s moneylending subsidiary disclosed unaudited outstanding loans and advances of RM127.92 million at Sept 30, including RM119.5 million in unsecured intra-group lending. EdgeProp’s Oct 6 report cited the Oct 5 filing. Defaults of at least three months totalled RM25,485, unchanged over the financial year; the disclosed default ratio was 0.020%. Penang reports RM2.3 billion in approved MedTech investment Penang recorded RM2.3 billion in approved MedTech investments across 40 projects from 2021 to 1Q2026, Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said, according to Bernama. Nearly 4,500 jobs were associated with the investments. The figures described a multi-year manufacturing pipeline, rather than new approvals issued today, and provided context for the state’s industrial economy. Land council considers tax-rate proposals and administration The National Land Council considered resubmitted Kedah and Perlis land-tax proposals, while Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim urged stronger action on encroachment. At the same meeting, Sarawak offered its eLASIS expertise, covering about 67 transaction types. The reports did not establish that revised tax rates had taken effect. Strategist calls for clearer Sarawak grid-access rules AGL Australia principal energy strategist Anselm Chang called for published grid-access pricing and clearer rules as Sarawak faced competing electricity demands from industry, exports and data centres. Borneo Post’s Oct 6 report covered his Oct 5 proposals for battery storage, rooftop solar and demand response. These were recommendations at IDECS, rather than new grid-access regulations or project approvals. Futurist proposes underwater data-centre opportunities Scientific futurist Dr Cathrine Ball proposed underwater data centres and solar infrastructure as opportunities for Sarawak, Borneo Post reported from IDECS. She cited the state’s subsea cable connections and existing floating solar infrastructure. The remarks described possible uses of established infrastructure; they did not announce a funded underwater data-centre development or construction timetable. Brokers assess housing support and infrastructure before Budget 2027 RHB expected stronger development spending to support construction awards, while household assistance could benefit property, Bloomberg reported. CIMB identified water, flood mitigation, rural infrastructure, grid investment and East Malaysian projects as potential beneficiaries. RHB also highlighted proposed price adjustments for bitumen and diesel. These remained forecasts before Oct 9 tabling. Everly Lhesson holds formal opening in Kuching The 238-room Everly Lhesson Kuching, above Vivacity Megamall, was officially opened by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg on Oct 6. He called for more quality accommodation ahead of major events, including the 2027 SEA Games, saying Kuching’s existing 13,000 hotel rooms were insufficient to meet growing demand. Today's roundup Landbank expansion and reported retail leasing pointed to continued development activity, alongside residential launches and plans for further housing supply. The reports reflected different stages of progress, from conditional purchases and bookings to leasing ahead of opening, with approvals and delivery still relevant to the eventual outcome. Asset operations also featured prominently. Fire-safety arrangements will require affected owners to prepare for additional responsibilities, while electricity costs, grid access and charging infrastructure remain considerations for developers and property managers. Hospitality demand added another dimension as Sarawak prepares for major events. The infrastructure and investment reports provided context for future property demand, but targets, approved investments and proposed technologies carried different levels of certainty. Ahead of Budget 2027, household support and development spending remained areas to watch. Their effects on housing demand, construction opportunities and operating costs will depend on the measures tabled and implemented. title: 'Cara mengelola keuangan di tengah gaya hidup tanpa dompet
body: 'JawaPos.com - Gaya hidup tanpa dompet fisik semakin lekat dengan keseharian generasi muda. Berbagai kebutuhan, mulai dari transaksi hingga menyiapkan dana masa depan, kini dapat dilakukan melalui layanan digital.  Melihat trend ini,  PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk (CIMB Niaga) meluncurkan OCTO untuk Pejuang Mimpi, sebuah inisiatif yang dirancang untuk membantu generasi muda mengelola keuangan secara lebih mudah, praktis, dan relevan dengan gaya hidup digital masa kini.  Head of Marketing, Brand & Customers Experience CIMB Niaga Amir Widjaya mengatakan, di tengah berbagai peluang yang tersedia saat ini, kemampuan mengelola keuangan menjadi salah satu fondasi penting agar generasi muda dapat terus berkembang dan mencapai tujuan hidup mereka.  “Karena itu, CIMB Niaga ingin hadir sebagai partner yang membantu mereka mengambil langkah finansial yang tepat sejak dini,” ujar Amir Widjaya pada talkshow “OCTO Go Dompetless, Wear Pocketless” yang menjadi bagian dari rangkaian Kejar Mimpi FEST 2026 di Senayan City, Jakarta, Sabtu (3/10/2026).  Untuk menjawab kebutuhan tersebut, CIMB Niaga menghadirkan OCTO melalui pendekatan Jurus O-C-T-O, yaitu Olah Dana, Capai Mimpi, Tangkis Risiko, dan Optimalkan Keseruan.  Melalui OCTO, generasi muda dapat mengelola kebutuhan finansial sehari-hari, menabung, berinvestasi, mempersiapkan dana untuk masa depan, serta menikmati berbagai pengalaman hidup secara lebih bijak.  Generasi muda juga dapat membuka rekening secara digital hanya dalam beberapa menit dan menikmati berbagai kemudahan transaksi sehari-hari, mulai dari transfer, pembayaran, dan top up e-wallet hingga akses ke berbagai pilihan tabungan dan investasi. Kemudahan tersebut dihadirkan agar mereka dapat memulai perjalanan finansial dengan lebih praktis dan sesuai kebutuhan.  Adopsi OCTO terus menunjukkan tren positif. Pada semester I 2026, transaksi QRIS melalui OCTO meningkat 65% secara year-on-year (YoY), sementara pembukaan rekening pertama melalui OCTO tumbuh 89% YoY. Selain itu, transaksi reksa dana meningkat 48% YoY dan transaksi obligasi naik 112% YoY, mencerminkan semakin tingginya preferensi nasabah terhadap layanan perbankan digital yang praktis, mudah, dan terintegrasi.  Pada kesempatan yang sama, CIMB Niaga juga memperkenalkan kampanye Go Dompetless, Wear Pocketless yang merefleksikan perubahan gaya hidup generasi muda yang semakin mengandalkan teknologi digital dalam berbagai aktivitas sehari-hari, termasuk bertransaksi dan mengelola keuangan.  “Go Dompetless, Wear Pocketless bukan sekadar soal meninggalkan dompet fisik. Ini merupakan simbol gaya hidup yang lebih praktis, fleksibel, dan efisien. Ketika urusan finansial menjadi lebih mudah, anak muda memiliki lebih banyak ruang untuk fokus mengembangkan potensi, mengejar passion, dan mewujudkan mimpi yang ingin mereka capai,” kata Amir.  Sebagai bagian dari rangkaian acara, CIMB Niaga menghadirkan fashion show bertema Pocketless, sebuah kampanye dengan semangat “The New Fashion Movement in Jakarta” yang mengeksplorasi semangat generasi muda dalam mengekspresikan diri.  “Kami percaya setiap generasi memiliki cara sendiri untuk mengejar mimpi. Melalui OCTO, kami ingin membantu generasi muda mengambil keputusan finansial dengan lebih percaya diri dan memiliki lebih banyak ruang untuk fokus pada aspirasi yang ingin mereka wujudkan,” tutup Amir.
description: 'Peluncuran OCTO untuk Pejuang Mimpi bagian dari komitmen berkelanjutan CIMB Niaga mendukung generasi muda mengembangkan potensi dan mengambil langkah nyata menuju masa depan yang mereka impikan.

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi disokong peningkatan penerimaan risiko - Portal Berita RTM
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR, 5 Oktober – Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi sedikit hari ini sejajar dengan prestasi positif di pasaran serantau susulan penerimaan risiko yang bertambah baik.

Peningkatan penerimaan risiko ini disokong oleh data lemah pasaran buruh Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang meredakan jangkaan Rizab Persekutuan AS mengetatkan dasarnya serta tekanan ke atas hasil bon.

Pada 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 0.88 mata kepada 1,631.75 daripada paras penutup 1,630.87 pada Jumaat minggu lepas.

Indeks petunjuk pasaran yang dibuka tinggi naik 2.55 mata kepada 1,633.42, bergerak antara paras 1,630.95 dan 1,640.46 sepanjang sesi dagangan.

Bagaimanapun, di keseluruhan pasaran, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 599 berbanding 564, manakala 523 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,087 tidak diniagakan dan 24 digantung.

Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion daripada 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion pada Jumaat minggu lepas.

Naib presiden penyelidikan ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata kaunter teknologi merupakan antara saham yang meraih keuntungan tinggi.

Di Wall Street semalaman, indeks S&P 500 meningkat 0.73 peratus kepada 7,722.72 dan Nasdaq Composite naik 1.19 peratus kepada 27,190.86.

Beliau berkata pasaran saham tempatan dijangka kekal positif dalam tempoh terdekat ini memandangkan FBM KLCI masih berada dalam kedudukan terlebih jual susulan penurunan ketara minggu lepas yang mana keadaan ini dijangka terus menarik minat pembelian pada harga rendah khususnya bagi saham mewah terpilih.

“Kecairan domestik juga terus menyokong, dengan institusi tempatan merekodkan pembelian bersih sebanyak RM352.4 juta pada minggu lepas, walaupun aktiviti penjualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing kekal menjadi faktor hambatan,” katanya kepada Bernama.

Justeru, Thong menjangkakan indeks petunjuk pasaran akan mencatatkan pemulihan secara beransur-ansur namun kekal tidak menentu, dengan FBM KLCI berkemungkinan diniagakan dalam jajaran 1,620-1,650 pada minggu ini.

Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Public Bank meningkat lima sen kepada RM4.71, CIMB naik lapan sen kepada RM7.73, Tenaga Nasional menokok empat sen kepada RM13.00, Maybank susut dua sen kepada RM10.00, dan IHH Healthcare turun empat sen kepada RM7.76.

Dalam kalangan saham aktif, V.S Industry meningkat tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 6.5 sen, Jaks Resources turun sedikit sebanyak satu sen kepada 17 sen, Excel Force MSC merosot empat sen kepada 17 sen, manakala NationGate tidak berubah pada RM1.83.

Dalam kalangan kaunter paling untung, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.00 kepada RM43.40, UMS Integration melonjak 37 sen kepada RM9.40, Kelington naik 49 sen kepada RM9.12, Nestle menokok 48 sen kepada RM90.00, dan Samaiden menambah 35 sen kepada RM3.19.

Dalam kalangan saham paling rugi, Batu Kawan susut RM1.48 kepada RM18.98, United Plantations turun 32 sen kepada RM31.06, Hengyuan Refining Company berkurangan 18 sen kepada RM3.46 manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong dan YTL Power International menyusut 14 sen masing-masing kepada RM20.86 dan RM5.54.

Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 meningkat 61.56 mata kepada 17,543.49, Indeks FBM Emas menambah 19.78 mata kepada 12,190.35, Indeks FBM Top 100 naik 15.70 mata kepada 11,973.38, Indeks FBM Emas Shariah menokok 8.69 mata kepada 12,069.01 dan Indeks FBM ACE melonjak 77.15 mata kepada 5,606.61.

Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian naik sedikit sebanyak 0.45 mata kepada 178.97 dan Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menambah 99.63 mata kepada 19,140.14, manakala Indeks Tenaga susut 3.09 mata kepada 829.94 dan Indeks Perladangan turun 125.52 mata kepada 8,931.03.

Jumlah dagangan Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 3.13 bilion unit bernilai RM2.41 bilion daripada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion pada Jumaat minggu lepas.

Jumlah dagangan waran naik kepada 1.04 bilion unit bernilai RM208.20 juta daripada 973.40 juta unit bernilai RM160.21 juta sebelumnya.

Jumlah dagangan Pasaran ACE menokok kepada 611.02 juta unit bernilai RM267.66 juta daripada 593.05 juta unit bernilai RM205.21 juta.

Sementara itu, kaunter produk dan perkhidmatan pengguna menyumbang sebanyak 248.10 juta saham di Pasaran Utama, diikuti produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (439.37 juta), pembinaan (183.56 juta), teknologi (1.76 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (49.02 juta), hartanah (106.95 juta), perladangan (22.08 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (10.76 juta), dana tertutup (152,900), tenaga (106.66 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (103.20 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (22.11 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (40.92 juta), utiliti (38.48 juta), serta amanah perniagaan (162,200). -BERNAMA

title: 'Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi susulan selera risiko bertambah baik
body: 'H: Bursa Malaysia ditutup tinggi susulan sentimen risiko bertambah baik KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia ditutup sedikit tinggi pada 5 Oktorber seiring pasaran serantau yang positif, susulan selera risiko bertambah baik berikutan data pekerjaan Amerika Syarikat (AS) yang lebih lemah, sekali gus mengurangkan jangkaan kenaikan kadar faedah lanjut oleh Rizab Persekutuan AS (Fed) dan meredakan tekanan terhadap hasil bon. Pada jam 5 petang, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) meningkat 0.88 mata kepada 1,631.75 berbanding 1,630.87 pada penutupan Jumaat lalu. Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 2.55 mata lebih tinggi pada 1,633.42 dan bergerak antara paras 1,630.95 hingga 1,640.46 sepanjang sesi dagangan. Bagaimanapun, di pasaran lebih meluas, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung dengan 599 berbanding 564, manakala 523 kaunter tidak berubah, 1,087 tidak diniagakan dan 24 kaunter digantung. Jumlah dagangan meningkat kepada 4.78 bilion unit bernilai RM2.89 bilion berbanding 4.23 bilion unit bernilai RM2.70 bilion pada Jumaat lalu. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata saham teknologi antara yang mendapat manfaat utama daripada sentimen pasaran yang bertambah baik. Beliau berkata, di Wall Street pada Jumaat lalu, S&P 500 meningkat 0.73 peratus kepada 7,722.72 mata, manakala Nasdaq Composite menokok 1.19 peratus kepada 27,190.86 mata. "Bagi pasaran tempatan, kami kekal sedikit positif dalam tempoh terdekat kerana FBM KLCI masih berada dalam keadaan terlebih jual selepas pembetulan ketara minggu lalu, yang sepatutnya terus menarik aktiviti pembelian ketika harga rendah, khususnya dalam saham mewah terpilih. "Kecairan domestik juga kekal menyokong pasaran, dengan institusi tempatan merekodkan pembelian bersih RM352.4 juta minggu lalu, walaupun jualan berterusan oleh pelabur asing kekal sebagai cabaran," katanya kepada Bernama. Sehubungan itu, Thong menjangkakan indeks penanda aras akan mencatat pemulihan secara beransur-ansur, namun kekal tidak menentu, dengan FBM KLCI dijangka didagangkan dalam julat 1,620 hingga 1,650 mata minggu ini. Dalam kalangan saham berwajaran tinggi, Public Bank meningkat lima sen kepada RM4.71, CIMB menokok lapan sen kepada RM7.73, Tenaga Nasional naik empat sen kepada RM13.00, Maybank susut dua sen kepada RM10.00, manakala IHH Healthcare turun empat sen kepada RM7.76. Dalam dagangan aktif, V.S Industry meningkat tiga sen kepada 32 sen, Zetrix AI susut lima sen kepada 6.5 sen, Jaks Resources turun satu sen kepada 17 sen, Excel Force MSC merosot empat sen kepada 17 sen, manakala NationGate tidak berubah pada RM1.83. Antara kaunter untung utama, Malaysian Pacific Industries meningkat RM1.00 kepada RM43.40, UMS Integration melonjak 37 sen kepada RM9.40, Kelington menokok 49 sen kepada RM9.12, Nestle meningkat 48 sen kepada RM90.00, manakala Samaiden melonjak 35 sen kepada RM3.19. Kaunter rugi utama diketuai Batu Kawan yang merosot RM1.48 kepada RM18.98, diikuti United Plantations yang susut 32 sen kepada RM31.06, Hengyuan Refining Company turun 18 sen kepada RM3.46, manakala Kuala Lumpur Kepong dan YTL Power International masing-masing susut 14 sen kepada RM20.86 dan RM5.54. Di papan indeks, FBM Mid 70 meningkat 61.56 mata kepada 17,543.49, FBM Emas menokok 19.78 mata kepada 12,190.35, FBM Top 100 naik 15.70 mata kepada 11,973.38, FBM Emas Shariah meningkat 8.69 mata kepada 12,069.01, manakala FBM ACE melonjak 77.15 mata kepada 5,606.61. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian meningkat 0.45 mata kepada 178.97, Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan menokok 99.63 mata kepada 19,140.14, manakala Indeks Tenaga susut 3.09 mata kepada 829.94 dan Indeks Perladangan merosot 125.52 mata kepada 8,931.03. Jumlah dagangan di Pasaran Utama meningkat kepada 3.13 bilion unit bernilai RM2.41 bilion daripada 2.67 bilion unit bernilai RM2.34 bilion pada Jumaat lalu. Dagangan waran meningkat kepada 1.04 bilion unit bernilai RM208.20 juta berbanding 973.40 juta unit bernilai RM160.21 juta sebelumnya. Jumlah dagangan di Pasaran ACE meningkat kepada 611.02 juta unit bernilai RM267.66 juta daripada 593.05 juta unit bernilai RM205.21 juta pada Jumaat. Sementara itu, kaunter produk dan perkhidmatan pengguna mencatatkan 248.10 juta saham didagangkan di Pasaran Utama, produk dan perkhidmatan perindustrian (439.37 juta), pembinaan (183.56 juta), teknologi (1.76 bilion), perkhidmatan kewangan (49.02 juta), hartanah (106.95 juta), perladangan (22.08 juta), amanah pelaburan hartanah (10.76 juta), dana tertutup (152,900), tenaga (106.66 juta), penjagaan kesihatan (103.20 juta), telekomunikasi dan media (22.11 juta), pengangkutan dan logistik (40.92 juta), utiliti (38.48 juta) serta amanah perniagaan (162,200). --BERNAMA

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Edges Higher as Risk Appetite Improves - MCI Group
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 5 — Bursa Malaysia closed slightly higher today, in line with upbeat regional markets, as improved risk appetite was supported by softer US labour data, that reduced expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening and eased pressure on bond yields. At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) rose 0.88 of-a-point to 1,631.75 from last Friday’s close of 1,630.87. title: 'A Reformasi government that arrests reformasi activists?
body: 'Kua Kia Soong Malaysia now has a Reformasi government arresting Reformasi activists. On 22 September, Amir Hariri Abdul Hadi, executive director of youth-led NGO Mandiri, and Dobby Chew, its finance director, were arrested under the anti-money-laundering law Amla after voluntarily presenting themselves to police to assist an investigation. They were remanded for three days and released on 24 September. Police say the investigation concerns suspected unlawful funds and that five bank accounts have been frozen. No, they are not podcasters. The podcasters came earlier. On 6 August, Brian Kong of Let’s Get It Podcast and Shamsul Saad of The Gut Shot Podcast were arrested and remanded for two days over an episode ‘Malaysia introduced me to racism’, which police said raised racial and religious sensitivities. They were investigated under the Sedition Act, Penal Code and Communications and Multimedia Act. So here we are. Activists arrested. Podcasters arrested. Human rights defenders investigated. Civil society bank accounts frozen. And this is supposed to be the government born of Reformasi. Perhaps the slogan has undergone a little institutional reform itself: - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Reformasi – formerly a movement against the machinery of repression. Reformasi 2.0 – now operating the machinery. The joke would be complete if the government announced that the next Reformasi rally will be held at the nearest police lock-up. The question for the former reformers This is where I would particularly like to hear from those who once stood on the other side of the barricades. Adam Adli was a student activist who became a symbol of youthful dissent before entering government. He is now deputy higher education minister. Fahmi Fadzil, once associated with the Reformasi generation, is now communications minister – the very portfolio intimately connected with freedom of expression and the regulation of online speech. Parliament records him as the minister responsible for the communications and multimedia legislation. So, gentlemen, a simple question: Where are your red lines? Is there a point at which the arrest of activists becomes unacceptable? A point at which the detention of journalists or podcasters becomes intolerable? A point at which laws inherited from the old order are used so aggressively that you say: “Enough. This is not the Reformasi we fought for”? And if that point exists, what is it? Is there a line beyond which you would resign in protest rather than remain in office and defend the indefensible? Or has entering government produced a miraculous transformation in political eyesight – where the handcuffs that once looked oppressive from the outside suddenly look perfectly reasonable from the inside? This is not a question about party loyalty. It is a question of principle. The great Reformasi rinse cycle Malaysia has seen this movie before. First comes the noble language: Reform. Justice. Democracy. Freedom. Rule of law. Then comes power. Then comes the discovery that the laws used against one’s opponents are actually rather useful. And finally comes the most beautiful phrase in the administrative vocabulary: “Let the authorities do their job.” Of course, the authorities must investigate genuine criminal allegations. But democracy requires another job to be done as well: the government must restrain the machinery of the state when that machinery threatens legitimate civil society, freedom of expression and political dissent. The UN special rapporteur on human rights defenders has already urged the Malaysian authorities to halt measures that misuse anti-money-laundering or anti-terrorism laws to harass or unduly restrict human rights defenders. Several international rights organisations likewise raised due process and chilling effect concerns over the crackdow on Mandiri and Hayat. These are not trivial questions. In a democracy, remand is not conviction. But deprivation of liberty is still deprivation of liberty. Perhaps the greatest irony is that many of today’s government politicians once understood this perfectly. They knew that democracy was not simply about winning elections. They knew that civil society had to be free to criticise the government. They knew that dissent was not treason. They knew that activists were not enemies of the state. So what happened? Did Reformasi finally succeed – only to discover that the former rebels had become the establishment? Or did the establishment simply swallow Reformasi whole? There is an old political warning: Power does not necessarily corrupt. Sometimes it merely reveals whether your principles were conditional on not having power. That is why the question to the former Reformasi activists now in government is so simple: What are your red lines? If an activist is arrested, what will make you speak? If a podcaster is detained, what will make you act? If freedom of expression is curtailed, what will make you resign? If the laws once used against you are now being used against the next generation of activists, how many arrests will it take before you say: “This is no longer Reformasi”? If there are no red lines, perhaps Malaysians should stop calling this a Reformasi government. Perhaps it is simply another government that has discovered the comfortable side of power. And perhaps the most appropriate Reformasi slogan for Malaysia in 2026 is: ‘Reformasi – please report to the lock-up.’ Dr Kua Kia Soong, a former MP, is the director of human rights group Suaram. title: 'PTT Synergy beli 4 kilang dalam pembinaan bernilai RM32 juta di Klang jana hasil sewa berulang - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 5 Okt — PTT Synergy Group Berhad bakal memperluas portfolio hartanah dengan pemerolehan empat unit kilang bernilai hampir RM32 juta di Klang, Selangor, yang disasarkan menjana pendapatan sewa berulang daripada penyewa industri. Menerusi makluman tambahan kepada Bursa Malaysia, ia berkata anak syarikat tidak langsung milik penuhnya, PTT Assets Sdn Bhd, akan memperoleh empat bidang tanah bersama unit kilang yang sedang atau akan dibina dengan jumlah pertimbangan tunai RM31.997 juta. Menurut kumpulan tersebut, pemerolehan itu bertujuan mengembangkan portfolio pelaburan hartanah kumpulan dan mewujudkan aliran pendapatan sewa berulang menerusi penyewaan keempat-empat unit kilang kepada penyewa industri. "PTT merancang memulakan proses mencari penyewa serta rundingan pajakan sepanjang tempoh pembinaan, dengan operasi sewaan disasarkan bermula selepas projek siap dan milikan kosong diserahkan, tertakluk kepada kerja pengubahsuaian yang diperlukan," katanya. Keempat-empat hartanah dijangka disiapkan dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh perjanjian jual beli (SPA) masing-masing, dengan kerja pembinaan telah bermula pada 7 Januari 2026 dan kini mencapai sehingga peringkat rangka struktur bangunan, atau kira-kira 55% siap. Dari segi pembiayaan, risiko pembelian itu disokong kelulusan pinjaman daripada CIMB Bank Berhad dengan margin pembiayaan 90%, selain rebat Bumiputera 10% yang diberikan penjual. Berdasarkan terma pembayaran, 10% daripada harga pembelian perlu dibayar sebaik sahaja setiap SPA ditandatangani, manakala baki bayaran dibuat secara berperingkat mengikut kemajuan pembinaan sehingga notis milikan kosong dikeluarkan. "Pembelian itu turut mengambil kira transaksi hartanah perindustrian berdekatan, termasuk sebuah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja Prime Industrial Park seluas 1,854.99 meter persegi yang didagangkan pada RM8.5 juta pada Jun 2026," jelas PTT. Satu lagi perbandingan ialah kilang berkembar di Bukit Raja 3 Industrial Park berkeluasan 2,024.99 meter persegi yang direkodkan pada harga RM7.689 juta pada Mac 2026. Sekiranya penjual gagal menyerahkan milikan kosong dalam tempoh 36 bulan daripada tarikh SPA, penjual perlu membayar ganti rugi dipersetujui pada kadar 5% setahun berdasarkan jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat PTT sehingga tarikh penyerahan sebenar. Dari segi kedudukan kewangan, nisbah penggearan proforma PTT dijangka meningkat kepada 2.01 kali selepas pemerolehan berbanding 1.91 kali setakat 30 Jun 2025, berdasarkan kedudukan kewangan proforma yang dinyatakan syarikat.

title: 'Court allows temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport
body:
'

The Sessions Court has granted the temporary release of former PM’s political secretary Shamsul Iskandar’s passport for travel to Germany and London.

KUALA LUMPUR: Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin, the former senior political secretary to the Prime Minister,  has obtained the Sessions Court’s approval for the temporary release of his international passport to enable him to attend several overseas programmes this month.

The passport had been surrendered to the court as an additional bail condition after he was charged with five counts of corruption.

According to his supporting affidavit obtained by the media, Shamsul Iskandar applied for the permanent return of his passport to facilitate overseas travel in connection with his duties.

He said he intended to travel to Frankfurt, Germany, to attend the Frankfurt Book Fair organised by Rex Education from Oct 7 to Nov 11.

“Based on my involvement with the Madani Community Leadership Academy, my participation in the book fair aims to foster synergy between organisations and provide mutual benefits to both entities.

“Therefore, this participation will provide valuable international exposure to support and strengthen ongoing grassroots initiatives aimed at empowering civil society in line with the MADANI principles, particularly through the promotion of literacy, leadership and knowledge,” he said in the affidavit.

Shamsul Iskandar also said he had registered to attend the fifth AlBaraka Summit, themed Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy, in London scheduled for Oct 13 and 14.

He said the summit aimed to strengthen ethical foundations for Islamic financial and non-financial institutions, governance systems and market practices.

Shamsul Iskandar also said he planned to attend programmes in Ireland, as well as Bosnia and Herzegovina, in November and December.

During today’s proceedings, lawyer Yusmadi Yusoff, representing Shamsul Iskandar, told Sessions Court Judge Suzana Hussin that his client had filed an application on Sept 30 for the permanent return of his passport.

He also sought its temporary release to enable Shamsul Iskandar to attend programmes in Frankfurt and London this month.

Deputy Public Prosecutor Julaila Jamaludin objected to the application for the permanent return of the passport, saying the supporting documents consisted only of an invitation letter and that the discussions could be conducted online.

However, she did not object to the application for its temporary release.

Judge Suzana subsequently allowed the temporary release of Shamsul Iskandar’s passport, effective today, on condition that it be returned to the court on or before Oct 16.

The court also ordered the prosecution to file an affidavit in reply to the application for the permanent return of the passport by Oct 19, with the decision on the application set for Dec 8.

Shamsul Iskandar, 51, faces two charges of agreeing to accept RM140,000 in cash from businessman Tei Jiann Cheing, also known as Albert Tei, as an inducement to assist a company owned by Tei in obtaining approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah.

He also faces two charges of obtaining furniture and electrical appliances worth RM14,580.03 and RM22,249, respectively, from Tei for the same purpose.

The offences were allegedly committed at premises in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, and a hotel car park in Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin, as well as at Jalan P14A 1/1, Precinct 14, Putrajaya, between Nov 24, 2023, and March 5, 2024.

In a separate charge, Shamsul Iskandar is accused of obtaining gratification amounting to RM64,924 from Tei, allegedly deposited into a CIMB Bank account belonging to Rahmalidya Buyong to cover the rental of a house in Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, in exchange for assisting Tei’s company in securing approval for a mineral exploration licence in Sabah.

All five charges were brought under Section 17(a) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009 (Act 694) and are punishable under Section 24(1) of the same Act, which provides for a maximum prison sentence of 20 years and a fine of at least five times the amount or value of the gratification, or RM10,000, whichever is higher, upon conviction.

title: 'Which Taxes Could Be Introduced Or Delayed In Budget 2027?
body: 'There is a growing sentiment that there will unlikely be any sweeping new taxes in Budget 2027, however stronger enforcement, wider e-invoicing adoption and refinements to existing taxes will offer more immediate opportunities to raise government revenue, according to tax expert Dr Veerinderjeet Singh.  The KPMG senior adviser on tax policy said the government is likely to remain conscious of cost-of-living pressures and its social agenda, limiting the appetite for substantial tax increases when Budget 2027 is tabled in Parliament on Oct 9. The government has similarly identified protecting households from rising living costs as one of the budget’s central priorities.  The report carried out by CIMB Securities highlighted that his central argument was that Malaysia should first “sweat our assets” — collecting more effectively from existing taxes and taxpayers — before turning to major new revenue instruments.  This would require greater investment in the Inland Revenue Board and Customs, particularly in data analytics to identify businesses outside the tax net and under-reporting among existing taxpayers.  GST Return Unlikely  Veerinderjeet does not expect the Goods and Services Tax (GST) to return in Budget 2027.  He estimated that the current Sales and Service Tax (SST) regime already covers about 78% to 80% of goods and services, approaching the breadth previously covered by GST.  Instead, he sees greater scope to improve the efficiency of SST, including considering broader exemptions for business inputs to reduce tax cascading along supply chains.  Such relief would, however, involve a trade-off because it would also reduce some government revenue.  E-invoicing is expected to become increasingly important in improving compliance and identifying previously unreported taxable activity. Malaysia’s rollout has already been implemented progressively across businesses according to annual turnover, with the framework most recently updated in August.  Veerinderjeet said wider participation could help bring more businesses into the tax system, although policymakers must recognise the technology and compliance costs faced by smaller companies.  No Dividend Tax Hike, CGT Expansion Expected  Budget 2027 is also unlikely to raise the existing 2% tax on annual dividend income exceeding RM100,000, although Veerinderjeet believes the rate could potentially increase over the longer term.  Similarly, he does not expect capital gains tax to be extended to listed shares in the near term. Malaysia currently imposes CGT on specified disposals of unlisted shares by companies, with the regime having taken effect from March 2024.  A further increase in Malaysia’s 30% top personal income tax rate also appears unlikely given regional competitiveness considerations.  No new windfall tax is expected, including on commodity sectors, while modest increases in alcohol and tobacco excise duties remain a possibility because demand for these products tends to be relatively inelastic.  Carbon Tax Could Be Delayed  Carbon pricing remains on the policy agenda, but Veerinderjeet believes current business cost pressures could push implementation to 2028 or later.  Budget 2027 may therefore reaffirm Malaysia’s intention to introduce carbon taxation without committing to an immediate implementation date. When eventually introduced, he expects the initial rate to be relatively low to limit the burden on companies.  The Global Minimum Tax is similarly unlikely to deliver substantial additional revenue immediately, with the first filing cycle needed before its actual contribution can be properly assessed.  Broader Tax Base Needed For Long-Term Revenue  Beyond Budget 2027, Veerinderjeet said Malaysia needs a broader tax base if it wants to lift its tax-to-GDP ratio towards 15%.  He estimated that only around 15% to 16% of the workforce currently pays personal income tax, making sustained wage growth important to expanding the taxpayer base over time.  Corporate tax reform could meanwhile include reviewing special and double deductions that have existed for decades and determining whether they still achieve their original objectives.  Removing outdated deductions could broaden the tax base and potentially create room for a lower headline corporate tax rate, while investment incentives should increasingly be evaluated according to the economic outcomes they generate.  Overall, Veerinderjeet sees better collection, stronger data analytics, wider compliance and expenditure discipline as more realistic near-term fiscal tools than introducing another round of major taxes.  CIMB noted that the message heading into Budget 2027 is consequently one of refinement rather than wholesale tax reform: improve the taxes Malaysia already has, widen the underlying revenue base over time and ensure government spending is managed more effectively.

title: 'Shamsul Iskandar mohon pasport dikembalikan untuk hadiri program luar negara
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: Bekas setiausaha politik kanan kepada perdana menteri, Datuk Seri Shamsul Iskandar Mohd Akin memohon untuk mendapatkan pasport antarabangsanya secara kekal bagi memudahkan beliau menghadiri beberapa program di luar negara. Pasport itu sebelum ini diserahkan kepada mahkamah sebagai syarat jaminan tambahan selepas beliau didakwa atas lima pertuduhan rasuah. Berdasarkan afidavit sokongan permohonan diperoleh media, Shamsul Iskandar berkata, permohonan tersebut adalah bagi membolehkan beliau melakukan perjalanan ke luar negara sebagai sebahagian daripada tugasnya dengan mudah. Shamsul Iskandar selaku pemohon berkata, dalam masa terdekat, beliau berhasrat untuk melakukan perjalanan ke Frankfurt, Jerman bagi menghadiri pesta buku bertajuk 'Frankfurt Book Fair' yang dianjurkan Rex Education, pada 7 Okt hingga 11 Nov ini. "Berdasarkan penglibatan saya dengan Akademi Kepimpinan Masyarakat Madani, penyertaan saya dalam pesta buku tersebut bertujuan untuk memupuk sinergi antara organisasi serta memberikan manfaat bersama kepada kedua-dua entiti. "Justeru, penyertaan ini akan bermanfaat bagi memperoleh pendedahan antarabangsa bagi menyokong serta mempertingkatkan inisiatif akar umbi yang sedang dijalankan bagi memperkasakan prinsip Masyarakat Madani, khususnya melalui promosi literasi, kepimpinan dan pemupukan ilmu," kata Shamsul Iskandar menerusi afidavit itu. Bagi lawatan di London, Shamsul Iskandar berkata, beliau mendaftar untuk Sidang Kemuncak AlBaraka ke-5 bertajuk Ethics in Action: Rebuilding Foundations and Advancing the Global Impact of the Islamic Economy' yang akan berlangsung dari 13 hingga 14 Okt ini. "Objektif utama sidang kemuncak tersebut adalah untuk memberi tumpuan kepada pengukuhan asas etika yang autentik bagi institusi kewangan Islam dan institusi bukan kewangan, sistem tadbir urus serta amalan pasaran," katanya dalam afidavit. Selain itu, Shamsul Iskandar berkata, beliau juga akan menghadiri program di Ireland serta Bosnia dan Herzegovina pada November dan Disember ini. Pada prosiding hari ini, peguam Yusmadi Yusoff yang mewakili Shamsul Iskandar memaklumkan kepada Hakim Mahkamah Sesyen Suzana Hussin bahawa selain permohonan bagi mendapatkan pasport secara kekal yang difailkan 30 Sept lalu, anak guamnya juga memohon agar pasport diserahkan secara sementara bagi membolehkan beliau menghadiri program di Frankfurt dan London bulan ini. Timbalan Pendakwa Raya Julaila Jamaludin yang membantah permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasport secara kekal berkata, dokumen dikemukakan dalam permohonan tersebut hanya berupa surat jemputan dan terdapat perbincangan yang boleh dijalankan secara dalam talian. Bagaimanapun, Julaila tidak membantah permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasport secara sementara. Hakim Suzana kemudian membenarkan permohonan Shamsul Iskandar untuk mendapatkan pasport secara sementara bermula hari ini dan perlu diserahkan semula kepada mahkamah pada atau sebelum 16 Okt ini. Selain itu, mahkamah memerintahkan pihak pendakwaan memfailkan afidavit balasan terhadap permohonan Shamsul Iskandar bagi mendapatkan pasport secara kekal pada atau sebelum 19 Okt ini dan menetapkan keputusan terhadap permohonan itu pada 8 Dis ini. Shamsul Iskandar, 51, didakwa atas dua pertuduhan bersetuju menerima suapan untuk dirinya, iaitu wang tunai RM140,000 daripada ahli perniagaan Tei Jiann Cheing atau turut dikenali sebagai Albert Tei sebagai dorongan membantu syarikat milik Tei untuk mendapatkan kelulusan lesen penerokaan mineral di Sabah. Dia turut didakwa atas dua lagi pertuduhan iaitu memperoleh untuk dirinya satu suapan berupa kelengkapan perabot dan barangan elektrik bernilai RM14,580.03 dan RM22,249 daripada individu sama bagi tujuan sama. Kesalahan itu didakwa dilakukan di premis di Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya; di tempat letak kereta sebuah hotel di Jalan Sultan Hishamuddin di sini; serta di Jalan P14A 1/1, Presint 14, Putrajaya, antara 7 Dis 2023 hingga 31 Jan 2024, serta antara 24 Nov 2023 hingga 5 Mac 2024. Shamsul Iskandar turut didakwa atas satu pertuduhan memperoleh suapan berjumlah RM64,924 yang dimasukkan ke dalam akaun CIMB Bank milik Rahmalidya Buyong bagi tujuan pembayaran penyewaan sebuah rumah di Jalan Medang Serai, Bukit Bandaraya, di sini daripada Tei bagi membantu syarikat milik Tei untuk mendapatkan kelulusan lesen penerokaan mineral di Sabah. Kesemua pertuduhan dikemukakan mengikut Seksyen 17(a) Akta Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia 2009 (Akta 694) dan boleh dihukum di bawah Seksyen 24(1) akta sama, yang memperuntukkan hukuman penjara maksimum 20 tahun serta denda tidak kurang lima kali ganda jumlah atau nilai suapan, atau RM10,000, mengikut mana lebih tinggi, jika sabit kesalahan.

title: 'Cover Story: Playing the long game at Forest City
body: 'Cover Story: Playing the long game at Forest City This article first appeared in City & Country, The Edge Malaysia Weekly on September 28, 2026 - October 4, 2026 It was a scorching afternoon when Country Garden Pacificview Sdn Bhd (CGPV) executive director and chief of regional industrial business development Kevin Li and regional vice-president Syarul Izam Sarifudin arrived at The Edge’s office in Petaling Jaya, Selangor. The pair had flown in from Johor Bahru to give an update on Forest City, a high-profile project in Johor that has dealt with some hot issues since its inception. “What we achieved [since 2015] up to 2025 was merely concentrating more on our operational stability, resource integration and preparing for our next phase of growth,” says Syarul. “In the early years, we were primarily viewed as a residential real estate developer. But we are now embarking into a new sector — managing townships and driving actual economic nodes of financial and industrial development in southern Johor.” The master developer of Forest City is a joint venture between China-headquartered developer Country Garden Holdings Co Ltd and Esplanade Danga 88 Sdn Bhd. Operating as an independent local management unit under Country Garden Malaysia’s executive umbrella, CGPV is responsible for Forest City’s master plan development and management, industrial park development and Special Financial Zone (SFZ) operation. Officially launched by the Malaysian government with duty-free island status in 2016, the 7,500-acre integrated development covers four reclaimed man-made islands over 5,000 acres and 2,500 acres on the mainland. Located in Iskandar Puteri, it sits along the Straits of Johor near the Malaysia-Singapore Second Link, just 2km across the water from Singapore. The ambitious development has made international headlines over the years, some of them for the wrong reasons, especially since it has fallen short of market expectations in terms of progress, sales and occupancy rates. These challenges were compounded by the Covid-19 pandemic and the well-documented financial restructuring of its parent company amid China’s broader real estate liquidity crisis. “When China’s property market faced a systemic downturn, amplified by global supply chain disruptions, macroeconomic shifts and strict pandemic controls, Country Garden — once China’s top property developer — was caught in the crossfire, just like many other big players in the country. However, late last year, our parent group successfully executed onshore and offshore debt restructurings in China,” says Li, who is also the chief financial officer of Country Garden Malaysia. Regardless of the situation faced by its parent company, he highlights that Country Garden Malaysia operates with complete operational and financial independence. “Since Country Garden entered Malaysia as its first overseas destination back in 2010 and 2011, the local operation has relied on an independent management team. For the past three years, our cash flow has been generated entirely within the country, allowing us to remain self-sustaining in terms of liquidity and debt servicing,” he says, adding that all five of its projects in the Klang Valley and Johor are performing steadily. According to Li, Country Garden Malaysia’s sales and cash collection was RM1.3 billion in 2023, more than RM1.1 billion in 2024, and RM1.3 billion in 2025. “More crucially, we utilised our local cash flows to fully settle bank borrowings and capital market obligations worth about RM2 billion over the past three years, including a RM1 billion sukuk … As at earlier this year, the remaining outstanding amount [of the sukuk] was only RM150 million. We pre-repaid them as our cash flow was comfortable.” With most of its debts cleared, local rating agency RAM upgraded Country Garden Malaysia’s outlook rating from negative to stable in March, reflecting its balance-sheet resilience despite global sector volatility. That financial stability has been supported by developments on the legal front. Malaysian courts have recently upheld the validity of sales and purchase agreements in favour of the developer. Dismissing buyer suits seeking to void contracts for reasons such as media portrayals of the project as a “ghost town”, the courts established that market downturns and post-purchase regret do not constitute grounds for breach. The decisions shield CGPV against speculative contract cancellations and protect its revenue base. “Forest City has completed and delivered 26,000 residential units so far. We understand that we cannot make every single person happy, and it is normal to receive feedback or complaints. We respect the buyers’ legal rights,” Li says. “But we also have our internal KPIs [key performance indicators] to meet. We are pleased to share that customer satisfaction consistently hits above 95% in our surveys and polls. Generally, the majority of our 20,000 residents are happy to live here, or they wouldn’t choose to continue staying. This is evidenced by our growing population.” A city waking up Today, Forest City is home to around 20,000 people living in 66 completed blocks, over 770 acres of the approved 5,000-acre reclaimed island land bank. “If you pass by from Iskandar Puteri towards Batam, you can see the lights on across the residential towers at night,” Syarul says. “It is a night-and-day difference compared with what people experienced immediately after the pandemic in early 2021.” Demographics have shifted significantly, he adds. While buyers were once predominantly mainland Chinese, the current resident base is largely local Malaysians, many of whom commute daily to Singapore or work in nearby industrial parks, as well as expatriates of different nationalities. “The township’s commercial pulse is also quickening,” says Syarul. “The Fisherman’s Wharf commercial street has seen steady footfall, with duty-free shops, eateries and premier banking facilities, including branches of Maybank and CIMB, with Affin Bank and AmBank joining the fold soon.” Forest City attracts between 1.5 million and two million tourists annually. Its crown jewel is Forest City Golf Resort, located on the mainland about 9km from the man-made islands. Featuring two 18-hole international championship courses, it draws golfers from Japan, South Korea and Singapore. There is also an affordable beachfront water park that offers weekend entertainment for visiting families. “Forest City is probably the only sandy beach in Johor Bahru. Otherwise, you have to go to Desaru, which is an hour away. To draw more visitors, we are also collaborating with some watersports academies on courses for adults and children. The beach and water park are very popular during school holidays and weekends, contributing to our growing annual tourist and visitor numbers,” Syarul says. Meanwhile, Network School, a start-up society and experimental community based on Silicon Valley entrepreneur Balaji Srinivasan’s book The Network State, was set up in the township in October 2024. Balaji’s private co-living and co-working hub at Marina Hotel drew hundreds of international digital nomads, crypto enthusiasts and tech workers. However, in July 2026, the Iskandar Puteri City Council (MBIP) revoked the Network School operator’s business licence for breaching local licensing conditions. The management of the school clarified that CGPV operates solely as a commercial landlord, and that the developer is fully cooperating with the local authorities to ensure all commercial tenants adhere to the regulatory framework. Strategic shift Li says while Forest City’s master plan is unchanged, CGPV is shifting its focus towards commercial and industrial developments, in alignment with the government’s broader economic development plan for the state. “We maintain the master plan as it is because, to us, it is still a very fantastic plan even after a decade. Of course, for such a mega development, you have to do it in phases, and there will be small twists and adjustments in between. But overall, we do not have plans to review the master plan. Now, we are embarking on the third phase of development. We foresee the entire master plan being completed only by 2040. It is now 12% to 13% developed,” says Syarul. The biggest “twists and adjustments” to the master plan were its integration into the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ) and designation as an SFZ. In August 2023, the government announced that Forest City would be designated as an SFZ to boost foreign investment, with incentives such as a 15% income tax rate for skilled workers and lower business operating costs. A year later, the government launched the tax incentive framework for the SFZ, which includes a zero tax rate for single family offices (SFO), a 5% corporate tax rate for fintech and global business services, and concessionary income tax rates. In early 2025, Malaysia and Singapore signed a bilateral agreement to establish the JS-SEZ. Under the agreement, Forest City was formally incorporated as Flagship G, one of nine primary flagship zones within the 3,505 sq km economic zone. “We started [the master plan] with residential and, maybe, this made people misunderstand that Forest City is focusing on high-rise residential developments. The SFZ designation puts us right back on track to [industrial projects],” says Li. “Under the SFZ blueprint, the development is divided into two distinct functional zones, where the island component acts as a core financial services hub, focusing on single-family offices, fintech, foreign payment operating systems and back-office financial services. Meanwhile, the mainland focuses on smart logistics, high-tech manufacturing and global business services.” To encourage direct investments in Forest City, the Malaysian government established the Iskandar Malaysia Facilitation Centre Johor (IMFC-J) at Forest City’s 42-storey primary office tower, Menara Delima Satu, to streamline the investment process. The centre houses 18 government agencies under one roof and acts as a single processing point for foreign investors. “A key cornerstone of the SFZ is attracting family offices. The SC (Securities Commission) set an AUM (assets under management) threshold of RM30 million for family offices setting up in Forest City, a far more accessible entry point compared with Singapore’s S$15 million (RM47.9 million) requirement or Hong Kong’s HK$240 million (RM124.7 million) benchmark,” Li says. Syarul stresses, however, that Malaysia is not competing with Singapore or Hong Kong in the SFO segment but is instead complementing them. “It is about synergy. Under the SFZ rules, family offices in Forest City can invest up to 90% of their AUM globally. This means that investors can set up their operational base here in Forest City at one-third to one-fourth of the operational cost, while still leveraging Singapore’s capital markets just across the strait. It is very attractive to many family offices,” he explains. Under the SFO Incentive Scheme guidelines issued by the SC, it is mandatory to establish a physical office in Forest City to qualify for and maintain SC approval and the accompanying 0% tax incentive. According to Li, over 40 SFOs have secured physical office space in Forest City, with nine having formally received SC approval to date. “We are very positive about this, though we do not have an actual target of having many of them in Forest City in the near future because it is beyond our control and SC has its plan. But it is a strong catalyst in helping to add vibrancy to Forest City because when the offices come, they bring in their professional teams — accountants, lawyers and finance and investment experts,” he adds. Forest City is also targeting global business services. CGPV is in advanced discussions with two major international banking institutions — one looking to relocate its back-office operations from Singapore, and another expanding its operational footprint from Kuala Lumpur. Forest City 2.0 Despite the tailwinds from the SFZ, Li and Syarul acknowledge that transforming the mega project into a self-sustaining regional economy is not without immediate, real-world hurdles. The most pressing challenge currently is cross-border physical connectivity and accessibility. “While the project is geographically proximate to Singapore, seamlessly moving people, goods and daily commuters across borders remains a complex, multi-jurisdictional effort,” says Li. “Furthermore, regional competition from peers like Thailand, Indonesia and Vietnam means that Malaysia must continually sharpen its execution speed and policy delivery to stay ahead.” To close this connectivity gap, Country Garden is taking interim measures while lobbying government authorities for long-term infrastructure approvals. “Before all the major government infrastructure projects are completed, we are bridging the gap ourselves. We currently run daily direct shuttles transferring residents and workers to the Sultan Abu Bakar CIQ Second Link complex,” Li says. For the long term, the developer has submitted plans to the joint Malaysia-Singapore ministerial committee under the Iskandar Regional Development Authority (IRDA) for a dedicated ferry terminal. Once approved, ferry routes will connect Forest City directly to Raffles Marina in Singapore and Batam in Indonesia. “We are also asking the government for assistance to permit a direct highway connection linking straight to Tuas, and to integrate Forest City into upcoming regional rail routes like the RTS [Rapid Transit System], ART [Automated Rapid Transit] and transport corridors heading to Kulai and Senai,” he adds. “Moving people efficiently is crucial to unlocking the full value of the JS-SEZ but because these are country-to-country matters, we have to keep pushing and following up continuously.” Simultaneously, the master developer is pivoting to boosting population density and creating high-value local jobs, away from traditional residential property sales, towards what the team calls “Forest City 2.0”. “We are not launching any more residential projects in the near future, but focusing on clearing the inventory. We will advance commercial and industrial land development earlier than originally scheduled to inject immediate economic vibrancy,” Li says. “Our next focus is to bring in companies and industries to invest or establish their presence here.” Acknowledging the importance of generating sufficient jobs to increase Forest City’s population, CGPV is actively trying to draw data centres, logistics players and manufacturers to its upcoming 418-acre industrial park. “We need to create real economic dynamics. If you don’t generate jobs and economic substance, you cannot sustain a population,” Li stresses. The response to this industrial shift has been positive. In the first half of this year alone, the developer logged over 300 company enquiries and secured a 40-acre industrial land deal with a manufacturer in Phase 1 of the industrial park, paving the way for ready-built factory developments in Phase 2 should market demand sustain. In another strategic partnership, Country Garden recently signed a term sheet with Penang-based Oriental Holdings Bhd (KL:ORIENT) to develop a RM750 million healthcare hub in Forest City, anchored by a 500-bed hospital alongside comprehensive medical supply chain services. “Internationally, we are actively introducing Forest City to big-name [multinational corporations]. It is not so much for their name, but the entire supply chain. We are looking to bring in ‘queen bee’ investors,” Li says. “We have been doing roadshows, especially in China, to introduce the JS-SEZ and Forest City SFZ. We went to Shenzhen and Suzhou, which have some of the most successful industrial parks in China.” Apart from the industrial park, CGPV has also received enquiries from international investors interested in private island parcels. “It is something that we are looking at. Instead of standard residential towers, we can custom-reclaim approved island plots, such as 1.5 to two acres, based entirely on an investor’s specific operational or residential requirements. It’s about being adaptive to what the current market actually demands,” he says. Road to 2030 and beyond Apart from Forest City, Country Garden Malaysia has four other major developments in Johor and the Klang Valley, executed largely through JVs. “Out of our five projects in Malaysia, four are structured as JVs,” Li explains. “Only Danga Bay is 100% held by Country Garden Malaysia. We welcome JVs because local partners bring value to the table, though for master site design, we prefer to lead.” In Johor Bahru, Country Garden Central Park has completed three phases comprising over 3,000 residential units that are nearly fully sold. The developer is now planning subsequent sub-phases over a 10- to 12-year development cycle. In Kuala Lumpur, the initial two phases of township development Lake City in Taman Wahyu are completed and sold out, with Phase 3 scheduled for launch next year. The remaining four parcels have been earmarked for development over a 15-year period. In Semenyih, Selangor, residential development Diamond City launched its final landed parcel in September 2025, which is expected to wrap up construction within two years. With a substantial land bank in its existing portfolio, the developer will focus its resources on executing its active pipeline over the next decade. As the interview draws to a close, both Li and Syarul reflect on the long-term nature of master township development. “Rome was not built in a day,” Li says. “When we first came to this coastal area in Johor, it was completely rural. Today, the infrastructure is firmly established. Development never moves in a straight upward line; it moves in spirals, but it always moves forward. “We wish the public to know that since the first day Country Garden has been here in Malaysia, we have wanted to be here long term. Of course, there are twists and turns over the years, but we cannot deny the contribution of the company in Malaysia.” He says Country Garden has invested RM32 billion in Malaysia, including RM20 billion in Forest City alone. “We have created jobs, contributed to the country’s tax revenues and trained local skilled workers. Most importantly, after so many challenges and uncertainties, we were here, and we are still here today. The fundamentals are in place, and we have absolute faith in what Forest City will become.” Save by subscribing to us for your print and/or digital copy.
