title: 'Kebijakan MDR QRIS 0% diperluas, bank hadapi tekanan fee dari bisnis acquiring
body: 'KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. Perluasan Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) QRIS 0% mulai 1 Oktober 2026 berpotensi menekan pendapatan berbasis komisi bank dari bisnis QRIS dan acquiring.  Namun, pertumbuhan jumlah merchant dan transaksi QRIS dinilai masih dapat membuka peluang bagi bank untuk menjaga kinerja bisnis melalui peningkatan aktivitas transaksi dan pemanfaatan layanan lainnya.  Seperti diketahui, Bank Indonesia (BI) memperluas MDR QRIS 0% untuk merchant Usaha Mikro (UMI) dengan transaksi hingga Rp500.000. Selain itu, MDR 0% juga berlaku bagi seluruh kategori merchant untuk transaksi hingga Rp100.000.  Gubernur BI Destry Damayanti mengatakan, kebijakan tersebut dirancang dengan prinsip keseimbangan, yakni memberikan manfaat bagi masyarakat dan ruang tumbuh bagi merchant sekaligus menciptakan peluang baru bagi penyelenggara jasa sistem pembayaran dengan tetap menjaga keberlanjutan industri.  Perluasan tersebut dilakukan ketika adopsi QRIS masih menunjukkan pertumbuhan kuat. Hingga Juni 2026, jumlah pengguna QRIS mencapai 65,77 juta pengguna, dengan 6,23 juta di antaranya merupakan pengguna baru sepanjang Januari-Juni 2026.  Jumlah merchant QRIS juga telah mencapai 44,86 juta, dengan 96,68% di antaranya merupakan UMKM. Sementara sepanjang semester I 2026, QRIS mencatat 12,55 miliar transaksi dengan nilai Rp1,12 kuadriliun, tumbuh 93,92% secara tahunan.  Kepala Pusat Makroekonomi dan Keuangan Institute for Development of Economics and Finance (Indef), M Rizal Taufikurahman menilai, perluasan MDR 0% secara langsung akan mengurangi komisi bank dari transaksi yang sebelumnya dikenakan MDR.  Menurut Rizal, biaya pemrosesan dan keamanan transaksi tetap berjalan meski tarif MDR bagi merchant menjadi 0%. Karena itu, bank dengan porsi transaksi berbayar yang besar akan lebih terdampak.  “Perluasan MDR QRIS 0% mengurangi komisi bank pada transaksi yang sebelumnya berbayar, sementara biaya pemrosesan dan keamanan tetap berjalan,” kata Rizal kepada kontan.co.id, Minggu (4/10/2026).  Ia menilai, ekspansi QRIS tetap perlu menghasilkan pendapatan yang mampu menutup biaya layanan. Sebab, lonjakan volume transaksi saja belum otomatis memperkuat profitabilitas bank.  Menurutnya, kompensasi atas potensi penurunan fee harus berasal dari peningkatan nilai transaksi yang masih dikenakan MDR maupun pertumbuhan komisi dari layanan lainnya.  Sebagai ilustrasi, kehilangan 20% pendapatan MDR membutuhkan kenaikan sekitar 25% nilai transaksi berbayar yang tersisa. Sementara kehilangan 30% pendapatan MDR membutuhkan kenaikan sekitar 43%, dengan asumsi komisi efektif tetap.  Rizal juga mengingatkan, transaksi dengan tarif 0% dapat meningkatkan aktivitas QRIS tanpa memberikan tambahan MDR kepada bank. Adapun dana murah yang berasal dari aktivitas merchant memang dapat membantu margin bunga, tetapi tidak dapat dianggap sebagai pemulihan pendapatan komisi.  Di sisi lain, ia melihat adopsi QRIS masih kuat. Hingga Agustus 2026, merchant QRIS BSI telah melampaui 604.000, tumbuh 17% secara tahunan, dengan nilai transaksi mencapai Rp5,7 triliun. Secara nasional, volume transaksi QRIS pada Agustus 2026 tumbuh 67,22%.  Namun, menurut Rizal, pertumbuhan penggunaan QRIS tersebut belum otomatis menunjukkan penguatan pendapatan non-bunga bank. Kemampuan menghasilkan pendapatan tetap bergantung pada jumlah merchant aktif, nilai transaksi berbayar, serta komisi efektif bank.  Untuk sisa 2026, Rizal memperkirakan jumlah merchant dan transaksi QRIS masih akan bertambah. Penurunan biaya penerimaan pembayaran dan momentum belanja akhir tahun menjadi salah satu pendorong.  Meski begitu, pertumbuhan transaksi QRIS dapat pula berasal dari peralihan pembayaran tunai ke digital tanpa disertai peningkatan belanja masyarakat. Alhasil, pertumbuhan komisi bank berpotensi tertinggal dibandingkan pertumbuhan transaksi.  “Keuntungan bank akan ditentukan oleh kemampuannya mempertahankan saldo merchant, memperluas penggunaan layanan berbayar, dan menekan biaya per transaksi,” ujarnya.  Di sisi lain,  Direktur Center of Economic and Law Studies (Celios), Bhima Yudhistira Adhinegara melihat dampak perluasan MDR QRIS 0% terhadap komisi bank masih berpotensi dikompensasi oleh pertumbuhan pendapatan dari layanan lainnya.  Menurut Bhima, semakin luas penetrasi pembayaran melalui QRIS dapat mendorong pertumbuhan fee based income dari produk asuransi dan investasi. Aktivitas merchant yang meningkat juga dapat memperbesar volume simpanan serta layanan cash management, termasuk payroll.  Dari sisi kredit, semakin banyak merchant yang menggunakan QRIS juga membuka peluang bagi bank untuk menghubungkan merchant dengan layanan pembiayaan, seperti factoring, kredit modal kerja, maupun jenis kredit lainnya.  Bhima menilai. kebijakan MDR 0% dapat membuat masyarakat dan merchant semakin nyaman menggunakan QRIS karena tidak ada pungutan yang dibebankan kepada merchant untuk transaksi yang masuk dalam ketentuan tersebut.  Ia juga memperkirakan, transaksi QRIS masih akan terus meningkat seiring dengan semakin luasnya penetrasi QRIS, termasuk pengembangan konektivitas pembayaran QRIS di kawasan ASEAN.  Sementara, SEVP Digital Business BTN Thomas Wahyudi mengatakan, perluasan MDR QRIS 0% memang berdampak terhadap pendapatan berbasis komisi, terutama untuk transaksi yang masuk dalam ketentuan MDR 0%.  Namun, BTN tidak melihat QRIS semata-mata sebagai sumber fee based income. Perseroan juga menjadikan QRIS sebagai bagian dari pengembangan ekosistem transaksi digital secara keseluruhan.  “Perluasan MDR QRIS 0% tentunya memberikan dampak terhadap pendapatan berbasis komisi, khususnya untuk transaksi yang masuk dalam ketentuan tersebut. Namun, bagi BTN, QRIS tidak hanya dilihat dari sisi fee based income, tetapi juga sebagai bagian dari pengembangan ekosistem transaksi digital secara keseluruhan,” kata Thomas.  Menurutnya, pertumbuhan jumlah merchant dan volume transaksi menjadi salah satu faktor yang dapat membantu menjaga kinerja bisnis QRIS setelah MDR 0% berlaku.  Penerapan MDR 0% pada segmen transaksi tertentu dinilai dapat mendorong merchant semakin memanfaatkan QRIS sebagai sarana pembayaran utama, baik dari sisi jumlah transaksi maupun nilai transaksi.  Meski demikian, Thomas menilai, kenaikan volume transaksi pada tahap awal lebih berperan menjaga kinerja bisnis QRIS secara keseluruhan, bukan menjadi pengganti langsung potensi penurunan pendapatan berbasis komisi.  Besarnya dampak terhadap pendapatan akan bergantung pada jumlah merchant, frekuensi transaksi, dan nilai transaksi ke depan. Karena itu, BTN akan terus memantau perkembangan tersebut dan menyesuaikan strategi bisnis acquiring melalui pengembangan layanan dan solusi yang dapat meningkatkan aktivitas serta nilai transaksi merchant.  Hingga September 2026, transaksi QRIS BTN telah meningkat sekitar 157% secara tahunan. Sementara volume transaksi tumbuh 166% YoY.  Pertumbuhan tersebut didorong oleh bertambahnya jumlah merchant, meningkatnya adopsi QRIS oleh nasabah BTN, serta berbagai program aktivasi transaksi yang dijalankan perseroan.  BTN juga melihat penerapan MDR 0% dapat memberikan sentimen positif dari sisi merchant karena biaya transaksi menjadi lebih ringan untuk transaksi yang masuk dalam ketentuan.  Hingga akhir 2026, BTN menargetkan jumlah merchant mencapai 480.000 merchant. Untuk mengejar target tersebut, BTN tidak hanya berfokus pada akuisisi merchant baru, tetapi juga meningkatkan kontribusi transaksi dari merchant yang sudah masuk dalam ekosistem perseroan.  BTN akan melakukan segmentasi pengembangan merchant. Akuisisi tetap dilakukan untuk memperluas ekosistem, sementara merchant non-UMI dengan volume dan nilai transaksi tinggi akan menjadi salah satu fokus pengembangan untuk menjaga pertumbuhan volume transaksi dan kinerja acquiring.  BTN juga mendorong aktivitas merchant melalui program Balé 3S (Santai, Santap, Sehat) dan Bale Connect the World.  “Pertumbuhan QRIS BTN diharapkan tidak hanya berasal dari peningkatan jumlah merchant, tetapi juga dari peningkatan frekuensi dan nilai transaksi,” ujar Thomas.  Adapun, Head of Digital Banking and Contact Center CIMB Niaga Lusiana Saleh mengakui perluasan MDR QRIS 0% akan mengurangi porsi fee perseroan dari transaksi yang masuk dalam kebijakan tersebut.  Meski demikian, CIMB Niaga menilai kebijakan tersebut tetap tepat karena dapat mendorong penggunaan transaksi nontunai dan menggerakkan aktivitas ekonomi.  “Sebenarnya menurut kami, kami agak shock sedikit, karena porsi kami berkurang sebenarnya. Tapi menurut kami, ini adalah gerakan yang cukup tepat karena kami mendukung untuk siklus ekonomi, roda harus berjalan,” kata Lusiana.  Menurut Lusiana, transaksi bernilai kecil seperti pembelian kopi yang berada di kisaran Rp40.000-Rp50.000 menjadi salah satu contoh transaksi yang dapat semakin didorong dengan kebijakan MDR 0%.  Ia menilai perluasan MDR 0% dapat membantu memperluas penggunaan transaksi cashless, termasuk di kalangan UMKM.  CIMB Niaga mencatat transaksi QRIS melalui aplikasi OCTO tumbuh sekitar 65% YoY pada semester I 2026. QRIS juga menjadi kanal transaksi digital dengan penggunaan tertinggi di CIMB Niaga, disusul transaksi transfer melalui BI-FAST.  Meski fee berpotensi berkurang, CIMB Niaga tidak terlalu mengkhawatirkan dampak kebijakan tersebut terhadap bisnis QRIS. Lusiana mengatakan QRIS memiliki fungsi strategis untuk meningkatkan loyalitas nasabah sekaligus mendorong aktivitas transaksi melalui OCTO.  “QRIS itu sebenarnya salah satu fitur utama yang kita pakai untuk menggaet loyalitas nasabah untuk melakukan transaksi,” ujarnya.  Menurut Lusiana, penggunaan QRIS juga lebih murah dan praktis dibandingkan transaksi menggunakan kartu maupun uang tunai. Dari sisi operasional, nasabah cukup menggunakan OCTO tanpa membutuhkan kartu fisik.

title: 'Multifinance perkuat strategi hadapi persaingan bank di pembiayaan kendaraan listrik
body: 'KONTAN.CO.ID - JAKARTA. Otoritas Jasa Keuangan (OJK) mencatatkan pertumbuhan signifikan pada penyaluran pembiayaan kendaraan listrik multifinance.  Per Juli 2026, OJK mencatat penyaluran pembiayaan kendaraan listrik di industri multifinance mencapai Rp 25,49 triliun per Juli 2026 atau tumbuh sebesar 37,84% jika dibandingkan dengan periode yang sama di tahun sebelumnya.  Namun tengah pertumbuhan pembiayaan kendaraan listrik oleh multifinance, sejumlah bank juga menunjukkan kinerja positif pada segmen ini.  Sebagai contoh, PT Bank Syariah Indonesia Tbk (BSI) mencatat pembiayaan kendaraan listrik sebesar Rp 574 miliar hingga Juli 2026. Nilai tersebut berkontribusi sebesar 9% terhadap total pembiayaan kendaraan atau BSI OTO.  Selain itu, PT Bank Central Asia Tbk (BBCA) mencatat pembiayaan kendaraan listrik telah mencapai sekitar Rp 4 triliun hingga semester I-2026 atau meningkat 25% secara tahunan.  Pengamat Industri Pembiayaan, Jodjana Jody menilai perkembangan pembiayaan kendaraan listrik oleh perbankan berpotensi berkompetisi langsung dengan industri multifinance.  Menurutnya, bank memiliki keunggulan berupa basis nasabah yang sudah terbentuk sehingga dapat menawarkan persetujuan kredit dan bunga khusus kepada nasabah dengan profil prima.  Kondisi tersebut membuat multifinance perlu mengoptimalkan keunggulan yang dimiliki, salah satunya melalui fleksibilitas dalam menawarkan produk pembiayaan dan kedekatan dengan ekosistem otomotif.  "Multifinance bagaimana pun sangat fleksibel dan lebih customer friendly, ini yang harus ditonjolkan. Selain itu multifinance biasanya memiliki hubungan khusus dengan dealer dan prinsipal merek kendaraan dan ini bisa dikapitalisasi," ujarnya kepada Kontan, Minggu (4/10/2026).  Salah satu perusahaan yang memperkuat strategi tersebut adalah PT CIMB Niaga Auto Finance (CNAF).  Hingga Agustus 2026, pembiayaan kendaraan listrik CNAF telah mencapai sekitar Rp1,41 triliun atau tumbuh 68% dibandingkan periode yang sama tahun sebelumnya yang sebesar Rp842 miliar.  Presiden Direktur CNAF, Ristiawan Suherman menilai perkembangan pembiayaan kendaraan listrik di perbankan merupakan bagian dari semakin terbentuknya ekosistem kendaraan listrik. Namun, peningkatan jumlah pemain juga membuat persaingan di industri pembiayaan makin ketat.  “Tentunya bagi industri multifinance, kondisi tersebut mendorong persaingan semakin dinamis,” ujarnya kepada Kontan, Jumat (2/10/2026).  Oleh karena itu, CNAF menerapkan sejumlah strategi untuk menghadapi kondisi ini.  Beberapa di antaranya adalah dengan menawarkan solusi pembiayaan yang cepat, mudah, dan sederhana, sembari tetap menjaga penerapan manajemen risiko secara prudent.  Dari sisi pricing, CNAF berupaya menjaga produk pembiayaan tetap kompetitif dengan tetap mempertimbangkan risiko dan kesehatan portofolio.  Perusahaan juga memperkuat kerja sama dengan dealer dan mitra, meningkatkan kualitas layanan, memanfaatkan digitalisasi dalam proses pembiayaan, serta mengembangkan produk sesuai kebutuhan konsumen.  Selain itu, CNAF akan memanfaatkan sinergi dengan ekosistem induknya, yaitu Bank CIMB Niaga untuk memperkuat proposisi pembiayaan dan memberikan nilai tambah bagi nasabah.  Sementara secara industri, Jody juga menilai kemampuan menawarkan bunga kompetitif juga menjadi salah satu faktor penting bagi multifinance untuk menghadapi persaingan dengan perbankan. Namun, tidak semua perusahaan multifinance bisa menerapkan strategi ini.  “Tipikal yang bisa begini adalah multifinance besar yang punya sumber pendanaan bervariasi dan tidak tergantung dari bank saja," katanya.  Meski demikian, multifinance dinilai masih memiliki ruang untuk memperbesar pembiayaan kendaraan listrik. Menurut Jody, perusahaan multifinance saat ini masih agresif masuk ke segmen tersebut sembari mempelajari karakteristik risikonya.  Salah satu perhatian adalah nilai jual kembali kendaraan listrik yang masih berkembang. Kondisi tersebut berpotensi memengaruhi nilai aset ketika terjadi penarikan kendaraan dan pada akhirnya berdampak terhadap kualitas pembiayaan.  Selain itu, biaya perbaikan kendaraan listrik setelah kecelakaan juga menjadi faktor yang perlu diperhatikan karena dapat memengaruhi biaya perlindungan asuransi pada periode berikutnya.  CNAF sendiri melihat prospek pembiayaan kendaraan listrik masih terbuka seiring perkembangan pasar dan ekosistem kendaraan listrik. Pertumbuhan segmen tersebut tidak hanya ditentukan oleh harga kendaraan dan skema pembiayaan, tetapi juga perkembangan infrastruktur pendukung, pilihan model kendaraan, pemahaman konsumen, serta kebijakan pemerintah.  Sementara itu, Kepala Eksekutif Pengawas Lembaga Pembiayaan, Perusahaan Modal Ventura, Lembaga Keuangan Mikro dan Lembaga Jasa Keuangan Lainnya OJK Agusman juga mengaku optimis dengan prospek pembiayaan kendaraan listrik oleh multifinance ke depannnya.  Hal ini sejalan dengan perkembangan pembiayaan oleh multifinance pada segmen ini yang terus mengalami pertumbuhan.  Sebagai gambaran, penyaluran pembiayaan kendaraan listrik industri multifinance tumbuh 32,05% secara tahunan, dengan nilai mencapai Rp 23,39 triliun per April 2026.  Kinerjanya pun makin bertumbuh. Per Mei 2026, tumbuh sebesar 32,48% dengan nilai mencapai Rp 23,94 triliun. Lalu, posisi per Juni 2026 tumbuh 34,70%, dengan nilai mencapai Rp 24,60 triliun.  Selain itu, wacana adanya wacana pemberian insentif motor listrik juga berpotensi mendorong pembiayaan kendaraan listrik ke depannya.  "Sebab, membuat harga motor listrik lebih terjangkau bagi masyarakat," ujar Agusman dalam lembar jawaban tertulis RDK OJK, Senin (14/9/2026).  Oleh karena itu dengan persaingan bank yang diperkirakan akan makin kuat, multifinance dituntut tidak hanya mengandalkan pricing saja, tetapi juga mengoptimalkan fleksibilitas, jaringan dealer dan prinsipal, kualitas layanan, serta teknologi untuk mempertahankan daya saing di pasar pembiayaan kendaraan listrik.

title: 'Senior Citizens’ Bill: Give older people a fairer deal
body: 'V Thomas The women, family and community development minister has said the Senior Citizens’ Bill will be tabled in Parliament in early 2027. The public is still being asked for input and feedback. Here are my suggestions for the bill. Dedicated hospital wings Major government hospitals should have a separate wing for older adults. It would focus on treatment, surgery and medication. At present, older people wait with everyone else until their name or number is called. Many are frail, in wheelchairs or ill. They should not have to wait so long for treatment. A separate wing would help the government judge whether it needs bigger budgets and more geriatricians. It would also be easier to manage well, as it would handle fewer patients. Better EPF returns Major banks in India offer older adults deposit interest rates of up to about 7-8%, depending on the bank and tenure. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Likewise, the Employees Provident Fund in Malaysia could pay older people a higher dividend on their savings. A rate of 10% on up to RM200,000 in savings would help. (The current rate is about 6.15%, declared for 2025.) A separate EPF scheme for older people could achieve this. At 10%, RM200,000 would earn about RM20,000 a year, or roughly RM1,666 a month. At present, members can deposit up to RM100,000 a year in aggregate across EPF’s voluntary contribution schemes. But the EPF voluntary contribution scheme now stops at age 75. That age limit could be extended to 80. More older people could then cope with the cost of living, medical bills and other expenses. Many older people would no longer have to seek help from the Social Welfare Department. Harnessing experience The government should use older people’s experience through incentives in residents’ associations and other local groups. Local authorities could help in these programmes. Town hall sessions would benefit from older people’s knowledge, particularly of local government. Local authorities should register older people’s associations freely and tell older people about programmes in their areas. Some light duties could be reserved for older people who can work. Older people are a vital asset, and the government should make full use of what they can contribute in their later years. Many capable older people could serve as local councillors and village development and security committee (JKKK) members because they know local needs well. A quota for older people among councillors could be considered. Older people should also have their own associations at state and national level. This would let them voice their needs, especially when the yearly budget is drawn up. The government would then understand their needs better and allocate the right funds for their wellbeing. The number of older people is rising fast. It is time for the government to plan soundly and strategically for this growing issue. V Thomas follows the Aliran website. title: 'A wage floor with a loophole
body: 'Charles Santiago On 26 September, Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim said workers were stuck on RM1,700 while productivity and profits kept rising. He was right. Four days later, Entrepreneur Development and Cooperatives Minister Steven Sim announced that the cabinet had agreed to exempt micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) from the next minimum wage increase for now. That is a direct contradiction. Two rules, one workforce MSMEs employ 8.1 million people, or 48.7% of Malaysia’s workforce. This exemption means two cleaners doing the same work could be legally entitled to different pay. One works for a large company and the other for a smaller firm. Can small firms afford it? The argument is that MSMEs cannot afford higher wages. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member But gross domestic product from MSMEs grew 5.7% in 2025, faster than the overall economy’s 5.2%. Labour productivity also rose 4.1% to RM85,299 per worker a year, or about RM7,100 a month. Low wages So where does that value go? For every RM100 Malaysia’s economy produces, workers receive about RM34. In the EU, workers get about RM48 and in Germany RM55. The government promised 40% of GDP to workers by 2025 under the 12th Malaysia Plan and missed it. People are already struggling with food, rent, transport, childcare and healthcare. Even RM2,000 is still far below a living wage. Bank Negara estimated a living wage for a single adult in Kuala Lumpur at RM2,700 about eight years ago. The benchmark used by government-linked investment companies and government-linked companies is now about RM3,100. A better way There is a better way to support small firms without sacrificing workers. When South Korea raised its minimum wage sharply in 2018, it kept one wage for everyone. It also gave small firms a monthly subsidy of 130,000 won for each low-paid worker. Firms that got the help kept their staff. Budget 2027 will be revealed on 9 October. The government should not be creating divides. It needs to lift the wage floor for every worker. Charles Santiago is a prominent Malaysian politician, economist and human rights advocate who served three terms as the MP for Klang and has twice chaired the National Water Services Commission. title: 'Bursa Sheds 2.4% For Week As Yields, Foreign Selling Hit Sentiment
body: 'Bursa Malaysia ended the Sept 28-Oct 2 week sharply lower, with the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) losing 40.75 points, or 2.4%, to 1,630.87 from the previous Friday’s 1,671.62, as rising global bond yields, elevated oil prices and persistent foreign selling weighed on sentiment.  The benchmark started the week marginally lower, slipping 0.09% to 1,670.02 on Sept 28, as investors remained cautious amid a lack of fresh catalysts and continued external headwinds.  Selling intensified the next day, when the FBM KLCI tumbled 26.06 points, or 1.56%, to 1,643.96, pressured by surging bond yields and Brent crude prices around US$107 a barrel, which reignited inflation concerns and dampened risk appetite.  The market rebounded 0.43% to 1,651.17 on Sept 30 as bargain hunters returned following the sharp sell-off, although broader sentiment remained cautious ahead of key US inflation data.  That recovery proved short-lived, with the index plunging another 1.26% to 1,630.36 the following day, dragged by selling in heavyweights including Maybank, Public Bank, CIMB, TNB and IHH Healthcare. Weak domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign outflows added to the pressure.  Bursa eked out a 0.03% gain to 1,630.87 to close out the trading week as bargain hunting cushioned the recent sell-off, but the rebound remained muted amid weakness across regional markets and caution ahead of US labour data.  Overall, the FBM KLCI recorded losses in three of the five sessions, with external rate and inflation concerns dominating trading despite intermittent bargain hunting.

title: 'CIMB Niaga siap perluas QRIS cross border ke Hong Kong dan Arab Saudi
body: 'KONTAN.CO.ID-JAKARTA. PT Bank CIMB Niaga Tbk terus memperluas layanan QRIS cross border seiring dengan pengembangan konektivitas pembayaran lintas negara oleh Bank Indonesia (BI).  Terbaru, CIMB Niaga menyatakan siap mengikuti perluasan QRIS cross border ke Hong Kong dan Arab Saudi.  Head of Digital Banking & Contact Center CIMB Niaga Lusiana Saleh mengatakan, perseroan akan mengikuti agenda BI untuk memperluas implementasi QRIS cross border ke kedua negara tersebut.  “Coming soon itu sudah dipatok sama BI, kita harus luncurkan itu. Oke, siap, kita akan luncurkan itu,” ujar Lusiana di Jakarta, Jumat (2/10).  Saat ini, CIMB Niaga telah mengimplementasikan QRIS cross border di sejumlah negara. Lusiana menyebut China dan Korea Selatan sebagai salah satu negara terbaru yang telah terhubung dengan layanan tersebut.  Menurut dia, penggunaan QR di China menjadi salah satu faktor yang mendukung perkembangan transaksi QRIS cross border CIMB Niaga di negara tersebut. Masyarakat China dinilai sudah terbiasa menggunakan pembayaran berbasis QR dalam transaksi sehari-hari.  “Proses kita di China mulai banyak, karena China itu juga negara QR, jadi secara otomatis orang terbiasa untuk menggunakan QR,” jelasnya.  Lusiana mengatakan, dari sisi kesiapan infrastruktur, CIMB Niaga tidak melihat adanya kendala berarti untuk mengikuti perluasan QRIS cross border.  Pasalnya, perseroan selama ini juga aktif mengikuti berbagai proyek percontohan yang dilakukan BI dalam pengembangan ekosistem pembayaran digital.  “Selama ini kita juga selalu mendukung Bank Indonesia, setiap tahun mereka piloting di beberapa negara pun, kita selalu ikutan,” kata Lusiana.  Selain QRIS cross border, CIMB Niaga sebelumnya juga turut berpartisipasi dalam pengembangan QRIS Tap dan implementasi tap in tap out pada layanan transportasi.  Dengan semakin luasnya konektivitas QRIS lintas negara, CIMB Niaga melihat peluang transaksi digital masih terbuka. Perseroan juga terus mendorong penggunaan transaksi nontunai di dalam negeri.  Lusiana mengatakan, QRIS saat ini menjadi salah satu transaksi digital dengan penggunaan tinggi di CIMB Niaga, diikuti transaksi transfer melalui BI-FAST.

Katanya, demi membiayai pengajiannya, ibunya yang berkerusi roda gigih membuat kuih bersama bapanya, Sudin Matsan, 63. title: 'PFI UiTM turut perlu disiasat – KMUiTM
body: 'Kolektif Mahasiswa UiTM (KMUiTM) menggesa Suruhanjaya Pencegahan Rasuah Malaysia (SPRM), Jawatankuasa Kira-Kira Wang Negara (PAC) dan Jabatan Audit Negara menyiasat keseluruhan projek Inisiatif Pembiayaan Swasta (PFI) UiTM, susulan perkembangan terbaharu mengenai tatakelola dan pengurusan kewangan UiTM Holdings. Menurut KMUiTM, perhatian terhadap UiTM Holdings tidak sepatutnya menyebabkan persoalan PFI UiTM yang melibatkan komitmen konsesi jangka panjang dan nilai kewangan yang dianggarkan berbilion ringgit kembali dilupakan, khususnya apabila persoalan mengenai kaedah perolehan dan kos konsesi projek itu telah dibangkitkan sejak 2014. Pada 2014 Rafizi Ramli mempersoalkan enam projek kampus UiTM di Pasir Gudang, Jasin, Seremban 3, Puncak Alam, Tapah dan Kota Samarahan yang menurutnya diberikan melalui rundingan terus, termasuk kepada syarikat-syarikat yang dikaitkan dengan ahli sebuah parti politik. Beliau menganggarkan kos pembinaan enam kampus tersebut sekitar RM1.8bn, berbanding kira-kira RM8.6bn jumlah bayaran konsesi yang didakwanya sepanjang tempoh 23 tahun. Rafizi turut mencabar kerajaan mendedahkan perjanjian konsesi supaya kos, keuntungan pemegang konsesi dan struktur perjanjian dapat diperiksa umum. Pada masa sama, PAC pada ketika itu turut mempersoalkan ketelusan enam projek tersebut dan menggesa maklumat mengenai projek konsesi didedahkan kepada umum, termasuk persoalan penggunaan rundingan terus serta sama ada kerajaan memperoleh value for money. Rekod rasmi Parlimen menunjukkan UiTM menerima RM881j peruntukan pembangunan pada 2022, tetapi RM858j atau 97.3% peratus daripadanya diperuntukkan untuk caj tetap PFI yang merangkumi ‘availability charges, maintenance charges dan maintenance reserve fund’. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Pada 2023 pula, RM865j atau 95.0% daripada RM911j peruntukan pembangunan diperuntukkan bagi caj tetap PFI. KMUiTM berkata angka tersebut menimbulkan persoalan mengenai kos lepas (opportunity cost) PFI kepada universiti. Setiap ringgit yang diperuntukkan untuk memenuhi komitmen konsesi jangka panjang tidak boleh digunakan pada masa yang sama untuk keperluan pembangunan lain seperti penyelenggaraan kampus, naik taraf fasiliti, pelaksanaan program pembangunan mahasiswa, pengambilan tenaga akademik tetap, pembinaan kolej kediaman serta kebajikan mahasiswa. “Persoalannya bukan sekadar berapa kos sebuah kampus dibina. Persoalannya ialah berapa jumlah yang dibayar sepanjang hayat konsesi dan apa yang UiTM terpaksa korbankan kerana sebahagian besar peruntukan pembangunannya terikat kepada komitmen tersebut,” menurut KMUiTM. Bagi KMUiTM, hakikat bahawa PFI masih mempunyai komitmen kewangan yang aktif menjadikan persoalan lama itu relevan untuk diperiksa semula, bukannya sekadar diarkibkan sebagai kontroversi 2014. Tuntutan itu turut mengambil kira perkembangan terhadap UiTM Holdings. PAC pada 2024 mengenal pasti kelemahan dalam tadbir urus kewangan serta kelemahan maklumat dan kawal selia pengurusan pelaburan UiTM Holdings – manakala SPRM kini menjalankan siasatan terhadap kerugian syarikat berkenaan dan beberapa isu berkaitan, termasuk isu pembayaran RM42j berkaitan projek solar Gambang yang menurut SPRM dibuat bagi tujuan yang tidak berkaitan dengan projek tersebut dan tanpa kelulusan lembaga pengarah. Perbandingan itu, kata KMUiTM, bukan bermaksud mendakwa PFI dan UiTM Holdings melibatkan kesalahan yang sama. Sebaliknya, ia menimbulkan persoalan mengenai standard akauntabiliti terhadap wang awam UiTM. Pada Januari 2026, persoalan tersebut telah pun diketengahkan oleh wakil KMUiTM dalam sidang media mahasiswa mengenai sistem perolehan universiti awam. Mereka ketika itu turut mengangkat semula konsesi kampus UiTM yang dibangkitkan Rafizi pada 2014 dan mengaitkan isu perolehan universiti dengan amanah kewangan awam, selain menggesa audit forensik terhadap projek dan tender universiti. KMUiTM kini menggesa supaya keseluruhan portfolio PFI UiTM dibuka kepada siasatan dan audit, termasuk proses penganugerahan kontrak asal, penggunaan rundingan terus, struktur pemilikan syarikat konsesi, jumlah bayaran yang telah dibuat, baki komitmen, kos penyelenggaraan dan penilaian value for moneyberdasarkan prestasi sebenar projek. Kumpulan itu turut menggesa kerajaan mendedahkan jumlah keseluruhan komitmen PFI yang masih berbaki dan menilai kos lepas kepada fungsi pendidikan UiTM akibat peruntukan pembangunan yang terikat kepada caj PFI. Menurut KMUiTM, penelitian tersebut juga penting kerana PFI bukan semata-mata model pembiayaan yang sudah ditinggalkan. UiTM masih mengurus portfolio PFI, dan sebarang cadangan untuk memperluas penggunaan model tersebut, termasuk bagi projek infrastruktur atau tenaga, perlu dibuat hanya selepas prestasi dan kos kontrak sedia ada dinilai secara bebas. Kewujudan kampus PFI juga didakwa menyebabkan pembinaan kolej kediaman baharu dan penambahan kemudahan kampus lebih rumit, memandangkan kampus-kampus berkenaan secara teknikalnya ibarat bangunan yang disewa oleh UiTM. KMUiTM berkata penyiasatan semula tidak bertujuan menghukum sesuatu model pembiayaan secara automatik, tetapi memastikan keputusan yang mengikat wang awam untuk puluhan tahun dapat dipertanggungjawabkan berdasarkan kos sebenar, prestasi sebenar dan manfaat kepada universiti. “Kalau benar PFI memberikan value for money, maka kerajaan perlu membuktikannya berdasarkan lebih sedekad data sebenar, bukan sekadar hujah ketika kontrak mula diberikan,” menurut kumpulan itu. – KMUiTM The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'A pay rise for only half the workforce
body: 'Lim Guan Eng was the first senior politicians to call for migrant workers in micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) to be exempt from the minimum wage and Employees Provident Fund (EPF) schemes. Now, the cabinet has exempted MSMEs from the upcoming minimum wage increase “for the time being”. The entrepreneur development and cooperatives minister, also from the DAP, announced the decision. Syabas (well done) on this remarkable ‘achievement’. Millions of workers in the sector have lost their right to a minimum wage increase. Official figures show about 48.7% of the country’s total employment are in MSMEs. That is 8.1 million people. Can Malaysia ever become a high-income nation with so many workers exempt from the minimum wake hike? We should also worry that wages will stay stagnant. Wage growth for 8.1 million workers will probably be held back. Two classes of workers Almost half of those workers will benefit from a higher minimum wage. The other half will, regrettably, be left at the mercy of their bosses for any wage reviews. This is discrimination in how we treat our workers. Even the government of the day never envisaged such injustice when it introduced the policy. The minimum wage was meant to set a floor for all workers. Since 2013, the government has never strayed from that core aim. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Now, under the supposedly caring ‘Madani’ government, low-wage workers are being treated unfairly to favour one class of employers. It is a case of “harapkan pagar, pagar makan padi”. Some businesses will feel the impact of a higher minimum wage. The government should address their concerns case by case, rather than excluding the whole MSME sector. Denying close to 8.1m workers coverage under the new minimum wage increase is deeply unjust and morally wrong. We call on the prime minister to reverse the decision to exempt MSMEs from the upcoming minimum wage increase. title: 'Apa yang mesti berubah sebelum pelajar lain dicederakan?/ What must change before another child is hurt?
body: '[ENGLISH VERSION BELOW] Kematian Muhammad ldlan Fareeq Shahril, 14 tahun, meninggalkan sebuah keluarga dalam kesedihan dan ibu bapa di seluruh Malaysia dengan satu pertanyaan yang amat membimbangkan: adakah anak saya selamat di asrama sekolah? Bagi pihak Children’s Protection Society Malaysia (CPSM), saya merakamkan ucapan takziah yang sedalam-dalamnya kepada ibu bapa dan keluarga Muhammad ldlan. Tiada kata-kata yang dapat meringankan kehilangan mereka. Mereka berhak mendapat ruang untuk berduka, dan jawapan yang benar serta keadilan. Kami mengambil maklum bahawa Menteri Pendidikan Fadhlina Sidek telah bertemu dengan keluarga dan warga sekolah serta mengarahkan audit segera. Kami menyambut baik jaminan beliau bahawa tiada sesiapa akan dilindungi sekiranya salah laku terbukti. Polis mesti diberi ruang untuk menentukan fakta, termasuk punca dan keadaan yang membawa kepada kematian Muhammad ldlan. Dakwaan tidak boleh dianggap sebagai dapatan, dan pelajar yang terlibat tidak wajar dihakimi oleh masyarakat sebelum siasatan selesai. Namun, siasatan terhadap satu kejadian tidak boleh menjadi noktah kepada perkara ini. Audit tersebut perlu menjawab soalan yang lebih sukar: adakah terdapat kebimbangan yang timbul sebelum kematian Muhammad ldlan, dan adakah pihak asrama mempunyai cara yang berkesan untuk mengenal pasti serta menanganinya? Soalan ini perlu diteliti tanpa membuat andaian tentang apa yang berlaku dalam kes ini. Apabila seorang pelajar tinggal di asrama, pihak sekolah memikul tanggungjawab menjaganya pada waktu ibu bapanya tidak dapat melihat keadaannya sendiri. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Tanggungjawab itu melangkaui daftar penghuni dan peraturan yang ditampal pada papan kenyataan semata-mata. la memerlukan orang dewasa yang mengenali pelajar, menyedari perubahan tingkah laku, mengambil tindakan apabila kebimbangan dibangkitkan dan bertanggungjawab terhadap keselamatan mereka selepas waktu persekolahan. Tiada pelajar berhak menguatkuasakan disiplin dengan kekerasan. Jika seorang pelajar disyaki melanggar peraturan, sama ada berkaitan dengan vape, barang yang hilang, sikap tidak menghormati orang lain atau apa-apa perkara sekalipun, urusan itu mesti dikendalikan oleh orang dewasa yang bertanggungjawab. Pelajar tidak boleh ditampar, dipukul, ditahan secara paksa, diugut atau dikenakan hukuman yang dikendalikan oleh pelajar lain. Sesiapa yang melihat sesuatu masalah hendaklah melaporkannya kepada warden atau guru disiplin. Tiada tempat bagi pelajar yang melantik diri mereka sendiri sebagai penguat kuasa di dormitori, asrama atau sekolah. Oleh itu, CPSM menyeru Kementerian Pendidikan supaya menggunakan audit semasa sebagai permulaan kepada semakan keselamatan asrama yang jelas dan mempunyai tempoh pelaksanaan yang ditetapkan. Semakan itu perlu merangkumi perkara berikut. Pertama, teliti sama ada tanda amaran terlepas pandang. Penyiasat dan pasukan audit perlu meneliti aduan terdahulu, laporan tidak rasmi, permintaan untuk bertukar bilik, kecederaan yang tidak dapat dijelaskan, ketidakhadiran, perubahan tingkah laku dan kebimbangan yang dibangkitkan oleh ibu bapa, sekiranya maklumat tersebut wujud. Mereka perlu mengenal pasti siapa yang menerima setiap maklumat, tindakan yang diambil dan sama ada keadaan pelajar berkenaan disusuli. Jika tiada aduan direkodkan, hal itu perlu dinilai secara bersama satu lagi persoalan: adakah pelajar mempunyai saluran yang selamat dan boleh dipercayai untuk bersuara? Kedua, pastikan penyeliaan orang dewasa ada pada waktu dan tempat pelajar memerlukannya. Warden sukar menjalankan pengawasan yang rapi jika mereka perlu menjaga terlalu ramai pelajar, beberapa bangunan atau terlalu banyak tugas serentak. Kementerian perlu menyemak jumlah petugas asrama, liputan pada waktu malam, serah tugas dan tatacara mendapatkan bantuan apabila sesuatu kejadian berlaku. Setiap asrama perlu mempunyai petugas yang jelas dikenalpasti sedang bertugas, pengganti apabila petugas tersebut tiada, serta rekod kebimbangan yang dibangkitkan dan tindakan yang diambil yang disimpan dengan selamat. Ketiga, sediakan saluran aduan yang diyakini pelajar. Seorang pelajar perlu boleh bercakap secara sulit dengan lebih daripada seorang petugas yang ditetapkan, termasuk seseorang di luar rantaian pengurusan harian asrama. lbu bapa juga mesti tahu siapa yang boleh dihubungi. Laporan mengenai keganasan atau ugutan perlu mendapat respons segera, penilaian terhadap keselamatan pelajar, perlindungan daripada tindakan balas dan tindakan susulan. Pelajar perlu diberitahu dengan jelas bahawa melaporkan perbuatan yang memudaratkan orang lain ialah tindakan berani, bukannya perbuatan tidak setia kepada rakan. Keempat, fahami keperluan setiap pelajar apabila mereka mula tinggal di asrama. Pihak sekolah perlu berbincang dengan pelajar dan ibu bapa tentang penyesuaian kepada kehidupan berasrama, sebarang kebimbangan keselamatan yang pernah timbul, dan sokongan yang mungkin diperlukan. Jika sesuatu kebimbangan memerlukan penilaian lanjut, profesional yang berkelayakan perlu dilibatkan. Maklumat yang diperoleh mesti dirahsiakan dan digunakan untuk merancang sokongan serta penyeliaan yang sesuai, bukan untuk melabel seorang pelajar atau menafikan aksesnya kepada pendidikan berdasarkan andaian yang belum diuji. Kelima, jadikan larangan terhadap keganasan suatu amalan yang benar-benar dilaksanakan. Pengetua, warden, guru disiplin, kaunselor dan, jika berkaitan, ustaz atau pendidik agama lain perlu menyampaikan mesej yang sama secara konsisten. Perhimpunan mingguan dan pertemuan di asrama boleh digunakan untuk membincangkan batas pergaulan, tekanan rakan sebaya, cara menegur dengan hormat dan cara mendapatkan bantuan. Toleransi sitar terhadap keganasan mesti diterjemahkan melalui tindakan yang konsisten: setiap laporan diambil serius, pelajar yang terlibat dilindungi, fakta ditentukan dan tindakan diambil secara adil. Arahan kepada pelajar mesti jelas: jangan gunakan kekerasan terhadap pelajar lain; laporkan masalah kepada orang dewasa; dan jika melihat kejadian yang membahayakan seseorang, dapatkan bantuan dengan segera tanpa meletakkan diri sendiri dalam bahaya. Keenam, laksanakan langkah keselamatan yang praktikal. Kementerian perlu menyemak peraturan keselamatan di asrama sekolah dan mengenal pasti kawasan bersama yang sesuai untuk pemantauan CCTV, dengan keutamaan kepada tempat yang mungkin mendedahkan pelajar kepada risiko apabila penyeliaan orang dewasa terhad. Penggunaan kamera mesti menghormati privasi pelajar dan tidak boleh menggantikan kehadiran orang dewasa yang peka. Setiap sistem perlu mempunyai petugas yang bertanggungjawab memastikan ia berfungsi, bertindak apabila kejadian dilaporkan dan menyimpan rakaman berkaitan sebelum rakaman itu terpadam secara automatik. Akses kepada rakaman hendaklah dihadkan dan direkodkan, manakala rakaman yang relevan perlu diserahkan segera kepada penyiasat melalui saluran yang betul dengan perlindungan terhadap identiti pelajar yang dirakam. Kebertanggungjawaban mesti melangkaui kes ini. Persoalan yang timbul daripada kematian ini mesti membawa kepada tindakan yang dapat dilihat oleh ibu bapa dan pelajar. Kementerian perlu menerbitkan dapatan utama audit sebaik sahaja hal itu dapat dilakukan tanpa menjejaskan siasatan polis atau privasi pelajar yang terlibat. Kementerian juga perlu menyatakan perkara yang akan diperbetulkan, pegawai yang bertanggungjawab dan tarikh setiap tindakan perlu diselesaikan. Semakan yang sama hendaklah diperluas ke asrama lain, dengan kemajuan pelaksanaannya dimaklumkan kepada umum. Mesej tentang keganasan yang diterima golongan muda di luar sekolah juga wajar diberi perhatian. Penggiat industri kreatif dan badan kawal selia perlu meneliti cara perbuatan membuli dipaparkan kepada penonton muda, khususnya apabila ugutan dan kekerasan digambarkan seolah-olah memberikan kuasa atau tidak membawa akibat. Pandangan golongan muda tentang mesej yang mereka fahami daripada kandungan yang ditonton patut didengar. Gambaran dalam karya kreatif tidak boleh dijadikan penjelasan bagi kematian Muhammad ldlan; fakta kes ini mesti ditentukan oleh penyiasat. Tanggungjawab menjaga keselamatan pelajar tetap terletak pada orang dewasa dan institusi yang diamanahkan menjaga mereka. lbu bapa menyerahkan anak kepada sekolah untuk dijaga, bukan semata-mata untuk memperoleh keputusan peperiksaan. Keluarga Muhammad ldlan berhak mengetahui kebenaran tentang apa yang berlaku. Setiap pelajar yang tinggal di asrama berhak mempunyai orang dewasa yang boleh dipercayai untuk diminta pertolongan, serta sistem yang bertindak sebelum sesuatu kemudaratan tidak lagi dapat dihalang. – CPSM Dato’ Seri Nazir Ariff ialah presiden Children’s Protection Society Malaysia. English version A child died in a school hostel. What must change before another child is hurt? The death of 14-year-old Muhammad ldlan Fareeq Shahril has left a family grieving and parents across Malaysia asking a painful question: is my child safe in a school hostel? On behalf of the Children’s Protection Society Malaysia (CPSM), I extend our deepest condolences to Muhammad ldlan’s parents and family. No statement can lessen their loss. They deserve compassion, privacy, truthful answers and justice. We acknowledge that Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek met the family and school community and directed an immediate audit. We welcome her assurance that no one will be protected if wrongdoing is established. The police must be allowed to establish the facts, including the cause and circumstances of Muhammad ldlan’s death. We must not turn an allegation into a finding or expose the children involved to public judgement before the investigation is complete. But an investigation into one incident cannot be the end of the matter. An audit must answer a harder question: were there concerns before Muhammad ldlan’s death, and did the hostel have a reliable way to recognise and respond to them? That question must be asked without presuming what happened in this case. A hostel takes responsibility for children during the hours when their parents cannot see them. That responsibility extends beyond a register of occupants and a set of rules on a noticeboard. It requires adults who know the children to notice changes in behaviour, respond to concerns and remain accountable for what happens after classes end. No student has the authority to enforce discipline by force. If a student is suspected of breaking a rule, whether it concerns vaping, a missing item, disrespect or anything else, the matter belongs with responsible adults. A child must never be slapped, struck, restrained, threatened or subjected to a punishment devised by other students. A student who sees a problem should report it to a warden or disciplinary teacher. There is no place for self-appointed enforcers in a dormitory, hostel or school. The CPSM therefore calls on the Ministry of Education to use the current audit to begin a clear, time-bound review of hostel safety. That review should address the following. First, find out whether warning signs were missed. Investigators and auditors should examine earlier complaints, informal reports, requests to change rooms, unexplained injuries, absences, changes in behaviour and concerns raised by parents, where such information exists. They should establish who received each concern, what action followed, and whether anyone checked back with the child. A finding that no complaints were recorded would need to be considered alongside whether children had a safe and credible way to speak up. Second, put adult supervision where and when children need it. Wardens cannot provide careful oversight if they are responsible for too many students, buildings or duties at once. The ministry should review hostel staffing, night coverage, handovers and escalation arrangements. Every hostel should have an identifiable adult on duty, a clear arrangement for cover when that adult is unavailable, and a secure record of concerns raised and action taken. Third, give children a reporting route they can trust. A child should be able to speak privately to more than one designated adult, including someone outside the hostel’s daily chain of command. Parents must know whom to contact. Reports involving violence or threats must receive a prompt response, an assessment of the child’s immediate safety, protection against retaliation and follow-up. Children must be told plainly that reporting harm is an act of courage, not disloyalty. Fourth, understand each child’s needs at hostel intake. Schools should speak with students and parents about adjustment to hostel life, previous safety concerns and any support the child may need. Where a concern warrants further assessment, a qualified professional should be involved. Information gathered must be kept confidential and used to plan appropriate support and supervision, not to label a child or deny access to education on the basis of an untested assumption. Fifth, make the rule against violence a living practice. Principals, wardens, disciplinary teachers, counsellors and, where relevant, ustaz or other religious educators should reinforce the same message. Weekly assemblies and hostel meetings can provide regular opportunities to discuss boundaries, peer pressure, respectful correction and how to seek help. Zero tolerance must mean a consistent response to violence: taking every report seriously, protecting the children involved, establishing the facts and acting fairly. The instructions to students must be unmistakable: keep your hands off another child, report the issue to an adult, and intervene safely by getting help. Sixth, act on practical security measures. The ministry should review security arrangements across school hostels and identify shared areas where CCTV would strengthen oversight, with priority given to locations where children may be particularly vulnerable and adult supervision is limited. Cameras must respect children’s privacy and cannot replace attentive adults. Any system must have designated personnel responsible for checking that it works, responding to reported incidents and preserving relevant recordings before they are overwritten. Access to footage should be restricted and documented, with prompt provision to investigators through proper channels and safeguards for the children recorded. Accountability must extend beyond this case. The questions raised by this death must lead to action that parents and children can see. The ministry should publish the audit’s key findings as soon as it can do so, without compromising the police investigation or the privacy of the children involved. It should state what will be corrected, who is responsible and when each action will be completed. The review should then be extended to other hostels, with progress reported publicly. The wider messages children receive about violence also deserve attention. Creative industries and regulators should consider how bullying is portrayed to young audiences, particularly when intimidation appears powerful or free of consequences. Young people should be heard on the messages they take from what they watch. Such portrayals cannot explain Muhammad ldlan’s death; the facts of this case are for investigators to establish. The duty to keep children safe remains with the adults and institutions entrusted with their care. Parents entrust schools with their children, not merely their exam results. Muhammad ldlan’s family deserves the truth about what happened. Every child living in a hostel deserves a trusted adult to turn to and a system that responds before harm becomes irreversible. – CPSM Dato’ Seri Nazir Ariff is the president of the Children’s Protection Society Malaysia. title: 'Religion is not a political tool: Due process must follow Noorazli’s remarks
body: 'Community Action Network (CAN) Malaysia views with grave concern the recent conduct of Sepang Umno chief Noorazli Said, who misquoted sacred biblical scripture Psalms 129 while making inappropriate remarks during the recent Umno general assembly. Faith is sacred – not a political punchline: Religion should never be weaponised, trivialised or used as a tool for political posturing. In a multi-religious society like Malaysia, leaders across the political spectrum must treat all sacred texts and religious communities with absolute respect. Exploiting faith and sacred traditions on political platforms damages the delicate fabric of social harmony. The rule is simple: all religions must be respected equally and just like the commandments we subscribe to, we must treat thy neighbours as how we want to be treated. Ignorance is no excuse for political leaders: CAN is deeply appalled that a senior political leader could recklessly misquote the Bible to deliver a crude and sexual analogy that is completely devoid of the original text. Leadership demands accountability, precision and basic literacy regarding the diverse beliefs of the electorate. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member If a leader lacks knowledge on a matter – especially one involving sacred texts, the standard must be simple: if you do not know, do not say it. Misinformation masked as political rhetoric sets a dangerous precedent. Apologies do not preempt the law – due process must take place: While CAN acknowledges that Noorazli has issued a public apology, an apology alone does not erase legal responsibility or mitigate the impact of inﬂammatory speech. A healthy democracy relies on the consistent application of the rule of law. Apologising cannot serve as a free pass to bypass statutory oversight. Authorities must handle this matter with complete impartiality. Due process must take its course, and a thorough investigation by the relevant enforcement bodies must be conducted to determine whether legal standards were breached. Equal enforcement of the law is necessary to signal that religious provocation will carry consequences, regardless of political affiliation. A reconciliation mechanism is much needed in Malaysia, particularly in the context of the religious rhetoric and controversies that have taken place over the years. Too often, there is no clear or meaningful process through which harm, hurt and grievances arising from statements or actions concerning religion can be acknowledged and addressed. A nation that moves forward is one that is courageous enough to acknowledge when words or actions have caused hurt, disrespect or oﬀence to another person’s religion, beliefs or place of worship. Reconciliation is not about assigning blame or suppressing diﬃcult conversations. It is about creating a constructive space for acknowledgement, dialogue, accountability and, where appropriate, an apology. In the light of this, CAN calls on all political leaders to elevate the standard of public discourse and refrain from dragging religious texts and ﬁgures into political theatrics and to advocate for a meaningful reconciliation mechanism that will provide a space, allowing grievances to be heard and addressed before they deepen existing divisions. At the same time, CAN applauds and commends the political leaders, civil society organisations and concerned people across party and religious lines who promptly called out this unacceptable behaviour. Their swift condemnation demonstrates that ordinary people are united in refusing to normalise religious disrespect, setting a necessary standard for interfaith courtesy and national unity. In this regard, it is also opportune for us to wish everyone a Happy Malaysia Day! May this day be remembered for the commonality we share as true-spirited people who care about a greater Malaysia. – CAN, 17 September The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'TNB Moving Higher Up The ESG Ladder
body: 'Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) is strengthening its environmental, social and governance (ESG) profile through major renewable energy and hydroelectric upgrades that align with Malaysia’s national energy transition agenda.  Following an investor webinar held by TNB on Oct 1, it was highlighted that the utility group’s Hybrid Hydro Floating Solar (HHFS) project at Tasik Kenyir and the Sungai Perak Hydro Life Extension Programme (HLEP) as two initiatives supporting the transition towards a lower-carbon electricity system.  Malaysia’s National Energy Transition Roadmap (NETR) targets renewable energy accounting for 70% of installed power capacity by 2050, a target reaffirmed by the government as recently as September.  The first phase of the Kenyir project, known as Kenyir #1, will comprise 595MWac of floating solar capacity integrated with a 297.5MW battery energy storage system (BESS).  The engineering, procurement, construction and commissioning contract has been awarded to the Cypark-Sunview consortium, with commercial operations targeted for the fourth quarter of 2028.  TNB expects the project to generate a high single-digit equity internal rate of return, despite floating solar requiring around 10% to 15% higher capital expenditure than conventional ground-mounted solar.  The economics are supported by a 21-year Corporate Renewable Energy Supply Scheme (CRESS) offtake agreement with DayOne Data Centers, CIMB said.  From an ESG perspective, TNB highlighted several advantages of the floating solar project. These include higher power output from the cooling effect of the water body, the avoidance of land clearing and an estimated reduction of 650,000 tonnes of carbon dioxide emissions annually.  The project is also expected to have limited impact on Tasik Kenyir’s biodiversity as the installation will occupy only about 1.4% of the lake’s surface area.  Alongside new solar capacity, TNB is investing RM5.8 billion in rehabilitating and upgrading its ageing Sungai Perak Hydroelectric Plant network.  The HLEP covers five hydroelectric stations with a combined installed capacity of 648MW. Progress had reached 36% as of June 2026, with commissioning scheduled progressively between 2026 and 2033.  Once completed, the plants are expected to operate for another 40 years under a new power purchase agreement, allowing TNB to preserve existing renewable generation assets while extending their productive lifespan.  CIMB said both initiatives fit with the NETR’s emphasis on expanding renewable generation and energy storage capacity. The roadmap identifies renewable energy as one of Malaysia’s core energy-transition levers.  The research house maintained its BUY call and RM15.90 target price on TNB, while keeping its FY2026-FY2028 core earnings forecasts unchanged.  CIMB does not expect the projects to provide a meaningful earnings boost over the next three years, given their development timelines, but views them positively for TNB’s longer-term sustainability positioning and said they could contribute to further improvements in the group’s ESG ratings.

title: 'Four Sikh scholars show the opportunities beyond SPM
body: 'By Manjit Singh | Malaysia | Four Malaysian Sikh students have secured fully funded scholarships for overseas studies in 2026, showing how strong academic results, co-curricular involvement and persistence can open doors to leading universities abroad. Dilpreet Kaur, Gurmansimran Kaur, Priety Kaur and Satishver Singh all began their scholarship journeys after completing the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM), the national public examination taken by all Form 5 secondary school students in Malaysia at the end of their 11th year of formal education. Their scholarships supported their progression through pre-university studies and on to undergraduate programmes overseas. SEE ALSO: Malaysian Sikh Education Aid Fund (MSEAF) Dilpreet will pursue a BSc in Chemistry at Imperial College London, while Gurmansimran will study Accounting and Finance at the University of Manchester. Priety will pursue an MEng in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, also at Manchester, while Satishver is pursuing Data Science at the University of California, Berkeley. Beyond their academic achievements, the four say scholarship applicants should start preparing early and recognise that selectors often look beyond examination grades. Leadership roles, competitions, volunteering, research, internships, community activities and other experiences can help students develop the skills and interests that strengthen an application. Their other key advice: apply widely. Scholarship applications can involve setbacks and rejection, they say, but students should continue looking for opportunities instead of allowing one unsuccessful application to end the journey. They also encourage students to seek internships or research experience connected with their intended university courses. Such exposure can help applicants better understand their chosen fields while demonstrating genuine interest beyond the classroom. Maintaining balance is equally important. The scholars say academic ambition need not come at the expense of friendships, community involvement or personal wellbeing. Co-curricular activities can build confidence, social skills and networks while helping students discover interests they may eventually pursue professionally. WHAT DO THEY SAY Dilpreet’s message to other students is simple: “You are more capable than you think. Believe in yourself.” Gurmansimran stresses the lasting value of education, while Priety encourages students moving away from home to remain independent but grounded and positive. Satishver advises youngsters not to allow setbacks to define their journey: “It is never too late to turn the page, rewrite the plot or begin a new chapter.” Collectively, the four encourage students to look seriously at scholarship opportunities after SPM. Major scholarship programmes available to Malaysian students include those offered by JPA, PETRONAS, Bank Negara Malaysia, Yayasan Khazanah, Yayasan Tenaga Nasional, Yayasan Telekom Malaysia, Yayasan Sime Darby, Shell Malaysia, Yayasan UEM, CIMB ASEAN and Yayasan Gamuda. Application periods, eligibility requirements and funding terms vary, so students should regularly check the respective organisations’ official scholarship pages. Their common message to younger students is to aim high, ask questions, seek opportunities and apply — even when a scholarship appears highly competitive. “We hope to see more Sikh students pursuing their ambitions on a global stage,” they said. title: 'Existing taxes key to 2027 Budget, expect few major changes: Expert
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia is likely to focus on improving tax collection and fine-tuning existing taxes rather than introducing major new levies in 2027 Budget, according to KPMG senior tax policy adviser Dr Veerinderjeet Singh. He said stronger enforcement, better use of tax agency analytics and broader tax bases could provide additional revenue while supporting the government's fiscal consolidation efforts. Speaking at a forum hosted by CIMB Securities, Veerinderjeet said the government should "sweat our assets". This is by improving collection efficiency, with scope to gradually raise Malaysia's tax-to-gross domestic product ratio towards 15 per cent through stronger personal, corporate and indirect tax bases. He expects few major tax changes in the upcoming budget, given the continued focus on cost-of-living support and social spending. Recent measures such as the dividend and capital gains taxes reflect a more progressive tax system, although he does not expect the two per cent dividend tax to be raised or capital gains tax extended to listed shares in the budget. A further increase in the 30 per cent top personal income tax rate also appears unlikely. On the sales and service tax (SST), Veerinderjeet estimates coverage has reached about 78-80 per cent of goods and services, bringing it closer to the breadth of the former goods and services tax (GST). He sees scope for broader input exemptions under SST to reduce cascading effects and business costs, although this would mean some revenue loss. GST reinstatement is not expected in thr 2027 Budget, with improving SST efficiency likely to take precedence. Wider e-invoicing participation could also help uncover unreported taxable activity, although exemptions for smaller businesses may be gradually reduced as economic conditions improve. On other measures, Veerinderjeet expects limited additional revenue from the global minimum tax until the first filing cycle provides clearer evidence of collections. A carbon tax remains on the policy agenda but could be delayed to 2028 or later amid business cost pressures. The budget may reaffirm the government's intention to introduce it, potentially at a low initial rate. He also sees only a slight possibility of modest excise duty increases on alcohol and tobacco, while no new windfall levy is expected. For real estate investment trusts, he does not expect the former 10 per cent final withholding tax on distributions to return, although he supports withholding mechanisms to reduce filing and monitoring costs.

title: 'Umumkan minit lembaga pengampunan / Make pardons board’s minutes public – 37 NGOs
body: '[ENGLISH VERSION BELOW] Pada ketika negara masih menanggung beban kewangan yang amat besar akibat berbilion ringgit yang diselewengkan dalam skandal 1MDB dan SRC International, persepsi bahawa seorang pegawai tertinggi yang telah disabitkan kesalahan, khususnya bekas Perdana Menteri Najib Razak, iaitu melalui pemberian pengurangan hukuman serta layanan penahanan istimewa (contohnya, diberikan hukuman tahanan rumah yang belum pernah berlaku sebelum ini) telah menjejaskan kepercayaan rakyat. Beban akibat rasuah peringkat tinggi akhirnya ditanggung oleh rakyat, yang menanggung kesan melalui kehilangan hasil negara, beban pembayaran hutang negara, serta pengurangan dana untuk infrastruktur awam dan pembangunan ekonomi yang penting. Terdapat kebimbangan kritikal yang menjejaskan negara kita. Keputusan berkaitan hasil perundangan Najib – daripada pengurangan separuh hukuman penjara asal 12 tahun dan pengurangan denda daripada RM210j kepada RM50j, hinggalah kepada peralihan bersyarat kepada tahanan rumah – menimbulkan persoalan mendalam mengenai ketelusan, akauntabiliti dan kedaulatan undang-undang di Malaysia. Bagi menegakkan integriti sistem keadilan Malaysia dan memenuhi tanggungjawab kepada rakyat, lembaga pengampunan mesti mendedahkan sepenuhnya minit serta justifikasi yang direkodkan dalam proses membuat keputusan. Pendedahan menyeluruh adalah penting untuk menjelaskan bagaimana kes yang melibatkan penyelewengan institusi berskala besar boleh berakhir dengan pelbagai pengurangan hukuman dan kini membolehkan Najib yang telah disabitkan kesalahan menikmati keistimewaan tahanan rumah. Ketelusan penuh daripada lembaga pengampunan bukan sekadar satu permintaan – ia merupakan langkah penting untuk memastikan prinsip layanan sama rata di bawah undang-undang tanpa wujudnya diskriminasi dalam pelaksanaannya (antara dua darjat) ditegakkan dan membuktikan bahawa tiada individu yang berada di atas undang-undang. The burden of high-level corruption ultimately falls upon the people, who pay the price through lost public revenue, national debt servicing, and reduced funding for essential public infrastructure and economic development. There are critical concerns that affect our nation. The decisions surrounding Najib’s legal outcome – from the halving of his original 12-year prison sentence and the reduction of his fine from RM210m to RM50m, to his conditional transition to house arrest – raise profound concerns regarding transparency, accountability and the rule of law in Malaysia. To uphold the integrity of Malaysia’s justice system and satisfy its obligation to the public, the pardons board must release the full minutes and recorded justifications of its decision-making process. Complete disclosure is essential to explain how a case involving massive institutional embezzlement resulted in multiple sentence reductions and the convicted Najib now given house arrest privileges. Full transparency from the pardons board is not merely a request – it is a vital measure to ensure that the principle of equal treatment under the law, without discrimination in its application (antara dua darjat or double standards) is upheld and to prove that no individual stands above the law. title: 'Are Chinese Malaysian-owned SMEs being ‘killed’ by the China onslaught?
body: 'The Gut Shot Podcast is joined by its geopolitical and economic consultant to governments and companies, Jason Leong. Signals from the ground have now raised alarm among segments of the Chinese Malaysian community. Malaysia’s private sector economy is largely driven by local ethnic Chinese businesses. Unlike the ecosystem of government-linked firms and investment companies, the private sector economy has none of the protection that bumiputra monopolies and oligopolies enjoy. The retail, mechanic workshops, construction services and supply chains, food and beverage and other service businesses are not abstract figures on an economist’s spreadsheet. They are livelihoods that have survived for decades. They have employed workers, paid taxes, supported families and funded the education of the next generation. Now a wave of imported competition from China, at scaled-down and even cut-throat prices, has reached our shores with devastating effect. When businesses across very different sectors begin telling the same story at the same time (vanishing margins, slowing customers, rising costs, price competition that cannot be met and a daily struggle to survive), we should not dismiss it as a series of isolated failures or a lack of competitiveness. This podcast explores the damage to local ethnic Chinese-driven small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in both macro and micro terms, calmly and without sentiment and makes some policy recommendations. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member It examines why, however efficient our supply chains become, resistance on scale alone will be futile: massive state subsidies, fierce internal competition within China that no other country can replicate, and a capital structure built to chase market share at any cost. The official macro numbers may not have captured this yet. Perhaps no one has measured it properly or raised the alarm. But the signals are real. By the time everyone agrees there is a crisis, many of these businesses could already be gone. If we fail to recognise the systemic forces behind China’s global dominance and act accordingly, we may be witnessing the beginning of the end of the traditional, generations-old Chinese Malaysian SMEs ecosystem. body: 'Bursa Malaysia meneruskan kenaikan pada tengah hari Jumaat, dengan indeks utama disokong oleh aktiviti belian ketika harga rendah dalam beberapa saham wajaran tinggi terpilih. title: 'High Court issues arrest warrant for accused in Palestinian abduction case
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court today issued an arrest warrant for an accused in the 2022 abduction of a Palestinian man after he failed to appear for pre-trial case management. Judge Datuk Mohd Arief Emran Arifin issued the warrant against Muhammad Iqmal Abdul Rahis, 31, the seventh of eight accused, after allowing an application by deputy public prosecutor Zaileen Nadia Zubir. During the proceedings, Zaileen told the court that Iqmal had been uncontactable since Sept 11 and that his bailor had lodged a police report. The judge then asked the bailor to explain the situation. She told the court that she had gone to Iqmal's house to look for him but was unable to locate him. "I also went to his village in Tanjung Sepat, Kuala Langat, in Selangor and even searched a nearby oil palm plantation. "However, even his siblings did not know his whereabouts. "That prompted me to lodge a police report on his disappearance," she said. Zaileen also said police had gone to Tanjung Sepat to interview Iqmal's parents about his whereabouts. "Police investigations showed that his father said his son had not returned to the village since January. Efforts to trace him are still ongoing," she said. In addition to issuing the arrest warrant, Arief Emran ordered the RM50,000 bail to be returned to the bailor after hearing that she had made efforts to locate Iqmal. Iqmal was represented by lawyer Goh Cia Yee. The other seven accused, who are out on bail, were present in court today. They are Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 45; Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 45; Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 46; Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 60; Nidarahayu Zainal, 40; Raibafie Amdan, 45; and Edy Ko'im Said, 46. The court had previously fixed the trial for Oct 12 to 15, Oct 19 to 23, and Oct 26 to 29. In October 2022, 13 men and a woman were charged at the magistrate's court here with abducting Palestinian Omar ZM Albelbaisy Raeda, 35, allegedly to obtain a reward in the form of information relating to software used to hack mobile phones. They were Edy Ko'im, 45; Mohamad Norakmal Hassan, 46; Dody Junaidi, 47; Tengku Arif Bongsu Tengku Hamid, 44; Mohamad Naziree Mustapha, 44; Faizull Hardey Mohd Isa, 45; Muhammad Iqmal, 30; Mohamad Sufian Saly, 28; Muhammad Al Hatim; Nidarahayu Zainal, 39; Raibafie Amdan, 44; Mohd Zaidi Mohd Zain, 59; Mohd Azwan Jamaludin, 42; and Tengku Hazarul Ismail Tengku Hamid, 54. They were charged with committing the offence at Jalan Mayang here about 10.40pm on Sept 28, 2022. The charge was framed under Section 3 of the Kidnapping Act 1961, read together with Section 34 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between 30 and 40 years and whipping upon conviction. On Oct 20, 2023, Tengku Arif Bongsu, together with married couple Nidarahayu and Raibafie, were also charged with 19 counts of money laundering involving more than RM250,000. For the first to fourth charges, Nidarahayu was accused of disposing of RM20,650.86 in proceeds from unlawful activity from her savings account at CIMB Bank into two other bank accounts at CIMB Bank and Maybank Islamic Bhd's Taman Maluri branch between Sept 15 and Oct 3, 2022. She also faced 13 charges of transferring RM184,985.46 into the accounts of four companies and eight individuals, also allegedly proceeds from unlawful activity, between Sept 15 and Oct 2 that year. Raibafie and Tengku Arif Bongsu were respectively charged with receiving RM30,350 and RM25,000 from two bank accounts belonging to Nidarahayu and a company at CIMB Bank's Jalan Bukit Bintang and Taman Mutiara, Cheras branches between Sept 29 and Oct 2, 2022. The charges were framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Anti-Money Laundering, Anti-Terrorism Financing and Proceeds of Unlawful Activities Act 2001, which carries a maximum 15-year jail term and a fine of five times the value of the unlawful activity or RM5 million, whichever is higher, upon conviction. On July 10, 2025, six men were sentenced to five years in jail by the High Court here after pleading guilty to an alternative charge of forcibly taking and confining the victim. Judge K. Muniandy, who is now a Court of Appeal judge, imposed the sentence on Mohamad Norakmal, Mohd Azwan, Dody, Mohamad Sufian, Tengku Hazarul Ismail and Muhammad Al Hatim. According to the charge, they were accused of forcibly taking the victim and wrongfully and secretly confining him at Jalan Mayang, Dang Wangi, here, at 10.40pm on Sept 28, 2022. All six were charged under Section 365 of the Penal Code, read together with Section 34, which carries a jail term of up to seven years and a fine. According to the facts of the case, the victim was abducted and confined at a chalet in Hulu Langat. A police raid, carried out based on information received, led to the victim's rescue. title: 'Bursa Malaysia’s Key Index Stays Higher at Midday on Bargain Hunting
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 – Bursa Malaysia’s benchmark index maintained its upward momentum through the Friday morning session, rising 0.33 per cent by midday as bargain hunting in key blue-chip heavyweights supported market sentiment. At 12:30 PM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) gained 5.44 points to reach 1,635.80, compared with Thursday’s close of 1,630.36. The index had opened 3.51 points higher at 1,633.87 and traded within a range of 1,630.63 to 1,640.78 throughout the morning session. Despite the rise in the benchmark index, broader market breadth remained slightly tilted toward decliners, with 507 stocks falling compared to 499 gainers. Another 494 counters traded unchanged, 1,273 remained untraded, and 24 were suspended. Half-day trading volume reached 2.24 billion shares valued at RM1.26 billion. Heavyweights and Active Counters Financial, utility, and healthcare blue chips provided the primary support to the key index: - Tenaga Nasional advanced 16 sen to RM13.06. - IHH Healthcare expanded 11 sen to RM7.81. - Maybank climbed 9 sen to RM10.04. - Public Bank added 4 sen to RM4.71. - CIMB edged down 1 sen to RM7.68. Active trading was led by technology and glove counters. JCY International surged 10 sen to 65.5 sen, Top Glove inched up 3.5 sen to 77 sen, V.S Industry ticked up 2 sen to 29 sen, and Jaks Resources added half a sen to 18.5 sen. Conversely, Zetrix AI declined 2.5 sen to 14 sen. Technology firms dominated the top gainers list: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Surged 84 sen to RM41.96. - UWC & United Plantations: Both perked up 36 sen to RM7.46 and RM31.32, respectively. - Vitrox & UMS Integration: Both accumulated 34 sen to RM10.34 and RM8.99, respectively. Decliners were led by plantation and consumer counters: - Kuala Lumpur Kepong: Led losses, dropping 46 sen to RM20.96. - Enra: Fell 29 sen to 69 sen. - Allianz Malaysia: Declined 28 sen to RM20.72. - BLD Plantations: Shed 26 sen to RM14.74. - Dutch Lady Milk Industries: Erased 20 sen to RM29.80. Index and Sectoral Performance Sectoral indices posted gains across the board at the midday break: - The Financial Services Index climbed 55.60 points to 19,116.51. - The Plantation Index gained 4.58 points to 9,031.15. - The Energy Index rose 1.06 points to 836.07. - The Industrial Products and Services Index edged up 0.99 of a point to 178.72. Across broader market indices: - The FBM Mid 70 Index rose 115.75 points to 17,474.73. - The FBM Emas Shariah Index climbed 66.45 points to 12,079.46. - The FBM Emas Index added 51.08 points to 12,194.61. - The FBM Top 100 Index advanced 50.09 points to 11,983.24. - The FBM ACE Index improved 6.33 points to 5,489.30. –NMT

title: 'TNB share price up on Kenyir project's outlook
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Tenaga Nasional Bhd's share price rose in early trading on Friday with its Kenyir Hydrogen Hybrid Fuel System (HHFS) project expected to generate a high single-digit equity internal rate of return. As at 9.57 am, TNB's share price rose eight sen to RM12.98 with 889,300 shares traded. According to MBSB Investment Bank (MBSB IB), electricity demand is also expected to remain strong, with growth projected at 5.4 per cent in calendar year 2026. "We continue to view TNB as a key beneficiary and enabler of Malaysia's energy transition, supported by rising regulated grid capex, growing battery energy storage system requirements and sizeable renewable energy opportunities through initiatives such as HHFS. As such, MBSB IB has maintained its "Buy" recommendation on TNB, with an unchanged discounted cash flow (DCF)-derived target price of RM16.31. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd has also maintained its "Buy" recommendation, with an unchanged DCF-based target price of RM15.90.

title: 'Ibu janji nak ambil dari sekolah, tapi dia pergi selamanya'
body: 'Gua Musang: Hancur hati dua beradik apabila ibu yang dinanti untuk menjemput pulang dari sekolah tidak kunjung tiba, sebaliknya berita duka diterima apabila insan tersayang itu meninggal dunia akibat kemalangan. Nur Arissa Najla Mohd Shazuam, 13, dan Nur Amani Nuwairah Mohd Shazuam, 15, menanti penuh sabar selepas ibunya, Nor Hasyikim Daud, 34, berjanji untuk mengambilnya pulang dari sekolah di Sekolah Menengah Kebangsaan (SMK) Bandar Chiku. Nur Arissa Najla berkata, dia menerima berita ibunya kemalangan daripada seorang rakan pada jam 1.40 tengah hari. Katanya, ketika itu dia bersama kakak sedang menunggu ibunya yang berjanji untuk mengambil mereka pulang dari sekolah. "Ibu ada maklumkan akan ke Bandar Gua Musang dengan rakannya dan berjanji mengambil saya dan kakak dari sekolah. "Pada hari kejadian, saya menduduki tiga kertas peperiksaan dan sangat teruja untuk memberitahu ibu yang saya boleh jawab semua soalan subjek Sejarah.
