title: 'DNB selesai pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion, pacu fasa baharu pertumbuhan 5G Malaysia
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) berjaya menyelesaikan pembiayaan berjangka Islamik bersindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan kewangan syarikat bagi menyokong perkembangan rangkaian 5G Malaysia.  Transaksi berkenaan antara kemudahan pinjaman bersindiket terbesar pernah diatur untuk sebuah syarikat tidak tersenarai di Malaysia.  Maybank Investment Bank Berhad bertindak sebagai Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner dan Coordinating Arranger, manakala AmInvestment Bank Berhad, CIMB Islamic Bank Berhad, RHB Islamic Bank Berhad dan United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Berhad bertindak sebagai Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers.  AmInvestment Bank Berhad pula bertindak sebagai penasihat kewangan kepada DNB.  Menurut DNB, kejayaan menyelesaikan pembiayaan itu merupakan perkembangan penting dalam evolusi syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa seterusnya dalam pelaksanaan rangkaian 5G dwi-rangkaian.  Pembiayaan berkenaan dijangka mengukuhkan kedudukan kewangan jangka panjang DNB selain memudah cara perancangan keluar MOF Inc. sebagai pemegang saham biasa syarikat.  Ia seterusnya membuka laluan kepada struktur pemilikan sama rata antara pemegang saham syarikat telekomunikasi mudah alih (MNO), iaitu CelcomDigi Berhad menerusi Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd.  Peralihan kepada struktur pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026.  Bagaimanapun, MOF Inc. akan mengekalkan satu saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan nasional.  Menurut DNB, saham khas itu akan membolehkan kerajaan terus memainkan peranan dalam perkara strategik utama, pada masa sama memberi ruang kepada syarikat meneruskan fasa pembangunan seterusnya.  Pembiayaan bersindiket itu turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF) DNB yang tamat tempoh pada 29 September 2026.  Langkah itu turut mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang yang lebih mampan bagi menyokong pertumbuhan DNB pada masa depan.  Spektrum 240 MHz diperkukuh  Penyelesaian pembiayaan itu turut dibuat serentak dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100 MHz dalam jalur 3.3 hingga 3.4 GHz atau F0 serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum DNB berjumlah 240 MHz kepada Spectrum Assignment.  DNB berkata, selepas Spectrum Assignment dikeluarkan Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC), penugasan itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober 2026.  Perkembangan itu memberikan kepastian kawal selia yang lebih tinggi selain mengukuhkan keupayaan DNB untuk menyokong keperluan kesalinghubungan 5G Malaysia yang semakin berkembang.  Pegangan spektrum 240 MHz berkenaan dijangka meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, sekali gus membolehkan kelajuan lebih tinggi, kependaman lebih rendah serta pengalaman pelanggan yang lebih baik.  Ia turut menyokong penggunaan teknologi 5G yang lebih maju termasuk Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced serta keupayaan rangkaian berasaskan kecerdasan buatan (AI).  DNB berkata, gabungan pembiayaan baharu dan penugasan spektrum itu akan memperkukuh keupayaan syarikat meningkatkan kualiti serta daya tahan rangkaian, memenuhi permintaan masa depan dan menyokong aspirasi ekonomi digital Malaysia.  Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif DNB, Datuk Azman Ismail, berkata penyelesaian pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion itu merupakan pencapaian penting yang mencerminkan keyakinan terhadap asas perniagaan, rekod operasi serta peranan jangka panjang syarikat dalam ekonomi digital Malaysia.  “Pembiayaan ini menyediakan platform yang mampan untuk DNB beroperasi secara sendiri, meneruskan pelaburan dalam peningkatan rangkaian dan peluasan kapasiti serta memanfaatkan aset spektrum kami yang telah diperluaskan.  “Ketika Malaysia bergerak maju di bawah rangkaian dwi-rangkaian, DNB kekal komited menyediakan infrastruktur digital bertaraf dunia yang menyokong pemegang saham, pelanggan, perusahaan dan agensi kerajaan,” katanya.  Beliau berkata, dengan kedudukan kewangan yang kukuh, sumber spektrum yang dipertingkatkan serta platform 5G nasional yang telah terbukti, DNB berada pada kedudukan untuk menyokong aspirasi kerajaan menjadikan Malaysia sebagai negara berteraskan AI.  “DNB akan membantu memacu fasa seterusnya pertumbuhan digital Malaysia,” katanya.  DNB turut merakamkan penghargaan kepada pemegang sahamnya, CelcomDigi, Maxis dan YTL, atas keyakinan serta sokongan berterusan terhadap syarikat.  Penghargaan turut diberikan kepada Kerajaan Malaysia dan MCMC atas bimbingan serta sokongan dalam menjayakan agenda transformasi digital negara.  DNB turut mengucapkan terima kasih kepada institusi kewangan dan penasihat, penasihat undang-undang serta penyedia perkhidmatan lain yang menyumbang kepakaran bagi memastikan transaksi pembiayaan itu berjaya diselesaikan.

title: 'IOIPG Malaysia REIT to Pay Out Quarterly Dividends, List With Assets Worth RM7.66b
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 24): IOIPG Malaysia REIT is planning to pay out at least 90% of its distributable income on a quarterly basis, as the real estate investment trust seeks listing on the Main Market. The trust is listing with properties in Klang Valley and Penang worth RM7.66 billion combined, according to its draft prospectus. The trust also has the right-of-first-refusal to acquire local assets owned by its sponsor IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG). IOIPG Malaysia REIT will also consider assets of other owners though the priority will be retail, office, industrial and hospitality properties in urban and suburban areas in Malaysia. The proposed initial public offering (IPO) will allow IOI Properties Group to trim its debt from an acquisition spree involving over RM1 billion in 2024. The developer is also considering spinning off its Singapore properties worth RM26 billion into another real estate investment trust. The listing of IOIPG Malaysia REIT was approved by the Securities Commission last month and the target was to complete the listing before the year ends. The IPO will be split into retail and institutional tranches, offering up to 40% of the total issued fund size upon listing. Institutional investors, including cornerstone investors, will be allocated 27% of the total units. Cornerstone investors — typically large institutional investors such as pension funds and insurers — commit to taking up a portion of the IPO shares before they are marketed to other retail and institutional investors. Their presence helps to build up other investors’ confidence to invest in the IPO. Under the retail tranche, shareholders of IOI Properties Group are entitled to 10% of the units on offer on the basis of one unit for every 10 existing shares of the developer held on a date to be determined later. The Malaysian public will only be allocated 2%, while eligible persons under pink form allocation get up to 1% of total units. Net proceeds from the listing will accrue entirely to IOI Properties Group after covering estimated listing expenses totalling about RM4 million. Maybank Investment Bank and AmInvestment Bank are the joint principal advisers, global coordinators, bookrunners, managing underwriters and underwriters. DBS Bank is the joint global coordinator and joint bookrunner. CIMB Investment Bank, Hong Leong Investment Bank, RHB Investment Bank and UOB Kay Hian are the joint bookrunners and underwriters. Oversea-Chinese Banking Corp is also one of the bookrunners. title: 'AEON Credit Closes in on One-year Low as 2Q Results Underwhelm Investors, Analysts
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 30): AEON Credit Service (M) Bhd (KL:AEONCR) fell to its lowest in nearly a year while analysts turned cautious following a weaker-than-expected quarter at the consumer finance firm. At least two research houses downgraded the stock post-results. Earnings in the first-half only accounted for about one-third of the consensus’ full-year forecast, and there are now concerns over rising provisions and write-offs of bad loans going forward. “In our view, this negative trend is likely to persist” into the rest of the financial year ending February 2027, CIMB Securities said and lowered its recommendation to 'reduce' from 'buy'. AEON Credit fell as much as 19 sen or a little under 4% to RM5.00, their lowest since October 2025. The stock closed at RM5.02, down 17 sen or 3.3%, valuing the group at RM2.56 billion. Shares of AEON Credit have been volatile this year as non-performing loans crept up while the company grappled with general slowdown consumer spending on big-ticket items amid macroeconomic uncertainties. Year to date, the stock has lost 12% of its value. RHB Research, meanwhile, cut its recommendation to 'neutral' from 'buy' and flagged rising non-performing loans weighing on profitability. AEON Credit’s pivot towards customers with better credit quality has also led to lower asset yields and some compression in net interest margins, further limiting earnings growth, the house noted. “While financing growth remains healthy, we believe the combination of higher credit costs and weaker yields warrants a more cautious stance,” RHB Research added. The stock still has three 'buy' calls from the five analysts tracked by Bloomberg. The average 12-month target price stood at RM6.25. On Tuesday (Sept 29), AEON Credit reported an 18% year-on-year decline in net profit to RM59.30 million for the second quarter ended Aug 31, 2026, as higher impairment losses on financing receivables offset 7.7% growth in revenue. For the first half, net profit rose 3.1% to RM154.47 million. title: 'ViTrox Hits New Record High as AI-driven Growth Boosts Outlook
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Shares in ViTrox Corporation Bhd (KL:VITROX) hit their highest level since the company’s listing on the ACE Market in 2005 on Tuesday, driven by its strong growth prospects amid the AI infrastructure boom. ViTrox designs & manufactures vision inspection system & handler for back-end semiconductor industry. In a The Edge Malaysia weekly’s Sept 21-Sept 27 issue, its co-founder and managing director Datuk Chu Jenn Weng said the company’s numbers will double this year, with strong growth momentum expected to continue over the next few years. The Penang-based automated test equipment maker’s shares charted an all-time high of RM10.08 before closing up 21 sen or 2.2% at RM10 on Tuesday, giving the company a market capitalisation of a little under RM19 billion. The share price remains below the consensus 12-month target price of RM10.67, while the highest 12-month target price is RM13. The majority of analysts covering the company have a “buy” call on the stock, with 11 “buy” calls, two “hold” calls and one “sell” call. Analysts noted that ViTrox has positioned itself as a key beneficiary of AI infrastructure spending. Research houses have also upgraded their earnings forecasts, with Apex Securities raising its net profit forecasts for FY2026, FY2027 and FY2028 to RM275.6 million, RM362.4 million and RM408.2 million, respectively, citing sustained AI infrastructure demand. CIMB Securities noted that ViTrox’s 1HFY2026 results exceeded expectations, coming in at more than 60% of its full-year consensus estimate. The research house reiterated its “buy” rating with a target price of RM10.00 and raised its FY2026–FY2028 earnings per share estimates by 28% to 37%, citing expanding order books, a favourable product mix and recurring service income. ViTrox saw its revenue double year-on-year in the second quarter ended June 30 (2QFY2026) to RM375 million from RM183 million in the same period last year. Net profit for the quarter jumped to RM85.04 million, bringing the company’s cumulative net profit for the first half of 2026 to RM136.24 million, surpassing its full-year net profit of RM133.18 million in 2025. Chu said the optimism surrounding the company is understandable, given that, much like its peers in the semiconductor-related industry, ViTrox is operating at full capacity and expanding to cope with the surge in demand. title: 'Tenaga Nasional Tells Analysts Extra Subsidy Is One-off, Mulls Permanent Solutions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 23): Tenaga Nasional Bhd (KL:TENAGA) said the extra subsidy earmarked for households is a one-off measure, and the national electric utility is mulling tweaks to its charges to better shield consumers. The initial estimate of up to RM150 million in costs to subsidise consumers from rising electricity bills is conservative and the actual cost may be lower for the company, according to several analysts that attended an investor briefing by Tenaga Nasional on Tuesday. Tenaga Nasional stressed that “this is a one-off corporate contribution outside the regulatory framework, rather than a change to the revenue-cap or price-cap mechanism”, BIMB Securities said in a post-briefing note. The briefing follows a decline in Tenaga Nasional’s share price as investors priced in earnings impact after the company agreed to absorb the impact from the electricity tariff fuel surcharge exemption that has been expanded to more households up until the end of this year. Consumers are seeing relatively higher electricity bills from soaring temperatures and work-from-home policy and other seasonal factors. Last week, the government announced that households consuming 800 kilowatt-hour of power or less monthly will now be spared from surcharges under the automatic fuel adjustment. The exemption is previously provided only to those using under 600 kilowatt-hour each month. More importantly, Tenaga Nasional and the government are working on a more permanent solution for 2027 onwards to address elevated fuel price, CIMB Securities said. One possible approach could be differentiated rates versus the current uniform rate, and similar to how the imbalance cost pass-through, or ICPT, was previously implemented with residential users paying a lower rate against large-scale commercial users, the house noted. While there is no clarity on the new structure, the previous framework under ICPT mechanism allowed “cross subsidisation and potentially greater protection” for residential consumers and even small and medium enterprises, TA Securities added. Under the previous mechanism that was replaced in June 2025 with the automatic fuel adjustment system, the final tariff to be paid by consumers was adjusted every six months in the form of rebates or surcharges on top of the base tariff. title: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, Construction Stocks Seen as Key Beneficiaries of Budget 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday. In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion. It believes the higher allocation “could provide a modest boost to mass-market consumption, particularly benefitting companies exposed to lower- and middle-income households”. Among the counters poised to benefit are 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (KL:99SMART), Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd (KL:ECOSHOP) and MR DIY Group (M) Bhd (KL:MRDIY), as well as food and beverage manufacturers Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:NESTLE), Life Water Bhd (KL:LWSABAH) and QL Resources Bhd (KL:QL). CIMB Securities also expects gross development expenditure to rise to RM83 billion in 2027, with higher spending on water infrastructure among the potential areas of focus. Among the counters it sees as well positioned to benefit are Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM), Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT) and Insight Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB). Separately, Maybank Investment Bank expects Budget 2027 to remain supportive of the healthcare sector. Potential measures include tax relief for healthcare and medical insurance, support for the nationwide MediAsas rollout, continued medical-tourism incentives and greater public-private collaboration to ease congestion at public hospitals, it said. Local pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturers may also benefit from continued government support for manufacturing, procurement, research and development, Maybank IB said. Its top picks include IHH Healthcare Bhd (KL:IHH), KPJ Healthcare Bhd (KL:KPJ), Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd (KL:SUNMED), PMCK Bhd (KL:PMCK), Duopharma Biotech Bhd (KL:DPHARMA) and Pharmaniaga Bhd (KL:PHARMA). title: 'DNB Secures RM5.2 Billion Financing As MoF Inc Prepares To Exit - Lowyat.NET
body: 'Digital Nasional Berhad (DNB) has secured RM5.2 billion through a syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, strengthening its financial position as Malaysia moves into the next phase of its dual 5G network framework. The financing also provides the company with a new long-term funding structure as it prepares to operate under an ownership model led by its mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders. The exercise comes as the Ministry of Finance Incorporated (MoF Inc) prepares to exit its ordinary shareholding in DNB, with the transition to equal ownership among CelcomDigi, Maxis Broadband and YTL Power International expected in early Q4 2026. MoF Inc. will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and key strategic matters. DNB’s shareholder structure has changed considerably in recent years, with Telekom Malaysia (TM) exiting its equity participation in 2023 and U Mobile divesting its stake in 2025 as it shifted its focus towards building Malaysia’s second 5G network. CelcomDigi remains a shareholder through Infranation Sdn Bhd, alongside Maxis and YTL, the parent company of Yes 5G operator YTL Communications. Strengthening DNB’s Position DNB said the RM5.2 billion financing ranks among the largest syndicated loan facilities arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia. Maybank Investment Bank acted as Mandated Lead Arranger, Bookrunner and Coordinating Arranger, with AmInvestment Bank, CIMB Islamic Bank, RHB Islamic Bank and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) serving as Joint Mandated Lead Arrangers. The facility includes the refinancing of DNB’s Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility, which expired on 29 September 2026. DNB said the new financing establishes a sustainable long-term funding structure to support its future growth and network investments. According to CelcomDigi, via a separate statement, the financing is also expected to reduce the need for additional equity funding from DNB’s MNO shareholders based on its current regulatory commitments and funding requirements. This should allow the shareholders to focus more on improving the efficiency and performance of the 5G network. DNB Now Holds 240MHz Under Long-Term Assignment The financing exercise comes alongside DNB receiving the full 100MHz allocation in the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz band, bringing its total spectrum holding to 240MHz. MCMC has also converted DNB’s entire spectrum holding into a Spectrum Assignment, which took effect today, 1 October 2026. DNB had previously received the additional 100MHz in July, giving it 200MHz of contiguous mid-band spectrum across the 3.3GHz to 3.5GHz range. The additional allocation was made available following U Mobile’s departure from DNB’s network as it proceeded with the rollout of its own 5G network. DNB says the expanded spectrum will improve network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. The 15-year spectrum assignment also gives CelcomDigi greater certainty for long-term network planning and investment. CelcomDigi To Bring Network Assets And Experience With the ownership transition, CelcomDigi says it will leverage its nationwide network assets and more than 30 years of telecommunications experience to support DNB’s next phase. The telco expects its existing infrastructure, sites and capabilities to create synergies with DNB’s network, helping to improve cost efficiency, expand coverage and accelerate indoor 5G deployment. It also sees opportunities to improve 5G capacity and coverage, expand indoor building solutions and maximise spectrum utilisation. (Source: DNB / CelcomDigi)

title: 'Malaysia-Myanmar: The repatriation question
body: 'A group of 1,476 people have been returned to Myanmar from Malaysia earlier this week, as part of a wider repatriation programme that could eventually involve up to 5,000 people. The government says the returns are voluntary, however the UN refugee agency has questioned whether people held in immigration detention can make a genuinely free and informed decision to return to a country still under ongoing conflict. body: 'Bursa Malaysia meneruskan penurunan pada tengah hari Khamis apabila tekanan jualan kembali mendominasi pasaran, selari dengan prestasi bercampur pasaran global ketika kenaikan hasil bon Perbendaharaan Amerika Syarikat terus mengehadkan sentimen risiko. Pada 12:30 tengah hari, FBM KLCI susut 15.36 mata kepada 1,635.81 berbanding 1,651.17 pada penutupan Rabu. Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 1.30 mata lebih rendah pada 1,649.87 sebelum bergerak antara 1,634.39 hingga 1,649.87 sepanjang sesi pagi. Kaunter Rugi Mendominasi Pasaran Sentimen keseluruhan kekal lemah apabila 583 kaunter mencatat penurunan berbanding 305 kaunter yang meningkat. Saham Bank Dan Tenaga Terus Tertekan Dalam kalangan saham berwajaran tinggi, Maybank dan Tenaga Nasional masing-masing susut 6 sen kepada RM9.93 dan RM12.90. title: 'Jamin peruntukan awam universiti, hentikan korporatisasi UiTM – Suara Siswa UiTM
body: 'Suara Siswa UiTM menggesa Kementerian Pendidikan Tinggi (KPT) dan Kementerian Kewangan menjamin peruntukan awam yang mencukupi dan berterusan kepada universiti awam, susulan perkembangan terbaharu berkaitan UiTM Holdings yang, menurut kumpulan itu, mencerminkan masalah lebih besar dalam model pembiayaan pendidikan tinggi. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu berkata pengakuan Menteri Pendidikan Tinggi Zambry Kadir pada 27 September bahawa kerajaan tidak lagi menanggung sepenuhnya keperluan kewangan universiti sejak 2017 menunjukkan universiti awam semakin didorong mencari sumber pendapatan sendiri, termasuk melalui syarikat pegangan, pelaburan dan kegiatan komersial. KPT pada masa sama mengakui sebahagian syarikat pegangan universiti tidak berfungsi dengan baik, dan proses meneliti serta menyusun semula syarikat berkenaan telah dimulakan sejak tahun lalu. Menurut Suara Siswa UiTM, UiTM Holdings tidak wajar dilihat semata-mata sebagai sebuah syarikat yang mengalami masalah kewangan. KPT sebelum ini mengesahkan kerugian sebelum cukai terkumpul UiTM Holdings sekitar RM157j bagi 2017, 2018, 2019 dan 2021, manakala Jawatankuasa Kira-Kira Wang Negara (PAC) pernah merekodkan suntikan modal UiTM berjumlah RM260j juta kepada syarikat itu antara 2007 hingga 2018 serta membangkitkan isu pematuhan dan tadbir urus. Kumpulan itu berkata perkembangan berkenaan perlu dibaca bersama dasar kewangan pendidikan tinggi negara. Menurut Pelan Pembangunan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia 2015-25 (PPPM) merekodkan sumbangan kerajaan kepada universiti awam bukan universiti penyelidikan turun daripada 85% perbelanjaan operasi pada 2015 kepada 76% pada 2022, sementara pendapatan dijana sendiri meningkat daripada 21% kepada 22%. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member Dokumen itu mengenal pasti kemampanan kewangan sebagai cabaran utama institut pengajian tinggi. Suara Siswa UiTM berkata keadaan itu menunjukkan universiti awam semakin diletakkan di bawah tekanan untuk mencapai kelestarian kewangan melalui penjanaan pendapatan, termasuk pelaburan, kegiatan komersial, konsultansi dan model perniagaan baharu. PPPM secara jelas meletakkan penjanaan pendapatan, pendanaan berasaskan prestasi dan model perniagaan inovatif sebagai sebahagian daripada agenda kelestarian kewangan institusi. [Hala tuju ini diteruskan dan diperkukuh dalam Rancangan Pendidikan Tinggi Malaysia 2026-35.] “Kami melihat persoalan UiTM Holdings sebagai sebahagian daripada masalah korporatisasi pendidikan tinggi,” kata kumpulan itu. “Apabila pembiayaan awam dikurangkan, risiko kewangan tidak hilang, tetapi dipindahkan kepada universiti untuk ditanggung melalui pasaran dan akhirnya kepada mahasiswa melalui pelbagai bentuk kos pendidikan dan sara hidup.” Suara Siswa UiTM menggesa kerajaan mengembalikan pembiayaan awam sebagai asas utama kewangan universiti, dengan peruntukan KPT dan Kementerian Kewangan yang mencukupi untuk menanggung fungsi teras seperti pengajaran, penyelidikan, penyelenggaraan kampus dan kebajikan mahasiswa tanpa memaksa universiti bergantung kepada keuntungan aktiviti komersial. Kumpulan itu turut menyeru supaya yuran dan kos wajib pendidikan dikurangkan secara berperingkat sehingga pendidikan tinggi awam dapat dinyahkomodifikasikan. Kumpulan mahasiswa itu turut menuntut supaya sebarang penyusunan semula UiTM Holdings tidak berakhir dengan sekadar mencari model perniagaan baharu atau menutup kerugian melalui suntikan dana awam tanpa perubahan struktur. Ia mahu kerajaan menilai semula aktiviti komersial universiti berdasarkan kepentingan pendidikan dan masyarakat, di samping memastikan pekerja universiti tidak menjadi pihak yang menanggung kesan penstrukturan. Dalam perkembangan berasingan, Suruhanjaya Pencegah Rasuah Malaysia mengesahkan siasatan terhadap UiTM Holdings masih berjalan dan melibatkan isu teknikal serta kelemahan tadbir urus, termasuk dakwaan pembayaran RM42j berkaitan projek solar 50MW di Gambang, yang dikatakan dibuat tanpa kelulusan lembaga pengarah dan bagi tujuan yang tidak berkaitan dengan projek. Suara Siswa UiTM berkata sebarang pertuduhan jenayah hendaklah tertakluk kepada hasil siasatan dan proses undang-undang, namun isu tadbir urus dan model pembiayaan universiti boleh dipersoalkan secara berasingan. “Universiti awam tidak sepatutnya dipaksa menjadi perusahaan yang mencari keuntungan untuk membiayai fungsi awamnya,” kata kumpulan itu. “Peruntukan pendidikan ialah tanggungjawab negara, manakala kekayaan dan aset universiti harus diprioritikan untuk mahasiswa, pekerja, pengajaran, penyelidikan dan kepentingan masyarakat.” – Suara Siswa UiTM The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. title: 'DNB raises RM5.2bil from Islamic loan for next 5G phase
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, one of the largest syndicated loan facilities arranged for an unlisted Malaysian company. DNB said the financing comes as it prepares for the next phase of Malaysia's dual 5G network framework. The financing is expected to support the planned exit of the Ministry of Finance Inc (MoF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder, it said today. It will also facilitate the transition to equal ownership among DNB's mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders - CelcomDigi Bhd through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd - expected in early fourth quarter of this year. MoF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. The RM5.2 billion facility also refinances DNB's government guarantee revolving credit facility, which expired on Sept 29. It provides the company with a long-term funding structure for its operations and network investments. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd were joint mandated lead arrangers. AmInvestment Bank also acted as financial adviser to DNB. The financing comes as DNB receives the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and converts its entire 240MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. The assignment, issued by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission, takes effect today. DNB said the expanded spectrum holding would increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, supporting faster speeds, lower latency and improved customer experience. It would also enable the deployment of technologies such as Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and artificial intelligence-driven network capabilities. DNB chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said the successful financing reflected confidence in the company's business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia's digital economy. "This financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate on its own, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and leverage our expanded spectrum assets," he said. Azman said DNB remained committed to providing digital infrastructure as Malaysia moved towards a dual network framework. "With strong financing, enhanced spectrum resources and a proven nationwide 5G platform, DNB is well positioned to support the government's AI Nation aspirations and help power Malaysia's next phase of digital growth," he said. DNB said the financing and spectrum assignment would strengthen its ability to improve network quality and resilience, cater to future demand and support Malaysia's digital economy ambitions.

title: 'DNB completes RM5.2 bil syndicated Islamic financing ahead of ownership transition
body: 'DNB completes RM5.2 bil syndicated Islamic financing ahead of ownership transition KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth. In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding. The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL:CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL:YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026. Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters. DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment. The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission. DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets. DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider. In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing. AmInvestment Bank was the financial adviser to DNB. title: 'DNB lengkapkan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion bagi menyokong fasa seterusnya pertumbuhan 5G - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) melengkapkan pembiayaan berjangka Islam secara sindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan pembiayaan jangka panjang syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa pertumbuhan seterusnya dwirangkaian 5G . DNB dalam kenyataan berkata pembiayaan itu akan memudahkan perancangan keluar Menteri Kewangan Diperbadankan (MOF Inc) sebagai pemegang saham biasa dan peralihan kepada pemilikan sama rata dalam kalangan pemegang saham pengendali rangkaian mudah alihnya, iaitu CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd. Peralihan pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026, manakala MOF Inc akan mengekalkan saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan negara. Pembiayaan berkenaan turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula kemudahan kredit pusingan DNB yang dijamin kerajaan dan tamat tempoh pada 29 September, selain mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang bagi menyokong pertumbuhan syarikat. Penyempurnaan pembiayaan itu bertepatan dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100MHz dalam jalur 3.3–3.4GHz serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum 240MHz DNB kepada penetapan spektrum. Penetapan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober. Menurut DNB, blok spektrum 240MHz tersebut akan meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, selain menyokong teknologi termasuk Massive MIMO, pengagregatan pembawa, 5G Advanced dan keupayaan rangkaian dipacu kecerdasan buatan. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif DNB, Datuk Azman Ismail berkata pembiayaan berkenaan menyediakan platform mampan untuk syarikat beroperasi secara bebas sambil meneruskan pelaburan dalam peningkatan rangkaian dan peluasan kapasiti. “Penyempurnaan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion ini merupakan pencapaian penting bagi DNB dan mencerminkan keyakinan kukuh terhadap asas perniagaan, rekod operasi serta peranan jangka panjang kami dalam ekonomi digital Malaysia,” katanya. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bertindak sebagai pengatur utama yang diberi mandat, pengurus buku dan pengatur penyelaras bagi pembiayaan itu. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd dan United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd pula merupakan pengatur utama bersama yang diberi mandat, manakala AmInvestment Bank bertindak sebagai penasihat kewangan DNB. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Extends Losses at Midday On Selling Pressure
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 – Bursa Malaysia continued its downward trend at midday on Thursday, October 1, 2026, as selling pressure persisted across the board, tracking mixed global market performance amid rising United States Treasury yields. At 12:30 PM, the benchmark FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) slid 15.36 points to 1,635.81 compared to Wednesday’s close of 1,651.17. The main index opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87 and fluctuated between an intraday low of 1,634.39 and a high of 1,649.87 throughout the morning session. Broader market sentiment remained negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 583 to 305, while 464 counters traded unchanged, 1,421 untraded, and 12 suspended. Half-day turnover stood at 1.65 billion shares valued at RM1.18 billion. Heavyweights and Active Stocks Major banking, utility, and healthcare blue chips pulled the benchmark index lower: - IHH Healthcare contracted 19 sen to RM7.64. - Maybank and Tenaga Nasional lost 6 sen each to RM9.93 and RM12.90, respectively. - CIMB decreased 5 sen to RM7.74. - Public Bank fell 4 sen to RM4.66. Among active counters, Zetrix AI and V.S Industry both added half a sen to 16.5 sen and 28.5 sen, respectively. Dagang Nexchange rose 1.5 sen to 50 sen, while Jaks Resources eased half a sen to 20 sen and ACE Market debutant GB Bond dropped 2.5 sen to 22.5 sen. Technology and plantation counters featured among the top gainers: - Malaysian Pacific Industries: Advanced RM1.26 to RM41.66. - MI Technovation: Rose 13 sen to RM5.33. - Ta Ann: Accumulated 12 sen to RM5.92. - Malayan Cement: Strengthened 11 sen to RM5.56. - Genting Plantations: Improved 10 sen to RM5.63. Declining counters were led by Kuala Lumpur Kepong, which dropped 76 sen to RM21.44. Other notable pullbacks included Allianz Malaysia (down 62 sen to RM21.00), as well as Fraser & Neave, Hong Leong Industries, and Batu Kawan, which trimmed 42 sen each to RM21.32, RM16.04, and RM20.10, respectively. Index and Sectoral Performance All major sector indices posted declines at the midday break, led by financial services and plantation stocks: - The Financial Services Index dropped 148.77 points to 19,067.72. - The Plantation Index tumbled 121.85 points to 9,074.82. - The Energy Index eased 7.79 points to 837.91. - The Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 1.16 points to 178.80. Across broader market indices: - The FBM Top 100 Index fell 99.00 points to 11,985.44. - The FBM Emas Index declined 94.18 points to 12,197.83. - The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 87.69 points to 12,088.65. - The FBM Mid 70 Index dropped 87.65 points to 17,487.02. - The FBM ACE Index contracted 31.14 points to 5,503.14. –NMT

title: 'DNB completes RM5.2bil financing to support next phase of 5G growth
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2bil syndicated Islamic term financing, strengthening its long-term funding position as Malaysia moves into the next phase of its dual 5G network framework. In a statement, DNB said the financing will facilitate the planned exit of Minister of Finance Inc (MOF Inc) as an ordinary shareholder and the transition to equal ownership among its mobile network operator shareholders, namely CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd. The ownership transition is expected in the early fourth quarter of 2026, while MOF Inc will retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests. The syndicated financing also includes the refinancing of DNB's government-guaranteed revolving credit facility, which expired on Sept 29, and establishes a longer-term funding structure to support the company's growth. DNB said the completion of the financing coincided with the award of the full 100 MHz of the 3.3–3.4 GHz spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240 MHz spectrum holding to a spectrum assignment. The assignment by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) takes effect from Oct 1. DNB said the 240 MHz spectrum block would enhance network capacity, efficiency and performance and support technologies including Massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and artificial intelligence-driven network capabilities. Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said the financing would provide DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently while continuing to invest in network enhancement and capacity expansion. “The successful completion of this RM5.2bil financing exercise marks a significant milestone for DNB and reflects strong confidence in our business fundamentals, operational track record and long-term role in Malaysia’s digital economy,” he said. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger for the financing. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd were joint mandated lead arrangers, while AmInvestment Bank was DNB's financial adviser.

body: 'Malaysia’s proposed Freedom of Information Bill is under renewed scrutiny after civil society groups raised concerns over broad exemptions, existing secrecy laws and the effectiveness of its appeals process. What needs to change for the bill to deliver genuine access to information, and can Malaysia balance greater government transparency with legitimate safeguards? title: 'Customary land: Between Orang Asli rights and the law
body: 'The sultan of Pahang has called for greater clarity over the use of the term tanah adat (customary land), saying Orang Asli land claims must be assessed according to the legal status of the land, including its gazetting, boundaries and history of occupation. However, for Orang Asli communities, the issue goes beyond what is written on a land title. So, where does customary land sit within Malaysian law? And what happens when customary claims meet the state’s gazetting process? Astro Awani’s Melisa Idris speaks with Bah Tony, the deputy chairperson of the Bar Council’s committee on Orang Asli rights, and Ismail Leh, a Pahang representative from Jaringan Kampung Orang Asli Semenanjung Malaysia (JKOASM). title: 'Bursa dibuka rendah pada pagi ini
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR,. Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah pada Khamis, menjejaki prestasi bercampur-campur Wall Street berikutan hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS yang lebih tinggi serta ketegangan berterusan di Asia Barat menjejaskan minat belian. Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) susut 3.74 mata atau 0.22 peratus kepada 1,647.43 daripada paras 1,651.17 ketika ditutup pada Rabu. Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 1.30 mata lebih rendah pada 1,649.87. Di pasaran meluas, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 200 berbanding 142, manakala 307 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,124 kaunter tidak diniagakan dan 12 kaunter digantung. Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 246.59 juta saham bernilai RM118.14 juta. Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd, Thong Pak Leng, berkata Wall Street ditutup bercampur-campur apabila inflasi yang lebih rendah mengurangkan jangkaan terhadap satu lagi kenaikan kadar faedah oleh Rizab Persekutuan AS, meskipun hasil bon yang kekal tinggi terus menjejaskan sentimen. Di peringkat domestik, beliau berkata, indeks penanda aras pasaran mungkin cenderung diniagakan berhati-hati, dengan sentimen keseluruhan pasaran yang lemah dan jualan asing baru-baru ini menunjukkan pelabur terus mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati. “Justeru, bagi hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks kekal dalam mod pengukuhan dalam julat 1,640-1,660, dengan aktiviti pembelian ketika harga rendah dijangka mengehadkan penurunan,” katanya kepada Bernama. Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank dan IHH Healthcare masing-masing tidak berubah pada RM9.90 dan RM7.83. Public Bank susut tiga sen kepada RM4.67, CIMB berkurangan satu sen kepada RM7.78 dan Tenaga Nasional turun dua sen kepada RM12.94. Dalam dagangan aktif, saham yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE, GB Bond susut setengah sen kepada 24.5 sen, manakala VS Industry tidak berubah pada 28 sen. Astro Malaysia menambah setengah sen kepada enam sen, Jaks Resources meningkat satu sen kepada 21.5 sen dan Divfex menokok dua sen kepada 11 sen. Antara kaunter untung utama, Keck Seng meningkat 11 sen kepada RM5.14 dan Petron Malaysia menambah tujuh sen kepada RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining dan Spritzer masing-masing naik enam sen kepada RM3.62 dan RM3.67, manakala Jati Tinggi mengukuh lima sen kepada RM1.44. Kuala Lumpur Kepong mendahului kaunter rugi apabila susut 18 sen kepada RM22.02. UWC pula berkurangan 15 sen kepada RM6.92, manakala Insights Analytics dan MISC masing-masing turun sembilan sen kepada RM1.20 dan RM7.55. Petronas Dagangan susut lapan sen kepada RM19.20. Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 susut 42.26 mata kepada 17,532.41, Indeks FBM Emas berkurangan 26.32 mata kepada 12,265.69, manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 turun 27.82 mata kepada 12,056.62. Indeks FBM Emas Shariah susut 22.09 mata kepada 12,154.26, manakala Indeks FBM ACE berkurangan 6.31 mata kepada 5,527.97. Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian susut 0.10 mata kepada 180.31, manakala Indeks Tenaga meningkat 1.41 mata kepada 847.11. Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan turun 27.47 mata kepada 19,189.02, manakala Indeks Perladangan merosot 33.34 mata kepada 9,163.33. — BERNAMA

title: 'Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah berikutan hasil bon AS lebih tinggi, ketegangan Asia Barat
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia dibuka rendah pada Khamis, menjejaki prestasi bercampur-campur Wall Street berikutan hasil bon Perbendaharaan AS yang lebih tinggi serta ketegangan berterusan di Asia Barat menjejaskan minat belian.  Pada 9.10 pagi, FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) susut 3.74 mata atau 0.22 peratus kepada 1,647.43 daripada paras 1,651.17 ketika ditutup pada Rabu.  Indeks penanda aras itu dibuka 1.30 mata lebih rendah pada 1,649.87.  Di pasaran meluas, kaunter rugi mengatasi kaunter untung sebanyak 200 berbanding 142, manakala 307 kaunter tidak berubah, 2,124 kaunter tidak diniagakan dan 12 kaunter digantung.  Jumlah dagangan sebanyak 246.59 juta saham bernilai RM118.14 juta.  Naib Presiden Penyelidikan Ekuiti Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd Thong Pak Leng berkata Wall Street ditutup bercampur-campur apabila inflasi yang lebih rendah mengurangkan jangkaan terhadap satu lagi kenaikan kadar faedah oleh Rizab Persekutuan AS, meskipun hasil bon yang kekal tinggi terus menjejaskan sentimen.  Di peringkat domestik, beliau berkata indeks penanda aras pasaran mungkin cenderung diniagakan berhati-hati, dengan sentimen keseluruhan pasaran yang lemah dan jualan asing baru-baru ini menunjukkan pelabur terus mengambil pendekatan berhati-hati.  “Justeru, bagi hari ini, kami menjangkakan indeks kekal dalam mod pengukuhan dalam julat 1,640-1,660, dengan aktiviti pembelian ketika harga rendah dijangka mengehadkan penurunan,” katanya kepada Bernama.  Dalam kalangan saham wajaran tinggi, Maybank dan IHH Healthcare masing-masing tidak berubah pada RM9.90 dan RM7.83. Public Bank susut tiga sen kepada RM4.67, CIMB berkurangan satu sen kepada RM7.78 dan Tenaga Nasional turun dua sen kepada RM12.94.  Dalam dagangan aktif, saham yang baru disenaraikan di Pasaran ACE, GB Bond susut setengah sen kepada 24.5 sen, manakala VS Industry tidak berubah pada 28 sen. Astro Malaysia menambah setengah sen kepada enam sen, Jaks Resources meningkat satu sen kepada 21.5 sen dan Divfex menokok dua sen kepada 11 sen.  Antara kaunter untung utama, Keck Seng meningkat 11 sen kepada RM5.14 dan Petron Malaysia menambah tujuh sen kepada RM3.47. Hengyuan Refining dan Spritzer masing-masing naik enam sen kepada RM3.62 dan RM3.67, manakala Jati Tinggi mengukuh lima sen kepada RM1.44.  Kuala Lumpur Kepong mendahului kaunter rugi apabila susut 18 sen kepada RM22.02. UWC pula berkurangan 15 sen kepada RM6.92, manakala Insights Analytics dan MISC masing-masing turun sembilan sen kepada RM1.20 dan RM7.55. Petronas Dagangan susut lapan sen kepada RM19.20.  Di papan indeks, Indeks FBM Mid 70 susut 42.26 mata kepada 17,532.41, Indeks FBM Emas berkurangan 26.32 mata kepada 12,265.69, manakala Indeks FBM Top 100 turun 27.82 mata kepada 12,056.62.  Indeks FBM Emas Shariah susut 22.09 mata kepada 12,154.26, manakala Indeks FBM ACE berkurangan 6.31 mata kepada 5,527.97.  Mengikut sektor, Indeks Produk dan Perkhidmatan Perindustrian susut 0.10 mata kepada 180.31, manakala Indeks Tenaga meningkat 1.41 mata kepada 847.11. Indeks Perkhidmatan Kewangan turun 27.47 mata kepada 19,189.02, manakala Indeks Perladangan merosot 33.34 mata kepada 9,163.33.- Bernama

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Opens Lower On Higher US Yields, West Asia Tensions
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 1 – Bursa Malaysia opened lower on Thursday morning, tracking a mixed overnight performance on Wall Street as rising US Treasury yields and persistent geopolitical tensions in West Asia dampened investor appetite. At 9:10 AM, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) fell 3.74 points, or 0.22 per cent, to 1,647.43 compared to Wednesday’s closing level of 1,651.17. The key index opened 1.30 points lower at 1,649.87. Market breadth across the broader market was negative, with decliners outpacing gainers 200 to 142, while 307 counters traded unchanged, 2,124 untraded, and 12 suspended. Early turnover reached 246.59 million shares valued at RM118.14 million. Heavyweights and Active Counters Financial and utility heavyweights dragged on the benchmark index during early trade: - Public Bank fell 3 sen to RM4.67. - Tenaga Nasional lost 2 sen to RM12.94. - CIMB shed 1 sen to RM7.78. - Maybank and IHH Healthcare traded flat at RM9.90 and RM7.83, respectively. In active trading, ACE Market debutant GB Bond fell half a sen to 24.5 sen, while VS Industry traded unchanged at 28 sen. Divfex gained 2 sen to 11 sen, Jaks Resources rose 1 sen to 21.5 sen, and Astro Malaysia added half a sen to 6 sen. Energy and consumer-linked stocks featured among the top gainers: - Keck Seng advanced 11 sen to RM5.14. - Petron Malaysia picked up 7 sen to RM3.47. - Hengyuan Refining and Spritzer each rose 6 sen to RM3.62 and RM3.67, respectively. - Jati Tinggi gained 5 sen to RM1.44. Plantation and technology counters led early losses: - Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 18 sen to RM22.02. - UWC shed 15 sen to RM6.92. - Insights Analytics and MISC each declined 9 sen to RM1.20 and RM7.55, respectively. - Petronas Dagangan lost 8 sen to RM19.20. Index and Sectoral Trends Sectoral performance was mostly lower, with financial and plantation stocks leading the decline while energy counters bucked the trend: - The Plantation Index retreated 33.34 points to 9,163.33. - The Financial Services Index dropped 27.47 points to 19,189.02. - The Industrial Products and Services Index slipped 0.10 of a point to 180.31. - The Energy Index rose 1.41 points to 847.11. Across broader index boards: - The FBM Mid 70 Index dropped 42.26 points to 17,532.41. - The FBM Emas Index fell 26.32 points to 12,265.69. - The FBM Top 100 Index lost 27.82 points to 12,056.62. - The FBM Emas Shariah Index weakened 22.09 points to 12,154.26. - The FBM ACE Index trimmed 6.31 points to 5,527.97. –NMT

title: 'Why is Malaysia sending back Rohingya refugees to Myanmar?
body: 'They sought refuge in Malaysia nearly a decade ago, fleeing persecution and war in Myanmar. But thousands of Rohingya refugees are being sent back to a nation still plagued by violence. The Malaysian government is facing accusations of forcibly deporting the refugees – a charge the goverment denies. It says the process is voluntary and coordinated with Myanmar’s government. But human rights groups say this process violates international law by sending refugees to countries where they risk facing prosecution or torture. So, will this concern stop the Rohingya being sent back to Myanmar? title: 'Mateen perlu RM8,000 beli ‘stroller’ khas
body: 'PETALING JAYA – Bayi hidrosefalus, Muhammad Mateen Aryan Muhammad Hanif, 15 bulan, dari Sungai Petani, Kedah, kini semakin aktif namun pergerakannya terbatas disebabkan kepalanya yang berat. Bapanya, Muhammad Hanif Zakaria, 32, berkata, Mateen kini cuba menggerakkan badan dan memusingkan badan, tetapi sukar berbuat demikian dengan kepala yang mencecah ukuran 90 sentimeter (cm). “Perkembangan dia okey. Dia pun cuba bergerak, nak pusing badannya, tetapi tak boleh sebab kepala dia berat,” katanya ketika dihubungi Kosmo!. Menurut Muhammad Hanif, keadaan Mateen kini semakin baik apabila sawan yang dialaminya semakin berkurang, namun apabila serangan berlaku, saiz kepala anaknya boleh kembali membesar. “Sejak kami mendapatkan rawatan alternatif, Mateen semakin kurang diserang sawan dan saiz kepala dia turun sedikit ke 89cm. Tapi apabila kena sawan, automatik saiz tu boleh naik balik,” ujarnya. Muhammad Hanif berkata, keperluan asas Matten kini mencukupi dan berterima kasih kepada pihak yang pernah membantu, namun dia dan isteri kini merancang untuk mendapatkan kereta sorong (stroller) khas bagi memudahkan pergerakan Mateen. Bagaimanapun dia menjelaskan, ia perlu ditempah khas mengikut keperluan Mateen, dengan anggaran kos sebanyak RM8,000 dan akan berbuat demikian apabila jumlah itu mencukupi. Orang ramai yang ingin membantu keluarga itu mendapatkan kereta sorong berkenaan, boleh menyalurkan sumbangan ke akaun bank CIMB bernombor 7632966954 di atas nama Muhammad Hanif. Terdahulu Kosmo! melaporkan, Muhammad Hanif yang bekerja sebagai pemandu lori bersyukur kerana anak bongsu daripada tiga beradik itu tidak pernah menangis kesakitan sejak lahir. Dia dan isteri, Habidah Nasruddin, 31, bagaimanapun berdepan kesukaran mengangkat Mateen disebabkan kepalanya yang makin membesar.

body: 'KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) has completed a RM5.2 billion syndicated Islamic term financing exercise, which it said will strengthen its financial position and support its next phase of growth.  In a statement, DNB said the financing, the largest syndicated loan facility arranged for an unlisted company in Malaysia, includes the refinancing of its Government Guarantee Revolving Credit Facility (GGRCF), which expired on Sept 29, 2026, and provides longer-term funding.  The exercise comes as DNB prepares to transition from a government-backed structure to equal ownership among its three mobile network operator (MNO) shareholders — CelcomDigi Bhd (KL: CDB) through Infranation Sdn Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd and YTL Power International Bhd (KL: YTLPOWR) — expected in early fourth quarter of 2026.  Minister of Finance Inc will exit as an ordinary shareholder but retain a special share in DNB to safeguard national interests and oversee key strategic matters.  DNB said the financing was completed alongside the award of the full 100MHz of the 3.3GHz to 3.4GHz (F0) spectrum and the conversion of its entire 240MHz spectrum holding into a spectrum assignment.  The spectrum assignment takes effect from Oct 1, 2026, following its issuance by the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission.  DNB said the spectrum assignment will increase network capacity, efficiency and performance, while supporting technologies such as massive MIMO, carrier aggregation, 5G Advanced and AI-driven network capabilities.  Chief executive officer Datuk Azman Ismail said in the statement the financing provides DNB with a sustainable platform to operate independently, continue investing in network enhancement and capacity expansion, and make use of its expanded spectrum assets.  DNB was established in March 2021 to accelerate Malaysia’s 5G roll-out and operate as the country’s sole wholesale 5G network provider.  In May 2023, the government announced a shift to a dual 5G network model. U Mobile Sdn Bhd was selected to develop Malaysia’s second 5G network in November 2024 and was subsequently offboarded from DNB’s network on June 30, 2026.  Maybank Investment Bank Bhd acted as mandated lead arranger, bookrunner and coordinating arranger, with AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd and United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd as joint mandated lead arrangers for the financing.

title: 'DNB lengkapkan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion bagi menyokong fasa seterusnya pertumbuhan 5G | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 1 Okt - Digital Nasional Bhd (DNB) melengkapkan pembiayaan berjangka Islam secara sindiket bernilai RM5.2 bilion, sekali gus mengukuhkan kedudukan pembiayaan jangka panjang syarikat ketika Malaysia memasuki fasa pertumbuhan seterusnya dwirangkaian 5G . DNB dalam kenyataan berkata pembiayaan itu akan memudahkan perancangan keluar Menteri Kewangan Diperbadankan (MOF Inc) sebagai pemegang saham biasa dan peralihan kepada pemilikan sama rata dalam kalangan pemegang saham pengendali rangkaian mudah alihnya, iaitu CelcomDigi Bhd, Maxis Broadband Sdn Bhd dan YTL Power International Bhd. Peralihan pemilikan tersebut dijangka berlaku pada awal suku keempat 2026, manakala MOF Inc akan mengekalkan saham khas dalam DNB bagi melindungi kepentingan negara. Pembiayaan berkenaan turut merangkumi pembiayaan semula kemudahan kredit pusingan DNB yang dijamin kerajaan dan tamat tempoh pada 29 September, selain mewujudkan struktur pembiayaan jangka panjang bagi menyokong pertumbuhan syarikat. Penyempurnaan pembiayaan itu bertepatan dengan pemberian penuh spektrum 100MHz dalam jalur 3.3–3.4GHz serta penukaran keseluruhan pegangan spektrum 240MHz DNB kepada penetapan spektrum. Penetapan oleh Suruhanjaya Komunikasi dan Multimedia Malaysia (MCMC) itu berkuat kuasa mulai 1 Oktober. Menurut DNB, blok spektrum 240MHz tersebut akan meningkatkan kapasiti, kecekapan dan prestasi rangkaian, selain menyokong teknologi termasuk Massive MIMO, pengagregatan pembawa, 5G Advanced dan keupayaan rangkaian dipacu kecerdasan buatan. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif DNB, Datuk Azman Ismail berkata pembiayaan berkenaan menyediakan platform mampan untuk syarikat beroperasi secara bebas sambil meneruskan pelaburan dalam peningkatan rangkaian dan peluasan kapasiti. “Penyempurnaan pembiayaan RM5.2 bilion ini merupakan pencapaian penting bagi DNB dan mencerminkan keyakinan kukuh terhadap asas perniagaan, rekod operasi serta peranan jangka panjang kami dalam ekonomi digital Malaysia,” katanya. Maybank Investment Bank Bhd bertindak sebagai pengatur utama yang diberi mandat, pengurus buku dan pengatur penyelaras bagi pembiayaan itu. AmInvestment Bank Bhd, CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd, RHB Islamic Bank Bhd dan United Overseas Bank (Malaysia) Bhd pula merupakan pengatur utama bersama yang diberi mandat, manakala AmInvestment Bank bertindak sebagai penasihat kewangan DNB. - DagangNews.com

title: 'Bursa Malaysia Closes Lower Amid Cautious Wall Street Influence
body: 'Kuala Lumpur:Bursa Malaysia ended the trading session lower on Thursday due to persistent selling pressure, influenced by a mixed and cautious performance on Wall Street overnight. According to BERNAMA News Agency, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) dropped 20.81 points, or 1.26 percent, closing at 1,630.36, down from the previous day's close of 1,651.17. The index opened slightly weaker at 1,649.87 and fluctuated between 1,630.10 and 1,649.87 throughout the day. The market trend showed a negative breadth, with 750 decliners outpacing 342 gainers, while 495 counters remained unchanged, 1,186 were untraded, and 12 were suspended. Turnover decreased to 3.1 billion units valued at RM2.7 billion, compared to 3.63 billion units worth RM3.62 billion on Wednesday. Mohd Sedek Jantan, the director of investment strategy and country economist at IPPFA Sdn Bhd, noted that the sentiment was cautious, exacerbated by weaker domestic manufacturing activity and continued foreign selling. He highlighted that softer manufacturing momentum and global portfolio rotation exerted pressure on the benchmark index, despite domestic institutional demand providing some balance against foreign outflows. The S and P Global Malaysia Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) slightly dipped below the neutral 50.0 mark, reaching 49.9 in September from 50.2 in August. This marks the first decline in four months following a period of improvement. Regionally, the S and P Global ASEAN Manufacturing PMI decreased to 52.1 in September from 52.3 in August. In terms of specific stocks, Maybank fell four sen to RM9.95, Public Bank lost three sen to RM4.67, and CIMB dropped 10 sen to RM7.69. Tenaga Nasional declined six sen to RM12.90, while IHH Healthcare erased 13 sen to RM7.70. Among active trades, Zetrix AI firmed half a sen to 16.5 sen, VS Industry dipped one sen to 27 sen, and Jaks Resources slipped 2.5 sen to 18 sen. ACE Market debutant GB Bond slumped 4.5 sen to 20.5 sen, with HHRG gaining half a sen to 16.5 sen. Top gainers included Malaysian Pacific Industries, which surged 72 sen to RM41.12, Ayer Holdings rising 20 sen to RM7.70, and Riverview Rubber Estates advancing 12 sen to RM3.02. Dutch Lady Malaysia Industries added 10 sen to RM30, while Vitrox gained nine sen to RM10. Among the biggest losers, Kuala Lumpur Kepong dropped 78 sen to RM21.42, Allianz Malaysia gave up 62 sen to RM21.00, and United Plantations fell 60 sen to RM30.96. Fraser and Neave, along with Hong Leong Industries, both slipped 32 sen to RM21.42 and RM16.14, respectively.

title: 'Life Water Poised for Further Growth as Capacity and Distribution Expand
body: 'Life Water Berhad (“Life Water”, Bursa: LWSABAH, 5328) is positioned for continued growth, backed by spare production capacity, an expanding distribution network in Sabah and rising demand for its bottled water and carbonated drinks. The Sabah-based beverage maker reported a 19.9% increase in revenue to RM207.31 million for the financial year ended 30 June 2026, while net profit grew 23.8% to RM37.15 million. Momentum strengthened towards the year-end, with fourth-quarter revenue up 28% year on year to RM57.01 million and net profit up 21% to RM10.95 million. The growth was driven by higher drinking water sales volumes, a price revision implemented in May 2026, seasonally stronger demand during hot weather and wider distribution. Gross margin reached 49.3% in the second quarter, supported by better operational efficiency and lower raw material costs. Life Water is the leading bottled water and carbonated drinks brand in Sabah and held about 11% of Malaysia’s bottled water market at the time of its Main Market listing in November 2024. Since then, its share price has risen from the IPO price of RM0.65 to around RM1.66, giving it a market capitalisation of about RM785 million. A key factor behind the group’s growth outlook is its available capacity. Following new production lines funded by its IPO, including the expansion of the Sandakan Sibuga Plant 1 completed in June 2025, annual drinking water capacity stands at about 626 million litres, with utilisation of around 60%. This allows the group to meet higher demand without major new investment. The group is also investing in reaching more customers. Its truck fleet has grown from 70 to 90 units, and new distribution centres are being established in Tawau, Lahad Datu and Keningau, extending coverage to Sabah’s east coast and interior. In December 2025, Life Water began supplying Sabah’s largest mini-market chain, which operates about 280 outlets. Its products are also included in the government’s Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) programme. External conditions are supportive. Visit Malaysia Year 2026 is drawing more visitors to Sabah, lifting demand from hotels, food service outlets and retailers, while bottled water demand during the dry season typically runs about 30% above normal. Beyond Sabah, the group has been building its presence in Sarawak and Brunei through local distributors. CIMB Securities has a Buy call on Life Water with a target price of RM2.05, and forecasts core net profit to grow at a compound annual rate of 22.9% from FY2025 to FY2028.

title: 'Lindung 24 Perkeso tidak jejaskan industri insurans secara ketara — CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 29 Sept - Skim Lindung 24 Pertubuhan Keselamatan Sosial (Perkeso) dijangka meluaskan perlindungan kemalangan kepada pekerja tanpa menjejaskan industri insurans dan takaful swasta secara ketara, menurut CIMB Securities. Skim yang berkuat kuasa pada 1 Jun 2026 itu memberi perlindungan kepada pekerja yang layak bagi kemalangan yang tidak berkaitan dengan pekerjaan, termasuk ketika berada di rumah, melakukan perjalanan peribadi atau menyertai aktiviti riadah. Ia melengkapi Skim Bencana Pekerjaan Perkeso yang melindungi pekerja bagi kemalangan berkaitan kerja. Menurut firma penyelidikan itu, Lindung 24 terutamanya memberi manfaat kepada pekerja yang kurang mendapat perlindungan, manakala insurans perubatan, hayat dan hilang upaya swasta masih mempunyai peranan tersendiri. Memetik Perkeso, firma itu berkata kira-kira 48% rakyat Malaysia mempunyai perlindungan insurans selain insurans motor. Dalam kalangan kumpulan berpendapatan 40% terendah (B40), kadar perlindungan dianggarkan hanya 4%. Menurut laporan berkenaan, kira-kira 38,000 tuntutan ditolak antara 2015 hingga 2025 kerana kemalangan yang dialami pekerja tidak memenuhi syarat bagi faedah bencana pekerjaan. Perkeso menganggarkan Lindung 24 boleh memberi perlindungan kepada kira-kira 250,000 pekerja setahun bagi kemalangan yang sebelum ini berada di luar skop skim sedia ada. Setakat 9 September, seramai 8.5 juta pekerja, bersamaan 87.6%, kekal menyertai Lindung 24 selepas tempoh memilih untuk tidak menyertai skim itu berakhir pada 31 Ogos. Kira-kira 1.2 juta pekerja memilih untuk tidak menyertainya, dengan 52% daripada mereka berpendapatan kurang RM3,500 sebulan. Caruman meningkat secara berperingkat Caruman yang ditanggung sepenuhnya oleh pekerja ditetapkan pada kadar 0.75% daripada gaji bulanan bagi tempoh 1 Jun 2026 hingga 31 Mei 2028. Kadar itu meningkat kepada 1% mulai 1 Jun 2028 dan 1.25% mulai 1 Jun 2031, tertakluk kepada siling gaji bulanan RM6,000. Penyertaan adalah secara sukarela bagi pekerja tempatan, tetapi mandatori bagi pekerja asing yang layak. Faedah skim ini merangkumi rawatan perubatan, bayaran bagi hilang upaya sementara atau kekal, pemulihan, faedah kepada orang tanggungan dan faedah pengurusan mayat. Anak tanggungan yang layak juga boleh memohon faedah pendidikan dalam bentuk pinjaman, tertakluk kepada syarat Perkeso. Kadar bayaran hilang upaya bergantung pada taksiran dan peraturan yang berkuat kuasa. Polisi kemalangan diri paling berpotensi bertindih Menurut CIMB Securities, pertindihan paling ketara dengan produk insurans swasta mungkin berlaku pada polisi kemalangan diri yang dibeli secara individu atau disediakan oleh majikan. Majikan boleh menilai semula faedah kemalangan yang bertindih dan mengalihkan sebahagian perbelanjaan kepada perlindungan perubatan atau manfaat pekerja yang lain. Bagaimanapun, polisi swasta kekal relevan, khususnya bagi pekerja yang pendapatannya melebihi siling gaji RM6,000 yang digunakan bagi Lindung 24. Produk swasta juga menawarkan pilihan perlindungan perubatan, hayat, penyakit kritikal dan pendapatan yang lebih luas. CIMB Securities berkata peningkatan kesedaran tentang jurang perlindungan dalam jangka panjang boleh mendorong permintaan terhadap produk insurans dan kesihatan lain. Firma itu mengekalkan pandangan `Neutral' terhadap sektor insurans, sambil menyatakan pandangan yang lebih positif terhadap LPI Capital berbanding Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga. — DagangNews.com

title: 'BERNAMA - Malaysia Entering More Supportive Water Investment Cycle  -- CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 28 (Bernama) -- Malaysia is entering a more supportive water investment cycle as ageing infrastructure, high water losses and rising industrial and data centre demand, as well as greater climate variability are increasing the urgency to improve water efficiency, reliability, and resilience. In a note today, CIMB Securities said the federal government had approved RM1.7 billion under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800 kilometres of critical pipes from 2026 to 2030, alongside a multi-year National Non-Revenue Water (NRW) Programme. It said sizeable projects including Langat 2 Phase 2, Rasau Phase 2, and the Northern Perak Water Supply Scheme should further strengthen water security and provide a visible pipeline for contractors, pipe manufacturers and ancillary solution providers. CIMB Securities said Malaysia’s NRW rate stood at 37.1 per cent in 2024. “Persistently high NRW, ageing distribution networks, and rising climate variability result in unnecessary raw water extraction, higher treatment and pumping requirements, weaker utility economics, and supply disruption risks. “Concurrently, population growth, industrialisation, and rapid data centre development are driving structural water demand, particularly across economic corridors in Selangor, Johor, and Penang,” it added. The stockbroking company said Malaysia’s water transition is seen broadening from purely building new infrastructure towards using existing water resources and assets more efficiently. It said sustainable NRW reduction requires physical rehabilitation alongside smart metering, leak detection, pressure management, telemetry, analytics, and intelligent asset-management systems. “These technologies can make water networks more visible, measurable, and manageable, improving the effectiveness of every ringgit spent on water infrastructure. “This is aligned with the Water Sector Transformation 2040 (WST2040), which promotes digitalisation, climate resilience, integrated water-resource management, and stronger sector governance,” it said. From an investment perspective, CIMB Securities said it favours companies positioned at either the efficiency or infrastructure-enablement layers of Malaysia’s water transition. “Insight Analytics Bhd is among the most direct listed proxies to water digitalisation and NRW management, while Gamuda Bhd offers exposure to large-scale treatment, transmission, and water security projects. “The key near-term risk remains the pace at which funding and policy commitments translate into tenders, project awards, and, ultimately, earnings,” it said. -- BERNAMA BERNAMA provides up-to-date authentic and comprehensive news and information which are disseminated via BERNAMA Wires; www.bernama.com; BERNAMA TV on Astro 502, unifi TV 631 and MYTV 121 channels and BERNAMA Radio on FM93.9 (Klang Valley), FM107.5 (Johor Bahru), FM107.9 (Kota Kinabalu) and FM100.9 (Kuching) frequencies. title: 'CIMB Says Lindung 24 Can Narrow Malaysia’s Protection Gap
body: 'Evidently, the SOCSO’s Lindung 24 social insurance scheme is expected to significantly broaden accident protection for workers without materially disrupting the private insurance and takaful industry.  In a sector report, CIMB Securities said Lindung 24, which was implemented by the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso) on June 1, extends protection beyond work-related accidents to provide eligible workers with 24-hour coverage for non-employment accidents, alongside income replacement, rehabilitation and dependants’ benefits.  The research house maintained its Neutral stance on Malaysia’s insurance sector, saying the scheme is primarily aimed at underinsured workers and complements rather than replaces private medical, life and disability coverage.  CIMB said the protection gap remains substantial. Citing Perkeso, it noted that only about 48% of Malaysians have insurance protection beyond motor insurance, while coverage among the bottom 40% income group is estimated at just 4%.  About 38,000 claims were rejected between 2015 and 2025 because employees did not meet traditional eligibility requirements for employment-related accidents. With Lindung 24, Perkeso estimates that roughly 250,000 employees a year could benefit from protection for accidents previously outside the conventional workplace definition.  Take-up has also remained high. As at Sept 9, 8.5 million workers, or 87.6% of the estimated workforce, remained enrolled after the opt-out period for local workers ended on Aug 31. Around 1.2 million workers opted out, with 52% of them earning below RM3,500 per month.  Lindung 24 covers non-work accidents occurring at home, during personal travel, recreational activities, religious activities and other off-duty situations, complementing Perkeso’s existing Employment Injury Scheme, which applies to work-related accidents.  The contribution rate is currently 0.75% of monthly salary until May 2028. It will increase to 1.0% from June 2028 and 1.25% from June 2031, with both contributions and benefits capped at a monthly wage of RM6,000.  Benefits include temporary and permanent disablement payments, medical treatment, rehabilitation, dependants’ benefits, funeral assistance and education support. CIMB noted that fully disabled contributors could receive up to 90% of covered income for life, subject to Perkeso’s assessment and applicable rules.  For insurers, CIMB sees the greatest potential overlap in standalone and employer-sponsored personal accident policies. Employers could eventually rationalise duplicated accident benefits and redirect spending towards medical coverage and other employee benefits.  However, private insurance remains relevant for higher-income workers because Lindung 24 benefits are capped at the RM6,000 salary ceiling, while private products provide broader medical, life, critical illness and income protection.  CIMB said the longer-term effect could be positive by raising awareness of underinsurance and encouraging insurers to focus on higher-value protection and health products. It maintained its Neutral sector view, while remaining more constructive on LPI Capital than Syarikat Takaful Malaysia Keluarga.

title: 'India’s Palm Oil Tax Cut Could Boost Earnings For Local Planters, CIMB
body: 'India’s decision to halve import duties on crude palm oil (CPO) could support demand for Malaysian palm oil and provide some relief to plantation companies, although stronger competition from sunflower oil may limit the upside, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest plantation sector report, CIMB said India reduced the basic import duty on CPO to 5% from 10%, effective Sept 24, as the country seeks to ease domestic edible oil prices ahead of its September-to-November festive season.  India also cut the duty on crude soybean oil to 5% and eliminated the 10% duty on crude sunflower oil.  The changes are particularly relevant to Malaysia, with India accounting for approximately 17% of Malaysia’s palm oil export volume in 2025, making it an important market for the country’s plantation industry.  Higher CPO Prices Could Benefit Malaysian Planters  CIMB said lower import duties should reduce the landed cost of CPO in India, potentially encouraging higher palm oil consumption and imports.  However, the research house cautioned that the larger duty reduction for sunflower oil could improve its competitiveness against palm oil, limiting any significant shift in Indian demand towards CPO.  Before the announcement, CPO was already trading at a price advantage in the Indian market. As at Sept 18, its landed price stood at approximately US$1,265 per tonne, compared with US$1,314 for soybean oil and US$1,380 for sunflower oil.  CIMB expects the benefits for Malaysian plantation companies to come primarily through firmer CPO prices rather than a substantial increase in export volumes.  Upstream producers such as Johor Plantations Group, Genting Plantations, Hap Seng Plantations, Ta Ann Holdings and United Malacca have greater earnings sensitivity to higher CPO prices.  Integrated plantation groups, including SD Guthrie, IOI Corporation and Kuala Lumpur Kepong, could also benefit from stronger upstream margins.  Crude Palm Oil Retains Advantage Over Refined Products  CIMB noted that India has maintained a sizeable import duty differential between crude and refined palm oil, which continues to favour CPO imports for processing by Indian refiners.  The basic import duty on refined palm oil was reduced to 27.5% from 32.5%, compared with the new 5% duty on CPO.  As a result, CIMB expects the impact on Malaysian downstream refiners to remain broadly neutral.  The research house maintained its CPO price forecasts at RM4,450 per tonne for 2026 and RM4,550 for 2027, alongside its Overweight rating on the Malaysian plantation sector.

title: 'CIMB Securities: Consumer, construction stocks seen as key beneficiaries of Budget 2027
body:
'

KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 22): Consumer and construction stocks could be among the key beneficiaries of the upcoming Budget 2027, as higher cash aid, potential tax relief and increased development spending are expected to support domestic demand and infrastructure activity, CIMB Securities said on Tuesday.

In a note, the research house expects allocations for Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (Sara) to rise by about RM2 billion to RM17 billion.

It believes the higher allocation “could provide a modest boost to mass-market consumption, particularly benefitting companies exposed to lower- and middle-income households”.

Among the counters poised to benefit are 99 Speed Mart Retail Holdings Bhd (KL:99SMART), Eco-Shop Marketing Bhd (KL:ECOSHOP) and MR DIY Group (M) Bhd (KL:MRDIY), as well as food and beverage manufacturers Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd (KL:NESTLE), Life Water Bhd (KL:LWSABAH) and QL Resources Bhd (KL:QL).

CIMB Securities also expects gross development expenditure to rise to RM83 billion in 2027, with higher spending on water infrastructure among the potential areas of focus.

Among the counters it sees as well positioned to benefit are Gamuda Bhd (KL:GAMUDA), IJM Corp Bhd (KL:IJM), Malayan Cement Bhd (KL:MCEMENT) and Insight Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB).

Healthcare sector seen supported

Separately, Maybank Investment Bank expects Budget 2027 to remain supportive of the healthcare sector.

Potential measures include tax relief for healthcare and medical insurance, support for the nationwide MediAsas rollout, continued medical-tourism incentives and greater public-private collaboration to ease congestion at public hospitals, it said.

Local pharmaceutical and biopharmaceutical manufacturers may also benefit from continued government support for manufacturing, procurement, research and development, Maybank IB said.

Its top picks include IHH Healthcare Bhd (KL:IHH), KPJ Healthcare Bhd (KL:KPJ), Sunway Healthcare Holdings Bhd (KL:SUNMED), PMCK Bhd (KL:PMCK), Duopharma Biotech Bhd (KL:DPHARMA) and Pharmaniaga Bhd (KL:PHARMA).
