title: 'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says
body: 'TNB Could Absorb Up to RM150 Million in Extra Costs From Expanded Electricity Relief, CIMB Securities Says KUALA LUMPUR — Tenaga Nasional Bhd could absorb an additional RM120 million to RM150 million in costs between September and December 2026 following the expansion of government exemptions covering electricity-related charges for residential consumers, according to CIMB Securities. The brokerage said nearly one million additional households are expected to benefit after the monthly electricity consumption threshold for the exemptions was raised to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) from 600 kWh. The change brings the total number of residential consumers covered to more than eight million. The exemptions involve the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charges and sales and service tax, reducing the immediate impact of electricity costs on a wider group of households. However, CIMB Securities said the arrangement means TNB is expected to absorb additional costs during the September-to-December protection period. The eventual financial impact will depend on the level of AFA charges during that period, which in turn is influenced by fuel costs. Unexpected cost for utility CIMB Securities described the development as a negative surprise because it had previously expected TNB to recover any government-sanctioned AFA subsidies through the Kumpulan Wang Industri Elektrik fund. The latest arrangement instead places an estimated RM120 million to RM150 million of additional costs on the national utility during the final four months of 2026. The research house noted that TNB had previously made a voluntary RM150 million corporate contribution towards the government’s tiered electricity rebate initiative between April and September 2020. That programme was introduced during the Covid-19 pandemic. CIMB Securities said it regarded the 2020 contribution differently because it was made in response to what it described as a severe and unprecedented crisis. The latest cost absorption therefore raises a broader question for investors over whether TNB could be required to shoulder similar costs beyond 2026. 2026 profit forecast trimmed Despite the additional burden, CIMB Securities maintained its “buy” recommendation on TNB and kept its discounted cash flow-based target price unchanged at RM15.90. The brokerage reduced its core net profit forecast for TNB’s full 2026 financial year by two per cent to account for the additional costs. Its core net profit forecasts for the 2027 and 2028 financial years were left largely unchanged. CIMB Securities said the immediate effect on TNB’s core earnings remained relatively small and was insufficient to change its valuation. Its longer-term concern centres instead on what could happen if fuel prices remain elevated and the expanded AFA exemptions continue beyond the end of 2026. Regulatory predictability in focus The research house warned that requiring TNB to absorb further subsidies could affect investor perceptions of the predictability of the utility’s regulated returns. TNB operates under Malaysia’s Incentive Based Regulation framework, which is intended to provide a structured mechanism governing electricity tariffs, costs and regulated returns. For investors, the issue therefore extends beyond the RM120 million to RM150 million estimated impact this year. CIMB Securities said continued cost absorption beyond 2026 could raise concerns about how consistently costs and returns would be treated under the regulatory framework. For households, meanwhile, the higher 800 kWh threshold extends protection from the specified electricity charges to almost one million more residential users. The balance between shielding consumers from higher electricity costs and maintaining the financial predictability of the regulated utility could consequently remain an important issue if fuel costs stay elevated into 2027.

title: 'Markets brace for tighter Fed path: CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Financial markets are pricing a more hawkish US Federal Reserve interest rate path than the latest forecasts from policymakers and economists: This could keep the US dollar supported into 2027, according to CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd. The firm said markets are pricing about 80 basis points of additional Fed tightening in 2027, equivalent to roughly 3.2 rate hikes. This is in comparison with the latest Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) projections for a 25-basis-point increase in the fourth quarter of 2026 and no further hikes in 2027. The FOMC's latest projection puts the policy rate at 4.25 per cent after the expected fourth-quarter move. CIMB Securities said market forecasts for end-2027 rates remain widely dispersed, ranging from 3.25 per cent to 4.50 per cent, with a median of 3.50 per cent. The firm said near-term upside risks to global energy prices and potential price shocks could keep markets positioned for tighter US monetary policy in the fourth quarter of 2026. It also revised higher its forecasts for US Treasury yields relative to German and Japanese government bonds. CIMB Securities raised its end-2027 two-year US Treasury-Bund and US Treasury-JGB spread assumptions by eight basis points and 15 basis points to about 160 basis points and 270 basis points respectively. The wider yield advantage is expected to support the dollar and reduce the case for sustained appreciation in the euro and yen. CIMB Securities said a return of Brent crude to US$100 a barrel could provide another source of support for the dollar, particularly as higher energy prices tend to weigh on currencies of major energy importers. The firm retained its near-term US Dollar Index (DXY) forecast at 101 but raised the third-quarter 2027 projection to 100. However, a decline in Brent below US$90 a barrel could reduce that support, with the DXY ceiling estimated at 99.8 under a lower oil-price scenario. For Asian currencies, CIMB Securities said the impact of higher US rates could be partly offset by relatively stable Chinese yuan conditions and higher regional yields. It expects Asian currencies to remain within their 12-month forecast ranges, with potential yuan strength ahead of a China-US summit providing some stability for the ringgit, Singapore dollar and Thai baht. Higher oil prices and US rates pose greater near-term risks to the Indonesian rupiah, they said, potentially adding pressure for a 25-basis-point Bank Indonesia rate hike in the fourth quarter of 2026.

title: 'Budget 2027 Preview: CIMB Sees More CASH Aid, Tax Relief, Higher Minimum Wage
body: 'Malaysians could see higher cash assistance, targeted personal income tax relief and a possible increase in the minimum wage under Budget 2027, as the government seeks to cushion living costs while maintaining its fiscal consolidation programme, according to CIMB Treasury and Markets Research.  In its Budget 2027 preview, Doing More Within Limits, the research house forecasts the fiscal deficit narrowing to 3.4% of gross domestic product (GDP) in 2027 from an estimated 3.5% this year, supported by lower fuel subsidy expenditure and stronger government revenue.  The budget, scheduled to be tabled on Oct 9, is expected to balance household assistance with development spending and measures to strengthen productivity, investment and the domestic economy.  CIMB expects the government to avoid a broad fiscal stimulus package, instead directing available resources towards targeted support and initiatives that could deliver longer-term economic benefits.  The Ministry of Finance’s Pre-Budget Statement has identified cost-of-living pressures, social protection, productivity, infrastructure and governance among the priorities for Budget 2027, although specific allocations and tax changes have yet to be announced  STR And SARA Could Rise To RM17 Billion  One of CIMB’s principal expectations is an increase in combined Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) allocations to RM17 billion from RM15 billion in 2026.  The additional RM2 billion would help maintain household purchasing power amid higher living costs, particularly for lower-income groups.  CIMB expects the increase to remain focused on the RM100 SARA payment for Malaysians aged 18 and above, alongside targeted STR payments determined by income and household characteristics.  However, the research house cautioned that household spending would increasingly depend on employment and private-sector wage growth as the impact of earlier civil service salary increases moderates.  Despite the proposed increase in assistance, CIMB expects total subsidies and social assistance expenditure to decline to RM73 billion in 2027 from RM79.1 billion in 2026, principally because of lower projected fuel subsidies.  Middle-Income Taxpayers May Receive Relief  CIMB also sees scope for targeted personal income tax relief aimed at middle-income Malaysians who face rising household expenses but may receive less direct cash assistance.  Its illustrative proposal involves reducing selected personal income tax rates by one percentage point and adjusting the tax bracket above RM100,000 in chargeable income.  Under this scenario, taxpayers with RM70,000 in chargeable income could save approximately RM200 annually, while those with RM100,000 could save RM500.  The maximum saving would reach RM1,000 annually for taxpayers with chargeable income of RM150,000 and above.  CIMB estimates that a package of this scale would cost the government approximately RM800 million annually.  These are possible adjustments examined by the research house, rather than confirmed Budget 2027 measures.  Businesses could also receive further Sales and Service Tax (SST) relief, particularly on production inputs and services where taxes are embedded at multiple stages of the supply chain.  CIMB expects selected exemptions to be expanded or extended, potentially benefiting manufacturing, construction and agriculture.  It has factored approximately RM1 billion in additional SST relief into its projections while forecasting overall SST revenue to increase to RM72 billion in 2027.  A broader mechanism allowing businesses to claim credits for tax paid on eligible inputs could be considered, although CIMB believes such a system would be more likely from 2028 onwards because of the administrative requirements involved.  Minimum Wage Could Increase To RM1,800–RM2,000  Another development that workers and employers will be watching is a possible revision to the statutory minimum wage.  CIMB sees scope for the current RM1,700 minimum wage to rise to between RM1,800 and RM2,000, with RM1,800 to RM1,900 considered more consistent with a gradual adjustment.  The research house noted that businesses are already contending with higher labour, energy and logistics costs, while productivity improvements have not necessarily kept pace with wage increases.  Against this backdrop, CIMB believes a broad implementation of the multi-tier foreign worker levy may be less likely in the near term, as employers require more time to absorb existing cost pressures and invest in automation.  Lower Fuel Subsidies Key To Fiscal Consolidation  CIMB’s projections depend significantly on an easing of fuel subsidy expenditure.  The research house expects petrol and diesel subsidies to decline to RM32 billion in 2027 from RM41 billion in 2026, assuming Brent crude averages US$85 a barrel and the ringgit averages RM4.10 against the US dollar.  The RM9 billion reduction would create additional fiscal room for household assistance and development programmes without reversing the government’s deficit reduction trajectory.  However, CIMB warned that prolonged disruptions to global energy supplies could keep oil prices elevated and undermine the expected savings.  In such a scenario, the government could face pressure to retain selected operating expenditure controls or tighten subsidised fuel quotas and eligibility requirements.  Higher fuel costs without sufficient offsetting savings would place additional pressure on the fiscal deficit.  Development Spending To Rise To RM83 Billion  Beyond household support, CIMB forecasts gross development expenditure increasing to RM83 billion in 2027 from RM80 billion this year.  It expects spending priorities to include infrastructure, energy and food security, productivity improvements and investment incentives that generate stronger domestic economic benefits.  The research house said the next phase of investment policy is likely to focus more closely on realised projects, local supply-chain participation, technology transfer and the creation of higher-quality jobs.  On the revenue side, CIMB projects federal government revenue rising 3.7% to RM373 billion, supported partly by a higher PETRONAS dividend of RM25 billion, compared with RM20 billion budgeted for 2026.  It also expects approximately RM1 billion in receipts from the global minimum tax.  Further details on Malaysia’s planned carbon tax could emerge in Budget 2027, although CIMB does not expect meaningful revenue from the measure next year.  Economic Growth Seen At 4.5% In 2027  CIMB forecasts Malaysia’s economic growth moderating to 4.5% in 2027 from 5.0% in 2026, with headline inflation easing slightly to 1.8% from 1.9%.  The research house expects Budget 2027 to provide modest support for domestic demand rather than generate a major acceleration in economic activity.  It also forecasts gross Malaysian Government Securities and Government Investment Issues issuance easing to RM181 billion in 2027 from RM185 billion, reflecting lower debt maturities.  Ultimately, CIMB expects Budget 2027 to centre on a fiscal balancing exercise: providing additional relief to households and businesses while preserving resources for development and gradually reducing the deficit.  The extent to which those objectives can be achieved will depend heavily on energy prices, government revenue performance and the ability to contain expenditure without disrupting essential services or investment.

title: 'Benign inflation keeps OPR outlook intact: CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's inflation may remain benign despite firmer monthly price increases and rising food and electricity costs, according to CIMB Securities. The research house said headline inflation rose to 1.9 per cent year-on-year (YoY) in August from 1.8 per cent in July, while core inflation eased to 1.7 per cent from 1.8 per cent, largely due to favourable base effects in information and communication. However, both headline and core prices rose 0.3 per cent month-on-month (MoM), compared with no change in July, indicating firmer sequential price momentum. "Nonetheless, other indicators in our inflation monitor, including the persistence signal, showed no signs of a pickup in underlying price pressures," CIMB Securities said in a research note. It said food-at-home inflation accelerated to 1.4 per cent YoY from 1.2 per cent, with egg prices rising 5.9 per cent and vegetable prices increasing 2.8 per cent. Electricity inflation also climbed to 3.6 per cent from 2.2 per cent following a higher imbalance cost pass-through surcharge in August. However, the expanded electricity surcharge exemption for Peninsular Malaysia households consuming up to 800kWh monthly, from 600kWh previously, should help contain further pressure between September and December. CIMB Securities expects headline inflation to remain around 1.9 per cent to two per cent in September, with the broader outlook staying manageable. "The softer core reading and still-contained underlying price pressures support our Bank Negara Malaysia policy outlook," it said, maintaining its expectation for the overnight policy rate to remain at 2.75 per cent at the central bank's Monetary Policy Committee meeting in November. On trade, CIMB Securities said August exports surged 45.5 per cent YoY, driven mainly by electrical and electronics and other manufactured goods. However, it cautioned that the strength remained concentrated, while softer momentum in non-E&E and non-petroleum manufacturing exports and potential US semiconductor tariffs continued to pose risks to the growth outlook.

title: 'Budget 2027 could deliver double relief for businesses, middle-income Malaysians - CIMB securities | Business | The Vibes
body: 'MALAYSIAN businesses and middle-income households could receive a double boost from Budget 2027 through wider sales and service tax (SST) exemptions and targeted personal income tax cuts, potentially easing operating and living costs, CIMB Securities says. CIMB Securities, in a research note, said there was scope to broaden SST exemptions for production-related inputs as businesses continued to face elevated energy, logistics and other operating costs. It expects further SST relief to reduce government collections by about RM1 billion, although underlying economic growth should still lift SST revenue by 5.5% to RM72 billion in 2027. title: 'Pelepasan cukai hingga RM1,000, pengecualian SST mungkin diumum dalam Belanjawan 2027 - CIMB Securities | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 18 Sept - Belanjawan 2027 berkemungkinan menyaksikan pengecualian cukai jualan dan perkhidmatan (SST) diperluaskan bagi mengurangkan kos cukai yang terkandung dalam perbelanjaan perniagaan, selain kemungkinan pelepasan cukai pendapatan individu untuk pembayar cukai berpendapatan sederhana, menurut CIMB Securities. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata, kerajaan mempunyai ruang untuk memperluaskan pengecualian SST ke atas input berkaitan pengeluaran ketika perniagaan terus berdepan kos tenaga, logistik dan operasi lain yang tinggi. CIMB Securities turut menjangkakan pelepasan SST tambahan akan mengurangkan kutipan kerajaan kira-kira RM1 bilion, namun pertumbuhan asas masih dijangka meningkatkan hasil SST sebanyak 5.5% kepada RM72 bilion pada 2027. Berbeza dengan cukai barang dan perkhidmatan (GST), SST tidak mempunyai mekanisme kredit cukai input secara umum. Ini bermakna perniagaan mungkin perlu membayar cukai ke atas input tanpa dapat menolaknya daripada cukai yang dikenakan terhadap jualan mereka sendiri. Menurut CIMB Securities, keadaan itu boleh menyebabkan kos cukai terkumpul dan terkandung dalam harga di sepanjang rantaian bekalan. "Peluasan beberapa pengecualian terpilih berkemungkinan menjadi pilihan yang lebih segera dalam Belanjawan 2027, manakala mekanisme kredit cukai input yang lebih menyeluruh mungkin diperkenalkan mulai 2028 atau selepasnya berikutan keperluan menyediakan rangka kerja pentadbiran dan bayaran balik tambahan," kata firma itu dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini. Pelepasan cukai untuk golongan pertengahan Pada masa sama, CIMB Securities melihat terdapat ruang untuk kerajaan menawarkan pelepasan cukai pendapatan individu secara bersasar kepada pembayar cukai berpendapatan sederhana, khususnya isi rumah yang berdepan peningkatan kos sara hidup tetapi menerima bantuan tunai langsung yang lebih rendah. Sebagai gambaran, firma penyelidikan itu berkata, kadar cukai bagi pendapatan bercukai antara RM50,001 hingga RM70,000 dan RM70,001 hingga RM100,000 boleh dikurangkan masing-masing sebanyak satu mata peratusan kepada 10% dan 18%. Kategori cukai semasa pada kadar 25% juga boleh dipecahkan dengan kadar 24% dikenakan terhadap pendapatan bercukai antara RM100,001 hingga RM150,000. Pakej itu berpotensi memberikan penjimatan cukai tahunan sebanyak RM200 kepada individu dengan pendapatan bercukai RM70,000, RM500 bagi pendapatan bercukai RM100,000 dan sehingga RM1,000 kepada mereka yang mempunyai pendapatan bercukai RM150,000 dan ke atas, menurut anggaran CIMB Securities. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata, pakej berkenaan yang dikemukakan sebagai gambaran akan melibatkan kos kira-kira RM800 juta setahun kepada kerajaan. Defisit fiskal dijangka mengecil Secara keseluruhan, CIMB Securities menjangkakan Belanjawan 2027 terus menyediakan sokongan kepada isi rumah sambil mengekalkan usaha konsolidasi fiskal. Ia mengunjurkan defisit fiskal mengecil sedikit kepada 3.4% daripada keluaran dalam negara kasar (KDNK) pada 2027 berbanding anggaran 3.5% pada 2026. Firma penyelidikan itu turut menjangkakan bantuan tunai menerusi Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) dan Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) meningkat sebanyak RM2 bilion kepada RM17 bilion, yang sebahagiannya disokong oleh pengurangan perbelanjaan subsidi bahan api. CIMB Securities mengunjurkan subsidi petrol dan diesel berkurangan kepada RM32 bilion pada 2027 daripada RM41 bilion, sekali gus menyediakan ruang untuk meningkatkan bantuan isi rumah dan perbelanjaan pembangunan sambil memastikan kerajaan kekal pada landasan konsolidasi fiskal. Dibentangkan pada 9 Oktober Belanjawan 2027, yang merupakan Belanjawan MADANI kelima dan belanjawan kedua di bawah Rancangan Malaysia Ke-13 (RMK13), dijadualkan dibentangkan di Parlimen pada 9 Oktober 2026. Kementerian Kewangan berkata, belanjawan itu akan memberi tumpuan kepada beberapa bidang termasuk tekanan kos sara hidup, daya saing perniagaan dan produktiviti, di samping mengekalkan disiplin fiskal. — DagangNews.com

title: 'Stronger MyCC Powers Put Competition Compliance Higher On Governance Agenda, CIMB Report
body: 'Competition compliance is set to become a more important corporate governance and ESG consideration for Malaysian companies as the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) gains stronger enforcement powers, according to CIMB Securities.  In its latest Malaysia strategy report, CIMB said the Competition (Amendment) Bill 2026, passed by the Dewan Rakyat on July 6, significantly broadens MyCC’s enforcement toolkit. As of the report dated Sept 15, CIMB noted that the amendments had yet to be gazetted. Parliament records confirm the Bill was passed on July 6.  The research house said the changes strengthen MyCC’s powers through new settlement mechanisms, whistleblower protection and rewards, and expanded authority to compel companies to provide information during market reviews.  Companies admitting liability after receiving a proposed decision may, according to CIMB’s account of the amendments, negotiate settlements with penalties potentially reduced by up to 40%.  CIMB said MyCC’s enforcement priorities remain focused on cartels, abuse of dominance, government procurement, food supply chains and digital markets, with the commission increasingly evolving from a traditional enforcement body into a broader economic regulator.  Cartels remain the main enforcement priority, particularly in food supply chains and public procurement. MyCC has also increased scrutiny of sectors affecting household living costs and industries where bid-rigging risks are higher.  The report highlighted the chicken feed cartel case as an example of more sophisticated enforcement. MyCC imposed RM415.5 million in total penalties across five companies, its largest competition penalty to date, after finding coordinated price increases between January 2020 and June 2022. The Competition Appeal Tribunal upheld the RM415.5 million decision in February 2026.  Digital markets are also emerging as a major regulatory frontier. MyCC’s review covers mobile operating and payment systems, e-commerce marketplaces, digital advertising, online travel agencies and data privacy, reflecting growing scrutiny of platforms that act as “gatekeepers” between businesses and consumers. MyCC’s official digital economy review identifies the same five areas and 34 competition, market and regulatory issues.  CIMB said competition compliance should increasingly be treated alongside anti-corruption policies, whistleblower mechanisms, board oversight and corporate ethics under the governance pillar of ESG.  It expects Malaysian companies, particularly those operating in concentrated industries, government procurement or sectors with extensive interaction among competitors, to increase investment in board oversight, employee training and formal competition compliance programmes.  While stronger enforcement could increase compliance costs and regulatory scrutiny in the near term, CIMB believes the longer-term impact should be positive for Malaysia’s capital markets by improving market integrity, corporate governance and investor confidence.  The research house does not expect competition enforcement to materially alter sector investment cases in the near term, but said governance standards are likely to become a more important differentiator as Malaysia’s competition regime matures.

title: 'U Mobile catat kerugian lebih besar akibat kos 5G - CIMB Securities | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 17 Sept — Penyedia rangkaian 5G kedua Malaysia, U Mobile Sdn Bhd terus mengukuhkan kedudukan dalam perkhidmatan mudah alih apabila bahagian hasil pasaran syarikat meningkat kepada 17.4% pada tahun kewangan 2025 (FY25), menurut CIMB Securities. Bahagian hasil mudah alih U Mobile meningkat 0.8 mata peratusan kepada 17.4%, meneruskan trend peningkatan daripada hanya 2.1% pada FY2012. Hasil perkhidmatan mudah alih juga meningkat 5% tahun ke tahun (YoY) pada FY2025. Prestasi itu mengatasi CelcomDigi Berhad yang mencatat penurunan hasil mudah alih 1%, manakala hasil Maxis Berhad tidak berubah dalam tempoh sama. Pertumbuhan U Mobile berkemungkinan disokong peluasan rangkaiannya di Sabah dan Sarawak, termasuk pelaburan dalam pengedaran dan liputan rangkaian. "Jualan barangan U Mobile turut meningkat 41% YoY selepas mencatat pertumbuhan 38% pada FY2024, menunjukkan permintaan lebih kukuh terhadap pelan pascabayar dan jalur lebar 5G yang digabungkan dengan peranti," kata CIMB Securities. Bagaimanapun, prestasi kewangan U Mobile terjejas oleh kos rangkaian yang lebih tinggi serta susut nilai dipercepatkan berkaitan peluasan rangkaian jalur lebarnya. Kerugian bersih syarikat meningkat 124% YoY kepada RM1.62 bilion pada FY25, dengan susut nilai dipercepatkan meningkat kepada RM1.03 bilion berbanding RM489 juta pada FY24. CIMB Securities berkata kerugian bersih teras (CNL) U Mobile meningkat 163% YoY kepada RM595 juta. Jika kos faedah daripada pendahuluan pemegang saham (SHA) dan saham keutamaan boleh tebus dan tukar (RCPS) tidak diambil kira, CNL syarikat berjumlah RM383 juta berbanding RM19 juta setahun sebelumnya. Pendapatan sebelum faedah, cukai, susut nilai dan pelunasan (EBITDA) pula susut 38% YoY kepada RM773 juta, manakala margin EBITDA turun 15.2 mata peratusan kepada 22.2%, kemungkinan disebabkan kos rangkaian dan peranti yang lebih tinggi serta caj sekali sahaja. Sementara itu, susut nilai dan pelunasan (D&A) yang dinormalkan turun 10% YoY kepada RM935 juta, mencerminkan asas aset tetap yang lebih rendah selepas susut nilai dipercepatkan terkumpul sebanyak RM1.5 bilion pada FY2024 dan FY2025. Kos faedah bersih meningkat 2% YoY kepada RM432 juta. Dalam masa sama, perbelanjaan modal (capex) yang dijana nilai, tidak termasuk spektrum, melonjak lebih enam kali ganda kepada RM1.23 bilion pada FY2025 berikutan pelaksanaan rangkaian 5G bermula pertengahan 2025. Peningkatan perbelanjaan itu dibiayai menerusi pinjaman berjangka yang meningkat RM338 juta YoY, pembiayaan vendor sebanyak RM493 juta serta kredit perdagangan jangka pendek. Tidak termasuk SHA dan RCPS, hutang bersih U Mobile meningkat 25% YoY kepada RM3.38 bilion, manakala nisbah hutang bersih kepada EBITDA meningkat kepada 4.4 kali berbanding 2.3 kali bagi CelcomDigi dan 1.9 kali bagi Maxis. Aliran tunai bebas kepada ekuiti turut berubah kepada negatif RM251 juta daripada positif RM123 juta sebelumnya selepas mengambil kira capex aliran tunai RM819 juta dan pembayaran balik bersih pembiayaan vendor RM103 juta. Struktur pemegang saham U Mobile juga berubah apabila Mawar Setia Sdn Bhd menjadi pemegang saham terbesar dengan pegangan 50.2% pada 17 Mac, manakala pegangan Singapore Technologies Telemedia (ST Telemedia) susut kepada 20.7%.

title: 'BernamaBiz - Potential Super El Nino Could Weigh On Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand Growth Into 3Q 2027 -- CIMB
body: 'Potential Super El Nino Could Weigh On Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand Growth Into 3Q 2027 -- CIMB KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 27 (Bernama) -- A potentially record-strength El Nino could weigh on economic growth in Malaysia, Indonesia and Thailand from late 2026 into the third quarter (3Q) of 2027, with Indonesia and Thailand likely to be hit earlier than Malaysia, according to CIMB Investment Bank Bhd. In its CIMB Treasury and Markets Research report today, it said the Relative Oceanic Nino Index (RONI) is expected to peak at between 2.5°C (Celcius) and 3.0°C in November and December 2026, with rainfall stress likely to emerge in Indonesia in 3Q 2026, followed by Malaysia and Thailand in 1Q 2027. “Gross domestic product (GDP) drag from adverse El Nino could run from late 2026 into 3Q 2027,” it said. Assuming a peak RONI of 2.5°C, CIMB said the impact on quarterly GDP growth is expected to peak at around 0.4 percentage point in Thailand and 0.3 percentage point in Indonesia in 1Q 2027. Malaysia is expected to experience the impact later, with quarterly GDP growth potentially taking a hit of around 0.2 percentage point at its peak in 3Q 2027, it said. Despite the potential impact on growth, CIMB said broader demand effects from El Nino appear to have been limited historically. However, the investment bank said growth risks are skewed to the downside due to fertiliser costs, water shortages and haze associated with adverse El Nino conditions. -- BERNAMA

title: 'CIMB Bank wins big at Euromoney Awards
body: 'PETALING JAYA: CIMB Bank Bhd and CIMB Investment Bank have won top accolades at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026, taking home top honours as Malaysia’s Best Retail Bank, Malaysia’s Best Digital Bank for SMEs, and Malaysia’s Best Investment Bank. The bank said in a statement that the awards reflected the ongoing focus on providing customer-centric solutions through innovation, digital capabilities and deep market expertise across its retail, small and medium enterprise (SME), and investment banking businesses. CIMB Group Holdings Bhd group chief executive officer Novan Amirudin commented that the recognitions are a testament to the trust of the group’s customers and the dedication of its teams. “They reaffirm CIMB’s purpose of advancing customers and society by making financial solutions more accessible, relevant and impactful for the people and businesses we serve,” he added. “As their needs continue to evolve, we remain committed to being a trusted partner supporting individuals in realising their aspirations and helping businesses achieve their growth ambitions through meaningful and lasting value creation.” CIMB’s latest wins come amid the bank’s continued efforts to empower customers through accessible, inclusive and purpose-driven financial solutions. In retail banking, it has been working to deepen its franchise through personalisation offerings, digitally enabled journeys, and stronger engagement across segments. The bank said revenue and profitability had advanced during the year, underpinned by market share gains in auto finance, credit cards and retail deposits, on top of progress in digital sales and customer cross-sell. It also continued to strengthen wealth proposition through differentiated investment solutions, broader product diversity, chief investment office-led advisory capabilities and enhanced digital wealth platform, with particular momentum seen in the “Preferred” affluent segment as it expands its advisory-led and relationship-based wealth capabilities. Meanwhile, the bank has continued to advance its SME services, having launched the CIMB OCTO Biz digital banking platform, which has amassed more than 280,000 customers to date. Additionally, it has expanded financing access through embedded merchant financing with TNG eWallet and its flexible financing through its SME FlexiCash. Beyond this, CIMB Investment Bank in 2025 secured the top ranking in Malaysian equity and debt capital markets by deal value and share of wallet, as well as the highest position in Asean equity and debt capital markets by deal value, cementing its position both locally and regionally.

title: 'CIMB raih tiga anugerah perbankan Euromoney 2026
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Bank Berhad dan CIMB Investment Bank (CIMB) terus mengukuhkan kedudukan dalam industri kewangan apabila meraih tiga anugerah utama pada Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026. CIMB dinobatkan sebagai Bank Runcit Terbaik Malaysia, Bank Digital Terbaik Malaysia untuk Perusahaan Kecil dan Sederhana (PKS) serta Bank Pelaburan Terbaik Malaysia. Pengiktirafan berkenaan mencerminkan prestasi, inovasi dan impak kepada pelanggan yang dicapai CIMB, selain usaha berterusannya dalam menyediakan penyelesaian kewangan berorientasikan pelanggan menerusi inovasi, keupayaan digital dan kepakaran pasaran yang kukuh. Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif Kumpulan CIMB, Novan Amirudin berkata, kejayaan itu membuktikan kepercayaan pelanggan serta komitmen pasukan bank dalam memenuhi keperluan individu dan perniagaan. “Pengiktirafan ini adalah bukti kepercayaan pelanggan serta dedikasi pasukan kami di seluruh bank. “Ia mengukuhkan semula tujuan CIMB untuk memacu kemajuan pelanggan dan masyarakat dengan menjadikan penyelesaian kewangan lebih mudah diakses, relevan dan memberi impak kepada individu serta perniagaan yang kami berkhidmat,” katanya dalam kenyataan. Menurut beliau, CIMB akan terus menjadi rakan kongsi dipercayai dalam membantu individu merealisasikan aspirasi mereka, selain menyokong perniagaan mencapai matlamat pertumbuhan melalui penciptaan nilai yang bermakna dan berkekalan. Dalam perbankan runcit, CIMB terus memperkukuh segmen perniagaannya menerusi penawaran diperibadikan, pengalaman digital serta penglibatan lebih kukuh dengan kumpulan pelanggan utama. Prestasi pendapatan dan keuntungan turut meningkat sepanjang tahun, disokong pertambahan bahagian pasaran dalam pembiayaan kenderaan, kad kredit dan deposit runcit, selain peningkatan jualan digital serta penawaran silang kepada pelanggan. CIMB turut memperkukuh penawaran pengurusan kekayaan menerusi penyelesaian pelaburan yang berbeza, kepelbagaian produk lebih luas, khidmat nasihat diketuai Ketua Pegawai Pelaburan (CIO) serta platform pengurusan kekayaan digital yang dipertingkatkan. Momentum itu khususnya ketara dalam segmen Preferred, mencerminkan penglibatan lebih mendalam dengan pelanggan berkemampuan tinggi serta tumpuan bank terhadap khidmat nasihat dan hubungan pelanggan dalam pengurusan kekayaan. Bagi segmen PKS pula, CIMB terus memperluas perbankan digital menerusi pelancaran CIMB OCTO Biz, yang menghubungkan pembukaan akaun, pembiayaan dan perbankan transaksi dalam satu perjalanan digital hujung ke hujung. Platform itu telah menarik lebih 280,000 pelanggan setakat ini, dengan menawarkan kemudahan melihat aliran tunai secara masa nyata, pembayaran, pertukaran asing, perdagangan serta perkhidmatan pembiayaan. Bank turut memperluas akses pembiayaan menerusi kemudahan pembiayaan pedagang bersepadu dengan TNG eWallet, selain pembiayaan fleksibel melalui SME FlexiCash. Kemudahan berkenaan menggunakan rekod sejarah akaun dan corak transaksi untuk menentukan had pra-kelayakan serta menghubungkan pembayaran balik kepada sebahagian daripada hasil perniagaan, sekali gus membantu perniagaan yang mempunyai aliran tunai tidak sekata. Sementara itu, kepimpinan CIMB Investment Bank dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang Malaysia, penggabungan dan pengambilalihan (M&A), serta penyelesaian nasihat kewangan khusus turut mengukuhkan kedudukannya sebagai bank pelaburan utama. Pada 2025, CIMB Investment Bank menduduki tempat pertama dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang Malaysia berdasarkan nilai urus niaga serta bahagian dompet (share of wallet). Bank itu turut menduduki kedudukan teratas dalam pasaran modal ekuiti dan hutang ASEAN berdasarkan nilai urus niaga, dengan kejayaan melaksanakan transaksi rentas sempadan yang mengukuhkan kedudukannya sebagai peneraju M&A dan khidmat nasihat di rantau ASEAN. Tiga anugerah berkenaan turut mengukuhkan janji jenama CIMB, Moving You Forward, yang mencerminkan komitmen berterusan bank dalam memperkasa pelanggan dan komuniti menerusi penyelesaian kewangan yang mudah diakses, inklusif serta berteraskan tujuan. Euromoney Awards for Excellence, yang telah berlangsung lebih 30 tahun, mengiktiraf institusi kewangan yang menetapkan penanda aras global dari segi prestasi, inovasi dan impak kepada pelanggan. Program anugerah itu menilai institusi kewangan menerusi rangka kerja penanda aras Euromoney dengan menggunakan metrik yang boleh dibandingkan, penyerahan maklumat berstruktur serta proses penyelidikan telus bagi menilai prestasi institusi berbanding pesaing masing-masing.-UTUSAN

title: 'CIMB Scheduled Downtime for Debit Card Users
body: '14th September 2026 - 2 min read You won’t be able to pay with your CIMB debit card for a few hours on 19, 22, and 23 September 2026. CIMB will be doing scheduled maintenance on its debit card system during the early morning on each of these days. The break covers debit cards from both CIMB Bank and CIMB Islamic. CIMB shared the dates in a notice to cardholders on 9 September 2026. All three maintenance breaks start at midnight. The first break starts when Friday night (18 September) turns into Saturday. The next two start straight after Monday night and Tuesday night. The longest break is on Tuesday, 22 September, when your card won’t work until 7.30am. If you usually pay for breakfast or your morning commute with your debit card, you’ll need another way to pay that morning. During these hours, you can’t make any purchases with your CIMB debit card. This includes tapping or inserting your card at a payment terminal in a shop, and entering your card details to pay on a website or app. It applies whether your card uses MyDebit, Visa, or Mastercard. So if you tap your card at a convenience store after midnight or pay for a late night food order with a saved card, the payment will fail. The card will work as usual again once each break ends. Paying through FPX, where you log in to your online banking to pay a website, doesn’t use your debit card. Neither do DuitNow transfers or scanning a DuitNow QR code with your banking app. CIMB’s notice only lists debit card purchases, so FPX and DuitNow payments aren’t included in this maintenance. If you need to buy something during these hours, pay for it earlier in the evening, or use FPX or DuitNow QR if the shop or website accepts them. If you’re unsure whether a specific payment will be affected, you can check with CIMB directly before the maintenance dates. For more information, you can read CIMB’s full notice [PDF]. title: 'CIMB wins Malaysia’s Best Retail, Investment and SME Banking Awards from Euromoney
body: 'Kuala Lumpur: CIMB Bank Berhad and CIMB Investment Bank (collectively “CIMB”) have been recognised for strong performance, innovation and customer impact, winning three key awards at the Euromoney Awards for Excellence 2026. CIMB was named Malaysia’s Best Retail Bank, Malaysia’s Best Digital Bank for SMEs and Malaysia’s Best Investment Bank.  These recognitions reflect CIMB’s continued focus on delivering customer-centric solutions through innovation, digital capabilities and deep market expertise across its retail, SME and investment banking businesses.  Novan Amirudin, Group Chief Executive Officer, CIMB Group, said, “These recognitions are a testament to the trust of our customers and the dedication of our teams across the Bank. They reaffirm CIMB’s purpose of advancing customers and society by making financial solutions more accessible, relevant and impactful for the people and businesses we serve.  We thank our clients and customers for the confidence they have placed in us over the years. As their needs continue to evolve, we remain committed to being a trusted partner supporting individuals in realising their aspirations and helping businesses achieve their growth ambitions through meaningful and lasting value creation."  In retail banking, the Bank continued to deepen its diversified franchise through personalised propositions, digitally enabled journeys and stronger engagement across key customer segments. Revenue and profitability advanced during the year, supported by market share gains across auto finance, credit cards and retail deposits, alongside continued progress in digital sales and customer cross-sell. The Bank also continued to strengthen its wealth proposition, underpinned by differentiated investment solutions, broader product diversity, CIO-led advisory capabilities and enhanced digital wealth platforms. Momentum was particularly strong within the Preferred segment, reflecting deeper affluent engagement and the Bank's continued focus on expanding advisory-led and relationship-based wealth capabilities.  For SMEs, CIMB continued to advance digital banking with the launch of CIMB OCTO Biz, connecting account opening, financing and transaction banking through a seamless end-to-end digital journey. The platform has onboarded more than 280,000 customers to date, offering real-time cash flow visibility, payments, foreign exchange, trade and financing services. The Bank also expanded financing access via embedded merchant financing with TNG eWallet, in addition to flexible financing through its SME FlexiCash, which uses account history and transaction behaviour to determine pre-qualified limits and link repayments to a proportion of revenue, better supporting businesses with uneven cashflows.  Meanwhile, CIMB Investment Bank’s leadership across Malaysia’s equity and debt capital markets, mergers and acquisitions, and bespoke financial advisory solutions, as well as its ability to execute complex transactions across multiple products, sectors and jurisdictions, further reinforced its position as a leading investment bank. In 2025, CIMB Investment Bank secured the #1 ranking in Malaysian equity and debt capital markets by deal value and share of wallet, while also capturing the top position in ASEAN equity and debt capital markets by deal value, with its execution of cross-border transactions reinforcing its position as a leading M&A and advisory house in ASEAN.  These three accolades reinforce CIMB’s brand promise, Moving You Forward, reflecting its continued focus on empowering customers and communities through accessible, inclusive and purpose-driven financial solutions.  For more than 30 years, Euromoney’s Awards for Excellence have recognised financial institutions that set the global standard in performance, innovation and client impact. The Awards for Excellence programme evaluates financial institutions through Euromoney’s benchmarking framework, using comparable metrics, structured submissions and a transparent research process to assess institutions against their peers.

title: 'CIMB Completes Malaysia’s First Tokenised Sukuk Settlement Using Tokenised Deposits
body: 'CIMB Group Holdings Bhd has completed a pilot to test the settlement of tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits in a controlled environment, paving the way for broader applications enabled by blockchain technology. These potential applications include instant, or atomic, settlement for cross-border transactions, as well as the democratisation of investment assets — such as enabling bonds to be sold in smaller amounts that retail investors can more easily afford. The pilot was carried out through CIMB Islamic Bank Bhd in connection with a RM1.68 billion issuance under CIMB Islamic’s existing RM10 billion senior sukuk wakalah programme, with tenors of five, seven, 10 and 15 years. Of the total issuance, RM1.38 billion was issued in tokenised form and subscribed to by 12 institutional investors, while the remaining RM300 million was issued as a traditional sukuk. The order book was covered 1.73 times, with the pricing date set at Aug 19 and settlement completed on Aug 27, according to Sylvia Wong, regional head of tokenisation at CIMB Group Wholesale Banking. The key distinction between CIMB’s pilot and an earlier pilot conducted by Khazanah Nasional Bhd lies in how settlement occurred. CIMB’s pilot involved settling both the tokenised sukuk and tokenised deposits, meaning the financial asset and the cash were both settled on-chain — though the tokens mirror legal records that continue to exist within the traditional system. A tokenised deposit refers to a bank deposit recorded as a digital token on a blockchain, effectively representing commercial bank money in digital form. In contrast, Khazanah’s tokenised sukuk, which settled in mid-May, was paid for using fiat currency, or the ringgit, through traditional payment rails rather than blockchain. In that case, only the financial asset was settled on-chain, while the cash portion moved through conventional channels. “For our pilot, we created tokenised deposits to settle the tokenised sukuk, so both of these settlements are on the blockchain,” Wong said, adding that the blockchain used for the settlement is called CIMB Blockchain Connect. The digital asset custodian (DAC) involved in the pilot — the entity responsible for safeguarding clients’ tokenised assets — is not among the two DACs currently registered with the Securities Commission Malaysia (SC). “For this pilot, we cleared with the SC that a DAC licence is not required. We just need the ability to custodise these assets and the deposits,” Wong said during a press conference. What It Means for Ordinary People Wong explained that the central feature of the pilot is atomic settlement, where a buyer’s money and a seller’s asset change hands at exactly the same instant. She noted, however, that this concept holds limited relevance for individual consumers, who can already transfer and settle smaller sums instantly through existing payment infrastructure such as DuitNow. Settlement remains far from instantaneous in the institutional market, though. When large sums of money are sent overseas — for purposes such as funding a child’s education — the process can take several days as funds move through traditional channels involving multiple banks. “Now, with blockchain technology, if everyone is on the same blockchain, it happens literally instantaneously,” she said. The pilot nonetheless follows a “digital twin” approach, meaning the on-chain token mirrors traditional legal records rather than replacing them entirely; the process is therefore not conducted wholly on-chain. “The technological capability [for atomic settlement] is there, but are we ready to go [completely] instantaneous? We may not be ready just yet. Imagine, it is fine if it is RM100, but it is a different story if the amount is RM100 million, for a bank. Banks are looking for less friction, but not frictionless for now,” she said. Adopting a digital twin model means banks such as CIMB are investing in testing tokenised solutions through blockchain technology, even as traditional legal records and processes continue to run in parallel — meaning cost savings have yet to materialise. However, as more processes shift on-chain in the years ahead, banking operations could become faster and more efficient, while tokenisation could also help democratise asset classes by making them more accessible to retail investors. Making Financial Markets More Efficient According to a press release, the pilot was carried out as part of CIMB’s participation in Bank Negara Malaysia’s Digital Asset Innovation Hub, which offers a controlled environment for financial institutions to test new digital asset applications. CIMB has also been engaging with the SC on the broader development of tokenised capital market products. The completion of the pilot was announced at Menara CIMB in Kuala Lumpur, at an event attended by Finance Minister II Senator Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan. Amir Hamzah said the pilot demonstrates how Malaysia can build on its established strengths in Islamic finance and capital markets as financial infrastructure becomes increasingly digital. “Malaysia has developed deep capabilities in both Islamic finance and the capital markets. The next step is to ensure that these strengths continue to evolve alongside changes in technology and the way financial transactions are conducted. This pilot is important because it moves tokenisation beyond theory and tests how digital financial assets and commercial bank money can work together in a controlled environment. The objective is not digitalisation for its own sake, but to explore whether technology can make financial markets more efficient, transparent and connected while preserving strong standards of governance, investor protection and shariah compliance,” he said. Novan Amirudin, group chief executive officer of CIMB Group, said the pilot provided the bank and regulators with practical insights into the operational, legal and regulatory requirements involved in tokenised financial transactions. “This pilot allows us to test how tokenised financial assets can operate alongside existing market infrastructure and, importantly, how tokenised deposits can be used for settlement. The potential benefits are practical. Greater automation and faster settlement could reduce friction in financial transactions, improve liquidity management and increase capital efficiency. The experience gained from this pilot will help us assess how these capabilities can be developed further in Malaysia and, potentially, across regional and cross-border applications,” he said. Beyond Technology: Partnership and Integration During the press conference, Ahmad Shahriman Mohamad Shariff, CEO of Group Islamic Banking, CIMB, said an equally significant achievement of the pilot was persuading major fund management firms and government agencies to build the infrastructure required to settle CIMB’s tokenised sukuk using tokenised deposits. “If they were to choose, it is easier for them to settle [with cash] in fiat [currency], as that’s business as usual for them. But in order to join the pilot, they have to set up their own infrastructure. While we are trying to encourage people to explore [tokenisation] and onboard them, there’s a fair amount of work on their side [to be completed] as well. And we are very glad and happy to see the responses. It was well-received,” he said.

title: 'Public Bank, Maybank and CIMB Among Eight Malaysian Banks on Forbes’ Global List
body: 'Eight Malaysian banks made Forbes’ inaugural ranking of the world’s top-performing banks in 2026. Public Bank ranked fifth in Tier 2, the highest position among Malaysia’s three entries in the category. Maybank placed 14th while CIMB Group Holdings ranked 35th. Tier 2 covers banks with assets from US$100 billion to US$500 billion. Hong Leong Financial Group ranked ninth in Tier 3 while RHB Bank placed 37th. The category covers banks with assets from US$50 billion to US$100 billion. Bank Rakyat placed 32nd in Tier 4 while AmBank Group ranked 68th. Tier 4 covers banks with assets from US$20 billion to US$50 billion. Alliance Bank Malaysia was the country’s sole Tier 5 entry and placed 90th. This category covers banks with assets from US$10 billion to US$20 billion. Forbes and Statista compiled the ranking using financial data, desk research and bank submissions. Unlike its survey-based bank rankings, the new list assesses financial performance. Banks were evaluated on profitability, earnings quality, resilience, asset quality and efficiency. Eligible institutions needed more than US$3 billion in assets, audited financial statements and at least three years of financial data. They were grouped into six tiers by asset size. The final list covered 500 banks across 89 countries, with no payment required to participate or be selected. title: 'Malaysia’s First Nuclear Power Plant Could Come Online By 2040-2046, CIMB
body: 'Malaysia could potentially commission its first nuclear power plant between 2040 and 2046, as the country begins the lengthy process of assessing nuclear energy as a firm, low-carbon source of electricity amid rising power demand and energy security concerns, according to CIMB Securities.  In a sector report assessing Malaysia’s nuclear option, CIMB said the country has recently restarted Phase 1 of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s (IAEA) Milestones Approach, with MyPOWER Corp appointed to coordinate the feasibility assessment. The process requires the government to complete feasibility studies and establish a national position before making a knowledgeable commitment to a nuclear programme.  The IAEA estimates that all three phases required to develop nuclear power infrastructure could take 10 to 15 years, although there is no fixed timeline. Assuming Malaysia completes Phase 1 and formally decides to adopt nuclear power by 2030-2031, CIMB estimates another three to four years would be required for regulatory preparation, site assessment, vendor selection and commercial negotiations before construction or fabrication begins.  CIMB said renewed interest in nuclear power comes as the West Asia conflict highlights vulnerabilities in Malaysia’s energy supply while electricity demand is accelerating, partly due to investments in data centres.  Nuclear Offers Firm, Low-Carbon Power  According to CIMB, nuclear energy could provide Malaysia with firm and relatively clean baseload electricity, while using less land than solar photovoltaic projects and reducing exposure to volatile fossil fuel prices.  However, nuclear is neither the cheapest nor fastest new-build clean energy option, given the extensive planning, regulatory requirements and capital involved. Public acceptance also remains an important challenge.  From an ESG perspective, CIMB said Malaysia would need to balance the potential benefits of reliable low-carbon electricity against issues including affordability, safety, radioactive waste, water use, public acceptance and long-term government accountability.  The research house’s readiness assessment shows several areas remain unresolved. No project cost, electricity tariff model or site has been determined, while the owner and financing structure remain undecided. Commercial spent-fuel and disposal arrangements have also yet to be established, alongside funding mechanisms for waste management and eventual decommissioning.  TNB Could Play Key Role  Malaysia has, however, already identified several important institutional players.  MyPOWER has been appointed as the country’s nuclear energy programme implementing organisation, while Atom Malaysia would serve as the nuclear and radiation licensing regulator. Nuklear Malaysia would provide technical expertise and workforce development, while the Energy Commission would oversee electricity market-related matters.  The owner-operator has yet to be determined, but CIMB views Tenaga Nasional Bhd (TNB) as the most logical anchor operator for a future baseload nuclear asset because of its balance sheet and control of the grid. An independent power producer with nuclear expertise could alternatively be involved to reduce project risk.  CIMB said private-sector participation during the initial stages would likely remain limited, apart from TNB’s potential role as the commercial delivery vehicle for a pioneering nuclear project. The research house maintained its BUY call on TNB with a target price of RM15.90, against RM13.90 at the time of the report.  Large Reactors, SMRs And Floating Plants Among Options  Malaysia has yet to settle on a reactor technology, with CIMB identifying conventional large-scale reactors, small modular reactors (SMRs) and floating nuclear power plants as possible options under evaluation.  Conventional reactors offer proven technology and economies of scale above 1,000MW but require substantial upfront investment and lengthy development. SMRs potentially offer lower initial capital requirements and modular expansion, although CIMB noted there are currently no proven commercially viable units demonstrating replicable economics.  Floating nuclear plants could reduce land constraints by locating reactors offshore, but may face complications involving international maritime law.  On ownership, CIMB considers full foreign control unlikely given Malaysia’s established government-linked entities. It suggested a structure similar to the UAE’s Barakah nuclear project could be more suitable, with TNB or another Malaysian project company retaining control while an experienced foreign nuclear supplier takes minority equity and provides turnkey construction and operating support.  CIMB said the ultimate decision should hinge not only on reactor technology but also on who bears the risks of construction cost overruns, delays, operating performance, fuel and waste obligations and long-term electricity tariffs.  For now, Malaysia remains at the assessment stage. CIMB noted that the next major milestones would be a formal commitment to a nuclear programme, followed by development of the regulatory framework, selection of reactor technology and finalisation of ownership and financing models.

title: 'CIMB Securities lifts 2026 GDP growth forecast to 5pct on domestic strength
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: CIMB Securities Research has raised its forecast for Malaysia's 2026 gross domestic product (GDP) growth to five per cent from 4.8 per cent previously, backed by stronger-than-expected domestic activity. "Following the weaker-than-expected July Industrial Production Index (IPI) outturn, the third quarter (Q3) 2026 GDP nowcast has edged down to 5.0 per cent from 5.2 per cent," it said in a note. However, CIMB Securities said the weakening in domestic manufacturing assumed in its house forecast has so far not materialised. The firm noted that domestic-oriented production outside the motor vehicle segment strengthened in July, while overall manufacturing output continued to expand sequentially. "We therefore raise our Q3 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4.5 per cent from 4.0 per cent previously, and our full-year 2026 forecast to 5.0 per cent from 4.8 per cent previously. "This reflects stronger-than-expected resilience in domestic activity," it said. On the overnight policy rate, CIMB Securities said its outlook remained unchanged, with the inflation trajectory the key factor in determining the timing of a rate hike. Nevertheless, the firm said renewed escalation in the Middle East remained a downside risk to growth, while prospective US semiconductor tariffs could weigh on electrical and electronics manufacturing and exports if introduced.

title: 'Gangguan bekalan arang batu Indonesia tidak jejas Malayan Cement, menurut CIMB Securities | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 10 Sept - Gangguan bekalan arang batu di Indonesia susulan faktor cuaca dijangka tidak memberi kesan ketara terhadap prospek Malayan Cement Bhd serta harga sahamnya, menurut CIMB Securities. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata, kekurangan itu masih boleh diuruskan menerusi beberapa langkah termasuk mengunci harga dan langkah penjimatan operasi lain. "Kesannya masih boleh diuruskan bagi Malayan Cement," katanya dalam nota penyelidikan hari ini. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata kebimbangan pelabur terhadap gangguan laluan utama pengangkutan arang batu menggunakan tongkang di Indonesia, selain ketegangan yang kembali memuncak di Timur Tengah, mungkin telah memberi tekanan kepada saham Malayan Cement. Bagaimanapun, CIMB berpandangan kesan susulan daripada gangguan bekalan arang batu di Indonesia terhadap Malayan Cement kekal terkawal. Malah, harga penanda aras terkini bagi arang batu gred rendah dan sederhana di Indonesia masing-masing susut 1.1% dan 1.9% secara separuh ke separuh (HOH) pada separuh pertama September 2026. Tambah firma itu lagi, Malayan Cement telah mengunci bekalan arang batu sehingga November 2026, sekali gus mengurangkan risiko gangguan bekalan akibat cuaca di Indonesia. Harga spot arang batu gred sederhana ketika ini sebanyak US$83 satu tan juga masih di bawah unjuran firma itu sebanyak US$90 satu tan bagi FY2027-FY2028. "Keadaan itu memberikan margin keselamatan terhadap andaian kos Malayan Cement, sekali gus mengurangkan kebimbangan terhadap tekanan kos akibat gangguan bekalan," katanya. Selain itu, sebarang kenaikan harga arang batu juga berkemungkinan dihadkan oleh permintaan lebih lembut dari China dan India, memandangkan kedua-dua negara mempelbagaikan sumber bekalan kepada Rusia, Afrika Selatan dan Australia. Harga simen stabil Dalam pada itu, harga simen tempatan dijangka kekal stabil bagi baki 2026, selepas berada dalam julat sempit RM25.30 hingga RM25.95 setiap beg sepanjang tujuh bulan pertama tahun ini. CIMB Securities berkata jangkaan itu turut sejajar dengan maklum balas daripada pemain sektor pembinaan dan hartanah yang tidak menjangkakan perubahan besar dalam harga simen bagi baki tahun ini, dengan syarat harga minyak kekal stabil. Pada masa sama, Malayan Cement telah memulakan pelbagai inisiatif bagi meningkatkan kecekapan operasi serta penggunaan bahan api dan bahan alternatif bagi mengoptimumkan kos pengeluaran. CIMB menjangkakan keuntungan bersih teras Malayan Cement meningkat daripada RM918 juta pada FY2026 kepada RM950 juta pada FY2028. Hasil dividen pula diunjurkan meningkat daripada 2.7% pada FY2026 kepada 3.6% pada FY2028, manakala gear bersih dijangka bertambah baik daripada 12.3% pada Jun 2026 kepada kedudukan tunai bersih menjelang FY2028. Mengambil kira kedudukan dominan Malayan Cement dalam pasaran, kunci kira-kira yang kukuh serta prospek pendapatan yang lebih baik, CIMB mengekalkan saranan "beli" terhadap saham syarikat itu dengan sasaran harga RM8.50. Sasaran tersebut menawarkan potensi kenaikan sekitar 55% berbanding harga saham semasa RM5.48. Malayan Cement kini didagangkan pada nisbah harga kepada pendapatan (PE) FY2027-FY2028 sebanyak 11 hingga 12 kali dan satu kali nilai buku sesaham (PBV) FY2026. CIMB berkata penilaian itu mencerminkan diskaun yang tidak wajar, memandangkan kedudukan pasaran dan kekuatan kewangan Malayan Cement. Penarafan konsensus pula menunjukkan enam saranan "beli", satu "pegang" dan tiada saranan "kurang", menunjukkan sokongan meluas penganalisis terhadap saham tersebut.

title: 'FBM KLCI expansion to improve sector diversification: CIMB Securities
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: The proposed expansion of the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) to 50 constituents is expected to materially improve sector diversification. CIMB Securities Sdn Bhd said the expanded benchmark will have lower exposure to financial services and utilities, while increasing representation across industrials, technology, consumer discretionary, energy, real estate and consumer staples. This is consistent with CIMB Securities' previous simulation, which estimated that the 20 new constituents could account for around 15.6 per cent of the expanded index at full inclusion. "We remain positive on the structural change as it should create a more representative Malaysian benchmark and broaden institutional exposure beyond the existing large-cap sectors," it said in a note. Meanwhile, CIMB Securities said FTSE clarified that full market capitalisation determines final stock selection, while free float determines index weights. Since passive FBM KLCI-tracking assets under management are relatively small and inclusion is phased at 50 per cent in December 2026 and 100 per cent in June 2027, the firm expects the near-term flow impact to be more stock-specific than market-wide. "The FBM70 will be reduced to 50 constituents and renamed FBM Mid-cap Index on Dec 21 while the FBM100 remains unchanged. "Derivatives specifications remain unchanged, while FTSE Russell is reviewing a relaxation of the fast-entry threshold for large initial public offerings," it said. CIMB Securities expects details to be reflected in an updated FTSE Bursa Malaysia Index Series Ground Rules notice once finalised at the end of this month. "Key dates to watch are the Nov 23, 2026 ranking cut-off, Dec 3, 2026 constituent announcement and Dec 21, 2026 first-stage inclusion, with full inclusion on June 21, 2027," it added.

title: 'Sektor teknologi dan industri jadi tumpuan selepas FBM KLCI diperluas kepada 50 kaunter - CIMB Securities | DagangNews - Berita Bisnes Anda
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 8 Sept — Sektor teknologi dan perindustrian berpotensi meraih banyak perhatian pelabur selepas indeks penanda aras FBM KLCI diperluas daripada 30 kepada 50 kaunter, serta mengurangkan dominasi sektor kewangan dan utiliti dalam indeks utama Bursa Malaysia, menurut CIMB Securities. Firma penyelidikan itu berkata pertambahan tersebut dijangka meningkatkan kepelbagaian sektor dengan memberikan bahagian perwakilan yang lebih besar kepada sektor perindustrian, teknologi, barangan pengguna pilihan, tenaga, hartanah dan barangan pengguna asas. Perubahan tersebut dilihat positif dari sudut struktur pasaran kerana FBM KLCI yang lebih pelbagai berpeluang menjadi penanda aras mencerminkan keseluruhan ekonomi Malaysia, selain meluaskan pilihan pendedahan pelabur institusi di luar kelompok syarikat bermodal besar sedia ada. "Simulasi terdahulu dilaksanakan kami menganggarkan 20 kaunter baharu itu boleh mewakili kira-kira 15.6% daripada FBM KLCI yang diperluaskan apabila penyertaan penuh dicapai," jelas CIMB Securities dalam nota analisisnya. Menurut firma berkenaan lagi, perluasan tersebut dijangka mengurangkan pemberat sektor kewangan dan utiliti, manakala sektor teknologi serta perindustrian antara segmen yang dilihat sebagai berpotensi mendapat perwakilan lebih besar dalam indeks berkenaan. Bagaimanapun ujarnya, impak aliran dana dalam tempoh terdekat dijangka lebih bersifat khusus kepada kaunter tertentu berbanding keseluruhan pasaran, memandangkan saiz aset di bawah pengurusan pasif yang menjejaki FBM KLCI masih relatif kecil. Kesan tersebut juga kata CIMB Securities, tidak akan berlaku secara mendadak kerana kemasukan kaunter baharu bakal dilaksanakan secara berperingkat, iaitu kira-kira 50% pada Disember 2026 sebelum mencapai penyertaan penuh 100% pada Jun 2027. "Pihak pengurusan FTSE sendiri sudah menjelaskan bahawa permodalan pasaran penuh akan digunakan bagi menentukan pemilihan akhir kaunter, manakala kaedah 'free float' atau pengapungan bebas akan menentukan pemberat setiap saham dalam indeks," tambahnya. Dalam perkembangan berkaitan, FBM70 akan dikurangkan kepada 50 kaunter dan dinamakan semula sebagai FBM Mid Cap Index mulai 21 Disember 2026, sementara FBM100 masih lagi dikekalkan tanpa sebarang perubahan jumlah kaunter didagangkan. Spesifikasi derivatif juga jelas CIMB Securities, adalahtidak berubah, manakala FTSE Russell sedang mengkaji kemungkinan untuk melonggarkan ambang kemasukan pantas bagi tawaran awam permulaan (IPO) yang bermodal saiz besar. Justeru, firma penyelidikan tersebut menjangkakan butiran lanjut mengenai perubahan struktur itu akan dimasukkan dalam kemas kini 'FTSE Bursa Malaysia Index Series Ground Rules' selepas dimuktamadkan pada akhir September 2026. Secara keseluruhan, ia kekal positif kerana perluasan itu berpotensi menjadikan FBM KLCI lebih pelbagai, sekali gus memberi ruang lebih besar kepada sektor teknologi dan industri dalam penanda aras utama pasaran saham Malaysia.

title: 'Passwords no longer supported: CIMB Bank only accepts biometrics or passcode for SecureTAC approvals from 19 September
body: 'CIMB Bank will officially phase out password verification for SecureTAC approvals on CIMB Clicks Web and online merchant transactions starting 19 September 2026.  Under this new security mandate, all web transfers and online card payments must be authenticated exclusively through the CIMB OCTO mobile app.  Users will now be required to verify their identity using biometrics such as Face ID and fingerprint scanning, or their custom 6 digit OCTO App passcode.  Why is CIMB removing password verification?  CIMB states that removing password verification within the OCTO app aims to strengthen security and protect accounts against unauthorised access and fraud.  In line with industry security standards, web transactions will no longer accept traditional account passwords for SecureTAC approvals.  Once the policy takes effect, every web purchase or Clicks Web transaction will strictly require Face ID, fingerprint scanning, or your personal 6 digit OCTO App passcode.  How online transaction approvals will work  Initiating a payment on Clicks Web or a merchant site will trigger a SecureTAC push notification to your primary phone.  Tapping the notification or manually opening the SecureTAC menu in the OCTO app displays the transaction details.  Upon selecting “Approve”, the app prompts for your phone security credentials, where a quick facial scan, fingerprint check, or your set OCTO App passcode completes the verification.  What happens if security is turned off?  For users who do not have biometrics or an in-app passcode enabled on the OCTO app, web transfers will fail.  You can still initiate a transaction on the web portal and receive the push notification on your phone.  However, selecting Approve in the app will trigger an immediate error stating that security is not set up, rejecting the payment until you configure biometrics or a passcode inside the OCTO app settings.  OCTO App passcode acts as the primary backup for biometrics  If your fingerprint scanner glitches or your front camera fails, your custom 6-digit OCTO App passcode serves as the primary fallback option.  This is the personal PIN configured directly inside the OCTO app settings rather than your phone screen lock or main Clicks password.  If you cancel the prompt or enter an incorrect passcode multiple times, the app displays an error message before closing and rejecting the web payment.  Account safety and self service troubleshooting  CIMB reassures customers that failed SecureTAC attempts will not lock your CIMB Clicks ID, nor will any funds be deducted from your account.  If a transaction fails, the recommended troubleshooting step is to ensure your OCTO app security settings are properly configured and retry the payment on Clicks Web.  The bank advises customers to contact their support centre only if approval issues persist after making a second attempt.

title: 'CIMB sees rising odds of BNM rate hike in 1H27
body: 'BANK Negara Malaysia (BNM) is expected to keep the Overnight Policy Rate (OPR) unchanged at 2.75% in November, although the probability of a rate hike in the first half of 2027 is increasing if economic growth remains firm and inflation pressures broaden, according to CIMB Treasury and Markets Research.   “We expect a hold in November, but see rising odds of a 25bps rate hike in 1H27 if growth stays firm and inflation broadens,” CIMB said in a report released today.   The research house viewed BNM’s Sept 3 monetary policy statement as carrying a hawkish tilt, pointing to the removal of the word “appropriate” from its description of the prevailing monetary policy stance, alongside the central bank’s increased vigilance over commodity-driven cost pressures.

title: 'El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities
body: 'El Niño could worsen Malaysia’s power, water stress, says CIMB Securities KUALA LUMPUR (Sept 7): Hotter and drier conditions from El Niño could put greater pressure on Malaysia’s electricity and water systems into 2027, according to CIMB Securities. The research house said El Niño is expected to persist into early 2027 and peak between March and May, potentially lifting electricity demand for cooling while worsening water shortages. It said Malaysia is particularly exposed as electricity demand is already rising, while about 37% of treated water is lost through non-revenue water (NRW). “Hotter and drier conditions could further strain both systems, strengthening the need for cooling efficiency, water conservation, and better infrastructure management,” CIMB said. Malaysia’s peak electricity demand is projected to increase to 33.5 gigawatts (GW) by 2035 from 21.3GW in 2026, while data centres could account for 31% of Peninsular Malaysia’s electricity demand by then. CIMB said hotter weather could further increase cooling demand across commercial buildings, industrial facilities and data centres, adding to the country’s underlying electricity load growth. On the water side, Malaysia’s NRW rate remained high at 37.1% in 2024, meaning more than one-third of treated water was lost before reaching consumers. The losses are estimated to cost more than RM2 billion annually. Water stress is already visible in some areas, with two of the 49 dams monitored nationwide at critical levels as at Aug 31, namely the Muda Dam in Kedah and Sungai Pagar Dam in Labuan. CIMB said the government’s RM2.5 billion National NRW Programme and RM1.7 billion allocation under the 13th Malaysia Plan to replace about 1,800km of critical water pipes should support efforts to improve water efficiency. The research house named KJTS Group Bhd (KL:KJTS) and Insights Analytics Bhd (KL:IAB) as its preferred beneficiaries of the theme. KJTS offers direct exposure to rising cooling demand through its cooling energy and energy-efficiency businesses, while Insights Analytics provides digital water solutions including leak detection, pressure management and smart metering. CIMB maintained “buy” calls on both companies, with target prices of RM1.35 for KJTS and RM1.95 for Insights Analytics. The content is a snapshot from Publisher.
