title: 'Penang’s draft plan could open more of its hills to building
body: 'Kam Suan Pheng and Evelyn Teh “Rising from the sea in that first light of dawn that touches reality with a gentle charm, the Penang hills provide an unforgettable landmark for the visitor sailing in by sea. From the palm-fringed bays as yet a black indistinguishable smudge, the eye follows the flowing silhouette of the hills.” – Margaret Khor, The Straits Times Annual, 1960. Ask anyone who has crossed on the ferry, or driven over the bridge at dusk, and they will say the same: that green line of hills is how you know you are home. That silhouette is part of what makes Penang, Penang. Beyond the scenery, the hills are part of the island’s natural public infrastructure – one that is rarely counted. They hold soil, absorb and direct water, support forests and wildlife, and shape the landscape where we and our ancestors have lived. That landscape could change significantly if the draft State Structure Plan 2040 is adopted without stronger safeguards for hill and slope development. First, some background. The current Penang State Structure Plan 2030 does not allow development on land 76 metres (250 feet) or more above sea level, or on slopes of 25 degrees or steeper. There are limited exceptions for infrastructure and utilities. The limit is stricter than the national guideline. The state set it because it recognised how fragile, and how important, the island’s hills are. - Sign up for Aliran's free daily email updates or weekly newsletters or both - Make a one-off donation to Persatuan Aliran Kesedaran Negara (ALIRAN), Maybank a/c 507246118995 or CIMB a/c 8004240948 - Make a regular pledge or periodic auto-donation to Aliran - Become an Aliran member The 2030 plan reads: Sebarang Pembangunan Perbandaran Yang Meliputi Pembangunan Skim Perumahan Perhotelan Resort Perdagangan Perindustrian Dan Sebarang Struktur Bangunan Footprint Tidak Dibenarkan Di Kawasan:- - Kawasan Tanah Tinggi Yang Diwartakan Di Bawah Akta Pemeliharaan Tanah 1960 Akta 385 Atau - Sebarang Tanah Yang Berada Pada Aras 76 meter 250 kaki) Ke Atas Atau - Kawasan Berkecerunan 25 Darjah Ke Atas KECUALI Bagi Pemajuan Infrastruktur Dan Utiliti Dibenarkan Dengan Syarat Syarat Dari Jabatan Teknikal Yang Berkaitan Dan Mendapat Kelulusan Dari Pihak Berkuasa Negeri. In English: Any urban development, including housing schemes, hotels, resorts, commercial or industrial developments, and any building structures, is prohibited in the following areas: - Highland areas gazetted under the Land Conservation Act 1960 (Act 385); or - Any land situated at an elevation of 76 metres (250 feet) or higher; or - Areas with a slope gradient of 25 degrees or steeper; EXCEPT for infrastructure and utility developments, which are permitted subject to conditions imposed by relevant technical departments and approval from the State Authority. The key concern The state government rolled out a new draft 2040 plan in August – years before 2030 arrives. It will overwrite the previous version. The draft 2040 plan says: Strategi Perancangan PS3-1: Pembangunan di Kawasan Khusus yang Melebihi Ketinggian 76 meter. Strategi ini merupakan pendekatan perancangan yang memberi kelonggaran kawalan ketinggian bangunan secara terpilih di kawasan khas yang telah dikenal pasti sebagai kawasan tumpuan pembangunan strategik. Pelaksanaan strategi ini bertujuan mengoptimumkan penggunaan tanah yang terhad melalui pembangunan berintensiti tinggi dan berorientasikan transit, khususnya di pusat bandar, koridor ekonomi dan kawasan pesisir yang mempunyai kapasiti infrastruktur mencukupi. Walau bagaimanapun, kebenaran ini tertakluk kepada penilaian teknikal terperinci seperti kesesuaian guna tanah, nisbah plot, kawalan kepadatan, impak trafik, keselamatan, impak visual serta pematuhan kepada garis panduan reka bentuk bandar dan kajian impak alam sekitar. In English: Planning Strategy PS3-1: Development in Special Areas Exceeding a Height of 76 Metres. This strategy is a planning approach that allows for selective flexibility regarding building height controls in specific areas identified as strategic development hubs. Its implementation aims to optimize limited land use through high-intensity, transit-oriented development, particularly in city centres, economic corridors and coastal areas with adequate infrastructure capacity. However, such approval is subject to detailed technical assessments covering aspects such as land-use suitability, plot ratio, density controls, traffic impact, safety, visual impact, and compliance with urban design guidelines and environmental impact studies. In plain terms, the 2040 draft swaps ‘don’t build there’ (in the 2030 plan) for ‘build there if the paperwork says it’s safe’. The 2030 plan took a precautionary approach: keep away from the risk altogether. The 2040 draft replaces it with case-by-case approval, where each project’s own technical studies decide whether a hill can take it. Are these adequate safeguards, or is this a problem waiting to happen? Why change the limit? The threshold of 76m above sea level was not arbitrary. It was a deliberate safeguard that Penang chose to keep. Penang had adopted stricter controls than the national KSAS (environmentally sensitive areas) elevation framework, which it is now reverting to. The Safety Guideline for Hillsite Development (second edition, 2020) says Penang Island covers roughly 285 sq km. About 40% of it is Class 3 and Class 4 land, with slopes steeper than 25 degrees. The first version of the guideline went further. It reduced the footprint of buildings on hill land to make slopes safer and keep more green areas. Now these precautions are set aside. The 2040 draft presents this as a development strategy, not as a finding that the 76m limit is irrelevant. Outside the draft, no new evidence, assessment or policy review shows that the precautionary approach is no longer needed. What evidence, then, supports such a significant change in risk management? Look closely at the numbers. The highest point in Penang is 833m above sea level, but the horizontal area of the hills is small. The slopes are therefore compressed into a limited range of height and width. Add the complex pattern of hills and ridges, and very few pockets of land are flat enough to build on without cutting into the surrounding slopes. Even if building is allowed on isolated pockets, the roads needed to reach them must cross steeper terrain. Their environmental impact will reach far beyond the site. We do not have to imagine what that looks like. In October 2017, a landslide at a construction site in Tanjung Bungah killed 11 workers. A year later, part of a ‘paired road’ at Bukit Kukus collapsed during construction, killing nine. Bukit Kukus was a road, exactly the kind of infrastructure the 2030 plan already allowed as an exception. If the exception alone could cost so many lives, what happens when the rule itself is lifted? This is probably why past planners chose the 76m (250ft) limit. That wisdom applies even more today, as climate change brings heavier and more frequent rain to fragile hills. And what happens on the hill does not stay on the hill. These slopes feed the Air Itam and Teluk Bahang dams that fill our taps. When forests can no longer hold the rain, it runs down into lowland streets as flash floods. One does not need to live on a hill to pay for what happens on one. Paperwork is not landscape planning Some may argue that a technical assessment before approval is a reasonable safeguard. It can tell us whether a project meets existing standards. These include the Penang Safety Guideline for Hill Site Development 2020, the EIA Guidelines for Development in Slope and Hill Areas issued by the Department of Environment, and the planning and management guide for environmentally sensitive areas by PLANMalaysia. But none of these answers the bigger question: how many projects can these hills absorb before the whole system gives way? The 2040 draft says hill development control is strengthened through risk assessment, including the environment’s carrying capacity and climate resilience. Any development on hill land between 300 and 1,200 metres, or between 150 and 300 metres, and on slopes above 25 degrees, must submit a geotechnical risk assessment and a climate risk assessment. However, we know of no publicly accessible study or official database that gathers the information needed as a baseline. This should be established before the first hill or slope proposal is submitted. It seems the draft simply adopted a guideline written for the highlands of the peninsula – not one drawn up for Penang island. Could we, or should we? With today’s engineering, there are many ways to stabilise a slope: retaining walls, modern drainage, soil nails, piles and engineered slopes. A project may well be shown to be safe on paper. But the natural slope will have been substantially altered. Its long-term safety then rests on things no approval can guarantee. These include construction quality, drainage maintenance, inspection, the capacity and funding of the agencies responsible, extreme weather and future changes in land use. The irony is that a retaining wall is only as safe as the last time someone cleared its drains. There is also no baseline of existing conditions or of the role the hills play. That role covers the watershed, ecological corridors, natural drainage and geological formations. Penang lacks a hill and slope master plan that understands how sensitive and connected the hills are. Only such a plan can properly define, map and measure the hills’ carrying capacity, including projected climate scenarios. So the question shifts. We could make hill and slope development safe. But should we, and at what cost, when we have no baseline data and no guarantee these projects will stay safe in the long term? A project being technically safe is not the same as the landscape being safe. Gazette first, assess later When a gazetted state structure plan marks an area as potentially developable, the effects ripple out quickly. Land values rise, investors form expectations, land changes hands, proposals are drawn up and contracts are signed. All of this happens long before any environmental impact or technical assessment is complete. That order of events tilts the outcome. Once money and contracts are committed, rejecting a project on environmental grounds carries legal and financial consequences. The seemingly rational way out is to reduce every risk to an ‘acceptable’ level and hope nothing goes wrong later. The assessment no longer decides whether to build, only how. Show us the evidence The 2040 draft marks a significant shift from precautionary restriction towards risk-based conditional development. That may be reasonable in some circumstances. But the draft must show why the previous limits are no longer needed. It must also explain how project-by-project checks will deal with risks that build up across the landscape, worsen with climate change and cannot be undone once a hill is cut. If Penang is deliberately moving beyond the precautionary framework to create more development opportunities, it should show us the evidence. That means the thresholds and landscape-level safeguards that justify the change, in the form of a hill and slope development master plan, published before the 2040 plan is gazetted, not after. In the end, for most of us, this is not really a debate about slope angles, geotechnical reports or even the state structure plan. It is about the hills we know, some of us since childhood. These are the hills we see from our windows, or on the drive home after a long day at work. On them lie the green trails we climb at weekends to take in the view of our beloved Penang from above. It is also about feeling safe when the torrential rain comes. Can we sleep soundly knowing the hills near us will keep doing what they have always done: holding the soil, soaking up the water and slowing the runoff before it reaches our neighbourhoods? Or will we rely more and more on concrete walls and drains to protect us from hills we ourselves have altered? Dr Kam Suan Pheng is a soil scientist and co-founder of Penang Hills Watch, with a doctorate in agronomy-soil from Cornell University. Evelyn Teh is a Penang-based public policy researcher and environmental scientist specialising in ecological management, climate change and urban studies. The views expressed in Aliran's media statements and the NGO statements we have endorsed reflect Aliran's official stand. Views and opinions expressed in other pieces published here do not necessarily reflect Aliran's official position.

title: 'Fire safety managers, officers mandatory for 9,451 buildings from April 2027
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). "From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises," he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce the department's workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. "In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by the department for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year," he said. To meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, the department expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide, he said. He said the fire department currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony.

title: 'Mandat Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran Bomba bagi 9,451 Bangunan Tonjolkan Permintaan Pematuhan untuk Unique Fire
body: 'Langkah Malaysia menjadikan pemilik bangunan bertanggungjawab secara langsung terhadap keselamatan kebakaran dijangka meluaskan pasaran pematuhan bagi pembekal perlindungan kebakaran, sekali gus meletakkan Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) antara syarikat yang berpotensi mendapat manfaat. Mulai 1 April 2027, pemilik 9,451 bangunan yang ditetapkan di bawah Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba akan diwajibkan melantik Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSM) dan Pegawai Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSO), serta menubuhkan Organisasi Keselamatan Kebakaran (OKK) di premis masing-masing. Ketua Pengarah Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM), Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad berkata, keperluan itu selaras dengan Seksyen 27A Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025. Menurut beliau, mana-mana bangunan yang diperiksa dalam tempoh satu hingga dua tahun akan datang dan diwajibkan memiliki Perakuan Bomba perlu melaksanakan struktur baharu tersebut. Beliau berkata demikian selepas melancarkan program FSM dan FSO di Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur pada 6 Oktober 2026, di mana kumpulan pertama seramai 174 FSM dan 324 FSO menerima sijil masing-masing. Perubahan utama melibatkan kaedah pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba. Selepas ini, JBPM akan menilai laporan pemeriksaan tahunan yang disediakan oleh FSM bagi tujuan pembaharuan perakuan, tanpa perlu menjalankan pemeriksaan fizikal ke atas setiap bangunan setiap tahun. JBPM kini mempunyai 13 penyedia latihan berdaftar dan telah mengeluarkan tender bagi menambah bilangan penyedia latihan serta jurulatih. Tanggungjawab pematuhan beralih kepada pemilik bangunan Rangka kerja ini memindahkan tanggungjawab keselamatan kebakaran harian daripada pihak berkuasa kepada pemilik bangunan dan kakitangan dalaman mereka yang bertauliah. Di bawah program ini, FSM menjalani kursus lima hari merangkumi pemeriksaan bangunan, perancangan pemindahan, pelaporan dan penyelenggaraan, manakala FSO menjalani kursus teknikal selama tiga hari. Dengan FSM bertanggungjawab ke atas laporan tahunan yang menjadi asas pembaharuan Perakuan Bomba, pemilik bangunan dijangka memberi penekanan lebih besar untuk memastikan alat pemadam api, gelung hos, pili bomba, sistem pemercik, peranti pengesan dan penggera serta sistem pemadaman kebakaran sentiasa berfungsi dengan baik. Ini menunjukkan permintaan yang lebih stabil bagi penggantian, penyelenggaraan dan pengisian semula peralatan di seluruh 9,451 premis yang ditetapkan, termasuk bangunan berpenghuni tinggi dan berisiko tinggi. Unique Fire, yang ditubuhkan pada 1997 dan beribu pejabat di Shah Alam, Selangor, terlibat dalam pemasangan, pembuatan dan pengedaran sistem, peralatan dan aksesori perlindungan kebakaran aktif untuk persekitaran terbina. Rangkaian produknya merangkumi alat pemadam api mudah alih, gelung hos, sistem pili bomba dan pemercik, sistem paip naik basah dan kering, peranti pengesan dan penggera kebakaran, serta sistem pemadaman kebakaran termasuk sistem kimia basah dan karbon dioksida. Kumpulan memasarkan produk di bawah jenama sendiri iaitu Unique, Unique227, Yama dan Commander, di samping jenama pihak ketiga seperti Kidde, serta menyediakan perkhidmatan penyelenggaraan peralatan perlindungan kebakaran dan mesin pengisian semula alat pemadam api kimia kering. Kumpulan telah pun mengenal pasti akta yang dipinda itu sebagai pemacu permintaan. Bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 31 Mac 2026, hasil Unique Fire meningkat 6.2% kepada RM114.7 juta, disokong oleh jualan pemasangan dan pengedaran yang lebih kukuh, terutamanya sistem pemadaman kebakaran. Pengarah Eksekutif, Marcus Liew berkata perniagaan teras perlindungan kebakaran terus berkembang dalam persekitaran kawal selia yang menyokong, dipacu oleh penguatkuasaan Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba (Pindaan) 2025 serta pelaksanaan projek di bawah Rancangan Malaysia Ketiga Belas, dan Kumpulan menjangkakan permintaan yang berterusan hasil keperluan pematuhan peraturan dan penganugerahan kontrak yang sedang berjalan. Kumpulan turut meluaskan jangkauan ke luar negara melalui Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, usaha sama 60:40 dengan Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd untuk mengeluar dan membekalkan pemercik kebakaran, dengan Shanghai Mosafe menyediakan sokongan teknikal ke arah pensijilan Underwriters Laboratories (UL). Dengan keperluan FSM dan FSO berkuat kuasa dalam tempoh kurang enam bulan lagi, rejim pematuhan baharu ini dijangka mengubah keselamatan kebakaran daripada pemeriksaan sekali setahun kepada tanggungjawab berterusan bagi pemilik bangunan, satu peralihan yang selari dengan tawaran produk dan perkhidmatan Unique Fire.

title: 'Bomba’s Fire Safety Manager Mandate for 9,451 Buildings Puts Compliance Demand in Focus for Unique Fire
body: 'Malaysia’s move to make building owners directly accountable for fire safety is set to widen the compliance market for fire protection suppliers, placing Unique Fire Holdings Berhad (“Unique Fire”) among the companies positioned to benefit. From 1 April 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint a Fire Safety Manager (FSM) and a Fire Safety Officer (FSO), and to establish a Fire Safety Organisation at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement is in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025. Nor Hisham said any building inspected over the next one to two years that is required to hold a Fire Certificate will have to put the new structure in place. He was speaking after launching the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank in Kuala Lumpur on 6 October 2026, where the first cohort of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs received their certificates. A key change lies in how Fire Certificates will be renewed. Going forward, JBPM will assess annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs for certificate renewal, instead of physically inspecting every building each year. JBPM currently has 13 registered training providers and has issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. Compliance shifts to building owners The framework transfers day-to-day fire safety responsibility from the authorities to building owners and their certified in-house personnel. Under the programme, FSMs undergo a five-day course covering building inspections, evacuation planning, reporting and maintenance, while FSOs complete a three-day technical course. With a certified FSM accountable for an annual report that underpins Fire Certificate renewal, building owners are expected to place greater emphasis on keeping fire extinguishers, hose reels, hydrants, sprinkler systems, detection and alarm devices and suppression systems in working order. This points to steadier demand for equipment replacement, servicing and refilling across the 9,451 designated premises, which include high-occupancy and high-risk buildings. Unique Fire, established in 1997 and headquartered in Shah Alam, Selangor, assembles, manufactures and distributes active fire protection systems, equipment and accessories for the built environment. Its range spans hand portable fire extinguishers, fire hose reels, hydrant and sprinkler systems, wet and dry riser systems, fire detection and alarm devices, and fire suppression systems including wet chemical and carbon dioxide systems. The Group markets products under its own Unique, Unique227, Yama and Commander brands alongside third-party brands such as Kidde, and also provides fire protection equipment servicing and dry chemical fire extinguisher refilling machines. The Group has already identified the amended Act as a demand driver. For the financial year ended 31 March 2026, Unique Fire’s revenue rose 6.2% to RM114.7 million, supported by stronger assembly and distribution sales, particularly of fire suppression systems. Executive Director Marcus Liew said the core fire protection business continued to grow amid a supportive regulatory environment, backed by enforcement of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025 and project rollouts under the 13th Malaysia Plan, and that the Group expects sustained demand driven by regulatory compliance requirements and ongoing contract awards. The Group is also extending its reach beyond Malaysia through Unique Mosafe Sdn Bhd, a 60:40 joint venture with Shanghai Mosafe Equipment Co Ltd to manufacture and supply fire sprinklers, with Shanghai Mosafe providing technical support towards Underwriters Laboratories (UL) certification. With the FSM and FSO requirement taking effect in less than six months, the new compliance regime is set to move fire safety from a once-a-year inspection exercise to a continuous obligation for building owners, a shift that plays directly into Unique Fire’s product and service offering.

title: 'VIB hoàn tất khoản vay quốc tế 285 triệu USD trong kế hoạch 1 tỉ USD
body: 'Ngân hàng Quốc Tế Việt Nam (VIB) đã hoàn tất khoản vay hợp vốn trị giá 285 triệu USD từ chín định chế tài chính tại châu Á.  Chi phí vốn cạnh tranh, mở rộng đối tác quốc tế  Giao dịch trên được đồng thu xếp bởi United Overseas Bank Limited (UOB), Maybank Securities Pte. Ltd. và Cathay United Bank Co., Ltd. Ba ngân hàng này cùng China Construction Bank Corporation giữ vai trò ngân hàng thu xếp chính và dựng sổ. Năm định chế tài chính quốc tế khác cũng tham gia cấp vốn. Khoản vay được giải ngân thành ba đợt trong năm 2026.  Với kỳ hạn 3 năm, chi phí vốn của khoản vay thấp hơn khoảng 30 điểm cơ bản so với khoản vay hợp vốn trước đó. Nguồn vốn này bổ sung kỳ hạn trung hạn, đồng thời giúp ngân hàng đa dạng hóa cơ cấu huy động.  Giao dịch có sự tham gia của bảy đối tác từng thực hiện các khoản vay hợp vốn trước đây và hai đối tác mới. Việc có thêm đối tác mới cho thấy ngân hàng tiếp tục mở rộng quan hệ với các định chế tài chính quốc tế trong bối cảnh thị trường tài chính toàn cầu còn nhiều biến động.  Bà Lee Chin Hwoi, Giám đốc Bộ phận Tài trợ Vốn vay, Khối Ngân hàng Đầu tư Tập đoàn UOB, cho biết giao dịch thể hiện sự hợp tác giữa hai bên và kỳ vọng vào triển vọng phát triển dài hạn của ngân hàng. Trong bối cảnh các định chế tài chính trong khu vực đang tìm cách đa dạng hóa nguồn vốn và tăng cường khả năng chống chịu của bảng cân đối, UOB tiếp tục kết nối khách hàng với nguồn vốn toàn cầu và các cơ hội tăng trưởng bền vững.  Chủ động nguồn vốn quốc tế cho chiến lược tăng trưởng  Khoản vay 285 triệu USD nằm trong kế hoạch huy động 1 tỉ USD nguồn vốn trung và dài hạn từ thị trường quốc tế của VIB trong năm 2026. Ngân hàng đang tiếp tục làm việc với các đối tác để triển khai những giao dịch tiếp theo.  Tổng số dư vốn huy động nước ngoài, gồm cả ngắn hạn và trung, dài hạn, hiện đạt 1,6 tỉ USD và dự kiến tăng lên 2 tỉ USD vào năm 2027.  Ông Hàn Ngọc Vũ, Tổng giám đốc VIB, cho biết ngân hàng tập trung vào chi phí vốn, kỳ hạn và sự đa dạng của các đối tác trong kế hoạch mở rộng nguồn vốn quốc tế trong năm nay. Việc bổ sung các nguồn vốn mới nhằm tăng tính chủ động trong quản trị thanh khoản và cân đối kỳ hạn giữa nguồn vốn với nhu cầu sử dụng vốn.  Nguồn vốn trung và dài hạn từ thị trường quốc tế cũng giúp đa dạng hóa các kênh huy động bên cạnh tiền gửi khách hàng và nguồn vốn trong nước.  Chi phí vốn cạnh tranh giúp ngân hàng chủ động hơn trong quản lý chi phí và cơ cấu nguồn vốn, từ đó hỗ trợ hiệu quả hoạt động và phát triển các giải pháp tín dụng phù hợp với nhu cầu khách hàng.  Nguồn vốn từ khoản vay hợp vốn vừa hoàn tất góp phần đáp ứng nhu cầu tín dụng của khách hàng cá nhân, doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa cùng các khách hàng doanh nghiệp khác, phù hợp với định hướng kinh doanh và quản trị rủi ro của ngân hàng.  Trong quý II-2026, ngân hàng triển khai chương trình tín dụng ưu đãi quy mô 15.000 tỉ đồng, với lãi suất từ 8%/năm, dành cho doanh nghiệp nhỏ và vừa, doanh nghiệp sản xuất, xuất nhập khẩu và các đơn vị tham gia chuỗi cung ứng.  Với khách hàng cá nhân, ngân hàng cung cấp các khoản vay mua nhà với lựa chọn cố định lãi suất đến 5 năm, giúp người vay chủ động tính toán chi phí tài chính.  Bên cạnh việc mở rộng nguồn vốn quốc tế, ngân hàng tiếp tục củng cố vốn tự có. Vốn điều lệ đạt 37.354 tỉ đồng sau khi hoàn tất phát hành hơn 323 triệu cổ phiếu để trả cổ tức với tỉ lệ 9,5%. Đến cuối quý II-2026, dư nợ tín dụng đạt gần 400.000 tỉ đồng, trong khi lợi nhuận trước thuế 6 tháng đầu năm đạt hơn 5.180 tỉ đồng.  Việc tăng vốn tự có và bổ sung nguồn vốn trung, dài hạn giúp ngân hàng có thêm nguồn lực đáp ứng nhu cầu tín dụng, đồng thời tăng khả năng chủ động trong quản trị thanh khoản và kiểm soát rủi ro. title: '马股闭市微升1.60点  顶级手套飙11.46% - 财经 - 即时财经
body: '马股闭市微升1.60点 顶级手套飙11.46% （吉隆坡6日讯）中东石油出口增加，促使国际油价回落，带动区域股市普遍上涨，马股周二盘中曾升至1641.20点，上升9.45点，可惜午盘之后回吐部分涨幅，最终只升1.60点，以1633.35点挂收。 反映大盘走势的富时全股指数上扬42.52点，至12232.87点，创业板指数也起52.31点，至5658.92点。  其他马股各大指数普遍上涨，当中科技和医疗保健指数涨势凌厉，全日猛涨超过3%，金融服务、产业和交通物流指数下跌介于0.08%至0.38%。 全场股项涨多跌少，有667只上升股，超过456只下跌股，另有551只平盘。全场有41亿7664万1900股，总值29亿4950万1489令吉。 综指成分股方面，上升、下跌和平盘各报14只、14只和2只。 上涨的综指股包括国油化学（PCHEM,5183,主板工业产品服务组）起17仙，至4令吉30仙；IHH医保（IHH,5225,主板医疗保健组)涨15仙，收于7令吉91仙；森牙直利（SDG,5285,主板种植组)升10仙，至6令吉12仙。 银行股表现逊色，大众银行（PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组)下跌4仙，收报4令吉67仙；马来亚银行（MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组)和联昌集团（CIMB,1023,主板金融服务组)各降3仙，分别跌至9令吉97仙和7令吉70仙。 顶级手套（TOPGLOV,7113,主板医疗保健组)第四季业绩亮眼，加上派发每股1.5仙终期股息，驱动股价午盘走势越战越勇，收盘上扬9仙或11.46%，至87.5仙，并以1亿6513万3800股的成交量，位居热门榜亚军。 近期跌跌不休的ZETRIX公司(ZETRIX,0138,主板科技组) 周二止跌回扬，闭市上涨2.5仙或38.46%，至9仙，成交量高达9亿6279万零400股，冲上热门榜榜首。 国际油价回落，以及美国科技股走稳，带动全球股市普遍上涨。 美国隔夜股市3大指数全面收高，收盘时，道琼斯工商指数起0.18%，标普500指数升0.66%，纳斯达克综指涨至历史新高，收盘上扬1.05%。 亚太股市大部分走高，印尼雅加达综指上涨1.21%，日本日经指数起1.05%，香港恒生指数上扬1.00%，台湾加权指数上升0.22%，新加坡海峡时报指数起0.40%，泰国曼谷综指升0.37%。 不过，菲律宾马尼拉综指和韩国首尔综指各跌1.15%和0.89%。中国股市今天休市。 马币方面，联储局升息的概率增加，带动美元指数走高，马币兑美元和新元双双下滑。 根据《彭博社》行情，马币兑美元全日游走于4.0848至4.0880之间，截至下午5时报4.0852，周一收于4.0845；马币兑新元全日在3.1915至3.1968之间徘徊，截至下午5时收报3.1951，低于周一的3.1941。 棕油需求增加，带动大马衍生产品交易所12月指标期货上扬4令吉，至每公吨4582令吉。  热门新闻 百格视频

title: 'Siapa Hijjas Kasturi? Tokoh Sebalik Mercu Tanda Di Malaysia
body: 'Siapa Hijjas Kasturi? Tokoh Sebalik Mercu Tanda Di Malaysia Beliau turut membina mercu tanda seperti Menara Maybank, Menara Telekom, Shahzan Tower dan lain-lain. - Hijjas Kasturi, bapa seni bina moden Malaysia, mencipta bangunan ikonik yang mencerminkan identiti budaya dan Islam negara. - Karya terkenalnya termasuk Menara Tabung Haji, Menara MBPJ, dan PICC, setiap satunya menggabungkan elemen tradisional Melayu. Jangan lupa follow channel Telegram TRPbm untuk ketahui updates semasa & relevan! Pemandangan ibu kota Kuala Lumpur dipenuhi dengan pelbagai bangunan dan pencakar langit yang mempunyai identiti, cita rasa serta seni bina tersendiri menghasilkan rupa unik. Namun, ramai tidak sedar bahawa di sebalik beberapa bangunan menghiasi ibu kota, terdapat satu nama yang sama. Nama tersebut ialah Hijjas Kasturi, seorang tokoh yang digelar sebagai bapa seni bina moden Malaysia. Sehingga kini, karyanya bukan sahaja menghiasi landskap negara, malah menjadi inspirasi kepada ramai generasi muda. Bermula Di Singapura Pada Tahun 1936 Hijjas Kasturi dilahirkan di Singapura pada 26 September 1936. Ibunya berketurunan Cina telah berkahwin dengan seorang lelaki berketurunan Jawa-Singapura. Beliau mendapat pendidikan di Raffles Institution, sebelum menerima biasiswa dari Kerajaan Australia untuk menyambung pelajaran. Menariknya, Hijjas telah mula belajar di University of Adelaide, sebelum menjadi graduan daripada University of Melbourne. Pada tahun 1967, Hijjas berpindah ke Malaysia dan mengasaskan program ijazah profesional pertama di negara ini, iaitu School of Art and Architecture di Institut Teknologi MARA (ITM). Bermula Sebagai Seorang Pelukis Pelan Perjalanan kerjaya Hijjas bermula seawal tahun 1956 sebagai seorang Draughtsman bersama Singapore Housing Trust. Dia bertanggungjawab untuk menyediakan master plan bagi kawasan Queenstown dan rumah apartment kos rendah. Kemudian, kerjayanya berkembang merentasi dua buah negara menerusi beberapa jawatan penting seperti: - 1959: Menyertai South Australian Housing Trust, menyediakan master plan Elizabeth Town dan skim perumahan. - 1961: Menjadi Pembantu Seni Bina dengan Brown & Davis yang terlibat dalam perancangan hospital, bangunan komersial dan perumahan. - 1965: Menjadi arkitek dengan Hume Proprietary Ltd, Melbourne bertanggungjawab merancang pembinaan kilang, gudang dan pejabat. - 1966: Kembali semula ke Singapura sebagai Arkitek / Perancang dengan Housing and Development Board (HDB). Hijjas turut mengetuai pasukan kajian penubuhan ITM dan menjadi Ketua Pengasas School of Art and Architecture. Pada tahun 1969, Hijjas menjadi rakan kongsi pengasas Arkitek Bersekutu, sebelum akhirnya menubuhkan firma sendiri, iaitu Hijjas Kasturi Associates Sdn (HKAS). Proses Mencari Identiti Seni Bina Melambangkan Malaysia Bagi Hijjas, seni bina bukan sekadar membina bangunan, tetapi membentuk identiti sebuah bangsa. “Saya mahu menyumbang kepada kebaikan budaya dan rakyat dengan mencipta landskap visual yang mencerminkan identiti Malaysia.” Pencarian identiti itu merupakan satu tindak balas selepas tamatnya zaman penjajahan di Tanah Melayu. Ketika negara kita mencapai kemerdekaan pada tahun 1957, kita masih belum mempunyai gaya seni bina nasional yang jelas. Apa yang ada pada waktu itu ialah seni bina rumah kampung tradisional dan telah menjadi inspirasi pertama Hijjas. Contohnya, rumah kampung Melayu terkenal dengan bumbung tinggi, dibina atas tiang dan mempunyai ruang seperti anjung untuk menyambut kehadiran tetamu. Elemen-elemen tradisional dan agama Islam tidak diterapkan secara bulat-bulat. Sebaliknya diolah menjadi sentuhan halus dan mempunyai maksud tersirat dalam setiap reka bentuknya. Menara Tabung Haji Menjadi Antara Karya Paling Ikonik Antara karya Hijjas yang paling dikenali ialah Menara Tabung Haji, siap sepenuhnya pada tahun 1984. Menara pejabat setinggi 37 tingkat mempunyai siluet dramatik, dengan bahagian sisi melengkung dan tirus menyerupai bentuk jam pasir. Pelan lantainya mempunyai bentuk bulat direka dengan lima tiang di bahagian sisi melambangkan Rukun Islam. Di samping itu, bangunan ini turut direka bagi menampung kemasukan jemaah haji setiap tahun, lengkap dengan ruang masuk kenderaan yang luas. Ia juga dibina sebelum kemunculan aplikasi perisian komputer (CAD) yang canggih menggabungkan lukisan tangan bagi setiap tingkat dengan teknik pembinaan pada zaman tersebut. Menara MBPJ Berdiri Megah Dalam Persekitarannya Satu lagi karya Hijjas yang menarik ialah Menara Majlis Bandaraya Petaling Jaya (MBPJ). Berbeza dengan bangunan lain, menara 27 tingkat ini mengutamakan sebuah dataran bandar yang luas dan kawasan membeli-belah di bahagian bawahnya. Dataran tersebut telah berhubung dengan kawasan pejalan kaki memudahkan orang untuk masuk ke dalam. Selain itu, bahagian menara turut berhubung dengan kawasan jalan sekeliling menerusi jambatan berbumbung. Reka bentuk bangunan ini cuba menyesuaikan diri dengan kawasan kedai-kedai di persekitarannya. Disebabkan itu, bangunan ini dihias bagi mengurangkan ketinggiannya dan melembutkan penampilannya secara semula jadi. Pusat Konvensyen Yang Menjadikan Kerongsang Sebagai Inspirasi Sering disebut sebagai antara karya Hijjas paling hebat ialah Putrajaya International Convention Centre (PICC) yang dibina atas sebuah bukit di Putrajaya. Siap pada tahun 2003, bentuk bumbung yang menyerupai pending perak, iaitu kepala tali pinggang tradisional digunakan oleh golongan diraja Melayu. Malah, reka bentuk bangunan ini juga mesra alam dengan menggabungkan penggunaan cahaya siang secara semula jadi. Selain itu, ia turut menampilkan laluan lapan, bumbung tergantung untuk menyejukkan ruang di bawahnya. Hasilnya ialah sebuah permata seni bina yang sangat cantik di atas sebuah bukit hijau. Dedikasi terhadap seni bina dan peka kepada budaya tempatan bukan sahaja telah mengubah pemandangan ibu kota negara, malah mengajar kita untuk menghargai setiap satu bangunan yang telah wujud. title: 'Over 9,000 building owners required to appoint FSMs, FSOs from April 1, 2027
body: 'Starting April 1, 2027, owners of over 9,000 designated buildings in Malaysia must appoint Fire Safety Managers and Officers under the Fire Services Act. KUALA LUMPUR: From April 1, 2027, owners of 9,451 buildings across the country designated under the Fire Services Act will be required to appoint Fire Safety Managers (FSMs) and Fire Safety Officers (FSOs) at their premises. Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the requirement was in line with Section 27A of the Fire Services (Amendment) Act 2025, which requires owners of designated premises to establish a Fire Safety Organisation (OKK). “From April 1, 2027, any building that we inspect within the next one or two years and which is required to obtain a Fire Certificate will have to appoint an FSM and FSO and establish a Fire Safety Organisation at the premises,” he told reporters after the launch of the FSM and FSO programme at Menara Merdeka Maybank here today. Nor Hisham said a preparation period of between six and 18 months would be given to building owners before full enforcement begins, depending on the expiry date of their existing certificates and the Fire Certificate inspection schedule. He said the enforcement was a strategic approach to reduce JBPM’s workload, particularly in conducting annual inspections of premises. “In future, the annual inspection reports prepared by FSMs will be assessed by JBPM for the renewal of Fire Certificates without requiring physical inspections to be conducted by the Fire and Rescue Department every year,” he said. Nor Hisham said to meet industry needs from 2026 to 2030, JBPM expected 6,000 FSMs and 18,000 FSOs to be appointed nationwide. He said JBPM currently had 13 registered training providers and had issued a tender to increase the number of training providers and instructors. A total of 174 FSMs and 324 FSOs who formed the first group to complete the training received their certificates at the ceremony.

title: 'Scheduling boo-boo: Malaysian hockey league matches originally set for Deepavali rescheduled - Twentytwo13
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Coaches of Premier League hockey teams scheduled to play on Deepavali day are happy they will now battle it out on different dates, as the Malaysian Hockey Confederation (MHC) repeats its 2018 scheduling boo-boo. Two matches – Terengganu Hockey Team against Armed Forces Hockey Team and TNB Thunderbolts versus Maybank – were originally scheduled for Nov 8, the day Deepavali is celebrated in Malaysia. However, the matches will now be rescheduled, much to the delight of TNB Thunderbolts and Terengganu Hockey Team. Mohd Harfizi Baharom of Terengganu said he had been informed that the match against the soldiers would now be played on Nov 9. “It is good that we will not be playing on such an auspicious day. It gives those celebrating the festival time to spend with their families,” Mohd Harfizi told Twentytwo13. “Several of our players have only just returned from the Asian Games. Unfortunately, there is a packed international calendar and the national team will be off to the Asian Champions Trophy from Oct 27 to Nov 5. “As such, having an extra day to prepare for the match against the Armed Forces is welcome. We are third in the standings, but have not given up hope of winning the title. One day can make a difference.” However, the new dates are not reflected on MHC’s website as of publication time. TNB Thunderbolts coach Nor Saiful Zaini, who is also the national junior coach, said he has yet to receive official notice of the new date. “I know it is not easy for MHC to juggle the calendar, but we shouldn’t play on Deepavali or any other religious festival. I am waiting for confirmation regarding the change of date,” said Nor Saiful. In 2018, the Razak Cup was initially scheduled from Nov 3-11, with Deepavali falling on Nov 6 that year. After protests from teams, especially Negeri Sembilan, which threatened to pull out of the tournament, MHC eventually brought forward the tournament to Oct 26-Nov 3. The repeat of the episode raised eyebrows, as those in charge of scheduling the league should have been fully aware of the festive seasons in the country. title: 'JBPM sasar pelantikan 24,000 FSM dan FSO, perkukuh keselamatan kebakaran premis | Sinar Harian
body: 'JBPM sasar pelantikan 24,000 FSM dan FSO, perkukuh keselamatan kebakaran premis KUALA LUMPUR - Jabatan Bomba dan Penyelamat Malaysia (JBPM) menyasarkan pelantikan 24,000 Pengurus Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSM) dan Pegawai Keselamatan Kebakaran (FSO) menjelang tahun 2030 sebagai langkah perkukuh kawal selia serta aspek keselamatan kebakaran di premis. Ini sekali gus menjadi kompenan penting dalam penubuhan Organisasi Keselamatan Kebakaran (OKK). Ketua Pengarah Bomba, Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad berkata, bagi pelantikan FSM, jumlahnya dijangka seramai 6,000 orang, manakala pelantikan FSO seramai 18,000 orang. Menurutnya, JBPM melihat sasaran ini sebagai satu keperluan strategik dan setakat ini seramai 498 lantikan telah dibuat membabitkan 174 peserta FSM dan 324 peserta FSO. "Ini merupakan sebahagian daripada keperluan untuk mematuhi Seksyen 27A Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba 1988 (Pindaan 2025) yang mensyaratkan bagi mana-mana premis yang dikenakan penguatkuasaan Perakuan Bomba perlu menubuhkan OKK. "OKK itu perlu ada jumlah yang minimum untuk dilantik dan dalam kalangan itu perlu ada seorang FSM dan tiga orang FSO," katanya dalam sidang akhbar selepas Majlis Pelancaran FSM dan FSO di Menara Merdeka Maybank, di sini pada Selasa. Tambahnya, sebagai persediaan ke arah OKK, JBPM telah melaksanakan pelbagai program libat urus bersama pihak berkepentingan. Katanya, Malaysia mempunyai sekitar 9,451 premis yang ditetapkan dengan profil dan tahap risiko keselamatan kebakaran yang berbeza. "Asasnya ialah bangunan yang telah kita kategorikan di bawah Akta Perkhidmatan Bomba," ujarnya. Jelas beliau, penguatkuasaan OKK secara penuh ini dijadualkan bermula 1 April 2027 sekali gus memberikan tempoh persediaan kepada pihak industri untuk membangunkan kompetensi, struktur organisasi dan tahap pematuhan yang diperlukan. "FSM dan FSO tidak akan mengambil alih peranan JBPM, tetapi melengkapkan ekosistem keselamatan kebakaran melalui pengurusan risiko secara berterusan di peringkat premis," ujarnya. Nor Hisham berkata, salah satu fungsi FSM ialah mengurangkan beban kepada penguatkuasaan berkaitan Perakuan Bomba. "Kalau pada amalan semasa ini berdasarkan prosedur-prosedur semasa kita periksa setiap tahun untuk kita keluarkan Sijil Perakuan Bomba. Tetapi di masa hadapan, tempoh itu akan kita jarakkan lagi. "Laporan pemeriksaan akan disediakan oleh FSM sebelum kita menilai dan membuat pembaharuan," ujarnya. title: 'Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst
body: 'Axis REIT ‘well positioned’ against rate risks amid RM250 mil deal pipeline — analyst KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 6): Longer-term financing secured much earlier is now providing Axis REIT (KL:AXREIT) cushion against rising interest rates as the real estate investment trust pursues deals, an analyst said. A 25-basis-point increase in policy rate would potentially raise its cost of borrowings by just 0.1 percentage-point to 4.06%, Maybank Investment Bank said, noting that Axis REIT has locked in 10-year and seven-year financing facilities over the past 12 months when rates were more favourable. “With the completion of signed acquisitions, gearing is expected to rise to around 39%, still having ample headroom before any equity raising is required,” the research house said. Axis REIT owns and manages more than 70 office and industrial assets worth over RM5 billion in Klang Valley, Penang, Johor, Pahang, Negeri Sembilan and Kedah. The trust is in the midst of acquiring a distribution centre, a warehouse, and an industrial complex for RM193 million combined. The stated aim is to nearly double the asset under management to RM10 billion by 2030, driven by high-growth sectors and key industrial hubs throughout Peninsular Malaysia. In the near term, Axis REIT has a RM250 million acquisition pipeline currently under negotiation, of which one or two transactions could be announced before year-end, Maybank Investment said and maintained its “buy” call on the trust. “We believe its acquisition pipeline should provide further income visibility” with most ongoing transactions fully occupied and carrying weighted average lease expiry of five years or longer, the research house said. Axis REIT has rebounded from its September lows when the US Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time in three years, sending global bond yields higher and triggering concerns of rising borrowing costs. Still, 10 out of 12 research houses tracked by Bloomberg recommend investors to “buy” Axis REIT and two are on “hold” calls. The average target price is RM2.22, a potential gain of up to 21% in the next 12 months from current price of RM1.84. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'Haze keeps air quality unhealthy across most of S'pore as smoke drifts from Indonesia; Will haze affect the S'pore F1 Grand Prix? No race-day forecast yet from weatherman: Singapore live news
body: 'Haze keeps air quality unhealthy across most of S'pore as smoke drifts from Indonesia; Will haze affect the S'pore F1 Grand Prix? No race-day forecast yet from weatherman: Singapore live news A curated selection of some of the biggest, most important, and fascinating news that's making waves online, featured by Yahoo Singapore Air quality in four of Singapore's five regions remained unhealthy early on Tuesday (6 Oct), with the 24-hour PSI at 6am reaching 130 in the central region, 117 in the west, 112 in the east and 107 in the north, while only the south stayed moderate at 95, according to reports. One-hour PM2.5 levels were elevated in the central, west and east regions but normal in the north and south, following a worsening on Monday evening when the east joined the west and central regions in the unhealthy band. The National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast a 24-hour PSI in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range as south-easterly winds carry moderate to dense smoke from Kalimantan and southern Sumatra towards Singapore. NEA advises healthy people to reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion while the PSI is unhealthy, with the elderly, pregnant women and children told to minimise it and people with chronic heart or lung disease told to avoid it. The PSI first breached the unhealthy threshold on 4 Sept, the first haze-driven breach since October 2023, and peaked at a 2026 high of 164 in central Singapore on 29 Sept. The Meteorological Service Singapore (MSS) said a strong El Niño could delay the end of the dry season, with the monsoon transition expected only in late October or early November. Political, business and cryptocurrency leaders, including Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, are gathering in hazy Singapore for finance conferences ahead of this weekend's Formula One Grand Prix. Hotel rates have soared, with the Fullerton Bay Hotel beside the track charging S$5,030 a night for a room that usually costs US$1,460, as hundreds of thousands of fans and about 90,000 top executives arrive, according to reports. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects F1 to generate S$160 million in tourism receipts this year, up from the usual S$145 million, while the Singapore Tourism Board (STB) said the events showed strong momentum despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty, Reuters reported. Slumping bond prices and cooling sentiment on artificial intelligence are expected to dominate the Forbes CEO Conference and the Milken Asia Summit, while a crypto event is nearly sold out even after the market's value fell about a quarter in a year. Singapore's National Environment Agency (NEA) forecast "high moderate to mid unhealthy" air for Tuesday (6 Oct) but gave no forecast for Sunday's race, and weather analyst Fergus Keatinge said there was no clear sign the haze would end quickly. Indonesia recorded 15,461 hotspots in September, second only to 2015, as a strong El Niño fuelled fires that left Singapore the world's third-most polluted city on 30 Sept. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, co-founder of his family's cryptocurrency business, are expected to attend, along with hundreds of thousands of F1 fans, according to Reuters. The Fullerton Bay Hotel beside the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933) a night for a room that usually costs US$1,460, as the night race and about 40 sideline events draw visitors. F1 generates about S$145 million a year in incremental tourism receipts, according to official estimates, and Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects that to reach S$160 million this year, plus broader gains from deals struck at sideline events, Reuters reported. The Singapore Tourism Board (STB) said F1 and its related events had strong momentum, reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. About 90,000 top-ranking executives are expected in town. Slumping bond prices and a shift in sentiment on artificial intelligence, from euphoric to cautious, are expected to occupy investors at the Forbes CEO Conference and the Milken Asia Summit, which begins on Wednesday (7 Oct). The total value of the cryptocurrency market has fallen about a quarter over 12 months to US$3 trillion, yet organisers of a crypto event said it was nearly sold out, with 25,000 attendees expected, matching last year, according to Reuters. Kuala Lumpur topped IQAir's global pollution rankings on 30 Sept, with Singapore third, and poor air quality had forced organisers to shorten a Singapore half marathon at the last minute the previous weekend. Indonesia's forestry ministry recorded 15,461 hotspots in September, above 2019 levels and second only to 2015, as a strong El Niño brought abnormally hot and dry conditions. - Joel Balbin Air quality unhealthy as smoke drifts from Indonesia into Singapore amid haze Air quality in four of Singapore's five regions stayed in the unhealthy range early on Tuesday (6 Oct), with the 24-hour Pollutant Standards Index (PSI) at 6am reading 130 in the central region, 117 in the west, 112 in the east and 107 in the north. Only the south, at 95, remained in the moderate band, where a reading of 101 to 200 is classed as unhealthy, Straits Times reported. One-hour PM2.5 readings, which guide immediate activities, were elevated in the central (60), west (59) and east (56) regions, while the north (48) and south (35) stayed at normal levels, according to Straits Times. The morning readings followed a deterioration on Monday evening, when the east reached a PSI of 101 at 6pm to join the west at 120 and the central region at 122 in the unhealthy band, with PM2.5 elevated in all five regions. The National Environment Agency (NEA) said in its 5 Oct advisory that with winds expected from the south-east or east-south-east, the 24-hour PSI was forecast to be in the "high moderate to mid unhealthy" range. Dry conditions are expected to persist over Kalimantan and southern Sumatra, where moderate to dense smoke plumes were seen drifting towards Singapore. Under NEA guidance, healthy people should reduce prolonged or strenuous outdoor exertion when the 24-hour PSI is unhealthy, while the elderly, pregnant women and children should minimise it and people with chronic heart or lung disease should avoid it. When PM2.5 is elevated, healthy people are advised to cut strenuous outdoor activity for the next hour, and vulnerable groups should avoid it. The PSI first crossed into the unhealthy range on 4 Sept, the first haze-driven breach since October 2023, and the year's highest reading of 164 was recorded in central Singapore on 29 Sept. title: 'Hilang Sumber Pendapatan Sejak Suami Sakit, Ibu Anak Empat Niaga Dalam Bonet Kereta Demi Sesuap Nasi
body: 'Diuji suami sakit secara tiba-tiba kerana sakit buah pinggang tahap empat dan kanser limfoma, ibu anak empat ini tetap gigih berdiri di bawah payung kecil yang dipacak di tepi bonet kereta demi mencari sesuap nasi dan selesaikan komitmen bulanan. Hilang Sumber Pendapatan Sejak Suami Sakit Kalau sebelum ini suaminya bekerja sebagai pemandu lori, sekarang hanya mampu duduk di atas kerusi dan terbaring di katil. Sesekali dia akan ulang-alik ke hospital untuk rawatan sakitnya. Dari beratnya 78kg, susut kepada 54kg disebabkan hilang selera makan. Beban mencari rezeki dan mengurus rumah tangga kini tergalas di atas bahu Puan Norin Sah binti Md Rejab selepas suaminya, Shaiful Bahari bin Muhamad Saad, 50, hanya terlantar di atas katil sejak disahkan menghidap penyakit kanser limfoma sejak bulan Januari tahun 2025. Ibu Anak Empat Niaga Dalam Bonet Kereta Demi Sesuap Nasi Setiap kali pelajar sekolah keluar dari pintu pagar, setiap kali itu lah wajah wanita berusia 44 tahun ini akan tersenyum dek kerana akan ada rezekinya masuk apabila jualan aiskrim Malaysia dan buah potongnya dibeli. Nampak kecil tetapi nilainya cukup besar bagi ibu yang gigih mencari rezeki demi anak-anak tersayang. Ibu kepada empat anak itu berkata, sejak suaminya disahkan menghidap kanser, kehidupan keluarganya berubah apabila suaminya tidak lagi dapat bekerja seperti sebelum ini. Tidak berharap lebih, tetapi cukuplah jika dapat bantu selesaikan apa yang patut dan suapkan anak-anak dengan rezeki yang halal. “Saya sendiri buntu memikirkan di mana hendak mencari duit selepas ini kerana perlu membuat bayaran macam-macam. Jual Makanan dalam bonet kereta tidak lah dapat banyak mana. tapi alhamdulillah, lepas lah buat beli lauk” katanya. Apabila keluar berniaga, Puan Norin atau lebih mesra dipanggil Kak Sya terpaksa tinggal suaminya di rumah sekejap. Dari segi sumbangan, ada dapat sedikit daripada kejiranan dan kebajikan sekitar taman. Orang ramai yang berhasrat membantu meringankan beban Kak Sya, boleh terus memberikan sumbangan menerusi nombor akaun ini: Maybank: 152116003190 Nama: Norin Sah binti Md Rejab Nilainya tak banyak tak mengapa, yang penting ikhlas untuk meringankan beban ibu ini. Semoga dengan sedikit pemberian kita hari ini dapat membuatkan wajah seseorang yang diuji kembali tersenyum dan rasa masih ada harapan untuk melangkah ke depan.

title: 'Un Singapur envuelto en humo se prepara para hablar de dinero antes de la F1
body: 'SINGAPUR, 5 oct (Reuters) - Líderes regionales, empresariales, del mundo de las criptomonedas y del deporte se reúnen en Singapur para asistir a una serie de conferencias centradas en las finanzas antes del Gran Premio de este fin de semana, mientras la niebla sigue envolviendo la ciudad-estado.  Se espera la presencia del presidente filipino Ferdinand Marcos Jr., del famoso inversor  Ray Dalio y de Eric Trump, cofundador de la empresa de criptomonedas respaldada por su familia, mientras que cientos de miles de aficionados a la Fórmula Uno se darán cita en la isla.  La carrera nocturna por las calles de la ciudad y los cerca de 40 eventos paralelos suelen ser un escaparate mundial para Singapur, y las tarifas de las habitaciones de hotel se han disparado.  El Fullerton Bay Hotel, situado junto al circuito, cobra 5.030 dólares singapurenses (3.933 dólares) por noche por una habitación que suele costar 1.460 dólares.  Este año es probable que la nube de humo procedente de los incendios más intensos que ha sufrido Indonesia en más de una década formen parte del telón de fondo. La agencia medioambiental de Singapur pronosticó para el lunes que la calidad del aire se situaría en el rango de "moderada alta a insalubre baja". No se facilitó ningún pronóstico a más largo plazo para el Gran Premio del domingo.  La oficina de turismo de Singapur afirmó que la F1 y los eventos que la rodean tienen un "fuerte impulso" que refleja confianza pese a la incertidumbre económica y geopolítica.  El nerviosismo en los mercados financieros —donde el precio de los bonos está cayendo en picado y la percepción en torno a la inteligencia artificial está pasando de la euforia a la cautela— ocupará a los inversores y a los directivos en la Conferencia Global de Directores Ejecutivos de Forbes y en la Cumbre Milken Asia, que comienza el miércoles.  Trump, cofundador de la empresa de criptomonedas World Liberty Financial, tiene previsto intervenir en el evento sobre criptomonedas TOKEN2049, en un momento en que los mercados de activos digitales se muestran frágiles tras doce meses muy duros.  El mes pasado, el marco regulatorio que se esperaba no logró ser aprobado en el Senado estadounidense, en parte porque las operaciones personales del presidente Donald Trump con criptomonedas se convirtieron en un punto de fricción para los demócratas.  A pesar de un reciente repunte, el valor total del mercado de las criptomonedas ha caído cerca de una cuarta parte en los últimos 12 meses, a 3 billones de dólares, según el agregador de datos CoinGecko.  Aun así, los organizadores afirman que las entradas para su evento están prácticamente agotadas y se esperan 25 000 asistentes, la misma cifra que el año pasado. El Straits Times informó de que unos 90.000 ejecutivos de alto nivel, o "c-suite", estarán en la ciudad.  La F1 genera unos 145 millones de dólares singapurenses en ingresos turísticos adicionales para Singapur cada año, según estimaciones oficiales. Chua Hak Bin, economista de Maybank, prevé que esta cifra alcance los 160 millones de dólares singapurenses este año, además de "beneficios económicos más amplios" derivados de los acuerdos alcanzados en los eventos paralelos.  (1 dólar = 1,2794 dólares de Singapur)  (Reportaje de Xinghui Kok y Tom Westbrook; edición de Kim Coghill)

title: 'Smoky Singapore gears up to talk money ahead of F1
body: 'SINGAPORE (Oct 5): Regional, business, cryptocurrency and sports leaders are meeting in Singapore for a slew of finance-focused conferences ahead of this weekend's Grand Prix as haze continues to shroud the city state. Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr, famed investor Ray Dalio and Eric Trump, a co-founder of the family-backed cryptocurrency business, are expected, while hundreds of thousands of Formula One (F1) fans will converge on the island. The night race through the city streets and some 40 sideline events are typically a global showcase for Singapore and hotel room rates have soared. The Fullerton Bay Hotel next to the race track is charging S$5,030 (US$3,933 or RM16,054) a night for a room that typically costs US$1,460. This year, the pall from Indonesia's most intense fires in more than a decade will probably form part of the backdrop. Air quality was forecast at the "high moderate to low unhealthy" range on Monday by Singapore's environment agency. No longer-range forecast was provided for Sunday's Grand Prix. Singapore's tourism board said F1 and its surrounding events had "strong momentum" reflecting confidence despite economic and geopolitical uncertainty. Jitters in financial markets where bond prices are slumping and sentiment around artificial intelligence is shifting from euphoric to cautious will occupy investors and business chiefs at the Forbes Global CEO Conference and Milken Asia Summit, which runs from Wednesday. Trump, a co-founder of crypto venture World Liberty Financial, is due to speak at the TOKEN2049 cryptocurrency event with digital asset markets fragile following a bruising 12 months. A hoped-for regulatory framework failed last month to clear the US Senate, in part as President Donald Trump's personal crypto dealings became a flashpoint for Democrats. Despite a recent bounce, the total value of the cryptocurrency market is down about a quarter over the last 12 months to US$3 trillion, according to data aggregator CoinGecko. Still, organisers say their event is nearly sold out with 25,000 attendees expected, the same as last year. The Straits Times reported that about 90,000 "c-suite", or top-ranking, executives will be in town. F1 generates around S$145 million in incremental tourism receipts for Singapore each year, according to official estimates. Maybank economist Chua Hak Bin expects it to hit S$160 million this year, along with "wider economic benefits" from deals struck at sideline events. Uploaded by Tham Yek Lee

title: 'UMK perluas peranan industri dalam ekosistem pembangunan universiti
body: 'KOTA BHARU: Universiti Malaysia Kelantan (UMK) memperluas peranan industri dalam pembangunan universiti dengan melibatkan pemain sektor industri secara langsung dalam sesi pengajaran, pembangunan bakat, penyelidikan dan penyelesaian masalah sebenar. Naib Canselor UMK Datuk Prof Dr Arham Abdullah berkata usaha itu digerakkan menerusi antaranya sesi penglibatan industri dalam pengajaran dan pembelajaran, pembangunan bakat, konsep “Industry on Campus (IoC)” serta pembiayaan mampan menerusi Dana Pembiayaan UMK. Beliau berkata langkah lain yang diketengahkan ialah “UMK Talent Bridge: Connecting Campus Talent to Industry Leaders” yang menumpukan kepada hubungan antara bakat mahasiswa dengan pemimpin sektor berkenaan. Kesemua inisiatif berkenaan menumpukan tiga pendekatan utama iaitu penglibatan industri, hubungan bakat serta pembangunan kerjaya bagi memastikan keperluan industri dapat diterjemahkan dalam pembangunan akademik dan kerjaya mahasiswa. “Kekuatan sesebuah universiti bukan hanya diukur melalui perkara yang berlaku di kampus, tetapi juga melalui sejauh mana ilmu, kepakaran dan bakat yang dimiliki universiti dapat memberi nilai di luar kampus,” katanya dalam kenyataan hari ini. Arham berkata UMK juga bersedia membantu industri mengatasi cabaran melalui kepakaran penyelidik serta menyediakan bakat yang memenuhi keperluan pasaran. “Sekiranya industri mempunyai cabaran, UMK mempunyai penyelidik. Jika industri memerlukan bakat, UMK mempunyai graduan,” katanya. Sementara itu, Timbalan Naib Canselor (Penyelidikan dan Inovasi) UMK Prof Dr Wan Ahmad Amir Zal Wan Ismail berkata pihak universiti itu berhasrat menjadikan program UMK CONNECT sebagai acara tahunan bagi memastikan hubungan akademia dan industri dapat dibangunkan secara berterusan. Beliau berkata platform berkenaan boleh membuka ruang untuk menterjemahkan kepakaran universiti bagi memberi manfaat lebih luas kepada graduan, masyarakat dan sektor industri. “Universiti memiliki ilmu, penyelidikan, bakat dan idea. Industri pula memiliki pengalaman, keperluan sebenar, teknologi, jaringan dan peluang. Apabila ilmu bertemu pengalaman, idea bertemu keperluan dan bakat bertemu peluang, kita mampu menghasilkan sesuatu yang jauh lebih besar,” katanya. Pada majlis UMK CONNECT 2026: Majlis Minum Petang dan Apresiasi Industri dan Kerjasama Strategik yang menghimpunkan 104 rakan industri daripada pelbagai bidang, pihak universiti menerima sumbangan keseluruhan RM1.1 juta daripada Maybank Islamic. Sumbangan itu bagi membiayai Program Pembangunan Siswa SULUNG (SULUNG) serta Projek Perumahan Orang Kurang Upaya (OKU) di Pusat Pemulihan OKU Kampung Aur (PROKA), Bachok, Kelantan. -- BERNAMA

title: 'PNB unit eyes up to RM600mil recurring annual income from Merdeka 118
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd expects recurring income from the completed Merdeka 118 development to reach RM500 million-RM600 million a year over the medium term. About 70 per cent of the project's office space is already sub-leased, according to MARC Ratings. The firm said the office component is fully leased to parent Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB) under a triple-net master lease. This shields PNB Merdeka from occupancy and most property-related cost risks. MARC said about 70 per cent of the tower's 1.6 million sq ft net lettable area (NLA) has been sub-leased. This comprises 40 per cent, or 33 floors, sub-leased to Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), 20 per cent to PNB and about 10 per cent to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to rise to about 90 per cent over the next five years, with the office tower projected to generate annual net property income of about RM137 million. MARC has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka's RM6 billion Merdeka sukuk Wakalah with a stable outlook. The rating aligns with PNB's AAA/Stable corporate credit rating, supported by PNB's unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee covering any shortfall in principal and profit payments under the sukuk. MARC said for the seven-storey retail mall, which is expected to open next month, lease agreements covering 81 per cent of its 750,324 sq ft NLA have either been signed or are under negotiation, at an indicative average rental of RM11.92 per sq ft. The Merdeka 118 development, near Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, has incurred RM10.6 billion in development costs to date. The cost was largely funded by two earlier sukuk programmes that have since been restructured into the current rated issuance. The planned residential components are expected to add another RM1.4 billion in development costs, to be funded through a mix of borrowings and equity injections. Two residential towers, with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM2 billion, are targeted for launch in the first half of 2027, while a serviced apartment project has an estimated GDV of RM745 million. MARC said these residential and serviced apartment components remain exposed to demand risk amid competing developments in Kuala Lumpur. PNB Merdeka is wholly owned by PNB and was established to undertake the Merdeka 118 project. This includes the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank, a 17-floor luxury hotel, a three-floor observation deck and the upcoming retail mall. PNB Merdeka is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both designated National Heritage sites.

title: 'Import Duty On Minted Gold Bars Drops To 0% From 1 November 2026
body: 'Small gold bars of 1g, 5g, or 10g have become a common way for people to put money aside a little at a time. Since 8 June 2026, though, anyone buying imported minted bars may have been paying for a 10% import duty included in the price. The Customs Duties (Amendment) Order 2026, P.U. (A) 350, cuts that duty from 10% to 0% from 1 November 2026. Gold Bars Covered By The Cut The cut applies to minted (stamped) gold bars, the small bars people buy to save. The most common sizes are 1g to 50g. The duty only ever applied to imported bars, so bars minted in Malaysia were never taxed and their prices have no duty to lose. Bank Muamalat sells imported bars, and it told customers in May that these bars would cost more once the duty applied. According to Tomei Consolidated group managing director Datuk Ng Yih Pyng, large cast bars, which weigh 1kg and up and are used by manufacturers, are classed differently and were already duty-free. Jewellery isn’t affected either. So this matters to you if you buy imported minted bars, or if you convert gold in your account into an imported physical bar. Possible Savings On An Imported Bar The duty is 10% of what a bar is worth when it arrives in Malaysia. So a bar worth RM100 costs the seller RM110 once the duty is added. When the duty is removed, RM110 drops back to RM100. That’s a saving of RM10 out of RM110, or about 9.1% off what the seller paid for the bar. On 5 October, Bank Muamalat sold a gold bar at RM605.02 a gram and gold in its account at RM584.53 a gram, according to its own price board. If the account price has no duty in it, the RM20.49 difference is the most the duty could be adding to each gram of the bar. The table below shows what that means for each bar size Bank Muamalat sells. RinggitPlus worked out these amounts using Bank Muamalat’s bar and account prices on 5 October 2026. Prices will change with the gold price. The real saving will be less than this, because part of the difference pays for making and packaging the bar, and that cost stays. Buying Now Or Waiting Until November If you buy gold every month through a gold account or gold savings plan, you probably don’t need to change anything. The Malaysia Gold Association’s president, Datuk Seri Louis Ng, said in September that the duty applies to minted bars in finished, packaged form, and not to kilobars and cast bars. So gold held in an account may not be affected, but check with your bank. If you’re planning to buy an imported minted bar in October, ask the seller two things. Did they pay the import duty on this bar, and will the price change after 1 November? Then work out how much more the bar costs than the seller’s gold account price, per gram. Do this now, and then again in the first week of November. If that difference shrinks, the duty removal has made the bar cheaper. If it doesn’t, any price drop is just the gold price moving. Do note that some sellers have already paid the duty on bars they have in stock now. They may keep their prices the same until those bars are sold, so prices may not drop straight away on 1 November. The gold price also changes every day. If the gold price goes up in November, it could cancel out what you save from the duty removal. Waiting makes the most sense if you were already planning to buy a 50g or 100g bar, and the seller confirms the duty is included in its price. Gold doesn’t earn interest, and gold accounts aren’t protected by PIDM the way savings accounts are. If you’re looking at gold accounts, see how Maybank Islamic’s MIGA-i works. body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: MARC Ratings has affirmed its AAAIS rating on PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Bhd’s (PNBMV) Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah Programme of up to RM6bil, with a stable outlook. The rating agency, in a statement, said the rating is equalised with the AAA/Stable corporate credit rating of Permodalan Nasional Bhd (PNB), based on publicly available information. It said the equalisation reflects PNB’s unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee to cover any shortfall in principal and profit payments under the sukuk programme. PNBMV, a wholly owned subsidiary of PNB, is undertaking the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in Kuala Lumpur. The development includes the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank, a retail mall and sites earmarked for two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. MARC Ratings said PNBMV has leased all 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement, under which PNB bears property-related expenses in addition to rental and service charges. About 70% of the office tower's 1.6 million sq ft of net lettable area has been sub-leased, comprising 40% or 33 floors to Maybank, 20% to PNB and about 10% to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to rise to about 90% over the next five years, while the office tower is projected to generate annual net property income of about RM137mil. For the 750,324 sq ft retail mall, lease agreements covering 81% of its net lettable area have either been signed or are under negotiation, at an indicative average rental rate of RM11.92 per sq ft. The mall is expected to open in November. Meanwhile, two residential apartment buildings with a combined estimated gross development value (GDV) of RM2bil are targeted for launch in the first half of 2027. A serviced apartment component, with an estimated GDV of RM745mil, is planned for a later launch. MARC Ratings noted that the residential and serviced apartment components are exposed to demand risk due to competing developments in Kuala Lumpur. The Merdeka 118 development has incurred RM10.6bil in development costs to date, while the upcoming residential projects are expected to require another RM1.4bil, funded through a combination of borrowings and equity injections. MARC Ratings said recurring income from the completed development could reach RM500mil to RM600mil annually over the medium term.

title: '国行:大马金融风险可控 需警惕地缘政治冲击 - 财经 - 焦点财经
body: '国行:大马金融风险可控 需警惕地缘政治冲击 （吉隆坡5日讯）中东地缘政治冲突成全球经济及金融市场主要下行风险“源头”，但国家银行指出，这对国内金融市场潜在带来的冲击仍处可管理水平，且整体金融体系直接受中东冲突的影响有限。  国行今日在主题为“国际油价以外：从地缘政治冲突到金融稳定风险”的10月观察报告披露，尽管国内金融体系展现韧性，但并无法完全免疫于未来冲击。 “因此，国行将保持警惕，持续开展监测工作，重点关注企业流动性、脆弱企业与家庭的还款趋势、银行融资状况，以及冲击经金融市场被放大的可能性。” 银行股表现不俗 马股金融服务指数今日走稳，闭市时起0.52%收在19140.14点。在32只银行股中，半数走高，以丰隆银行（HLBANK,5819,主板金融服务组）表现最为亮眼，冲高24仙至22令吉88仙，是场内第11大上升股。 其他表现不俗还有大马银行（AMBANK,1015,主板金融服务组），闭市报6令吉50仙，攀高11仙。至于联昌集团（CIMB,1023,主板金融服务组）和大众银行（PBBANK,1295,主板金融服务组）则分别走高8仙与5仙，收在7令吉73仙及4令吉71仙。 贵为马股最大市值的马来亚银行（MAYBANK,1155,主板金融服务组）今日在9令吉98仙至10令吉10仙区间拉扯，最终滑落2仙收在10令吉。 报告点出，金融稳定风险虽仍可控，但在市场不确定性持续的情况下，还需保持警惕；若中东冲突进一步恶化或更持久，恐将对原产品带来更大的价格冲击、持续扰乱供应链，及拖累全球经济增长前景。 “随着投资者重新评估地缘政治发展、原产品价格前景以及主要经济体利率走向，全球金融市场料续高度波动。尽管如此，迄今为止的种种数据显示，这些对国内金融稳定风险还是处于可管理水平。” 国行表示，金融压力目前主要集中在特定领域及特定借贷人群体，整体信贷素质还稳健，且融资持续流向实体经济，而金融机构也维持强劲资本、流动性及拨备缓冲。 年初宏观压力测试仍可参考 报告说明，国行年初进行的宏观压力测试仍具参考意义，因有关情境已涵盖地缘政治演变所引起的全球风险规避情绪，以及供应链中断和大宗商品价格上涨所带来的通胀压力。 “而若冲突持续时间拉长或进一步恶化的潜在影响，也在上述压力测试的结果范围内，即使面对更为不利的经济环境，金融体系依然有韧性。” 国行指出，目前国内金融体系的贷款偿表现仍稳定，而压力主要集中在特定商业领域，银行的融资成本虽面临一些上行压力，但流动性状况仍获支撑。 “银行、保险公司及伊斯兰保险业者继续维持充足财务缓冲，确保金融中介活动不受干扰，另国内金融市场深度与多元化的投资者基础，也有助限制外部市场波动的传导；主要传导渠道是通过实体经济和全球金融市场，而非是信贷或融资风险敞口传导。” 此外，报告认为，避险情绪升温也可能促使投资者重新调整组合，加剧资本流动波动，影响资产估值、债券回酬率、汇率及市场流动性。综合来看，这些影响可能导致信贷及融资收紧。 “这对金融机构的相关影响，最终或体现在更高信贷及理赔成本、估值损失、融资及流动性压力，以及获利和资本能力减弱。” 国行指出，地缘政治冲突引起的冲击并非孤立发生，而是与其他全球经济及金融发展相互叠加，至于对国内金融稳定的影响，取决于这些综合冲击与现有金融脆弱性的相互作用。 “目前的迹象显示，金融压力进一步放大的风险仍有限，金融体系的高度韧性足以吸纳相关冲击带来的影响。整体商业状况持稳，主要是国内需求持续、电子电器产品出口强劲，以及投资活动持续。” 中小企普遍面对挑战 不过，国行在与企业交流的过程发现，部分企业正面对投入及物流成本上升、付款延迟，以及现金周转周期拉长等问题。 “这些挑战在中小型企业更普遍，因通常赚幅较薄、流动性缓冲较小，在多元化供应商或吸收成本上涨方面的空间也较有限。这情况在批发及零售贸易、建筑业，以及部分制造领域尤其明显。” 报告披露，企业也已采取相应措施缓和营运压力，包括改善成本效率、多元化供应商及采购渠道、调整生产与库存计划，和加强现金流管理。 “截至目前，这些调整措施有助控制企业财务状况所受到的影响，整体企业贷款素质仍稳健。截至今年6月，企业总减值贷款率为2.8%，而被归类为信用风险增加的第二阶段贷款占比，仍低于近期平均水平。” 不过，国行提醒，部分中小企业已出现偿债压力，包括交通物流、批发及零售贸易，以及初级制造领域。 “这些情况说明，部分持续面对流动性压力的企业，潜在的信贷风险可能正在累积，因此持续从借款人及行业层面进行监测，还是相当重要。” 金融市场压力指数升 另一方面，国行点出，地缘政治紧张情绪升温，加上市场对美国货币政策预期的变化，导致全球风险情绪转变，并持续加剧金融市场波动，这些发展促使包括我国在内的新兴市场外国投资者，重新调整组合配置。 “与此同时，马股与指数相关的再平衡操作（将综指成分股扩大至50只），也影响外国投资者的持仓情况。随着外部环境波动加剧，金融市场压力指数平均为9%，比2021至2025年平均7.4%的水平高。” 美国与伊朗今年4月达成2周停火协议前，这个压力指数曾从14.2%的高峰回落，但因地缘政治持续不确定性，以及近期先进经济体债券回酬率走高夹击，这压力指数仍维持在较高水平。 尽管如此，国行相信，国内金融市场仍有能力吸收这些外部冲击，并保持有序运作。 “境内外汇市场维持稳健，平均每日成交额达219亿美元（约894亿令吉）。马币兑美元汇率今年以来按年贬值0.43%，纵然美元整体走势波动，但我国经济基本面稳定持续助力马币走稳。” 而报告也点出，大马政府债券回酬率紧随全球债券回酬率走高，尽管外国投资者持续调整投资组合，但今年来在我国持有的政府债券仍增加81亿令吉。 “大马政府债券与美国国债之间的回酬率落差续扩大，加上届满的政府债券规模较大，可能增加投资组合资金流动对外部环境变化的敏感度，但深厚的金融市场和多元化投资者基础，加上国内金融机构韧性，将继续支撑市场有序运作。” 国行重申，国内银行领域仍有余力可吸收不利经济及金融环境所带来的影响，银行体系总资本适足率为风险加权资产的17.9%，远高于监管要求。 信贷风险仍受控 “而强劲的盈利能力进一步增强银行体系的韧性，股本回酬和资产回酬率分别为11.5%和1.3%。另外信贷风险仍受控，截至今年6月的整体贷款减值率维持在1.4%，而第二阶段贷款占比则今年3月的6.1%降至5.9%。” 报告指出，银行领域也继续维持审慎拨备水平，贷款损失覆盖率（包括监管储备）为124.6%，流动性及融资状况同样保持稳健。银行体系整体流动性覆盖率和净稳定资金比率分别为149.6%和114.7%，均高于监管最低要求。 存款竞争加剧 “部分融资工具的融资成本逐步上升，归咎于银行争取存款的竞争加剧，对融资成本造成一定的上行压力，但涨幅仍在可控范围内。无论如何，这些变化尚未演变成更广泛的融资压力，也没有限制银行支持信贷中介活动的能力。”  热门新闻 百格视频

title: 'MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 Strengthens ASEAN Healthcare Cooperation
body: 'MH WellFest Cambodia 2026 is a healthcare cooperation between Cambodia and Malaysia, merging medicine with financial services and community health in Phnom Penh. The event was held on October 3 and 4 at Borey Peng Huoth Eco Park and was organized by Maybank Cambodia and the Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council. The move is part of a wider trend in ASEAN to make cross-border healthcare more accessible. The event showcased practical means of streamlining medical travel in the region by connecting Cambodian families with Malaysian healthcare providers and financial services. Malaysian Healthcare Expertise Reaches Cambodia The event gathered 14 leading Malaysian hospital groups and medical specialists in Phnom Penh. Cambodian families were able to have discussions with health professionals about preventive health care, specialty care and potential medical travel arrangements. This direct engagement can help patients to better understand treatment options before traveling overseas. It also builds linkages between the healthcare providers of both countries and raises greater awareness in the region of Malaysia’s medical services. Maybank Connects Healthcare With Financial Services Maybank Cambodia took the opportunity to showcase cross border payment solutions, medical travel privileges and financial planning support at the event. These services are intended to help families overcome some of the financial and administrative barriers to arranging treatment overseas. The addition of banking support with access to healthcare provides a more rounded medical travel experience. For patients considering treatment in Malaysia, planning for finances can be an important part of managing the transportation, hospital expenses and other associated costs. Community Wellness Takes Center Stage MH WellFest wasn’t just about medical travel, it was about preventive health and community participation. The MH WellFest Run added a public wellness aspect to the event with over 800 runners and walkers in the 5km and 10km categories. Visitors also could attend health screening booths, medical presentations and family-oriented cultural activities. Supporting ASEAN Medical Tourism Goals The event was part of the wider Malaysia Year of Medical Tourism 2026 by the Malaysia Healthcare Travel Council. Malaysia has been marketing itself as a regional hub for international patients looking for specialized medical services. Regional medical tourism could bloom with stronger healthcare links to Cambodia and other ASEAN markets. title: 'MARC Ratings Affirms PNB Merdeka Ventures’ Sukuk Rating - MARC
body: 'MARC Ratings has affirmed the rating of AAAIS on PNB Merdeka Ventures Sdn Berhad’s (PNBMV) Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah Programme of up to RM6.0 billion with a stable outlook. The affirmed rating is equalised with the AAA/Stable corporate credit rating of Permodalan Nasional Berhad (PNB) which is based on publicly available information. The rating equalisation is premised on the unconditional and irrevocable rolling guarantee from PNB to cover any shortfall in principal repayments and profit payments on the Merdeka Sukuk Wakalah. PNBMV is wholly owned by PNB and was set up to undertake the 40-acre Merdeka 118 development in the vicinity of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara in Kuala Lumpur. The development comprises several components, chiefly the 118-storey Menara Merdeka Maybank (formerly known as Menara Merdeka 118), a single tower with 84 floors of office space, a 17-floor luxury hotel and a three-floor observation deck. Adjacent to the tower are a seven-floor retail mall which is expected to open in November 2026, and sites earmarked for the future construction of two residential towers and a serviced apartment building. PNBMV is also the landowner and custodian of Stadium Merdeka and Stadium Negara, both of which are listed as National Heritage sites. PNBMV has leased the entire 84 floors of office space in the tower to PNB under a triple net master lease agreement. PNB undertakes all property-related expenses, including quit rent, insurance and repair costs, in addition to the monthly net rental and service charge. PNBMV is therefore not exposed to the occupancy risks or other risks associated with the office component of the tower. As at date, about 70% of the 1.6 million sq ft of net lettable area (NLA) of the office tower has been sub-leased: 40% or 33 floors to Maybank, 20% to PNB, and about 10% to other tenants. Occupancy is expected to increase to approximately 90% over the next five years. The office tower is expected to generate an annual net property income of around RM137.0 million. Lease agreements for 81% of the 750,324 sq ft of NLA in the retail mall have either been signed or are under negotiation to be signed with tenants at an indicative average rental rate of RM11.92/sq ft. Meanwhile, the two residential apartment buildings, with an estimated combined gross development value (GDV) of RM2.0 billion, are targeted to be launched in 1H2027. The serviced apartments, to be launched later, will have an estimated GDV of RM745 million. The residential apartment and serviced residence components are exposed to demand risk given competing developments in Kuala Lumpur. The Merdeka 118 development has so far incurred a development cost of RM10.6 billion, largely funded by two earlier sukuk programmes that have since been restructured into the current rated issuances. The upcoming residential projects are expected to add a further RM1.4 billion in development cost and will be funded through a mix of borrowings and equity injections. The rolling guarantee covers any shortfall for the periodic distribution and upcoming principal repayments throughout the entire sukuk programme through automatic renewal on each profit payment date. Upon completion of the entire project, cash flow generation from recurring income streams could amount to about RM500 million to RM600 million p.a. over the medium term.
