title: 'New Hilux catches fire after 40 days, son and mother awarded RM427,000
body: 'KUALA KUBU BARU: The Sessions Court has awarded more than RM427,000 in damages to a man and his mother after their new Toyota Hilux caught fire 40 days after it was registered, with the blaze spreading to their house. Judge Norhayati Johar found that the fire was caused by electrical arcing at the vehicle's battery terminal connection and ruled that the Hilux did not meet the safety, durability and quality reasonably expected of a new vehicle. She ruled in favour of plaintiffs V. Thiagarajan and V.C. Kamalam in their suit against Maybank Islamic Bhd and Toyota dealer Telagamas Motors Sdn Bhd. The plaintiffs were awarded RM397,220 in special damages and RM30,000 in general damages, as well as RM25,000 in costs and interest. Telagamas was also ordered to indemnify Maybank for the judgment sum and damages for which the bank was liable. According to the grounds of judgment, Thiagarajan bought a new Toyota Hilux D/C 2.8 Rogue from Telagamas under a hire-purchase facility provided by Maybank. The vehicle was registered on Aug 19, 2023. On Sept 28, the Hilux caught fire while parked at the porch of the plaintiffs' house in Rumah Murah Kilat near Kerling here. The fire started at the front of the vehicle before spreading to the house, causing substantial damage to the Hilux and the property. On the cause of the fire, Norhayati said the evidence pointed to electrical arcing at the battery terminal connection. The court found that the Hilux was new, stationary and had its engine switched off when the electrical failure occurred. Norhayati said the short period between the vehicle's registration and the fire was significant when considering its durability. "I do not regard the 40-day period, by itself, as determinative. However, this was a new vehicle which suffered a serious failure within that period, resulting in its destruction. "In those circumstances, I find that the vehicle did not possess the durability reasonably expected of a new motor vehicle," she said. She said no misuse, modification, improper maintenance or other intervening conduct by the plaintiffs had been established. The court found that the vehicle was not of merchantable quality, was not reasonably fit for its purpose and did not meet the standard of acceptable quality under the Hire-Purchase Act 1967 and Consumer Protection Act 1999. Maybank had relied on several clauses in the hire-purchase agreement concerning inspection, suitability, warranty and maintenance to dispute the claim. However, Norhayati said the contractual provisions could not defeat the statutory protections afforded to the buyer. She said there was no evidence that the electrical condition which caused the fire was externally apparent or could reasonably have been discovered during an ordinary examination before delivery. On Telagamas' liability, the court accepted evidence that its salesman had described the Hilux as strong, durable, safe and reliable during the purchase. Norhayati said those qualities concerned the condition and expected performance of the vehicle itself. "An electrical failure at the battery terminal connection which caused a new vehicle to catch fire approximately 40 days after registration is difficult to reconcile with those descriptions," she said. Thiagarajan was alerted by the vehicle's alarm and horn before discovering the Hilux on fire at the car porch. He tried unsuccessfully to extinguish the blaze before he and his family were forced to escape through the rear of the house. Norhayati said the family home became uninhabitable and they had to relocate to Behrang. "The deprivation was substantial. This was not a case involving minor defects or temporary inconvenience while the occupants remained in the premises," she added. The plaintiffs were represented by K.M. Kabilan, while Kirpal Singh Sarban Singh and Jasmeetpal Singh acted for Maybank and Telagamas respectively.

title: 'Liyana shares lead after sizzling start at The Ladies
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Defending champion Liyana Durisic made a strong start to her title defence at The Ladies 2026 after firing a seven-under 64 to share the opening-round lead with Genevieve Ling at The Mines Resort & Golf Club on Thursday. Malaysian two-time Olympian Kelly Tan is also among the leading names competing this week. The tournament began with Wednesday's Royal Pro-Am and official opening ceremony, which was officiated by Tengku Ampuan Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah. title: 'Stock Today: Maybank Gains 0.5% After ASB Disposal
body: 'Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) rose 0.5% in late morning trade on Friday, despite Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB) having disposed of 13 million shares in the bank earlier this week.  As of 10.56am, Maybank gained five sen to RM10.00, after opening at RM9.95. The stock traded between RM9.93 and RM10.02 during the session.  Some 1.33 million shares had changed hands, with the last done price above the previous adjusted close of RM9.95.  At the time, 598,000 shares were queued to buy at RM9.99 while 1.52 million shares were queued to sell at RM10.00.  Maybank disclosed on Oct 1 that AmanahRaya Trustees Bhd, as trustee for ASB, had disposed of 13 million shares on Sept 29 through a sale of shares.  Following the disposal, ASB’s direct stake in Maybank stood at 3.418 billion shares, representing 28.261% of the bank’s issued shares.  The notice of change in substantial shareholding was dated Sept 29 and received by Maybank on Oct 1.

title: 'Anak syarikat ES Sunlogy tuntut RM1.17 juta daripada Ecolectric, Maybank terlibat prosiding garnisi - Newswav
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 2 Okt - Anak syarikat milik penuh ES Sunlogy Berhad, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd sedang mengambil tindakan untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman mahkamah bernilai RM1.17 juta terhadap Ecolectric Engineering Sdn Bhd selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan prosiding garnisi melibatkan Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank). Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membenarkan permohonan Savelite bagi Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab terhadap Maybank, yang dinamakan sebagai garnisi pertama Ecolectric, dalam pendengaran ex parte pada 30 September lalu, menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy kepada Bursa Malaysia. Mahkamah menetapkan 21 Oktober 2026 bagi pendengaran tunjuk sebab. Perintah Garnisi atau Garnishee Order merupakan proses undang-undang yang membolehkan pihak yang memperoleh penghakiman mahkamah memohon mendapatkan bayaran daripada wang milik pihak yang berhutang di bawah penghakiman tetapi dipegang oleh pihak ketiga, seperti bank. Dalam kes ini, Maybank dinamakan sebagai garnisi dan perlu menunjukkan sebab kepada mahkamah sebelum mahkamah memutuskan sama ada wang yang mungkin dipegang bagi pihak Ecolectric boleh digunakan untuk memenuhi penghakiman tersebut. Savelite akan mendapatkan Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab itu dan mengatur penyerahannya kepada Maybank mengikut arahan mahkamah. Prosiding itu menyusuli penghakiman ingkar pembelaan yang direkodkan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026 berhubung pertikaian kerja pemasangan elektrik bagi projek pembangunan kediaman di Damansara Heights. Pertikaian projek Damansara Heights Menerusi penghakiman itu, Ecolectric diperintahkan membayar RM1,174,327.72 kepada Savelite dalam tempoh 14 hari. Jumlah itu merupakan RM1,234,551.27 yang diputuskan mahkamah selepas ditolak wang tahanan RM60,223.55 yang dipegang Savelite. Pertikaian itu berpunca daripada surat anugerah bernilai kira-kira RM1.65 juta bertarikh 25 April 2022, apabila Savelite melantik Ecolectric sebagai subkontraktor untuk membekalkan tenaga kerja bagi pemasangan perkhidmatan elektrik untuk projek pembangunan kediaman 54 unit di Damansara Heights. Savelite mendakwa Ecolectric gagal atau enggan menempatkan tenaga kerja yang mencukupi atau berkemahiran di tapak, menyebabkan kerja tidak dapat dilaksanakan mengikut program yang dipersetujui. Savelite memfailkan writ saman dan penyata tuntutan terhadap Ecolectric pada Julai 2026. Menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy, Ecolectric tidak memasukkan kehadiran dalam tempoh 14 hari selepas writ saman dan penyata tuntutan diserahkan serta gagal memfail dan menyerahkan pembelaannya dalam tempoh ditetapkan. Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian merekodkan penghakiman ingkar pembelaan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026. Selain bayaran RM1.17 juta, mahkamah memerintahkan ganti rugi am ditaksir dan kos RM528 dibayar oleh Ecolectric kepada Savelite. ES Sunlogy sebelum ini berkata Savelite telah membuat rosot nilai penuh sebanyak RM3.17 juta ke atas jumlah terhutang daripada Ecolectric berkaitan projek Damansara Heights dan Old Klang Road, mencerminkan penilaian kumpulan terhadap kebolehkutipan jumlah tersebut. - DagangNews.com

body: 'KUALA LUMPUR 2 Okt - Anak syarikat milik penuh ES Sunlogy Berhad, Savelite Engineering Sdn Bhd sedang mengambil tindakan untuk menguatkuasakan penghakiman mahkamah bernilai RM1.17 juta terhadap Ecolectric Engineering Sdn Bhd selepas Mahkamah Tinggi membenarkan prosiding garnisi melibatkan Malayan Banking Berhad (Maybank). Mahkamah Tinggi Kuala Lumpur membenarkan permohonan Savelite bagi Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab terhadap Maybank, yang dinamakan sebagai garnisi pertama Ecolectric, dalam pendengaran ex parte pada 30 September lalu, menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy kepada Bursa Malaysia. Mahkamah menetapkan 21 Oktober 2026 bagi pendengaran tunjuk sebab. Perintah Garnisi atau Garnishee Order merupakan proses undang-undang yang membolehkan pihak yang memperoleh penghakiman mahkamah memohon mendapatkan bayaran daripada wang milik pihak yang berhutang di bawah penghakiman tetapi dipegang oleh pihak ketiga, seperti bank. Dalam kes ini, Maybank dinamakan sebagai garnisi dan perlu menunjukkan sebab kepada mahkamah sebelum mahkamah memutuskan sama ada wang yang mungkin dipegang bagi pihak Ecolectric boleh digunakan untuk memenuhi penghakiman tersebut. Savelite akan mendapatkan Perintah Garnisi Tunjuk Sebab itu dan mengatur penyerahannya kepada Maybank mengikut arahan mahkamah. Prosiding itu menyusuli penghakiman ingkar pembelaan yang direkodkan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026 berhubung pertikaian kerja pemasangan elektrik bagi projek pembangunan kediaman di Damansara Heights. Pertikaian projek Damansara Heights Menerusi penghakiman itu, Ecolectric diperintahkan membayar RM1,174,327.72 kepada Savelite dalam tempoh 14 hari. Jumlah itu merupakan RM1,234,551.27 yang diputuskan mahkamah selepas ditolak wang tahanan RM60,223.55 yang dipegang Savelite. Pertikaian itu berpunca daripada surat anugerah bernilai kira-kira RM1.65 juta bertarikh 25 April 2022, apabila Savelite melantik Ecolectric sebagai subkontraktor untuk membekalkan tenaga kerja bagi pemasangan perkhidmatan elektrik untuk projek pembangunan kediaman 54 unit di Damansara Heights. Savelite mendakwa Ecolectric gagal atau enggan menempatkan tenaga kerja yang mencukupi atau berkemahiran di tapak, menyebabkan kerja tidak dapat dilaksanakan mengikut program yang dipersetujui. Savelite memfailkan writ saman dan penyata tuntutan terhadap Ecolectric pada Julai 2026. Menurut pemakluman ES Sunlogy, Ecolectric tidak memasukkan kehadiran dalam tempoh 14 hari selepas writ saman dan penyata tuntutan diserahkan serta gagal memfail dan menyerahkan pembelaannya dalam tempoh ditetapkan. Mahkamah Tinggi kemudian merekodkan penghakiman ingkar pembelaan terhadap Ecolectric pada 17 Ogos 2026. Selain bayaran RM1.17 juta, mahkamah memerintahkan ganti rugi am ditaksir dan kos RM528 dibayar oleh Ecolectric kepada Savelite. ES Sunlogy sebelum ini berkata Savelite telah membuat rosot nilai penuh sebanyak RM3.17 juta ke atas jumlah terhutang daripada Ecolectric berkaitan projek Damansara Heights dan Old Klang Road, mencerminkan penilaian kumpulan terhadap kebolehkutipan jumlah tersebut. - DagangNews.com

title: 'ASB Disposes 13 Million Shares In Maybank
body: 'AmanahRaya Trustees Bhd, as trustee for Amanah Saham Bumiputera (ASB), disposed of 13 million shares in Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank) on Sept 29, 2026.  In a filing, Maybank said the disposal was made through a sale of shares and involved ASB’s direct interest in the banking group.  Following the transaction, ASB’s direct shareholding in Maybank stood at 3.418 billion shares, representing 28.261% of the bank’s issued shares.  The notice of the change in substantial shareholding was dated Sept 29 and received by Maybank on Oct 1.  Maybank shares closed lower at 9.95, the stock has come down 14% over the last 6 months.

title: 'Nanta titip pesanan buat Syed Saddiq, Bella-‘Perkahwinan umpama jalan raya’
body: 'MENTERI Kerja Raya Datuk Seri Alexander Nanta Linggi berkongsikan pertemuannya dengan bakal pengantin Ahli Parlimen Muar, Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman dan selebriti Bella Astillah.  Namun, apa yang lebih menarik nasihat dititipkan Nanta terhadap pasangan dua sejoli itu yang sedang menghitung hari untuk bergelar raja sehari.  Pesanan Nanta kepada pasangan berkenaan agak menarik apabila menyifatkan perkahwinan “seumpama jalan raya”.  “Bila berjumpa orang muda yang bakal melangkah ke alam perkahwinan, sempatlah saya kongsi sedikit pesanan.  “Saya kata, perkahwinan ni umpama jalan raya — mesti dua hala, tak boleh sehala. Kena saling memberi, saling menerima dan sama-sama bertolak ansur.  “Dalam rumah tangga, bukan soal siapa betul atau siapa menang. Yang penting, dua-dua kena tahu bila nak jalan, bila nak berhenti, dan kadang-kadang bila kena bagi laluan,” katanya dalam hantaran di Facebooknya.  Nanta turut mendoakan agar segala urusan Syed Saddiq dan Bella dipermudahkan dan semoga perjalanan yang bakal ditempuh bersama nanti sentiasa diberkati dan dipenuhi kebahagiaan.  Syed Saddiq dan Bella dijadualkan akan melangsungkan akad nikah pada 10 Oktober ini di aras 118, Menara Merdeka Maybank, Kuala Lumpur.- MalaysiaPost

title: 'Opinion: When audit opinions meet uncertain numbers
body: 'Opinion: When audit opinions meet uncertain numbers Two lawsuits filed within days of each other in late July and early August have renewed a question that matters to every investor. When financial statements rest on estimates that could go either way, what does a “clean” audit opinion actually guarantee? The liquidators of Serba Dinamik Holdings Bhd are seeking at least RM1.56 billion from KPMG, alleging that unqualified opinions between FY2016 and FY2019 failed to detect revenue overstatements of up to 87%. The suit claims the misstatements would have been uncovered earlier, before the group paid RM1.795 billion in dividends, which the claim links to the alleged audit failures. Around the same time, the Sabah government, together with other plaintiffs, sued Ernst & Young for RM2.4 billion over its audits of Sabah Development Bank, alleging that EY issued unqualified opinions for years even though, according to the claim, 85.94% of the bank’s loan portfolio had been recorded as non-performing loans by FY2018. Both claims remain before the courts, and the allegations have not been tested at trial. The cases will turn on negligence and evidence. But they expose a deeper structural tension that the courts cannot resolve. There is a gap between what an audit opinion actually asserts and what investors assume it guarantees. The lawsuits concern alleged audit failures. The broader issue, however, exists even where there is no allegation of failure. To see that tension clearly, it helps to separate alleged audit failure from the routine judgements in every set of audited accounts. Serba Dinamik and Sabah Development Bank are outlier cases. The structural issue is visible in ordinary audits of Malaysia’s largest companies, whose auditors have not been accused of anything. Maybank’s FY2025 audited accounts provide one illustration. The auditors identified expected credit losses on loans, advances and financing as a Key Audit Matter (KAM). These assets represent 64.3% of the group’s total assets. The auditors stated that measuring expected credit losses (ECL) “requires the application of significant judgement and increased complexity”, involving forward looking factors, probability weighted scenarios and management overlays. They tested models, challenged assumptions and engaged credit modelling specialists. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. Tenaga Nasional Bhd’s FY2025 statements offer another. Post employment benefit liabilities of RM13.3 billion at group level were valued using actuarial assumptions on salary increases, medical cost inflation and discount rates. The auditors “focused on this area because of the significant estimates made by management”, checked assumptions against historical data and compared discount rates to market yields with valuation experts. They found no material exceptions. The opinion was unqualified. These are not presented as cases of audit failure. The system is working as designed. Yet TNB reports that a one percentage point movement in the discount rate can change its defined benefit obligation by more than RM1 billion. Maybank’s KAM similarly describes extensive audit procedures without showing investors the range of possible outcomes. The KAM explains the judgement, but not how sensitive the number may be. International Standard on Auditing (ISA) 701 requires auditors to communicate KAMs and allow them to highlight matters requiring significant auditor attention, while the opinion remains on the financial statements as a whole. But the framework is binary while uncertainty is not. Two competent valuers may reach different estimates, and a figure can be reasonable without being the only supportable answer. KAMs can therefore become lists of procedures rather than explanations of risk. Estimation uncertainty exists on a continuum while audit reporting remains categorical. The question is not whether KAMs should exist, but whether they tell investors enough about how uncertain the most consequential numbers really are. Malaysia’s Audit Oversight Board has identified “failure to sufficiently review significant risk areas and significant judgements” as a recurring enforcement concern. The International Organization of Securities Commissions (IOSCO) highlighted in its November 2025 statement the importance of high-quality valuation practices, appropriate use of valuation experts and rigorous audit assessment. The International Forum of Independent Audit Regulators (IFIAR) has likewise identified accounting estimates, including fair value measurement, as an area where audit regulators have consistently found deficiencies. When auditors use KAMs to flag a valuation without qualifying the opinion, they are telling investors that the matter involved significant judgement but that the financial statements nevertheless met the requirements for an unmodified opinion. That may be technically correct for Maybank and TNB. But the Serba Dinamik case illustrates how insufficient that signal can be for investors. The concern is not simply whether auditors get the judgement wrong. Even a sound audit can leave investors unable to see how fragile a reasonable estimate may be. That is the gap the current reporting model should address. Four reforms would help. First, require sensitivity disclosure in the KAM. Auditors should disclose the reasonable range of outcomes and its impact on the financial statements. TNB’s statements already include sensitivity analysis on discount rate assumptions. This information should be connected directly to the KAM, rather than leaving investors to piece the implications together from different sections of the annual report. Second, consider graduated reporting for significant estimation uncertainty. Such reporting could signal that an estimate falls within an acceptable range but remains highly sensitive, without implying that there is a material misstatement. The existing Emphasis of Matter framework under ISA 706 could provide a starting point. Third, require independent valuation review for specified material Level 3 assets. A second valuation would provide an additional check on management bias. The auditor could assess the divergence as evidence and consider the additional data point when applying professional scepticism. Fourth, strengthen audit committee disclosure. Audit committees should disclose how they challenged management’s fair value assumptions. If the committee accepted management’s numbers without meaningful scrutiny, that should be visible to shareholders. None of these solutions are radical. Each builds on existing frameworks, including Malaysian Financial Reporting Standard 13 (MFRS 13), ISA 701, ISA 540 and Malaysia’s corporate governance code. They require recognition that the current approach to fair value auditing, while technically sound, is insufficiently transparent for the risks involved. Judgement is unavoidable. Opacity is not. A KAM should do more than say, “we looked at this”. It should help investors understand what drove the estimate, how sensitive it is and what could change the auditor’s assessment. A “clean” audit opinion was never meant to guarantee that every number is right. But as financial statements rely increasingly on complex estimates, audit reporting should show more clearly how uncertain the most consequential numbers are. Hijat A Jabbar and Siti Zabedah Saidin are professors of accounting at Universiti Utara Malaysia. The content is a snapshot from Publisher. Refer to the original content for accurate info. title: 'IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances
body: 'IOI Properties now agrees to buy Shenton House from group CEO for S$1, settle S$217m advances KUALA LUMPUR (Oct 1): IOI Properties Group Bhd (KL:IOIPG) has agreed to acquire Shenton 101 Pte Ltd, which owns Singapore's Shenton House, from its group chief executive officer and major shareholder Datuk Lee Yeow Seng for a nominal S$1.00. Under the deal, announced in a filing with Bursa Malaysia on Thursday, IOI Properties will also settle S$217.06 million (RM696.43 million) worth of shareholder advances (as at July 31, 2026) that Lee had injected into Shenton 101, the vehicle he incorporated to acquire the property. The final repayment sum will be determined on completion. The transaction marks a reversal by the group’s non-interested directors, who turned down an earlier offer from Lee in August 2024, citing heavy capital commitments following several asset acquisitions at the time. To manage potential conflicts of interest, IOI Properties had entered into project and property management agreements for the building instead. Shenton 101 acquired Shenton House — a 25-storey strata-titled commercial development completed in the mid-1970s sitting on a 3,377-sq-metre site — via tender for S$538 million in November 2023, with the purchase completed in June 2024. The vehicle secured S$376.23 million in bank borrowings to finance the acquisition, with the remainder of the purchase price, buyer's stamp duty (S$26.87 million), planning consultation fees and ongoing holding costs funded via interest-free advances from Lee. These existing bank borrowings will be consolidated into IOI Properties' accounts upon completion of the deal. No shareholder approval needed The acquisition, which will be funded through IOI Properties’ internal funds, does not require shareholder approval as its highest percentage ratio is 3.79% — below the 5% threshold under Bursa's listing rules. However, it will require Bank Negara Malaysia's green light as the foreign currency investment exceeds the group's permissible limit, as well as consent from Shenton 101's lenders and the Singapore Land Authority. IOI Properties said the acquisition will allow it to strengthen its presence in Singapore's Marina Bay precinct and unlock synergies with its existing asset portfolio, given Shenton House's walking distance to IOI Central Boulevard Towers and the recently acquired Asia Square Tower 2. The group said it is revisiting the deal, on the request of Lee, after its "circumstances and strategic position have evolved". It pointed out that IOI Central Boulevard Towers has achieved over 95% committed occupancy and is self-sustaining in debt servicing. It has also completed the acquisitions of the remaining 50.1% stake in Scottsdale Properties Pte Ltd — which owns South Beach Tower, South Beach Avenue and JW Marriott Hotel Singapore South Beach — and Asia Square Tower 2. It noted that its acquisitions in Malaysia have also continued to perform satisfactorily, and that shareholders had, on Sept 30, approved injecting W Kuala Lumpur hotel and Courtyard by Marriott Penang hotel into the upcoming IOI Properties REIT, in support of the group's capital recycling strategy. “Although the group’s gearing has increased, the increase is largely attributable to acquisitions of income-generating assets in Singapore that have enhanced the quality of the group's investment property portfolio and strengthened its position in key gateway markets,” it said. Plans for a 35-storey mixed-use landmark The group plans to redevelop Shenton House into a 35-storey mixed-use landmark featuring 12 floors of Grade-A offices, a 10-storey luxury hotel (165 keys), a retail basement and three carpark levels. This will expand its total net lettable area from 20,276 sq metres (218,246 sq ft) to 36,528 sq metres (393,185 sq ft). The underlying land tenure, which has a remaining lease of about 42 years, is expected to be renewed to a fresh 99-year term. Savills appraised the market value of Shenton House as a redevelopment site at S$585 million, with an estimated gross development value of S$1.61 billion against total redevelopment costs of S$973.65 million. Maybank Investment Bank is the principal adviser for the exercise. Although not mandated by listing rules, IOI Properties also appointed Affin Hwang Investment Bank as an independent adviser to advise non-interested directors on the deal's fairness and reasonableness. Lee and his brother Datuk Lee Yeow Chor, who is a non-independent non-executive director, are deemed interested parties and have abstained from all board deliberations and voting on the proposal. The deal is expected to be completed in the fourth quarter of 2026. Shares of IOI Properties closed six sen or 1.73% lower at RM3.40 on Thursday, valuing the group at RM18.72 billion. title: '债息升冲击本地金融业 马银行9个月首跌破10令吉
body: '债息升冲击本地金融业 马银行9个月首跌破10令吉 （吉隆坡1日讯）美国国债收益率持续走高，银行持有债券面对更大的账面亏损压力，加上融资成本可能上升，本地银行股今日普遍走低，马银行（MAYBANK，1155，主板金融股）更跌破10令吉大关，为近9个月来首次。 马银行连续三个交易日下跌，今日收市跌4仙或0.4%，报9令吉95仙；联昌国际（CIMB，1023，主板金融股）及丰隆银行（HLBANK，5819，主板金融股）则双双下跌逾1%。 涵盖保险公司及证券行等非银行金融企业的富时大马金融指数，也跌至10个月来最低水平。 艾芬黄氏投行指出，债券收益率走高通常会对银行造成压力，因为银行持有的债券价格下跌，将导致较大的账面亏损，侵蚀资本；若银行出售有关债券，则必须确认相关亏损。 与此同时，银行也可能需要提高存款利率以吸引存户，进而推高融资成本。 该行今日发布的研究报告指出，这将对银行短期非利息收入及资本充足率造成压力。 美联储上个月上调利率，为3年来首次加息，带动10年期马来西亚政府证券（MGS）收益率一度升至4.18%，随后略为回落。 随着越来越多经济学家预期，国家银行可能在11月举行今年最后一次预定货币政策会议时上调隔夜政策利率（OPR），市场对利率走势的关注进一步升温。 艾芬黄氏投行表示，债券收益率走高通常也会推高企业债券收益率，并影响银行及其他企业的融资决策，进而影响银行所赚取的费用收入。 根据该投行分析，马银行及安联银行（ABMB，2488，主板金融股）的债券组合久期最长。债券久期除了代表债券通过现金流收回成本所需的时间，也反映债券对利率变化的敏感度。 相比之下，大众银行（PBBANK，1295，主板金融股）及丰隆银行的债券组合久期最短。 在资本适足率方面，艾芬投行认为，马银行、兴业银行（RHBBANK，1066，主板金融股）及联昌国际可能面对较大的资本比率跌幅；大众银行及丰隆银行由于债券组合久期较短，所受影响则相对较小。 The content is a snapshot from Publisher. title: 'AHB kekal agihan pendapatan 5.00 sen seunit
body: 'KUALA LUMPUR: Amanah Hartanah Bumiputera (AHB) mengekalkan agihan pendapatan sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit bagi tahun kewangan berakhir 30 September 2026, membabitkan pembayaran keseluruhan RM236.41 juta kepada lebih 82,000 pemegang unit. Agihan itu merangkumi agihan pendapatan akhir sebanyak 2.10 sen seunit bagi tempoh enam bulan berakhir 30 September 2026, selain edaran bonus 0.40 sen seunit yang diumumkan oleh Pelaburan Hartanah Bhd (PHB) selaku penaja dana. Edaran bonus berkenaan diberikan bagi pegangan sehingga satu juta unit pertama bagi setiap pemegang unit, menjadikan jumlah keseluruhan agihan bagi tempoh enam bulan itu sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit. Jumlah berkenaan adalah tambahan kepada agihan interim sebanyak 2.50 sen seunit yang diumumkan pada April lalu, sekali gus menjadikan keseluruhan agihan bagi tahun kewangan 2026 sebanyak 5.00 sen seunit. Pengarah Urusan Kumpulan PHB, Mazuki Abdullah @ Muhammad, berkata prestasi itu mencerminkan daya tahan AHB serta kekuatan portfolio hartanahnya yang disokong pendekatan pengurusan aset dan pelaburan berdisiplin. Beliau berkata, pengumuman penawaran tambahan sebanyak 400 juta unit AHB baru-baru ini juga turut mencerminkan usaha pihaknya dalam memperluas peluang kepada lebih ramai pelabur Bumiputera untuk mengambil bahagian dalam pelaburan hartanah komersial utama. "Kami percaya AHB akan terus memainkan peranan penting dalam menyokong pembentukan kekayaan jangka panjang Bumiputera, di samping menjana nilai mampan kepada pemegang unit. "Kami akan terus memperkukuh kedudukan AHB sebagai instrumen pelaburan pilihan Bumiputera menerusi pengurusan modal berhemat, strategi pelaburan dinamik dan pengoptimuman portfolio secara berterusan bagi memastikan pertumbuhan mampan serta penciptaan nilai jangka panjang," katanya. Mazuki berkata, komitmen itu turut selaras dengan aspirasi Pelan Transformasi Ekonomi Bumiputera 2035 (PUTERA35) yang bertujuan memperkukuh penyertaan ekonomi, pemilikan aset dan pembentukan kekayaan Bumiputera. Sementara itu, Ketua Pegawai Eksekutif PHB Asset Management Bhd (PHBAM), Zulkifli Ishak, berkata pihaknya kekal komited menguruskan AHB secara bertanggungjawab bagi memastikan dana berkenaan terus menjadi pilihan pelaburan yang mudah diakses oleh pelabur Bumiputera. PHB turut berkata, menerusi agihan akhir tahun kewangan 2026, sebanyak RM120.13 juta akan diagihkan kepada pemegang unit dan dikreditkan dalam bentuk unit AHB ke akaun masing-masing selewat-lewatnya pada 13 Oktober ini. "Agihan berkenaan akan dilaburkan semula secara automatik bagi membolehkan pemegang unit meningkatkan pegangan pelaburan serta berpotensi menikmati manfaat pertumbuhan jangka panjang menerusi pengkompaunan," katanya. Pelabur Bumiputera boleh melanggan AHB pada harga tetap RM1 seunit, dengan pelaburan minimum RM100 dan maksimum RM1 juta. Sejak penubuhannya, dana itu sudah mengagihkan sejumlah RM2.7 bilion kepada pemegang unit Bumiputera. Langganan boleh dibuat melalui cawangan pengedar yang sah di seluruh negara, iaitu Malayan Banking Bhd (Maybank), AmBank Bhd, AmBank Islamic Bhd, Bank Islam Malaysia Bhd dan Bank Kerjasama Rakyat Malaysia Bhd.

body: 'The FBM KLCI rebounded 0.4% to 1,651 points on Wednesday after the previous day’s sharp selloff as caution appeared to persist on equities amid a mixed backdrop on the broader Asian markets with rising international bond yields, particularly US 10-year Treasury yields. Construction (+2.07%), Utilities (+0.6%) and Property (+0.4%) led sectoral gains, led by Nestle Malaysia (+1.1%), Tenaga Nasional (+1.9%) and Petronas Gas (+1.3%). Market breadth remained weak, with 695 losers against 410 gainers, while 583 counters were unchanged. Asian markets closed mostly higher on Wednesday, supported by easing oil prices and gains in technology stocks, although elevated US Treasury yields continued to weigh on risk appetite. Japan’s Nikkei 225 rose 1.9% to 66,753.7, Taiwan’s TAIEX gained 0.7% to 47,940.1, Hong Kong’s Hang Seng advanced 0.4% to 24,613.3, and the Shanghai Composite edged up 0.3% to 3,842.2, while South Korea’s KOSPI fell 0.5% to 6,838.0. In South Korea, losses were led by Samsung Electronics (-0.92%), Hyundai Motor (-1.29%), KB Financial Group (-2.42%), Shinhan Financial Group (-3.62%) and Kia Corp (-2.67%), as Samsung Electronics and SK hynix have completed around 80% of their combined KRW55tn share buyback plans, raising concerns that the earlierthan-expected completion could reduce support for KOSPI demand. In China, the latest official and private PMI data offered some relief to investors, with gains led by Industrial and Commercial Bank of China (+1.35%) and Kweichow Moutai (+1.81%), while NAURA Technology (-2.06%) and Suzhou Dongshan Precision Industry (-2.15%) underperformed. European equities ended September under pressure on Wednesday, as elevated global bond yields and persistent inflation concerns weighed on investor sentiment ahead of the final quarter. The STOXX 50 declined 0.8%, while the broader STOXX 600 fell 0.4%, with most sectors ending in negative territory. Banks weakened by around 0.5%, while energy and food & beverage stocks were among the biggest decliners, each losing 1.4%. Technology stocks bucked the broader trend, rising 2.5% to reach their highest level in a month and leading sector gains. US stock indices closed mixed on Wednesday as a rebound in oil prices offset softer-than-expected PCE inflation. The S&P 500 fell 0.3% and Dow lost 444 points, while Nasdaq CI gained 0.2%. Financial and industrial stocks weighed on the broader market amid elevated yields and limited progress in US-Iran peace talks, raising concerns over persistent energy-driven inflation. Meanwhile, easing core PCE inflation supported expectations that the Fed may hold rates steady in October. AI and chip stocks mostly advanced ahead of Micron’s earnings, with Alphabet, Microsoft, Nvidia and Intel gaining 0.9%, 0.8%, 0.5% and 3.7%, respectively. US: 10 Year Treasury Note Yiled rose to 5.3% on Wednesday The US 10-year Treasury yield rose to 5.3% on Wednesday, approaching its highest level since 2002, as the bond market appeared largely unshaken by softer-than-expected inflation data. The PCE price index rose 0.3% in August, below expectations for a 0.4% increase, while core PCE advanced 0.2%, also missing forecasts. Meanwhile, final Q2 GDP data showed the US economy expanded at an annualized rate of 2.2%, up from the earlier estimate of 1.5%, while the ADP report showed private-sector employment growth exceeded expectations in September. (Trading Economics) US: Oil Steadies as Middle East Uncertainty Persists Crude oil steadied above $90 per barrel on Thursday after rising in the previous session, as investors weighed signs of a recovery in Middle East flows against an ongoing impasse in US-Iran negotiations. Crude shipments from the region were nearing pre-war levels after Saudi Arabia restored half the capacity of its East-West pipeline, while flows through the Strait of Hormuz climbed to 13.2 million barrels per day. However, markets remain cautious about the durability of the recovery without a lasting agreement to end the Iran war, with both Tehran and Washington claiming full control over the strategic waterway. (Trading Economics) US: PCE Inflation Rises Less Than Expected The US PCE price index rose 0.3% month-over-month in August 2026, following a downwardly revised 0.1% gain in July and slightly below market expectations of 0.4%. Goods prices increased 0.3%, rebounding from a 0.1% decline in July, led by a 0.5% rise in nondurable goods, mainly due to a 4.4% jump in gasoline and other energy goods prices. Durable goods inflation, meanwhile, eased to 0.1% from 0.4%. Services prices also accelerated to 0.3% from 0.1%, driven mainly by higher transportation services (1.4%) and food services and accommodations (0.5%). (U.S. Bureau of Economic Analysis) US: Goods trade deficit widens sharply in August The US trade deficit in goods widened sharply in August amid a surge in imports, suggesting that trade could remain a drag economic growth in the third quarter. The goods trade shortfall increased 11.5% to US$132.6 billion (RM541.2 billion) last month, the Commerce Department's Census Bureau said on Wednesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the goods deficit at US$115.0 billion. (Reuters) US: Inflation rises less than expected in August; consumer spending surges US inflation increased less than expected in August, which could see financial markets further reduce the odds of another interest rate increase from the Federal Reserve next month. The Personal Consumption Expenditures Price Index rose 0.3% last month after a downwardly revised 0.1% gain in July, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said on Wednesday. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast the PCE price index rising 0.4% after a previously reported 0.2% gain in July. (Reuters) US: Second-quarter GDP revised higher amid robust consumer spending The US economy grew at a solid clip in the second quarter, driven by robust consumer spending and business investment related to the buildout of AI infrastructure. Gross domestic product increased at a 2.2% annualised rate, revised up from the previously estimated 1.5% pace, the Commerce Department's Bureau of Economic Analysis said in its third estimate of second-quarter GDP on Wednesday. (Reuters) US: Mortgage rates rise to almost three-year high of 7.3% US mortgage rates climbed for a sixth straight week to an almost three-year high, thwarting would-be homebuyers. The contract rate on a 30- year fixed mortgage rose 18 basis points in the week ended Sept 25 to 7.30%, the highest since November 2023, according to Mortgage Bankers Association figures released Wednesday. (Bloomberg) US: Private payrolls growth picks up in September, ADP says US private payrolls growth accelerated in September, the ADP National Employment Report showed on Wednesday. Private employment rose by 90,000 jobs this month after a downwardly revised 36,000 in August. Economists polled by Reuters had forecast private employment increased by 70,000 after a previously reported 38,000 advance in August. (Bloomberg) US: Dollar enjoys best month since June on Fed's inflation fight The dollar is wrapping up its best month since June after the Federal Reserve’s renewed focus on taming inflation pushed interest-rate expectations and US bond yields higher. The Bloomberg Dollar Spot Index has risen 1.8% in September, touching the highest level in two months. Solid US economic data and heightened inflation risks have been lifting the currency. (Bloomberg) UK: Inflation jumps across eurozone, raising pressure on ECB to hike Inflation rose far quicker than expected in some of the eurozone's biggest economies this month due to the energy-price shock of the Iran war, increasing pressure on the European Central Bank to raise interest rates again. The ECB has lifted rates twice this year to prevent rapid price growth from getting embedded, and investors have sharply raised rate hike bets in the past few weeks as natural gas, petrol and diesel prices have all soared. (Reuters) UK: Economy grew faster than thought in 2Q, cementing G7 lead Britain's economy grew more quickly than previously thought in the second quarter, consolidating its position as the fastest-growing Group of Seven (G7) economy in the first half of 2026 before Finance Minister John Healey's first budget in October. Economic output expanded by 0.5% in the April-to-June period, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said on Wednesday. (Reuters) CN: Biggest stimulus push since 2024 fails to impress market China’s latest economic stimulus package appears designed to keep economic growth on target rather than deliver a broad revival, underwhelming investors who worry it’s leaving the country’s underlying demand weakness largely unaddressed. Government agencies unveiled mortgage subsidies and expanded central bank support for targeted sectors after markets closed Tuesday. The State Council, China’s cabinet, pledged a day earlier to introduce “a package of practical and effective additional policies” to meet this year’s economic and social development goals. (Bloomberg) CN: Factory activity expands in September amid AI boom China's factory activity expanded in September, official and private surveys showed on Wednesday, as easing weather disruptions allowed factories to resume operations and a global AI boom supported the industrial sector. But the recovery remains uneven, as weak consumption and investment continue to weigh on the outlook. (Reuters) CN: Central bank announces enhanced financial support for economy The People's Bank of China (PBOC), China's central bank, announced a raft of strengthened support measures on Tuesday, including making adjustments to several monetary policy tools in an effort to promote innovation-driven, high-quality and sound economic development. The new measures included cutting the one-year interest rate of the Pledged Supplementary Lending (PSL) facility from 1.75 percent to 1.5 percent to better incentivise policy banks to support the real economy and serve national strategies. (The Star) JP: Foreigners in Japan on skilled worker visa hit record high The number of foreign nationals in Japan working under a government programme aimed at stemming staff shortages in certain sectors hit a record high, according to data released by the government on Tuesday. As of June, 444,256 people resided in Japan as part of the “Specified Skilled Worker” programme, a 13.8% increase from the end of December. (Bloomberg) JP: Yen strengthens past 157 per dollar, outperforming G-10 peers The yen outperformed all its Group-of-10 peers on Wednesday as a series of government warnings on the currency and quarter-end flows provided support. Japan’s currency strengthened as much as 0.6% to 156.38 before paring some of the gains and trading at 156.97 at 3.45pm local time (2.45pm in Malaysia). It also rose as much as 0.6% against the euro and 0.9% against the Australian dollar. (Bloomberg) MY: Ringgit opens lower against major currencies, US dollar The ringgit opened lower against major currencies including the US dollar on Wednesday as weaker US consumer data weighed on investor sentiment and reduced risk appetite in the foreign exchange market. At 8.02am, the ringgit edged down to 4.0795/4.0850 against the greenback from Tuesday’s close of 4.0790/4.0850. (Bernama) MY: Among 6 Apac economies set to grow faster than China in 2026 Malaysia is among six major Asia-Pacific (Apac) economies expected to record faster real GDP growth than China in 2026, with its growth supported by integration into the artificial intelligence supply chain, according to Moody’s Analytics. In its “Asia-Pacific Outlook: RAMpocalypse Now” report, Moody’s Analytics said Taiwan, Singapore, Malaysia, India, Vietnam and Indonesia are projected to grow faster than China this year. (Free Malaysia Today) SOLID: Co-founder Ker Boon Kee transfers shares to children, son Keddy emerges as second-largest shareholder One of the brothers who co-founded Solid Automotive Bhd, Ker Boon Kee, has transferred his shares in the company to his children, making his son and executive director Ker Keddy the company’s second-largest shareholder. Boon Kee made off-market transfers of 48.44 million shares, or his entire 9.33% interest in the company, to his four children on Sept 29. This included the transfer of 12.11 million shares, equivalent to a 2.33% stake, to Keddy. (The Edge) WILLOW: Unit scores second win this week with RM25m in Singapore deals amid divestment Willowglen MSC Bhd has secured RM24.9 million in contracts, its second win within a week, through its soon-to-be divested Singapore subsidiary Willowglen Services Pte Ltd. In a bourse filing, Willowglen said wholly‑owned subsidiary Willowglen Services has been awarded two contracts by SP PowerAssets Ltd to maintain supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems in cable tunnels in Singapore. (The Edge) BKAWAN: Takeover of MKH crosses 95% Batu Kawan Bhd’s unconditional mandatory takeover of MKH Bhd has crossed the 95% threshold, paving the way for the property developer’s delisting. As at market close on Wednesday, Batu Kawan and its wholly owned unit Whitmore Holdings Sdn Bhd, together with parties acting in concert, held 548.85 million MKH shares, representing a 95.16% stake, according to a statement issued on their behalf by Maybank Investment Bank Bhd. (The Edge) ZETRIX: IPVG Employees extend deadline of MyEG Ventures deal by three months Zetrix AI Bhd and IPVG Employees Inc have agreed to extend by three months the deadline to complete the Malaysian company's purchase of a 50% stake in Philippines-based MyEG Ventures Inc. The digital services provider said in a bourse filing that both sides agreed to complete the share purchase agreement at the end of the fourth quarter. (The Edge) DFX: Wins RM120m data centre equipment jobs in Penang Divfex Bhd said it has secured two contracts worth RM120.12 million to supply equipment for a 15MW data centre fit-out in Penang. Under agreements signed on Wednesday, its wholly owned subsidiary Diversified Gateway Bhd will supply generator sets, transformers, switchgear and low-voltage equipment worth RM84.44 million, while 51%-owned Excel Commerce Solutions Sdn Bhd will supply RM35.67 million worth of cables. (The Edge) CHGP: Exits commercial vehicle business in RM62m cash deal Chin Hin Group Property Bhd is selling its entire equity interest in four loss-making subsidiaries involved in the commercial vehicle and bodyworks business for a combined RM62 million in cash, to focus on its property development business. In a bourse filing on Wednesday, CHGP said it entered into a share sale agreement with HSG Sdn Bhd for the disposal of Boon Koon Vehicles Industries Sdn Bhd, BKCV Sdn Bhd, Boon Koon Fleet Management Sdn Bhd and BK Fleet Management Sdn Bhd. (The Edge) IOIPG: Expands hospitality pipeline with four new Marriott hotels totalling 888 rooms IOI Properties Group Bhd and Marriott International Inc have expanded their strategic relationship with the signing of a portfolio deal for four new hotels in Malaysia. According to a press statement issued on Sept 30, the hotel deal comprises W Langkawi; The Ritz-Carlton, Putrajaya; Aloft by Marriott Sepang and Aloft by Marriott Johor Bahru Plentong, with a total of 888 rooms. (The Edge) EXSIMHB: Bags construction subcontracts from Taghill Exsim Hospitality Bhd said on Wednesday that it has secured three subcontracts worth RM27 million for construction works. In a bourse filing, the group said its subsidiary Exsim Concepto Sdn Bhd, which specialises in fit-out services for hospitality property assets, was awarded the subcontracts by Taghill Projects Sdn Bhd, a wholly-owned unit of Taghill Holdings Bhd. (The Edge) ASTRO: Forex losses, lower subscription revenue pull Astro into the red Astro Malaysia Holdings Bhd sank into the red in the May-July quarter — its first quarterly loss since late 2023 — dragged by unrealised foreign exchange losses while its top line declined on lower subscription revenue. The group recorded a net loss of RM25.80 million for the second quarter ended July 31, 2026 (2QFY2027), from a net profit of RM16.39 million a year earlier, while revenue dropped 7.24% to RM633.75 million from RM683.21 million, a bourse filing showed on Wednesday. (The Edge) VIS: Hits 3½-year high after quarterly earnings turnaround VisDynamics Holdings Bhd shares on Wednesday opened at 53.5 sen, its highest level since March 2023, after the automated test equipment maker reported a sharp improvement in earnings. The level is up 11.5 sen or 27.38% from Tuesday’s close of 42 sen. The counter later pared some of its gains, hovering between 47.5 sen and 53.5 sen. (The Edge) PTT: Buys industrial land in Klang from Sime Darby Property Industrial construction and automated logistics company PTT Synergy Group Bhd is acquiring four parcels of land with a combined area of 8,778 square metres in Bandar Bukit Raja, Klang for RM32 million in cash. PTT Synergy is buying the freehold industrial properties from Sime Darby Property (Bukit Raja) Sdn Bhd, a wholly-owned subsidiary of Sime Darby Property Bhd, according to a bourse filing on Wednesday. (The Edge) KLK: Coalfields Retail Park scheduled to reach 100% occupancy by 1Q2027 KLK Land Sdn Bhd's newly soft-opened Coalfields Retail Park in Sungai Buloh is scheduled to achieve 100% occupancy by 1Q2027, according to a press statement issued on Tuesday. The lifestyle retail hub, developed by the property development arm of Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd, spans 21 acres with approximately one million square feet of gross built-up area. (The Edge) NEXG: Gets shareholders' nod to revert to Datasonic name Shareholders of NexG Bhd, Malaysia’s sole supplier of passport booklets and MyKad identity cards, approved the company’s proposed name change back to Datasonic Group Bhd at its annual general meeting on Wednesday. In a statement, NexG said the name change supports its ambitions to pursue new opportunities globally. It will take effect upon the issuance of the notice of registration of new name by the Companies Commission of Malaysia (SSM). (The Edge) HENGYUAN: Drops sharply after recent rally, stock still up over 360% Hengyuan Refining Company Bhd fell over 20% in morning trade on Wednesday, prompting a suspension in the intraday short selling of the stock. The counter fell as much as 92 sen to RM3.42 from Tuesday’s close of RM4.34, nearly erasing gains made by the petrochemical company in the last two weeks. Hengyuan pared its losses to close at RM3.56 — down 78 sen or 18% from the previous day — giving it a market capitalisation of RM2.14 billion. The stock is still up over 360% year-to-date. (The Edge) YTLPOWR: How much more upside for YTL Power? YTL Power International Bhd’s share price has risen by 72.7% year to date. The gains come as its data centre (DC) segment has begun reporting standalone earnings, while its water and sewerage segment has strengthened and power generation has shown signs of stabilisation. In addition, speculation about a potential spin-off or listing of its DC segment has likely added to the group’s re-rating. The only question now is whether there is a ceiling for YTL Power’s share price gains. Analysts think the stock has more room to run. (The Edge) KIPREIT: Adds 20th property with RM435m Setapak Central Mall purchase, eyes 7.2% yield KIP Real Estate Investment Trust acquired its 20th property with the completion of its RM435 million acquisition of Setapak Central Mall, which delivers an attractive yield of 7.2%. The new addition lifted its total net lettable area by approximately 16% to 3.8 million sq ft and boosted the REIT’s total assets under management to RM2.2 billion, surpassing its RM2 billion target for 2027, according to a press statement issued on Wednesday. (The Edge) PBBANK: Declares distributions of over RM61m for two funds Public Bank Bhd’s wholly-owned subsidiary, Public Mutual Bhd, has declared distributions totalling more than RM61 million for two funds for the financial year ended Sept 30, 2026. In a statement today, Public Mutual said the gross distributions comprised 3.25 sen per unit for the Public Enterprises Bond Fund and 0.80 sen per unit for the Public Institutional Bond Fund. (The Edge) GAMUDA: Hits 10-month high on renewable energy venture with SD Guthrie Gamuda Bhd hit a 10-month high on Wednesday after its joint venture with SD Guthrie Bhd (KL:SDG) and Gentari Sdn Bhd signed a term sheet with a US-based technology company for a 680MW renewable energy project in Perak. Gamuda shares rose as much as 30 sen or 6% to RM5.28, their highest level since Nov 27, 2025. The counter later ended at RM5.18, still up 4%, with more than 87 million shares changing hands, valuing the group at RM31.3 billion. (The Edge) UWC: Ends FY2026 with record numbers as 4Q profit more than doubles UWC Bhd achieved record performance for its financial year 2026, following a more than doubling of its fourth quarter earnings. Net profit for the fourth quarter ended July 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) surged to RM37.6 million, 129.7% more than the RM16.37 million it recorded in the corresponding quarter a year earlier, as revenue jumped 71.1% to RM186.18 million from RM108.8 million, its bourse filing on Wednesday showed. In its bourse filing on Wednesday, the energy solutions provider said it made a net loss of RM5.64 million for the quarter ended July 31, 2026 (4QFY2026) compared with a net profit of RM5.38 million a year ago. (The Edge) YINSON: Posts 27% rise in 2Q amid absence of refinancing charge Yinson Holdings Bhd said its net profit for the second quarter grew 26.7% year-on-year amid the absence of a one-off charge related to the refinancing of the floating production storage and offloading (FPSO) Maria Quitéria project financing loan. Shares of HFC jumped to around 600 yuan from their initial public offering (IPO) price of 76.86 yuan per share at the opening bell, before hitting an intraday high of 630.01 yuan. The stock then retreated to 613 yuan at Tuesday’s noon break. title: 'Daily Brief - 29 Sep 2026
body: 'The local stock market traded sideways with slight downward bias on Monday, as subdued domestic catalysts and heightened global uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The FBM KLCI inched down by 1.60 points to close at 1,670.02, off an low of 1,668.61 and high of 1,674.11, as losers led gainers 748 to 388, on total turnover of 3.11bn shares worth RM2.40bn. Uncertainty surrounding Middle East tensions and persistent inflationary pressures is likely to continue clouding the outlook for the local market. Immediate support for the index stays at the June 2026 low (1,655), with stronger support coming from the 76.4%FR (1,610) and 61.8%FR (1,564). Meanwhile, immediate resistance is maintained at the June 2026 high (1,722), followed by tougher upside hurdles at the 123.6%FP (1,759) and 138.2%FP (1,805) ahead. Any weakness on Maybank shares towards the 38.2%FR (RM9.74) or the 23.6%FR (RM9.27) should encourage buying on weakness ahead of recovery upside towards the 76.4%FR (RM10.96) with next resistance coming from the 25/02/26 high (RM11.71). Sime Darby shares remain in base building mode pending recovery to the 123.6%FP (RM2.67), with a confirmed breakout to aim for the 138.2%FP (RM2.82) and 150%FP (RM2.94), while immediate chart supports are from the 30-day ma (RM2.45) and 76.4%FR (RM2.19). Asian markets traded mixed on Monday as uncertainty over the Middle East weighed on sentiment, following U.S. President Donald Trump’s rejection of Iran’s proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. Over the weekend, US President Donald Trump rejected an Iranian proposal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, claiming Tehran was desperate to make a deal. Trump said talks would continue this week, though Iran shows no sign of watering down its proposals. Rates will be in focus again this week, with a slew of key economic data on deck. The August personal consumption expenditure price index, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, is due on Wednesday. New U.S. manufacturing numbers are due Thursday, while the closely watched September jobs report is set for release Friday. Central banks have responded with a round of rate hikes, with the Reserve Bank of Australia likely to be the next to tighten when it meets on Tuesday. Australia’s S&P/ASX 200 gained 0.17% to 8,679.70, while South Korea’s Kospi slumped 2.70% to 6,889.74. In Japan, the Nikkei 225 fell 0.73% to 65,877.62 and the Topix lost 0.40% to 4,112.00. In the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index dropped 1.67% to 3,823.62, while Hong Kong’s Hang Seng Index gained 0.54% to 24,642.51. Wall Street closed lower overnight as renewed US-Iran tensions pushed oil prices higher, while rising Treasury yields added pressure ahead of a week packed with key economic data. The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 0.67% to 51,481.51. The S&P 500 slipped 0.77% to 7,683.69, while the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.92% to 26,820.38. Crude oil prices initially surged after US President Donald Trump rejected a peace proposal from Iran but gains later eased as hopes grew that Qatari mediators could help bring the two sides back to the negotiating table. Iran presented the proposal during last week’s United Nations General Assembly in New York and said it had been conveyed to the United States through Qatar. With officials back at the negotiating table, Trump told Axios that US negotiators were expected to continue discussions with Iran this week. Meanwhile, a packed week of inflation and labour market data awaits investors. From the Personal Consumption Expenditures report on Wednesday to the monthly employment report on Friday, investors will find new insights on the health of the economy. Expectations for a rate hike from the Fed at its October meeting have climbed in recent d ays, in part due to economic data indicating the economy was growing at a solid pace. Gamuda Bhd said on Monday it secured an A$790mn (RM2.3bn) engineering, procurement and construction (EPC) contract in Australia to develop the first stage of the Mortlake Energy Hub. (The Edge) KKB Engineering Bhd (Not Rated) secured RM462mn in new contracts from Sarawak Shell and other customers, including a major offshore EPC project for the SK408 TeJa & Populus and Temu & Inai field developments. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) Willowglen MSC Bhd (Not Rated) secured a RM108mn, 8-year-11-month systems contract through its Singapore subsidiary, which is currently being divested as part of its proposed RM215.2mn disposal to Elixir II. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) AWC Bhd (Not Rated) has secured two contracts from Gujarat International Finance TecCity Co Ltd (GIF) in relation to upcoming developments in the Domestic Tariff Area and Special Economic Zone areas in Gujarat International Finance Tec-City, Gandhinagar, Gujarat, India, for a combined sum of RM13.1mn. (The Star) HSS Engineers Bhd’s (Not Rated) associate HSSI secured a RM11.0mn, 42-month engineering consultancy and site supervision contract for sewage treatment plant upgrades in Negeri Sembilan and Melaka. (The Star) Hap Seng Consolidated Bhd (Not Rated) agreed to dispose of its 50.82% stake in Hafary for RM447mn, realising an estimated RM187.3mn gross gain, with proceeds earmarked for partial repayment of its borrowings. (The Edge/Bursa Malaysia) AYER Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) proposed to acquire 9.11 acres of freehold land in Jalan Kuchai Lama for RM138mn, at a 4.8% discount to valuation, for future development, funded 20% internally and 80% through bank borrowings. (The Edge/ Bursa Malaysia) Sunsuria Bhd (Not Rated) proposed to dispose of 183,973 sq m of freehold commercial land in Sepang to Amazon Data Services Malaysia for RM316.8mn. (The Star) GUH Holdings Bhd (Not Rated)received the final RM23.7mn compensation payment from the Suzhou government, completing the RM114.9mn disposal of its industrial land and paving the way for the recognition of a RM95.3mn gain. (The Edge) Kinergy Advancement Bhd (Not Rated) founder Datuk Dr Lai Keng Onn acquired a 20.02% stake in Avangaad Bhd (Not Rated) for RM69.6mn, raising his direct holding to 23.08% and making him the marine vessels operator’s largest shareholder, alongside his existing 51% indirect interest. (The Edge) Willowglen MSC Bhd (Not Rated) shareholders have been advised to approve the proposed RM215.2mn disposal of its core remote building automation businesses to Elixir II, which is deemed fair and reasonable and would allow Willowglen to retain a 37.8% stake in Elixir II while unlocking value and funding a 5 sen/share dividend. (The Edge) IHH Healthcare Bhd (Not Rated) reiterated that its 2018 Fortis Healthcare investment was conducted through a transparent and fully regulated bidding process, while it will cooperate with the ongoing forensic audit following the Indian Supreme Court ruling. (Bernama/ The Star) Zetrix AI Bhd’s (Not Rated) external auditor TGS TW PLT resigned, citing portfolio rationalisation and resource management, with the company to appoint a new auditor within the required 21-day notice period. (The Edge) Aumas Resources Bhd (Not Rated) CEO Chong Tzu Khen has been placed on administrative leave after being charged with three counts of alleged bribery involving RM18,000, while the company said its mining operations will continue under senior management. (The Edge) Poh Kong Holdings Bhd (Not Rated) posted a record FY2026, with net profit surging 59.7% YoY to RM193.4mn on 14.5% higher revenue, driven by stronger gold prices and margins, while proposing a higher 5 sen final dividend. (The Edge) RedPlanet Bhd (Not Rated) launched its ACE Market IPO at 19 sen/share, aiming to raise RM15.2mn, with RM13.3mn earmarked mainly for expansion, project procurement, working capital and business development ahead of its scheduled listing on Oct 22. (The Edge) PESB Bhd (Not Rated), an electrical engineering specialist with RM35.2mn FY25 net profit, has filed for an ACE Market IPO to fund capacity expansion, project performance bonds and working capital amid rising demand for power infrastructure driven by data centre growth. (The Edge) Thong World Bhd (Not Rated), operator of the Thong Bowl restaurant chain, plans an ACE Market IPO of 176.8mn shares to fund outlet expansion and its packaged food segment. (The Star) Malaysia’s Producer Price Index (PPI) local production rose by 10.7% in August 2026, compared to a 9.7% increase in July 2026, said the Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM). In its PPI Local Production report for August 2026, DOSM said the mining sector jumped by 41.2% in August 2026, up from 30.5% in July 2026, driven by the extraction of crude petroleum and natural gas, which rose by 49.8% and 14.7%, respectively. “The manufacturing sector increased by 8.8%, compared to 8.2% in the preceding month, mainly driven by the manufacture of coke and refined petroleum products (33.5%) and the manufacture of computer, electronic and optical products (12.4%),” it said in a statement. The agriculture, forestry and fishing sector also increased by 4.6%, although this moderated from the 7.2% growth recorded in July 2026, with animal production registering an increase of 13.9%. The utility-related sectors also continue their upward trend, with water supply and electricity and gas supply increasing by 7.8% and 6.4%, respectively. (The Edge, Bernama) Any decision on a possible increase in the minimum wage to RM2,000 should be left to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s announcement when tabling Budget 2027, Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said. He said the impact of any adjustment, particularly on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs), would also need to be taken into consideration to ensure employers could sustain higher operating costs. “We are taking into account several segments and how implementation can be balanced so that we can continue to look after our workers while ensuring the sustainability of employers, particularly small businesses and MSMEs,” he told reporters after visiting the Kluang District Police Headquarters (IPD) quarters here on Monday. (The Edge, Bernama) The Federation of Malaysian Manufacturing (FMM) has called for any review of the minimum wage to be negotiated through the National Wages Consultative Council’s tripartite process, with factors including productivity, cost of living and employers’ capacity to pay taken into account. The statement follows Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s comments that the government will announce more decisive measures on wages in Budget 2027, to be tabled on Oct 9. FMM president Jacob Lee Chor Kok said employers recognise the need for better wages, but the ability to absorb higher payroll costs varies between companies. “Many larger firms already pay above the statutory minimum wage, while smaller manufacturers and labourintensive businesses generally have less room to absorb a sudden increase in payroll costs,” said Lee in the statement. Profits of a small number of highly successful corporations should not be taken as representative of the wider business community, with Lee noting that micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) accounted for 96.1% of business establishments in 2024, based on figures from SME Corporation Malaysia. (The Edge) The Malaysian Automotive Association (MAA) is proposing that the government provide a personal income tax rebate for the purchase of electrified vehicles (xEVs) and voluntarily scrapping of old vehicles in Budget 2027. MAA president Mohd Shamsor Mohd Zain said the association is suggesting a personal income tax rebate of between RM7,000 and RM10,000 to accelerate the mainstream adoption of xEVs, particularly among middle-income taxpayers keen on xEVs but sensitive to the price. The MAA proposal was submitted to the Ministry of Finance recently, he told Bernama. Mohd Shamsor said there is no direct purchase subsidy or tax rebate currently available for xEV buyers, citing that the existing relief is mainly limited to charging equipment. Mohd Shamsor said the MAA proposed that the government extend the existing RM2,500 individual income tax relief for home charging expenses beyond 2027. (The Edge, Bernama) Malaysia's financial markets adjusted in an orderly manner despite external pressures, and conditions remain conducive for corporates to raise funds, Bank Negara Malaysia's Financial Markets Committee (FMC) said. In a statement on Monday following the FMC's meeting on Sept 21, the committee cited sound economic fundamentals and strong foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows for the resilience of the domestic market. It said United States Federal Reserve rate hikes that led to a stronger US dollar and higher US Treasury yields were main drivers of recent market movements. “Nevertheless, the domestic financial markets continued to adjust in an orderly manner, supported by balanced two-way flows that ensured effective price intermediation among market participants,” said the FMC. The committee noted strong interest in corporate bond issuance and increased hedging as the ringgit moderated in September after being relatively stable in July and August, and increased Malaysian Government Security yields after remaining flat for a prolonged period. (The Edge, BNM) China and the United States have agreed to cut tariffs imposed on US$60bn worth of goods imported from each other, on an array of products ranging from US corn to cosmetics, and from Chinese household appliances to toys. Under the US-China Board of Trade, both countries have each recommended US$30bn of trade in non-sensitive goods for more favourable tariff treatment, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement on Sunday. For the United States, that was "unlocking improved market access" for about 30% of US exports to China, he said. The reciprocal tariff reduction as well as an extension of a trade truce were among the key takeaways from the second summit this year between President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, hosted in Washington last week. One of two lists from the White House showed that China planned to trim duties on a variety of US agricultural goods including corn, wheat, sorghum, meat, dairy, vegetable oils and meals. It did not include soybeans. Beijing will also look to reduce levies on US fish and seafood, logs and wood products, cosmetics and medical devices. (Reuters) China's industrial profit growth slowed further in August as strength in technology manufacturing amid the AI boom was outweighed by persistently weak domestic demand. Firms are increasingly struggling to maintain pricing power due to soft consumption and excess capacity in some sectors. Profits at China's industrial firms in August rose 4.2% from a year earlier, down from 11.2% in July, while profit increased 15.7% in the first eight months, easing from 17.6% in the January-July period, National Bureau of Statistics (NBS) data showed on Monday. Profits in computer, communication and other electronic equipment manufacturing led the gains, jumping 110% in the first eight months, according to a breakdown of NBS data. By contrast, the wine, beverages and refined tea manufacturing industry was among the worst performers, with profits falling 34.7%. (Reuters) White House National Economic Council Director Kevin Hassett suggested that, while the US economy is now on track for strong growth, “outside” factors could get in the way of the administration’s hopes for at least a 3% expansion rate. Given gains in US productivity and wages, economic growth “should be cruising around 4% instead of 3%,” Hassett said to the Economic Club of New York in an event Monday. He said that was his “sort of base case — no disruptions from the outside world.” While administration officials including Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent have targeted a 3% sustained pace for gross domestic product gains during President Donald Trump’s current term in office, private economists expect growth closer to 2%. The artificial intelligence investment boom has supported GDP gains in recent quarters, but economists point to a slowdown in labour-force growth as a key headwind. Turning to the fiscal outlook, Hassett also indicated that complications — which he didn’t spell out — could thwart achieving the target of a 3% budget gap as a ratio of GDP that Bessent has laid out. (Bloomberg) US President Donald Trump said he is still looking “very seriously” at implementing a US ban on diesel exports to combat high prices, even as others in his administration continue to focus on other possible steps. “That can oftentimes lead to a little bit of an increase on gasoline for cars, so we’re looking at it very seriously — we may do it,” Trump told a Fox News reporter on Sunday while attending the Presidents Cup golf tournament final near Chicago. Several farm-state lawmakers have urged Trump to limit US diesel exports during the peak of the fall harvest season, as global fuel markets reel from the disruption to flows in the critical Strait of Hormuz and Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries. The US has emerged as the supplier of last resort to the world, with diesel exports surging to a weekly record near two million barrels a day last month. National Economic Council director Kevin Hassett, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer have been analysing the ramifications of a potential short-term ban on US diesel exports over the last week, underscoring the seriousness of the administration’s consideration of the idea. (Bloomberg) Rising bond yields will curb economic expansion and limit the transfer of elevated energy costs to inflation, European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde said. “While growth has been resilient, since our last meeting long-term interest rates have risen notably, which will slow growth and reduce pass-through by more than projected in our September exercise,” Lagarde said Monday. With second-round effects so far absent, that means the ECB should adopt a “measured response as appropriate to keep inflation in check,” she told European lawmakers in Brussels. Traders pared monetary-tightening bets and now see a less than 40% chance of a hike by the ECB next month. ECB officials are weighing the need for further interest-rate increases to bring inflation under control and avoid higher energy costs spilling into broader prices and wage demands. As well as the conflict in the Middle East, they’re grappling with a global bond-market selloff that’s a particular worry for some fiscally strained members of the euro zone. body: 'The local stock market traded sideways with slight downward bias on Monday, as subdued domestic catalysts and heightened global uncertainty weighed on investor sentiment. The FBM KLCI inched down by 1.60 points to close at 1,670.02, off an low of 1,668.61 and high of 1,674.11, as losers led gainers 748 to 388, on total turnover of 3.11bn shares worth RM2.40bn. Uncertainty surrounding Middle East tensions and persistent inflationary pressures is likely to continue clouding the outlook for the local market. title: 'F1 Singapore Grand Prix value proposition still strong after 18 years
body: 'SINGAPORE – For 18 years, Singapore has marketed its Formula 1 Grand Prix not just as a motor race, but as a showcase of what the Lion City can do when it turns several kilometres of floodlit roads along the waterfront at dusk into a global stage.  Since September 2008, the Marina Bay Street Circuit has become one of the most iconic events on the F1 calendar, offering something no other city did – the first-ever night race.  The spectacle helped establish Singapore as a distinctive stop on the F1 calendar, while giving the city-state a high-profile platform to promote its hospitality industry, infrastructure, business environment and ability to stage a complex international event.  Now, a few countries in the region are seeking to replicate Singapore’s success and join the F1 bandwagon in hopes of global attention and attracting high-spending visitors.  After a nine-year hiatus, Malaysia is set to host an F1 race in Sepang again in October, while Thailand is targeting a street race in Bangkok’s Chatuchak area as early as 2028.  The emergence of new Asian contenders raises questions about whether the Singapore Grand Prix can continue to distinguish itself or if fans will be drawn away to rival races.  Market observers and economists believe it can.  “F1 is still delivering benefits to Singapore that outweigh the cost of hosting the event,” said Brian Lee, an economist at Maybank.  “While the direct tourism benefits may face diminishing returns, the race remains valuable as a platform for attracting high-spending visitors, business events and global capital,” he added.  He noted that the 2025 F1 race weekend drew a sell-out crowd of more than 300,000 fans. That was the second-highest attendance in the event’s history and an almost 12 per cent jump from 2024, suggesting the novelty remained.  Guy Llewellyn, academic director for Asia-Pacific at EHL Hospitality Business School, said it would be hard for other cities to replicate Singapore’s experience after it has run the event for 18 years, coordinating different stakeholders and building a strong international reputation.  “Singapore’s strategy has gradually evolved from hosting a sporting event to hosting a citywide festival. The concerts, entertainment zones, dining experiences, and new Barge Stage programming mean that visitors can spend an entire day in Marina Bay without focusing exclusively on racing,” the assistant professor said.  The Barge Stage waterfront amphitheatre will be unveiled in 2026 along with a line-up of international DJs.  “Few destinations can offer a Formula 1 circuit, internationally branded hotels, fine dining, nightlife and entertainment venues all within walking distance of one another,” Llewellyn said.  However, while being the first night race was once a powerful differentiator, the novelty naturally fades over time, making the broader ecosystem increasingly important in setting the experience apart, he added.  Faizal Yahya, senior research fellow at the Institute of Policy Studies at NUS’ Lee Kuan Yew School of Public Policy, also believes the race should go on.  The returns have been “a massive net positive”, as Singapore has gained a lot economically, strategically, and in terms of its global image, Yahya said.  From the inaugural night race in 2008 until 2024, the event generated around $2.2 billion in incremental tourism receipts, mostly for accommodation, attraction tickets, food and beverage, shopping and airfares. It also attracted more than 720,000 visitors over the period.  Lee said that this is equivalent to $129 million a year in incremental spending from tourists attending the race. That is 0.4 per cent of Singapore’s 2025 aggregate tourism receipts.  While this may be close to the $140 million annual cost of organising the race, there are other beneficiaries that are not captured by the tourism receipt figures.  These include companies involved in the track and venue setup, advertising and others that support the event, ranging from raw material suppliers, equipment rental, logistics and even laundry and cleaning services, Lee said.  Beyond grandstand ticket sales, F1’s ripple effect extends to drawing other high-profile events around the race period.  Every year, about 25 to 30 international conferences – including the Forbes Global CEO Conference, the Milken Institute Asia Summit and TOKEN2049 – have been held around race week, bringing in around 90,000 C-suites to Singapore.  High-net-worth travellers, who make up 30 per cent of F1 visitors, account for 40 per cent of tourist spending during race week, pushing up occupancy rates and hotel room rates even outside the race vicinity.  A large share of the race’s contracts is subcontracted to Singapore-based small and medium-sized enterprises, including firms in engineering, construction and hospitality, the Ministry of Energy, Trade and Industry (METI) said.  About 30,000 staff, contractors and stakeholders work on each race. More than 1,000 students from the Institute of Technical Education and polytechnics are also trained each year for roles around the circuit, giving them exposure to the organisation of a major international event.  “This creates temporary employment for over 30,000 workers and students across logistics, advanced engineering, hospitality and specialised event staging,” Yahya said.  With millions of people around the world watching the Singapore race on television and online, the event is a global advertisement for the Republic, showcasing its infrastructure, safety, business environment and city life, he added.  The 2019 Singapore Grand Prix was estimated to have generated $70 million to $75 million in media value, according to a McKinsey study cited by METI.  Maintaining the head start  In 2026, Singapore will host its first-ever F1 Sprint race, on Saturday, Oct 10 – a two-day, 100km race that is hosted by just six circuits this season.  The Sprint format alters the dynamic of the traditional Marina Bay Street Circuit weekend, and could make the Singapore race weekend feel like two big race days instead of one, said Llewellyn.  Saturday gets its own race, giving fans another reason to come earlier and stay longer.  For hotels, it offers an opportunity to earn more if more guests arrive on Thursday and stay longer.  It remains to be seen whether fans will see the Sprint as a must-attend event, since this is Singapore’s first time hosting a Sprint, Llewellyn said.  To keep its competitive edge, experts said Singapore must continue to convert more F1 race visitors into long-term tourists and business connections by linking race week with high-value conferences, business-cum-leisure packages, and MICE (meetings, incentives, conferences, and exhibitions) events.  Regional travel partnerships can encourage onward trips across ASEAN, while digital matchmaking connects delegates with local businesses. Hosting networking events in Marina Bay and Orchard Road can further showcase Singapore’s commercial ecosystem.  The Singapore Grand Prix was never just a sporting event from the start. It is being used as a tourism draw, a business-networking platform, a showcase for local companies and a recurring global advertisement for the city.  “The issue is less about whether Singapore should continue hosting F1, and more about whether it can continue extracting scarcity value from the event as competing cities replicate the street-race model,” Lee said.
